neutral: The letter dated the 20th was received a few days ago. Instructions are requested regarding books, clothes, and other items, as well as the start date of the academic year. Presumably, information has been provided regarding the $525.00 bill from St. Francis. Guidance is sought concerning this bill prior to arrival, assuming cash payment is not possible.
styled: I received your welcome letter of the 20th a few days ago. I would ask now what I should do with regards to books, clothes, etc, as also when your scholastic year begins. I suppose you were informed about my bill of $525.00 at St. Francis'. What should I do about that before I go to join you? - supposing I could not pay cash.

neutral: Act kindly towards those who dislike you, and wish well for those who harass and spread false accusations about you. A desire for guidance and a favorable outcome for everyone is expressed. A small donation from the community leader is included to assist with current needs.
styled: "Do good to them that hate you, and pray for them that per- secute and calumniate you. Praying Almighty God to direct you and them - and us all according to His merciful will and inclosing a little donation from Rev. Father Superior to help you in your present need, I remain

neutral: Father visited on the 10th, and everyone at home is well. He mentioned that you appeared to be lonely in your remote location. I urge you to be content for now and to maintain hope, just as Mother did during her times at the River-bank and Trimbelle. You are aware that she faced difficulties in those locations and demonstrated patience and acceptance. Now, after many years, Father speaks of great comfort. It is enough to inspire admiration and gratitude when one considers our parents' past and now observes their present circumstances and prospects. May their future continue to improve as they approach the end of their lives. Personally, I commend you for your current difficulties, preferring them over you experiencing material prosperity, even if you were close to community and spiritual comforts. I believe you and your family are safer, especially in the long term, provided you maintain your moral and spiritual discipline.
styled: Father was here on the 10th and all are well at home, thanks be to God! He said that you seemed to be lonesome out there, being so far from church etc. Well Dear Ella, I only pray you to content yourself for the present and pray and hope-even as you know poor dear Mother did, at the River-bank & at Trimbelle. You must know that there were trials in those places and indeed patience & resignation exercised. Now after so many years Father speaks of great consolation. It is really enough to draw a tear of admiration and gratitude for God's merciful providence, if one only considers the past (of our dear Parents) and now beholds their present circumstances and prospects. May their sky continue to brighten as their end approaches. For my part dear Sister I congratulate you on your present trials much rather than if you were "prospering" in riches even within a block of the Most Blessed Sacrament. I think you and yours are safer, especi- ally in the long run. If you only make your acts of contrition, etc.

neutral: Thank you for the card with holiday greetings. It is the first picture of a patron figure I have received. I also send similar well wishes to you and everyone at Graymoor. I am grateful that someone was inspired with principles of compassion and justice, as demonstrated in your gentle protest to the plaintiff attorneys in the Graymoor property case. I am confident that many people who value justice, including those who read 'The Lamp' and considered that letter, would not remain silent if your community were unjustly ejected from Graymoor. I believe that any reasonable person who understands the facts and current situation at Graymoor will support these views and acknowledge them as ethical.
styled: Please accept my sincere thanks for the little card you sent with Easter greetings. It is the first picture of my dear Patron I have ever received. Be sure also that I here- with return similar good wishes for yourself and for all at Graymoor. I take this occasion also Dear Sister, to assure you that I thanked Almighty God - and do thank Him for hav- ing inspired some one with such truly Franciscan sentiments as were manifest in your gentle protest to the plaintiff at- tornies of that Graymoor Church property case. I am fully con- fident that there are too many upright lovers of justice even among our separated brothers and sisters who read the Lamp and paused at that letter ever to hold their peace while an act of such injustice were perpetrated as would be perpetrated should your community be ejected from Graymoor. In my opinion there is no sane man who has a spark of Christianity who will hesi- tate when he knows the facts and the present circumstances at and around Graymoor, to second these sentiments - and acknow- ledge your sentiments as really Christian.

neutral: With Pope Pius X's urgent call for an effective Catholic press still remembered, and in light of the diligent work of capable publishers, it is concerning to observe that publications identified as Catholic show signs of relying on atheistic ideas. This is particularly notable given the mainstream media's general tendency to confuse fact with fiction, exploit emotions, and demonstrate hostility towards justice and truth. Furthermore, these Catholic publications sometimes exhibit unquestioning obedience to news agencies described as being controlled by a single power, which is widely condemned internationally as the primary source of crime and injustice. The author of this message does not believe you intend for your otherwise respected weekly publication to contain such content. Indeed, the author is confident that you are unaware of such material being published. This confidence persists despite negative reactions (hisses) that the author attempted to dismiss at a recent public gathering, primarily attended by Catholics, when your publication was mentioned.
styled: . With the earnest appeal of the late Pope Pius X regarding an efficient Catholic Press, fresh in memory; and with the honest efforts of able pub- lishers before our eyes; and in view of a secular press everywhere, that in general, makes nothing of confusing fact with fiction, ready at any time to cater to Passion and "Bitterly hostile to Justice and Truth", it is surely not without regret that one sees in pages labeled "Catholic", indications of dependence on sources of thought, positively atheistic -- not to say mani- festations of docile servility to dictations of news Agencies, responsible for their existence to that one power, of all powers on earth internation- ally hated as the most prolific source of crime and injustice. Your present correspondent hardly believes that you wish your, other- wise esteemed little weekly to be a Publication of any such pages. In fact he is confident that you are not conscious of its ever leaving the Press as such, -- and this, notwithstand hisses which he tried to frownaway at a re- cent mass meeting, mostly Catholic, when the Catholic News was mentioned.

neutral: The Superior, who has been ill with a severe cold for about two weeks, asked that our sympathy be conveyed to the community of women. This was due to an unreasonable and unjust eviction, which a strict interpretation of the law allowed unethical individuals to carry out against them. It is anticipated that the majority of those with similar affiliations will condemn this action as having been done in their name and will regret it. There was a general hope that the situation would never escalate to such a contradiction of common justice and compassion. However, worldly successes are often temporary, and ultimate outcomes are not always determined by human intentions. It is held that a higher power has allowed this situation to unfold with an ultimate positive purpose, intending to transform adversity into benefit. Regardless, the principle of finding strength and encouragement when unjustly criticized and persecuted should offer comfort and motivation. The community of women's best course of action would be to earnestly wish well for those who persecute them, in line with these principles.
styled: Rev. Father Superior who has been in with a severe cold for about two weeks wished me to convey our sympathy to the Sisters on account of the unreasonable and unjust eviction which the "killing letter of the law" has enabled unscrupulou men to score against them. - an eviction which we are confi- dent the great majority of our separated brethern will con- demn as done in their name and will regret. Needless to say we all hoped that things would never come to such a farce a- gainst common justice and charity. However, the victories of the world are short-lived- "man proposes but God disposes." We may be sure that Almighty God has not permitted things to take such a course without some good design of His own - to turn evil into good. At all events the words of our Divine Master, "Blessed are ye when they shall revile you and per- secute you ... unjustly for my sake .... ", should be a consola- tion to you and an encouragement. The sisters will hardly be able to do anything better than to pray earnestly for their persecutors, according to the same divine authority.

neutral: He wants to point out that you occasionally publish articles demonstrating independence. As evidence for this claim, he asks you to review your own editorial titled "A SANE VIEW OF IRELAND" in your August 5th issue, or your August 26th editorial titled "A SAD BLOW FOR IRELAND." He suggests examining the latter editorial first. Throughout that article, a weakness is evident, which is unfortunately common even among honest editors. Specifically, you demonstrate a regrettable one-sidedness of information, which might be excusable in an ordinary reader. In relation to the information sources in question, you appear to adopt views on the situation in Ireland that Britain would very much like to be considered the only correct ones. He asks you to review it and consider whether such an article would be more expected in a London newspaper or in any sensationalist metropolitan publications, all of which are completely aligned, not with an oppressed nation or with Catholic principles, but with Britain, which is portrayed as brazen and brutal.
styled: Nevertheless, he wishes for the general good to call your attention to the fact, that, occasionally at least, you do give out pages indicating such said independence. As a proof of this contention he would ask you to review, just your own Editorial: "A SANE VIEN OF IRELAND", in your issue of August 5th; or again your Editorial of August 26th: "ASAD BLOW FOR IRELAND." Let us consider this latter, first. From the very beginning, and throughout, a weakness, sadly common even among our honest Editors, manifests itself. You show, namely, what might be quite excusable in an ordinary reader, a regrettable one-sidedness of infor- mation. With the above-referred to Agencies you seem to espouse views of the situation in Ireland, which Britain would like very much to "believe personally" to be the only proper views. Please just glance it over, and ask yourself if such an article might not be expected rather in a London Daily, or in any of our Metropolitan Yellow Jackets -- every one of them heart and soul in sympathy, not with a crucified Nation or with Catholic Principle, but with Brazen Brutal Britain.

neutral: This discussion will not evaluate the merits or demerits of the treaty-proposed "Free State" or its promoters and founders, who were once recognized as champions of the Republic but are now perceived as working to suppress it. However, it is asserted that if Britain supports the "Free State"—and it appears to do so strongly—then those who genuinely prioritize Ireland, truth, and justice should oppose it. This is because, as demonstrated by centuries of broken treaties and perceived British hypocrisy, the English government or its people cannot have an honest or unselfish interest in Ireland.
styled: Now it is not the object of this correspondent to discuss the merits or the demerits of the treaty-proffered "Free State", or that of its pro- moters and founders -- one time acknowledged Champions of the Republic which now they seem to have given their lives to suppress. I will only say this just now, in favor of the same or against them; if Britain is in favor of the said "Free State" - and she seems to mightily so-then, honest, un- selfish, lovers of Ireland, and of truth, and of justice, ought to be opposed to it. Why? Because as centuries of Britain-broken Treaties, and British hypocrisy make manifest - the English government or the people composing it cannot be honestly or unselfishly interested in Ireland.

neutral: If someone were completely unaware of the objectives or demands of any Irish faction or party—for instance, the Republic and the Free State, the latter of which its creators apparently intended to gradually replace the former with a British-aligned system—that person would simply consider the history of British involvement in Ireland and ask: "Which side of the dispute has British support?" In the current situation, even the least informed individual would find it astonishing that anyone could genuinely ask such a question, or perhaps be so poorly informed.
styled: Consequently if your correspondent knew absolutely nothing of the claims or the aims of any faction in Ireland - or of any party in Ireland -- for example just now, the legitimately established Republic and the said free-state, which later as its authors evidently hoped, was to sneak real British - fashioned into the place of the former, he would simply point to the history of British interest in Ireland and ask the one little question: "On which side of the dispute is British Favor?" In the present crisis, the thickest thug in the tombs prison to whatever side he might incline, would wonder that anyone might be so "thick" as honestly to ask such a question -- perhaps rather, so ill-informed.

neutral: You don't need to be concerned about the frequency of your verbal admissions of wrongdoing or your spiritual connection to the sacred meal. I also ask you to arrange for our prayer services at Trimbelle to be replicated, and for Brother Owney to attend if possible. Please also invite your neighbors, even if they are not Catholic. And during your prayers using beads, please remember to think of me sometimes. I was appointed sub-deacon on December 8th and will likely be ordained as a deacon and then a priest before August. May a guiding spirit direct my superiors in their decisions concerning this, and may its will be done in all matters. I asked my superior for materials and permission to write to you, and he also gave me this small picture for you. My regards to Brother Thomas (Traynor), Owen, and everyone, and a gentle touch for the children, from your brother. P.S. Advise Brother Owney not to neglect the highly beneficial practice of giving to charity for the poor and orphans.
styled: properly you need not be so uneasy about so frequent oral confession - and then your spiritual Communion. I pray you also to have our "Mass- prayers" at Trimbelle imitated, and Owney come to the same if possible- your neighbors, also even if they are not-Catholics, and do not neglect, in your rosaries to think at least sometimes of poor me. I received sub- deaconship Dec. 8th and will probably be ordained deacon-and priest be- fore August. May the Holy Ghost direct my Superiors in their decisions in this regard & His holy Will in all things be done. I asked my Super- ior for material and permission to write to you and he gave me also this little picture for you. With love to Br. Thomas ( Traynor) and Owen and all & a caress for the Little Ones from your brother. P.S. Admonish Br. Owney not to neglect the most salutary -- almsgiving for poor and orphans.

neutral: This situation stems from their direct or indirect dependence for existence on that power. Furthermore, shortly thereafter, that power organized its most brutal criminals (excluding higher intellectuals) from British prisons, equipping them with modern instruments of violence, and deployed them against Ireland. Ireland was unarmed, relying solely on its religious faith. It was not provocative, apart from its unwavering determination to uphold the principles of justice and freedom—principles for which humanity suffered immense losses between 1914 and 1919. The question remains whether these sacrifices will ultimately be without purpose.
styled: Is it not because of their direct or indirect dependence for ex- istence on that same power - that furthermore and immeidately after the "trice" uniformed its most inhuman criminals (Higher intellectuals excepted, ) and sent them from British penetentiaries equipped with every implement of modern savagery against poor little Ireland? Aye, Ireland unarmed except by her Faith in God! Unoffensive except for her surpassing determination to stand by the principles of righteous Freedom -- principles for which from 1914 to 1919 humanity was bled white! Great God! Is it to be all for nothing?

neutral:
Certain information, widely accepted without critical examination by many American editors and leaders, is dangerously inconsistent with both fact and reason. Consequently, it falls far short of the ideal for an efficient press.

Regarding your perspective on Ireland: your initial analysis is thoughtful, based on fair observation and honest conviction. You correctly advise readers to be cautious about accepting newspaper reports as absolute truth. However, you do not explain why these newspapers should be distrusted, or why they are unable to report the truth—especially concerning Ireland—even if those directly responsible were inclined to do so.

The underlying reason, I suggest, is that the power influencing these newspapers is the same one that, through slander and deception, led our country to participate regrettably in events that resulted in the current degradation of Central Europe.
styled: music, so in harmony with the little Welsh "Wizard's" notes, and so cleverly and unsuspiciously danced to by so many Editors and even Clergy and other leaders in America, - are dangerously at variance with both fact and reason; And therefore, dangerously far from Pius X's ideal of an "efficient Catholic Press." Now, as to your above mentioned "SANE VIEW OF IRELAND"; briefly, you start out quite as a thinker, on the authority of fair observation and honest conviction might be expected to do; and you rightly admonish "ordinary Readers" to beware of accepting "Newspaper Reports" above re- ferred to as "Gospel Truths" But you do nottell us why such newspapers should be suspected; or why they dare not tell the truth - especially about Ireland- even if those immediately responsible were so disposed. Let me ask you: Is it not because the Power behind such cewspapers is quite the same as that which through calumny and hypocrisy got our own Country to take such a re- grettable share in what has resulted in the present degradation of Central Europe?

neutral: The author criticizes the endorsement of a perspective on Ireland from an individual holding an official British title and commission. The author notes the extensive quotation of this individual, spanning nearly half a column. The author then quotes a portion of the statement: "Therefore, my first word to you about Ireland is: Do not be too much disturbed by rumors about affairs in Ireland. 'Ireland is on the way to Peace.'" The author expresses skepticism about the reassuring tone of these words, particularly for an American audience. The author questions whether there is a coordinated message among certain agencies and newspapers. The author states that the meaning of Lord Shaw's words is not clear to them. The author questions whether the individual's inspiration comes from the President of Ireland or the Prime Minister of England. Finally, the author asks if the predicted peace is one achieved through suppression, reminiscent of Cromwell's actions, or the peace for which Irish nationalists like Pearse, MacSwiney, Brugha, and Boland sacrificed their lives from 1916 onward.
styled: And you hestitate not to commend as a sane view, in regard to Ireland, the dictum of one holding his title of honor and his commission from that same intriguing, hypocirtical power? And look how you quote him! Nearly half a column! Let me cite just a line or two from your quotation, " ... Therefore, my first word to you about Ireland is: Do not be too much dis- turbed by rumors about affairs in Ireland. "Ireland is on the way to Peace." Smoothe words indeed! How soothing to anxious souls in America! Do you not suspect the polished parallel of the referred to Agencies and Newspapers. Is the meaning of these words of Lord Shaw satisfactorily clear to you? They are not so to me. I would ask: Does your hero - if he be not a wily Briton - get his inspiration from the President of Ireland or from the Primer of England? Is it Cromwelian Peace he predicts, or is it the Peace for which Pearse and Comrades died in 1916 and since, down to MacSwiney and Brugha and Boland?

neutral: The outcry across British circles regarding Collins's death occurred not in December, when his reputation shifted due to his involvement in the London Pact, moving from a position of Irish nationalist confidence to being perceived as serving British interests. Instead, it happened eight months later, when he died while promoting the interests of that pact – which some also attributed to British interests – thereby removing him from any potential British influence. This British outcry would indicate the extent to which Collins's death might, given the circumstances, be accurately described as "A SAD BLOW FOR IRELAND." This suggests that more information is available regarding the current Irish-British relationship than what most editors seem to focus on. It is also hoped that the British perspectives on the Irish situation – particularly those disseminated by influential media organizations –
styled: The wail, therefore, that went up all over British quarters at the fall of unfortunate Collins, not in December, when by the weight of his own name on the London Pact, he lost his balance and tumbled from the heights of Patriotic confidence to the plain of England's "Hero Irishman", but eight months later, when pushing the interests of that pact - some of course say of Britain too - he fell from said plain, beyond all hope of British dic- tation, - that British Wail, I say -- would indicate satisfactorily to my way of reasoning, just about in how much the death of Collins, R. I. P., might, under existing circumstances, be rightly termed "A SAD BLOW FOR IRELAND". Pardon me the rather long digression; but you will probably see thereby that there must be quite a little obtainable information about present Irish- British relationship other than, perhaps the majority of our, otherwise honest Editors seem to be concerned about. It is hoped, too, that the British views of the Irish situation - perhaps we ought to say the Northelif- Hearst and Co.

neutral: The passage questions whether the current situation represents the peace sought by DeValera and his associates, or a more pragmatic peace, such as one a character like Shaw's King might accept. It notes that the speaker explicitly identifies as an experienced British politician. It is noted that his noble title inherently signified his political involvement. There is concern that an official investigation might again reveal that the government's welfare efforts in Ireland are still considered highly objectionable, even more so than a year and a half prior. Before quoting from an individual recognized for their eloquent but deceptive language – an "old politician" from an earlier period whose political insights remain pertinent in the 20th century – it is clarified that this is not done with any malicious intent.
styled: Is it finally the peace for which DeValera and comrades are still holding out, which God only can give -- and is giving shortly - or what Shaw's King would be satisfied to call Peace? Do not forget that he tells you plainly that he is, "talking as an old Politician" - a British one, of course. Strange he did not know that his title assures us that he was both, before he was lorded. Ah Shaw! "Do not be too much disturbed -- "lest it be once more officially probed and found that your government's welfare work in Ireland still "stinks" in the nostrils of civilization "worse than it did eighteen months ago. Now before quoting from an acknowledged adept at lingual smoothness and duplicity - "an old politician", before poor Shaw was born or thought of, and undoubtedly as active in 20th century politics as any of his titled juniors - let me assure you that your correspondent is not doing this in any spirit of vindictiveness or out of malice to any one.

neutral: It is evident that individual leaders have been and continue to be guilty of criminal silence and mockery, just as it is clear that nations are composed of individuals. However, their actions now appear to escalate their wrongdoing. Instead of showing personal and national shame that no one has emerged to expose those acting hypocritically, some leaders are now openly aligning themselves with the very forces causing harm and destruction, specifically identifying with the primary aggressor against nations. They calmly debate minor moral distinctions, thereby intentionally or unintentionally shifting focus from the actual causes of problems in Ireland: the presence of British soldiers and British corruption (as noted by Dr. Ryan, for example, in "America"). This situation clearly exemplifies focusing on trivial matters while ignoring significant issues. Those who mislead others deserve condemnation. Bitterness, like falsehood and exaggeration, serves no constructive purpose in a just cause.
styled: Aye, God help us, and forgive us! That individual leaders have been and are guilty of that criminal silence and that mockery, is as positively clear as the fact that nations are made up of individuals. They seem now, however, to be going further into crime. In- stead of blushing for shame, personal as well as national, that no one has a- risen like Daniel of old to convict the hypocrites, some of them are be- ginning to come out on the side of shame itself, on the side of the bull-dog and the lion -- the side of the arch-ravager of nations. They speculate with the coolness of game-cook gamblers on hair-splitting points of morality, thus wittingly or unwittingly-diverting attention from the real source of troubles in Ireland-the presence of British Soldiers, and of British corrup- tion (See Dr. Ryan, E.G. in"America" ) Is not this clearly a case of the Scriptural, "Straining at a gnat, and swallowing a camel?" Shame on the "blind Guides"! Pardon me if your correspondent seem acrimonious, and may the Lord help us to see clearly! for Bittemess like falsity and Exaggeration is to no purpose in an honest cause.

neutral: The author expresses concern for peace in Ireland, believing it to be threatened by Shaw and those who share his views, and by the kind of peace they envision for the nation. The author finds civilization's understanding to be profoundly flawed. People, the author notes, often marvel at the naivety of early humans and their unquestioning acceptance of deception. However, despite advancements in science and historical knowledge, the author contends that contemporary society refuses to acknowledge, or even consider, that the modern press, which the author describes as offensive, is influenced by the same malevolent force attributed to the serpent in ancient narratives. The author asserts that the "Great Press" of today is indeed offensive, citing its perceived hostility to justice and truth, which the author equates with hostility to God, who is considered the embodiment of both. A reference to Pope Leo XIII's 1902 encyclical is provided. The author observes that humanity, whether considered civilized or not, generally behaves as if this malevolent power is merely a childish myth, and questions why this is the case.
styled: Alas, too, for peace and Ireland unless the Lord deliver her from Shaw and his kind, and from the peace they would wish for the Ireland of the Saints! God help our civilization at all events, for its hopelessly darkened understanding. We sometimes wonder at the simplicity of our poor first Parents and at their docile blindness toward their seducer. Yet, with all our science and with all the manifestation of historic ages, we refuse to recognize -- nay even to suspect-behind the blasphemous press of to-day, the same power that animated the wretched serpent. Aye, positively nothing less than blasphemous in the "Great Press" of to-day, because "Bitterly hostile to justice and truth" and therefore hostile to God himself who is eternally both. (See encyc'1 Leo XIII-1902) A civilized humanity, or as uncivilized, we act in general these days as though that power were nothing more than a childish myth. How?

neutral: Millions of young men are sacrificed for the principle of "Self-Determination." However, nations remain silent regarding MacSweeney's 74-day protest unto death and his nation's prolonged suffering and protest. These protests are made in the name of that sacrifice and for justice, opposing an international attempt to undermine that fundamental principle. Such silence alone reveals civilization as a sham and a farce, an outrage against intelligence and decency. It also exposes the allied nations' stated justifications for their war against and degradation of Central Europe as clear hypocrisy. No nation or individual should deceive themselves; consequences will eventually follow. The allied nations and their civilization have been mocking the honest peoples of the earth. Who is to blame? Where is the ideal press, both proactive and defensive?
styled: We sacrifice untold millions of our choicest youth and manhood for the prin- ciple of "Self-Determination" - nothing more or less in reality than a jus- tification of the Catholic Dogma of "Free Will" - and the nations stand mute at the 74 days martyrdom of a MacSweeney protesting and the age-long cru- cifixion of his nation protesting in the name of that same awful sacrifice and in the name of eternal justice against nothing less that the astounding outrage of an international attempt to destroy that very fundamental prin- ciple" - that God-given faculty. Does not such silence alone brand our so-called civilization as a sham and a farce? An outrage it is, pure and simple, on intelligence and decency. Does it not brand the professions of the allied nations for their war against and their degradation of Central Europe as manifest hypocrisy? Let no nation, much less individuals deceive themselves: God will not be mocked forever! And the allied nations, and their civilzation have been mocking the honest peoples of the earth, and surely not less the Eternal God of honest people. Who is to blame? Where is our ideal Catholic Press? Offensive and Defensive? God help us!

neutral:
The individual aims to protect not only The Catholic News but also the broader honest press from a more severe humiliation than any legitimate criticism could inflict. This humiliation is seen as inevitable unless action is taken to stop the regrettable tendency to favor British viewpoints, British false accusations, and, most dangerously, British distorted truths.

Considering the ongoing conflict in Ireland, which is characterized as British-initiated, supported, and waged, one might observe that Lord Shaw's statements bear a resemblance to a passage found in the third chapter of Genesis. This passage reads: "And the Serpent said to the Woman: No, you shall not die, for God knows that on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil." (Genesis 3:4).

This serves as an example of distorted truth and a questionable prediction. While it is not disputed that their eyes were opened, the resulting understanding was unfortunate, a sentiment extended to the reader's own understanding.
styled: He wishes simply to save, not only The Catholic News, but as much as he can, the honest press in general from humiliation more serious than any honest criticism could be, and that must come unless something be dore to arrest the above lamented in- clination of positively favoring British views, and British Calumnies, and worst of all because more dangerous, British Colored Truths. Who will doubt, at second thought and in the light of the present British-Begotten and British-fostered - and I must say British-waged War in Ireland that the above words of Lord Shaw are at least a weak parallel to those we find in the Third Chapter of Holy Writ? Here they follow: "And the Serpent said to the Woman: No, you shall not die the death, for God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened and you shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil." (Gen. 111, 4) That is just an example of colored truth and of dubious prediction. No one doubts that their eyes were opened. But alas for their vision! and alas for your vision and mine!

neutral:
The author observes a recurring pattern in history. A bishop condemned Joan of Arc for witchcraft. Under pressure from the British, this bishop (who was considered Catholic at the time) subjected her to severe cruelties before she was ultimately burned at the stake as a heretic. Reports indicate that some high-ranking American clergy would treat a number of Irish women similarly, even without British influence.

The author challenges the view that Eamon DeValera "seems to have completely lost his reason," asking who is responsible if not the power supported by these clergy members—a power DeValera has resisted, evaded, and endured for four years, a period that has been long and difficult for Ireland and for DeValera himself. Beyond British hypocrisy, the author also points to international silence and the previously mentioned leaders as contributing factors.
styled: But history, it seems here as well as elsewhere, must repeat itself, It was a Bishop that condemned St. Joan of Arc for witchery and that a little later, durressed as he was by the British (and at that, time supposed to be a Catholic), exposed her to unmentionable cruelties and finally burned her at the stake as a heretic. If reports be true there are one or two pre- lates in America who would do the like for a number of Irish Joans, even without British duress. May the Good God deliver us from scandals! But I would ask his Lord- ship from Buffalo and his Grace from Baltimore if "Eamon DeValera seems to have completely lost his reason", who is to blame, if not the despicable power his own Grace and his lordship seem to be now espousing and that DeValera has frustrated, escaped and withstood these four years -- so long and so bitter for poor Ireland, and for DeValera? What is to blame after British hypocrisy more than the above mentioned international silence? More than the already referred to leaders and guides?

neutral: The author declines to discuss the details of the matter, citing a lack of experience and inclination to analyze such documents. However, the author observes that if "differences arise between honest lovers of a common cause mostly because of misunderstandings," then regardless of the motive for publishing the personal correspondence between De Valera and his opponents, the publication has, intentionally or not, positively contributed to resolving disagreements between Ireland (as represented by De Valera) and those in America who genuinely oppose De Valera. The documents, including De Valera's message, the reply it prompted, and the two pages signed "J.D.," would lead a reader unfamiliar with the Irish question to question the nature of the friendship between the F.O.I.F. and Ireland.
styled: For my part, I cannot think of going into details about it at this time, being as you know only a simple religious and therefore, not experienced in and not inclined to analyse such documents. This much, however, I will say in its favor: If "differences a- rise between honest lovers of a common cause mostly because of misun- derstandings," then, whatever the motive for publishing the personal correspondence as therein given between DeValera and his opponents, the author has wittingly or unwittingly taken a positive step in the direction of settling differences between Ireland, in her representa- tive, and those in America who honestly oppose the same representative, De Valera. Personally, at least, if I had never followed up the Irish ques- tion at all, as I certainly have been and am, I would be inclined to ask, on reading DeValera's message and the reply it occasioned - to say nothing of the two pages signed "J. D." -- I would be more than inclined to ask: "Is this the Friendship that joins the F.O. I.F. and martyred Ireland?

neutral: De Valera's repeated statements reveal a loss of trust, diminished optimism, and a resolve bordering on desperation. This resolve is misinterpreted by Ireland's opponents as unyielding pride, though even Ireland's staunchest critics concede that her representative is undoubtedly conscientious. Judge Cohalan's reply does not indicate any willingness to cooperate with De Valera or with Ireland. Instead, it shows clear prejudice and a predetermined intent to resist, and even obstruct, cooperation from the F.O.I.F. In his reply to De Valera, the judge appears to represent himself and his constituents as aligning more with an American Protective Association than with the F.O.I.F.
styled: Does not DeValera's sentence after sentence show at once a disappointed confidence and a depressed hope as well as a determination forced almost to desperation?" -- which determination opponents of Ire- land seem to mistake for unbending pride: though even the bitterest of them have to acknowledge that her representative is , "doubtlessly conscientious." But I would ask further, as I ask now: "Is there anything in Judge Cohalan's reply that would manifest even a consent to co-operate with De Valera, or with Ireland herself in the person of her representative?"is there not, on the contrary, evidence of a decided prejudice and a preconceived determinaation to resist -- not to say thwart cooperation on the part of the F.O.I.F .? In other words, does not the judge, in said reply to DeValera speak for himself and his constituents as really more an American Pro- tective Association than as the F.O. I.F.

neutral: When an individual, machine, organization, or small group prioritizes itself over the cause it serves, it ceases to be beneficial and begins to cause harm, irrespective of its past achievements. These words, written in Rome on January 1, 1920, seem to anticipate issues that many sincere members of the F.O. I.F. have considered personally significant, a view also shared by numerous members of the A.A.R.I.R. The author expresses a wish for sincere members of both organizations to exhibit selfless justice, consistency, and genuine goodwill, and extends this wish to every sincere reader of the Irish World and Industrial Liberator. In a postscript, the author indicates that if space allowed, they would suggest printing the previously mentioned personal correspondence, convinced that it would reveal the true origin of the potential problem.
styled: "The moment a man or a machine or an organization or a clique gets bigger than the cause, get away from any or all of them because they have ceased to be of any good and have begun to do harm no matter what the past record of any or all of them be." Coming from Rome where they were written January 1, 1920, these words have the ring of at least a foresight of what many an honest member of the F.O. I.F. has taken as a kind of personal matter of thought as is manifested from the multitudes of their brethren of the A.A.R.I.R. May God bless the honest members of both with a sense of unsel- fish justice and consistency and unaffected charity. And may He bless every honest reader of the Irish World and Industrial Liber- ator! P.S. If it were not for your lack of space, I would suggest printing the personal correspondence above referred to so convinced I am that the real root of the would-be trouble is thereby shown.

neutral: The author expresses a wish for compassion and understanding for the leaders involved, despite the perceived gravity of their actions and responsibilities. It is genuinely believed that if Eamon DeValera remains mentally capable, this would be an extraordinary occurrence. If he still commands the support of 30,000 dedicated individuals, even if they are largely unarmed, there remains hope for self-determination and democracy. Regardless, if the principle of self-determination for individuals is inherently just, then the majority in Ireland still supports the core ideals of the Republic. Furthermore, despite all opposing reports, criticisms, and forces, if the fundamental principles and the Republic of Ireland are inherently just, then the majority in Ireland supports DeValera. DeValera, drawing upon deep conviction, similar to his stance when facing execution in 1916, is predicted to ultimately overcome all adversaries, achieving victory even through profound sacrifice, if necessary.
styled: May God in his mercy overlook the crime of it all and pity such leaders and their respon- sibility. Your correspondent prays for them without exception. But if Eamon DeValera, as it is honestly believed, has still his wits about him, is it not really next to a miracle of God's Providence? If he still has 30,000 patriot soldiers behind him, though practically without arms, is there not still hope for "Self Determination", and hope for Democracy? At all events, if Almighty God is in favor of the principle of "self- determination" for men of free-will, then the majority in Ireland is behind the soul of the Republic still: and notwithstanding all reports to the con- trary, and all criticisms to the contrary, and all powers to the contrary, if God is still for Principle and for the Republic of Ireland, the majority in Ireland are behind DeValera; and DeValera, appealing to the Sacred Heart, as when sentenced to be shot in 1916, will triumph in the end over every enemy, if need be even as the Maiden-Soldier Saint triumped in the crown of a glorious Martyrdom!

neutral:
Regarding a document recently circulated, which claimed to be a statement from Michael J. Gallagher about Eamon DeValera's visit to the United States (a copy of which was reportedly sent to the recipient's office), the author commended the recipient's dignified silence or prudent oversight. This non-response was considered appropriate, especially given the recipient's extensive experience and responsible position, and preferable to the Irish World expressing resentment.

The author found it difficult to believe that the statement was truly a carefully considered expression from Michael J. Gallagher, whom the author admired and believed to be dedicated to Ireland and justice. However, it was considered possible that Gallagher might have been misled, and that the author was mistaken. This possibility brought to mind a similar self-deception approximately 10 months prior. At that time, regarding Cohalan's recently revealed "unfortunate break" with DeValera, the author had expressed a hope that Cohalan's motives were not unworthy. It was suggested that further time and honest criticism of the statement might elicit different views or statements from Gallagher.
styled: Rather than find bitterness in the Irish World concerning the folder recently sent out purporting to be a "statement by Right Rev. Michael J. Gallagher, D.D. dealing with the visit to the United States of Hon. Eamon DeValera," a copy which I have been assured duly reached your office, I want to congratulate you on the digni- fied silence (or prudent oversight) which in this case especially be- comes your long experience and your really responsible position. I do not like to believe that said statement "is really and ex- pression, carefully considered, of a Bishop whom in more than one way I have admired, and who undoubtedly loves Ireland and justice. Pos- sibly, however, he has been beguiled and I deceive myself, as it seems now that I die deceive myself about 10 months ago when speaking about Cohalan's unfortunate break with DeValera, then recently made manifest, I asked you, "let us hope that his motives are not so unworthy." Per- haps a little time and honest criticism of the "statement will bring out other views and other expressions from Bishop Gallagher.

neutral:
Individuals who cause division in any important endeavor are those who abandon core principles for selfish reasons. Similarly, the true strength of any nation can be measured by its widespread commitment to moral integrity. This commitment, however, seems lacking in the nation claiming to be the "greatest republic," given the government's prolonged silence regarding alleged wrongdoings by Britain and its allies.

If the F.O. I.F. is considered the product of one individual's unique talent and thus their personal property, it is understandable for that person to react strongly when others do not acknowledge their claim. However, if, as some believe, such organizations are considered to have a purpose beyond individual ownership, then the more and longer an individual reacts strongly in such a situation, the more unreasonable and pathetic they appear.

In conclusion, I would highlight the practical advice of McGinnis, a former president of the F.O. I. F., who now leads his broader organization.
styled: The splitters -- would-be or other- wise -- in any great cause are those who for selfish motives swerve from first principles, even as the real greatness of any nation --- republic or other -- may be measured by the pervading spirit of national righteousness which, by the way, considering our governmental silence these many moons regarding British and allied outrages, etc, is not saying much for the "greatest republic." Of course, if the F.O. I.F. is the fruit of any one's personal gen- ius, and therefore liable to be claimed as personal property, nobody can blame such genius for frothing a little when a stranger refuses to ac- knowledge his right, but if, as quite a few of us believe, such societie are divinely providential then the more and the longer such a "genius" frothes the more ridiculous and the more pitiable -- not to say contempti- ble he makes himself. In conclusion, while I trust the above may offend no one, I would call attention in a very practical advice of a former president of the F.O. I. F., the dear Carmelite Father McGinnis, now General of his whole Order.

neutral: There was likely some concern regarding Pasqual, also known as George Gordon. While the speaker considered it inappropriate to take special interest in Pasqual's case, Pasqual seemed to confide in the speaker, a trust he did not extend to others who could have offered more help. The speaker believed that a few details might be useful. An impression was formed, either shortly before Pasqual arrived from Garrison and went to the hospital, or during his hospital stay, that he was not very practical. The speaker visited Pasqual twice during his hospitalization. It was noted with regret that, to the speaker's knowledge, no one else from their location visited him. The reception Pasqual received upon his return to the community residence was also regrettable, as it conveyed the impression that he was not welcome or wanted. The speaker attempted to excuse this reception but was unsure if the attempt was successful.
styled: You will have been naturally more or less anxious about Brother Pasqual if we may still speak of him as such, instead of George Gordon. It would hardly be in place for me to take special interest in his case, but he seems to have a sort of confidence in me that, sorry to say he does not show to others who would be able to do more for him. I am sure a few minor details in this regard will not be unwelcome, and possibly will be of use - I can not say just how, but I got the impression shortly before 3. P. came here from Garrison and went to Hospital, that he was not very practical or it was while he was in the hospital. Nevertheless I visited him twice during his stay there as a patient. I regretted that no one else (that I know of) visited him from here. More still I regretted the reception given him at his return to the Monastery. It seemed to me as an assurance that he was not welcome or wanted. I tried to excuse it. I do not know if I succeeded or not.

neutral: If an organization is defined as 'an association of American citizens founded to assist the Irish people in securing freedom for the Irish people,' then it is justifiable for Ireland's representative to refuse even to discuss a compromise with leaders of a society whose general membership would be rightly indignant at certain suggestions. These leaders, despite their stated affiliation, might in reality hold views akin to those of groups historically hostile to Irish interests, rather than genuinely being 'Friends of Ireland.' Any apprehension regarding an alliance between Ireland and England is as baseless and disingenuous as the historical American Protective Association's unfounded fears of an alliance between the Pope and perceived evil forces. Concerning the alleged 'Cuban blunder' attributed to De Valera, his subsequent statements and actions, including his return to Ireland, clearly demonstrate that this accusation is a calumny. Discussions or accusations regarding division are without merit when the fundamental objectives are practically identical.
styled: is defined -- "an association of American citizens founded to assist the Irish people in securing freedom for the Irish people?" How, then, can anyone blame the repre- sentative of the Island of Saints and Sages for refusing, even "to dis- cuss the question" of a compromise with such leaders of a society whose rank and file members would be justly indignant at the very insinuation, though in all truth they might be called real "A.P.A's" instead of Friends of Ireland? Their fear of danger from Ireland's alliance with England would be, or is, just about as reasonable as the fear of the original A.P.A. from an alliance of the Pope with the professed powers of Hell -- just as affected, too. As to DeValera's "Cuban blunder," well, DeValera's every utterance ever since, not to say his every action, including his tragic return to Ireland, seals that as an evident calumny. Talk about "splitters," as long the objective is practically iden- tical sounds to me like so much wind.

neutral: He was informed, as he started upstairs, that while he could stay, the location was not a hospital. Approximately thirty minutes later, he came downstairs, stating he was going to St. Vincent's Hospital for a thorough examination. Unaware of the circumstances and assuming this was an instruction from someone at St. Francis, the speaker only asked if he would return that night. He reportedly indicated he would go to Pitt Street. This occurred on Sunday afternoon. On Tuesday morning, he arrived at the office unshaven, expressing uncertainty about the treatment he had received both there and at Pitt Street. The Guardian was absent upon his arrival, and he appeared disinclined to see him. He was strongly advised to go and see the Definitor in East New York, with the assurance that a phone call would be made in the interim. The Guardian arrived before B.P. departed and was informed of B.P.'s presence and that he had been persuaded to go to Martin. It was then proposed, when Brother...
styled: I heard the words told him as he was starting upstairs: "You can stay here of course, but this is no hospital - - " About half an nour afterwards he came down, saying he was going to St. Vincent's Hospital to get a thorough examination. Not knowing the circumstances, and thinking that was the order of some one at St. Francis, I asked him no questions except if he would be back tonight. I believe he said he would go over to Pitt St. That was Sunday afternoon. Tuesday moming he came to the office sine- barba - doubting what to think of the manner of treatment here and at Pitt St. etc. Fr. Guardian was out when he came, whom he did not seem to want to see, and I told him he should by all means go over and see Father Definitor in East N. Y. and that I would try and phone over in the meantime. Fr. Guardian came in before B. P. left and I told him he was there, and that I had determined him to go to Fr. Martin. Then I proposed - when Br.

neutral: He was gone, and I was instructed to call on his behalf to explain the situation. However, I was forbidden to do so. I heard nothing further about the matter until two days ago, when I received the accompanying letter. Paul was here last evening, discussing Br. I informed him about this letter. This morning, I conducted a religious service in the Assisium. Afterwards, I walked two blocks west to the Hotel Theresa and spoke briefly with Br. He had been sleeping until I called. He seemed normal and did not explicitly complain about anyone, but rather seemed to ponder the implications of the situation. He stated he was unsure how to interpret the situation. He had consulted a friend, who is a lawyer, yesterday and explained the entire situation to him, to determine if a resolution could be reached.
styled: was gone - that I phone in his name and tell them something of the situation etc. I was simply forbidden to do so. That was the last I heard about the case till two days ago when I received the enclosed letter. Fr. Paul was here last evening and talking about 3r. I told them of this letter. This morning I said holy Mass up in the Assisium and afterwards returning I went of two blocks west to the Hotel Theresa and had a short talk with Br. He had been sleeping till I phoned up. He seemed quite himself; did not exactly complain against anyone, but seemed rather to wonder, what it all should come to. He told me he did not know what to think about it. He had been to a friend of his - a lawyer - yesterday and told him all about the case, to see if he could get something decided etc.

neutral:
This report is presented without assigning blame or offering excuses. Paschal appears willing to follow instructions and seems aware that he did not receive entirely fair treatment from the superior.

A large package of certificates for the Seraphic Mass Association was received yesterday. They arrived promptly and in good condition. The Guardian reported that $1002.00 in cash has been received this month. Reports of positive outcomes attributed to this source continue.

Adelhelm visited today from Glencliff, bringing chronicles and positive reports. Current information indicates that all members in this part of the Province are well. John Parsons, a student in Yonkers, has shown significant improvement.
styled: Now Dear Father Provincial I do not wish to blame anyone or to excuse anyone else. "Brother Paschal" seems to me willing to be directed. He seems quite conscious that he did not receive entirely "a fair deal" with the superior above - - - Well, may our dear Lord God direct him and us all We received quite a large package of certificates yesterday, for the Seraphic Mass Association. They came in good time and shape. Fr. Guardian just told me that the cash received this month already is $1002. 00. Thanks be to God! the reports of favors as through this source continue. Fr. Adelhelm was down Today from Glencliff with chronicles and good reports. As far as I know all the brethren in this end of the Province are well. The student John Parsons in Yonkers seems quite improved.

neutral: Thank you for your recent communication. I am pleased to hear you are doing well. Please convey my best wishes to any friends you encounter in Yonkers. This is the busiest location I have experienced to date. It has been nearly 31 years since I moved to Yonkers. Willie was associated with Father Stephan.
styled: My Dear Willie: - Many thanks for favor just read. you are well and doing. Thank God for everything. I am glad to know I wish you would convey best wishes and blessings to all my friends you chance to meet in picturesque, beautiful Yonkers. This has been the busiest place I been located in so far . . · Near 31 years now since I went to Yonkers - and Willie was one of Fr. Stephan's boys.

neutral: This information is too late to save Garland's employment. However, if the truth about Garland and the prominent individual who previously undermined him is discovered, it will become clear what was lost by dismissing such a promising employee. Furthermore, this knowledge will provide clear guidance for decisive action should an opportunity arise to assist Garland and the sender.
styled: This of course is coming too late to save Garland his employ- ment, but if you find out the truth about him as I know it, and about said prominent party who has knocked him before, you'll realize something of what you've lost in dropping such a promising employee. But more than this, you will know what to do without hesitation if occasionally you have an opportunity to do him and me a favor.

neutral: Numerous examples demonstrate this. In March or early April, when Mr. Portius faced a serious difficulty, Mr. Garland provided a solution that yielded remarkably positive results. Prior to that, when Mr. and Mrs. Dory were in a desperate situation and felt incapacitated, Garland brought them to this location, and they subsequently regained their vitality. The ongoing hospitalization of Mr. J. Phillips provides another instance of compassionate assistance. When C. H. Chisholm was threatened with a severe infection, Garland immediately contacted me by phone and then visited in person to arrange for the enrollment card to be sent. The positive outcome of that situation is well known. The purpose of these details is to caution you against harmful rumors concerning Rae Garland, originating from a prominent individual who was significantly involved in the illegal acquisition of Garland's cemetery, the Mt. Vernon Memorial Park.
styled: I need not go far for examples to prove this. When your Mr. Portius was in anxiety last March or early April about a very threatening difficulty, Mr. Garland had a remedy astonishingly happy in its marvelous results. Before that, when Mr. Dory and wife seemed next to desperate, and religiously paralized Garland brought them hither and they seemed to take on new life and energy. The story of Mr. J. Phillips' still in the hospital afords another example of fraternal charity, - When C. H. Chisholm was threatened with blood-poison Garland could not wait to get over but phoned first and then came over to have me send the enrollment card. You know better than I what resulted. But why all such details? I simply want to put you "wise" against poisonous intimations regarding Rae Garland, on the part of a certain prominent party" who had a big share in the robbing of Garland of his cemetery, the Mt. Vernon Memorial Park.

neutral: I informed him that I was not personally impressed by what I perceived as his lack of earnestness or commitment regarding a particular observance while he was with us at Our Lady of Angels. Therefore, I suggested he should seriously consider making a personal commitment to improve his conduct in this or other areas, especially if his circumstances became more favorable for his well-being. He then mentioned the possibility of undertaking a period of reflection with the Jesuites, which I affirmed would be, in my opinion, the most beneficial course of action for him. I informed him that I would write to you about him, and he expressed his desire for me to do so. I had intended to inform the Guardian about my visit and my plan to write to you regarding the matter, but I ultimately decided it was more prudent to keep silent about it. However, before I had the opportunity to inform him, and even before I made the decision to remain silent, he prohibited me from corresponding with "3r. P." Furthermore, during a specific communal event before dinner, he delivered a notable admonition, generally related to this situation, while we were all in a kneeling posture as novices.
styled: I told him as much as that I had not been personally edified at what seemed to me his want of fervor or devotion to holy Communion while he was with us in Our Lady of Angels; and therefore I thought he ought to turn earnestly to Headquarters - meaning the Tabernacle and make some promise to do better in this, or some other regard, if things adjusted themselves favorably to his peace. Then he said something about making a retreat with the Jesuites. I told him that would, in my opinion, be the best thing he could do. I told him I would write you about him and he said he wished I would. I wanted to tell Father Guardian of my visit and of my proposition to write you all about the case, but I decided it as prudent to say nothing to him about it. Before I had a chance to do so, before deciding, he forbade me to correspond with "3r. P." and at culpa before dinner gave quite a little admonition, in a general way, bearing on this case, while we all knelt as novices.

neutral: It is 10:30 p.m. and I should probably be asleep, but I want to write you a few words of encouragement, which I've had to postpone until now. I am pleased with reports of your continuous improvement. I would have liked to visit you today, but it was raining, and after leaving the dentist, I only had time to go home for dinner. I hope you continue to improve until you are back at work. It is possible that your knee may remain slightly impaired, though we hope for the best and accept whatever outcome may occur. Considering your condition during the first week or two, it seems remarkable that you recovered at all. I believe your suffering was not in vain, and that others, not just yourself, gained a profound benefit from it.
styled: It has just struck 10:30 p.m. and I perhaps ought to be slum- bering before this, but I want to do what I've been forced to put off thus far - write you a few works of encouragement, etc. I surely am pleased with words and reports of your now constant im- provement. I would like to have called to see you today but it was raining and when I left the dentist I had just time to get home for dinner. ... I hope you will continue to improve till you are back "on the job" again. Of course it is possible that you may be a little lame in that knee of yours, though we will hope for the best and leave it all to the divine Lover of our Souls - Yes leave everything to Him - offering ourselves to Him to suf- fer whatever His love may permit. When I think of your condition for the first week or two it looks to me almost like a miracle that you pulled through atall. Thank God for it all! I am sure your sufferings were not lost, and that more than yourself have profited by them spiritually.

neutral: The author expresses disappointment regarding the decision to terminate Garland's employment. Garland reportedly enjoyed the work and showed an unusual level of interest in it, also liking his employer and colleagues. The author's familiarity with Garland's abilities created an expectation that he would enjoy the work, and the author would have been disappointed if he had not. Garland does not blame anyone, though he was initially surprised by the decision. He is described as someone who does not dwell on minor grievances and wishes to move past the situation, expecting the author to do the same. The author clarifies that Garland would object to any complaint being made and that this communication is not a complaint, nor is it made with Garland's knowledge. The author believes this information will be valuable, provided the recipient considers it patiently. Having known Garland for approximately ten years, the author describes him as exceptionally willing to help others and highly effective at proposing solutions during challenges.
styled: God bless you. I hope you are well. I was rather disapointed in your decision to drop my friend Garland from your employ. I know that he liked the work and that he took an interest in it such as few of your employes are wont to take. He liked his employer and his associates. I would have been disapointed had he failed to so, because I know something of his ability. Mr. Garland blames no one, though he was dazed at first. He is too big a character to hold petty mis- understandings, etc. He wants me to forget it as he hopes to do himself. I know that he would object to complaining to you and I am not coplaining. I am doing this without his knowledge. I am confident that you will not regret this my information, -- at least if you will have just a little patience with my effort. I have known Mr. Garland for about ten years and I can honestly say that I doubt if I have ever met a person more solicitous to do a favor or more practical in suggesting remedies in time of difficulties.

neutral: The passage emphasizes the importance of showing appreciation for favors received. It is considered crucial to be grateful for enthusiasm, acknowledging those who demonstrate it. Appreciation and gratitude are presented as being as fundamental for social order and harmony as the laws of gravity are for the physical world. The speaker, on behalf of the Capuchin Community, extends thanks to everyone. It is hoped that mutual appreciation will continue to be a core element of their future relationship, just as the event at the Armory suggests it has been in the past.
styled: What I want to stress To-day is the importance these days of appreciation for favors -- on our part; that we be grateful for such enthusiasm -- grateful to God first for such friends' and then to the friends themselves; for in my humble conviction APPRECIATION with its synonum GRATITUDE IS as necessary for social order and harmony as are the laws of gravity for the physical order of inanimate beings. ONCE more, therefore, let me thank you my brethren, one and all, in the name of our Capuchin Community. May mutual appreciation be the soul of our relationship in the future as this affair in the Armory seems to prove it has been in the past. God Bless You All.

neutral:
According to a historical account, Solomon was told that because he had requested wisdom to make sound judgments, rather than long life, wealth, or the lives of his enemies, his request would be granted. He was given a wise and understanding mind, such that no one like him had existed before.

Given the enthusiasm shown by all people, regardless of their background, the organization speaking here considers it a privilege to express its profound appreciation and gratitude. This refers to the generous efforts of numerous individuals who arranged an event for the organization, held this evening at the Naval Armory. The event received enthusiastic support from the general public in the Detroit River region.
styled: "And the Lord said to Solomon: Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life or riches, nor for the lives of thy enemies, but hast asked for thyself wisdom to discern judgement, Behold I have done for thee ac- cording to thy words, and have given thee a wise and under - standing heart, insomuch that there hath been no one like thee before thee .... " In the light of the enthusiasm on the part of our neigh- bors and friends -- our contemporaries without distinction of creed or color -- it is a privilege of our Capuchin Community, in whose name these few words are spoken, to express something of the appreciation that ought to overwhelm us -- something of the gratitude that surely ought to fill our hearts. I refer, of course, to the generous activity on our behalf of, quite a num- ber of our personal friends in arranging the affair, conducted on our behalf in the Naval Armory this evening at O'clock, and so enthusiastically seconded by the public in general on both sides of the Detroit River.

neutral: The enclosed returned letter partly explains the writer's silence regarding your sorrow last August. However, despite that silence, the writer had not forgotten your bereavement. The writer believes that suffering, particularly when it involves children, ultimately serves a benevolent purpose. The writer suggests that you should find happiness this season in the belief that Owen, who was an altar boy, is now considered part of a special group of children in the afterlife. With this perspective, and while also offering condolences, the writer extends wishes for a happy holiday season.
styled: The returned letter herewith inclosed will partly explain my silence at your sorrows last August. But though silent, I have not been al- together unmindful of your bereavement. However we may confidently trust in God to manifest some day a merciful design - not only in your case of such sorrow but in every case where He has per- mitted suffering in order that little children may come to Him. How happy you ought to be in reality this holy season! to have your little Owen, not only an altar boy, but one of the great heavenly army of holy Innocents. In this thought, while in another sense I condole with you, I wish you a holy and a happy Blessed Christmastide!

neutral: It can sometimes be difficult to maintain courage. A key to achieving peaceful contentment involves understanding the vast difference between the finite nature of time and the infinite nature of eternity. Even at its longest, time is brief. The concept of eternity, however, is immeasurable. Therefore, it is important to appreciate our existence. A profound and valuable purpose is presented as understanding, appreciating, and contributing to this existence. This perspective is described as immensely valuable, offering a profound sense of fulfillment for those who embrace gratitude. It is asserted that a force detrimental to one's well-being is particularly encouraged by any form of ingratitude. This is because ingratitude causes significant damage to one's relationship with others and to one's overall sense of connection or purpose. A proverb states that those who are valued or cared for are often subjected to corrective challenges. It is suggested that one might eventually appreciate difficult experiences.
styled: You may think sometimes that it is hard to keep up courage. One phase of contentment - rather I will say a feature of the key to contented peace, - is this: To try to realiz the contrast ( rather than the difference) between Time and Eternity. At the longest time must be so short. But O! Who can fathom Eternity ?!! Then be grateful for what we have -- Existence -- The True Faith God made me to know Him - O what a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure reste in the same. It's Heaven begun - for the grateful on earth To treasure aright? !? !! ... Highest Heaven its worth. Be sure, if the enemy of our souls is pleased at any thing in us it is ingratitude - of whatever kind. Why? ingrati- tude leads to so many brakes with God & neighbor. "Whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth. Some day you will thank God for having been leaf. . God bless you Dorothy B. ...

neutral: Regarding Mrs. Martha Casey's specific request and for guidance, we are certainly willing to assist with these matters. Best wishes to you and your family, Martha. We are pleased to hear you are all well; please continue to maintain your well-being. Cultivate confidence in the future. This will become critically important in the near future, within months or even weeks.
styled: Mrs. Martha Casey - for her special intention. and for His holy guidance - --- God willing, Of course we be glad to pray for same too .. God bless you Martha; you and yours. Glory be to God that you all seem to be well. Keep it up. Foster Confidence in divine Pro- vidence. It will be "crying necessary" be- fore many decades - of months - even of weeks.

neutral: Best wishes to Owen, Martha, and the entire family. Thank you, Owen, for your message last week from Los Angeles. It is good to hear that everyone there is doing well. M. Joachim and I are also well. I hope to visit him soon. I am confident that this experience of his will prove to have been very beneficial for him and for all of us. I hope this proves to be the case.
styled: God bless you Owen and Martha and all the family. Many thanks Owen for your kind favor of last week from Los Angeles. Glad to know all are well down there. Thank God Fr. M. Joachim and myself are well too. I am hoping co go down to see him before long. I am confident that this experience of his will prove to have been a manifest blessing for him and for us all. Pray that it may.

neutral:
The Book of Job states that human life on Earth is a struggle, making no exceptions. The Psalms contain universal calls for profound personal change. One passage (79:20) specifically asks for a higher power to enact this transformation, to manifest its presence, and thereby ensure well-being.

One poet observes that humans are like lost travelers in a turbulent existence, constantly buffeted by circumstances. Imagination and intellect only illuminate a difficult path, and true tranquility is found only in a state of ultimate peace.

More encouraging, especially for those who acknowledge their limitations, the passage states that Jesus Christ, a significant spiritual figure, offers assurance: "My purpose is to call those who have erred."

Drawing on these and similar perspectives, the speaker addresses the audience as fellow individuals and, under current circumstances, intends to discuss Capuchin-Franciscan Appreciation.

A notable historical request, which was considered to have met with ultimate approval, was King Solomon's plea for wisdom to distinguish between right and wrong, and to judge fairly.
styled: Holy Job tells us, "the life of man on earth is a warfare". He makes no exceptions. The Psalmist appeals to us all without exception: "Be ye converted to the Lord your God." and in another place "O Lord God of hosts convert us : and show thy face, and we shall be saved." (Ps. 79-20) A Christian poet whispers to us as a loving brother : "Poor wanderers of a stormy day "From wave to wave we're drive: And fancy's flash and reason's ray serve but to light the troubled way, "There's nothing calm but Heaven. Moore More encouraging than all -- for those who realize their weak- ness -- Jesus Christ, the long promised Messiah our Redeemer, assures us: "I am come to call sinners In the light of Christian reasoning, therefore, brightened by these and similar expressions, I presume to address this audience as my brothers and my sisters; and under present cir- cumstances, on the subject of Capuchin-Franciscan Appreciation. One of the outstanding prayers of all history, with consequent approval of Heaven, was the prayer of King Solomon for wisdom to discern between good and evil -- for wisdom to judge justly.

neutral: Solanus, H.J. Macey, and a nun were present. H.J. had left school due to blindness, which lasted for several weeks. H.J. was brought to the monastery and enrolled in an organization. On January 2, 1934, H.J. was reading on the way home and returned to school the following day. H.J., their father, and two younger siblings had undergone a formal initiation ceremony on December 24th. H.J. now participated in a significant ceremony for the first time. This event, along with many similar reported positive outcomes, was noted. The author observed their own aging. Twenty years had passed since a significant meeting, bringing considerable change. The author pondered what further changes the next twenty years would bring and suggested preparing for the future, referencing J.T.'s preparedness.
styled: Fr. Solanus with H.J. Macey and Sister. H.J. had left school, for some weeks blind. Was brought to Monastery and enrolled in Ser. Mass Assoc'n. reading on way home (Jan 2 - '34) : went back to school next day. Had been baptized with their father and two younger - Dec. 24th. Now received 1st Holy Communion. Thanks be to God for this and many similar favors reported. You see Dear Owen, I'm getting to look like an old man. 20 years since you and I met, have made quite a change; but O! --- what will 20 yrs. more bring? Let us get ready as J. T. got ready. ·

neutral: Your card arrived yesterday while I was repairing a particular cell. It reminded me of our visit thirty months ago when you presided over a significant religious service and the nuns sang. Afterward, following breakfast, we had a meeting with the prisoners. Many changes have occurred since those pleasant days. Thank you, Martha, for your thoughtful card. I wanted to reply to it repeatedly. We have not heard from Edward since September, nor from Guam—which was first taken by Japanese forces—since before the conflict began. I believe it is best not to be overly anxious about future events. One thing we can be certain of is that events are being observed, and in due course, they will unfold in a way that benefits everyone who remains dedicated to their purpose. It appears to me that history is repeating itself, particularly in relation to moral transgressions, such as infidelity. Happy New Year.
styled: God bless you and yours. I was fixing up a certain cell yesterday when this card showed up. It reminded me of our visit some thirty months back when you served the high Mass and the sisters inside sang - and . after breakfast, we had a conference with the prisoners of Jesus. Quite some changes since those pleasant few days .... Many thanks Martha for your beautiful card, etc. I wanted to answer it again and again ..... We have not heard from Fr. Edward since September nor from Guam - first taken by the Japs - since before the trouble .... I think it best to be, not over anxious about whats coming. One thing we may be sure of - God is watching all and in His own time and way will turn all to His glory and ours in as much as we shall persevered in His service. It seems to me it is once more "history repeating itself as against sins"Thou shalt not comit adultery". Happy New Year.

neutral: Good wishes are extended for the recipient's well-being. A request is made to the recipient, known only by reputation, for assistance in finding employment for the bearer, Edmund Walsh, who is described as honest. This request is made with deference, acknowledging potential imposition, and is contingent on the availability of suitable opportunities. Any assistance that can be conveniently provided would be appreciated.
styled: God bless you and yours, I hope you are well. I hope too that I may not be presuming too much in asking your- self of whom I have only heard, to guide the bearer, honest Edmund Walsh to employment, if you have anything in view. I would appreciate anything you might find convenient to do for him.

neutral: Thank you for your communication of the 16th. I am glad to know Bernard M. is feeling more contented. I enjoyed his visit, and I believe he did as well.
