I had limited time with him, but I generally tried to convey the belief that, regardless of one's abilities, the primary purpose of every rational being is to understand the divine and, by adhering to certain principles (which are considered guidelines for overall well-being), to secure one's ultimate fulfillment.
styled: Many thanks for favor of the 16th. Thanks be God! I am glad to know Bernard M. is feeling more contented. I enjoyed his visit as I think he did. I had very little time to really give him but tried at least in a general way, to impress him with the conviction that what ever our faculties be, the one primary purpose of every rational creature is to know God and by keeping the commandments - really just rules of health for body and soul - save our poor souls and gain the crown Eternal.

neutral: I extend my sincere thanks for your kind assistance, though this acknowledgment is belated. Today, I successfully mailed Bernard's certificate. This airmail shipment is expected to arrive quickly. Please inform Patrick that I have not forgotten his letter from several weeks ago, to which I still owe a reply. I am currently overwhelmed with work.
styled: JOY, PEACE AND GRACE BE YOURS - Better late than never. Many thanks for your charitable favor. I succeeded To-day in getting Bernard's certificate off in the mail. By air this ought to fly over it .. Please tell Patrick our dear Brother I am not forgetting his letter - the one I Owe for his several weeks back. - just now "snowed under."

neutral: Sister Mary Rosella was noted on August 9th. Her certificate has been prepared accordingly and is enclosed. I hope it is satisfactory. Thank you for bringing this to my attention. Please excuse the oversight and resulting delay. I understand the demands of working long hours in the hospital. It is a demanding but valuable work, offering opportunities for self-sacrifice and service. Naturally, social life often suffers, and regrettably, family life can also be affected. Family life is truly important and should be supported as much as possible. I trust that you and O.J. have found a source of strength, and I hope that you will continue to find the most effective support possible under the circumstances.
styled: I found Sister Mary Rosella noted on August 9th: so have made out her certificate accordingly and am herewith inclosing. I hope it will be satis- factory - glad you called my attention. Please pardon oversight and consequent delay. I can easily understand something of how you feel, hustling all day in the hospital, etc. It's a great work in itself and a wonderful opportunity to prac- tice charity and of course mortification in so many ways, which brings one nearer to God and endears to the Sacred Heart. Naturally "social life" often suffers - and what is to be regretted in many cases - family life too. This latter is realy important and in every way should be supplied as far as possible. . Prayer in your and O. J.'s case, I trust has helped - and let us hope will help more than anything else under circumstances.

neutral: I am grateful for your support, which I rarely have time to acknowledge. Neil Mccluskey conducted a religious service here last Thursday and remained until approximately 2 p.m. We are expecting Genevieve, his mother, soon, once she arrives at Mildred's in Chicago. M. and Dean are planning to bring her here before meeting Neil in New York and traveling overseas for a course in Louvain.
styled: Many thanks for your favor - aye for you many favors, - that so seldom get time to acknowledge, Rev. Fr. Neil Mccluskey, S.J. had holy Mass her last Thursday and stayed till about 2 p.m. We are expecting M. Genevieve his dear Mother these days when she gets to Mildred's in Chicago. M. and Dean are figuering on bringing her down before joining Neil in N.Y. and going overseas for coure in Louvain. Love and God's grace to all, including each of your patients. .

neutral: These are unsettled times, marked by both worrisome predictions and significant positive events. Edward arrived yesterday afternoon and is preparing to depart for Fort Wayne. He looks well and appears as energetic as usual. I have started to write to you several times in recent months, but with 15-19 hour workdays, I find it difficult to know where to begin. Edward is now traveling to New York.
styled: God bless you and yours these unsettled days - at once of threatening forebodings and of God's outstanding mercies. Rt. Rev. Monsignor Edward is about to leave for Ft. Wayne here since yesterday P.M. He looks well and still seems pushing as usual. I have started several times these later months to write you but, God helps! I hardly know where - 15-19 hour days go to -- Fr. Ed. is going now to New York. P.S.

neutral: Greetings to you and your family. It is hoped that this enrollment will accelerate the anticipated improvement in Sister Mary Thomas' health. This approach rarely fails. Monsignor E. stopped in Fort Wayne (25 miles northeast) last Friday and then traveled here, where a religious service was conducted with the sender's assistance. He had been in the East since July. He was quite successful in his endeavors and appeared to be in good health. Information was received that Owen was scheduled for an operation that day. It is hoped that he has made a full recovery. The profound advantages of one's spiritual beliefs are often underestimated.
styled: God bless you and love Martha - you and yours. Hope this - enrollment - speed the hoped-for improvement in Sister Mary Thomas" health. Thank God it hardly ever faill. Fr. - Rt. Rev Mons. - E'd stopped off last Friday at Fort Wayne (25 miles N.E. ) and came down and I served his holy mass. He had been East since July. Thanks be to God he was quite successful in his mission efforts and looks well. I had word that Owen was to have an operation that day. We hope this finds him well back on his feet. How little we appre- ciate our incalculable privileges - blessings of our holy Faith. Glory be to God.

neutral: Your message has been received and noted. I hope you are all well. E'd visited for a few days around Christmas and appeared to enjoy the visit. I am writing to him tonight; a day of personal significance for him is on the 139 E'd.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor - duly received and noted. I do hope you all keep well - avoiding worry and too much ambition. .... Fr. E'd was down a couple days at Christmas, seems to have enjoyed visit. Am writing him Tonight - his Name day is the 139 E'd.

neutral: Pat continues to do well. I think of him daily. He is close to me in age and must be 83 years old now. I plan to send Pat a letter soon. However, with so many urgent needs, it is difficult to know whom to assist first. This is nearly constant. Finally, we should always encourage gratitude for the many positive aspects of our lives. I am dictating this letter to my brother, Gabriel. Regards to Patrick, Sisters M. Genevieve, Margaret, and all our family and friends in the West.
styled: I am sure glad, that poor brother Pat, with the grace of God is keeping up. I pray and think of him every day. He is next to me in age. He must be 83 now. Please God, I must reach Pat, with a letter soon. Though there so many urgently crying for help, that one heartly known which one to help first. This is almost continuely. God's will be done, in all His blessed designs. In conclusion let us exhort one another on every occasion to be gratuateful to God for the un- countable graces by which we are surrounded. I am dictating this letter to one of my brothers, my dear brothers. Brother Gabriel. With loving regards to Brother Patrick, Sisters M. Genevieve, Margaret and all our dear ones in the West. I remain

neutral: I hope you are well. I have recently read about the activities in your region and found them interesting. My niece, Mary, visited a few days ago and is well. She reported that all individuals in the west, including Maurice, also appear to be well. Ed Sampson sends his regards.
styled: I hope you are keeping contented. I've been reading of the missions up that way lately and it sure is interesting. Niece Mary was in a few days ago. is well as are seemingly all in the west - and Fr. Maurice. Ed. Sampson sends best regards.

neutral:
The message conveys goodwill to all. It describes the return of the Infant as a means to alleviate sorrow. The Infant's love, power, and gentleness are presented as an appeal to every individual, encouraging them to accept its spiritual significance. Its love, wisdom, and wonders are stated to confirm its identity as the Son of the Virgin, as foretold. The hope is for this figure to distance individuals from wrongdoing and its associated guilt, and to remain perpetually in their inner being.

Patrick is greeted with good wishes, and the sender expresses satisfaction regarding his busy schedule. A wish is conveyed for his continued frequent and daily participation in religious observances. A request for divine mercy is made for John and Thom. The sender found great comfort in their consistent adherence to this practice, noting that John had been a daily participant for 17 years. The message concludes with an expression of thanks.
styled: With love and with Christmas blessings to all Comes the Infan once more to free us from sorrow Whose love and Whose power and Whose gentleness call To each heart and Each soul for a manger tomorrow Whose love and Whose Wisdom, Whose wonders proclaim Him the Son of the Virgin as promised of your. O may He estrange us from sin with its shame And reigh in our hearts as His crib ever more! God bless you Brother Patrick Glad to hear your busy. I hope you keep up your frequent and daily communions. Lord have mercy on John and Thom. It was a great consolation to know that they had been practical in this - John for 17 yrs was daily communicant. Thanks be to God. Deo Gratias.

neutral: Communication has been received, after a prolonged period of silence from the sender. The sender has been in Detroit for medical treatment for the past three weeks, not due to illness but rather exhaustion. An operation was performed on a growth under the left eye. Medical professionals report that it is healing well. The sender had previously begun and nearly completed a letter to the recipient multiple times. However, this letter cannot be included in the current correspondence as it is located approximately 200 miles away, in St. Felix, Huntington. The letter was written just before Oune's death. Sympathy is extended to the recipient, their family, and all mutual acquaintances, while also acknowledging the congratulations offered to Oune's friends for his admirable character. The individual's long and difficult struggle has concluded. This marks another death within the family, a circumstance for which the parents had consistently hoped their children would experience a peaceful end.
styled: Glad to hear from you again, not withstanding the long silence on my part. I have been here in Detroit doctoring for the last three weeks not that I have been sick actually, I guess I was run down. I had an operation on a grout /growth/ under my left eye. The doctors say that is healing up nicely. I started to write to you a number of times, and I had just about finished it, but I cannot put in this letter, because it is about 200 miles from here, at St. Felix, in Huntington. I had written the letter just before Oune's death. May his soul rest in peace. I surely sympathize with you and yours, and all our dear one and friends, not withstanding the congraulations I offer all his friends for the admir able disposition. Thanks be to God for the grace granted to him and accompanied him in his long heroic struggle for life eternal. Another beautiful death in the family, for which father and mother prayed for faithfully per- severingly; that all their children would be granted the grace of a happy death.

neutral: It is unclear if dinner was eaten on the train, but a small lunch was consumed, consisting of a glass of milk that cost 25 cents. This prepared the person for a substantial supper and a night's rest upon arrival in St. Paul. Only upon arrival in St. Paul were the location, time, and other specifics of the funeral learned. Grandma Conley, Helen, and John, rather than taking the person directly with them, insisted the person return to the train, and they all continued to Minneapolis together. From Minneapolis, the person was instructed to take another train an hour or so later to Ortenville, 200 miles further. The next morning, the plan was to attend a service and then travel with a local leader, George Campbell, by car for the remaining 20 miles to Graceville. Despite wearing an overcoat, the train was not warm. After approximately six hours or more of attempting to sleep and observing the snow-covered landscape, the journey continued in cold conditions.
styled: I forget if I took dinner on the train but I did take a small lunch, a glass of milk, I believe .25 cents, and was in good shape for a worth- while supper - and a night's rest when we got to St. Paul. Then only, however, it was that I learned the particulars about the place, time etc. of the Funeral. Grandma Conley with Helen, and John, instead of whiffing me away, stressed that I get back on the train and they with me, went on to Minneapolis. There I should take another train an hour or so later, for Ortenville 200 miles further on; say Holy Mass next morning and thence, go with the Pastor, dear Father George Campbell, by auto the balance of the trip, 20 miles to Graceville. ... The train was not too warm even with an overcoat, so after about six hours or more of trying to sleep, watching the snow-touched landscape, etc, under a

neutral: He had been associated with the group for almost ten years when a severe carbuncle incapacitated him. Two companions brought me to Fort Wayne to board the Golden Arrow Train on the Pennsylvania Railroad. If on schedule, it would arrive in Chicago in time to connect with the widely advertised Hiawatha train on the Milwaukee Road. However, it had snowed that morning, which indicated a probable delay in train service. Indeed, as we departed Fort Wayne, the conductor informed us that the train was 25 minutes late. This meant that if no further time was lost during the 150 miles to Chicago, we would still make the Hiawatha connection and arrive in St. Paul around 7 P.M. However, after departing Huntington, we had engaged in a customary practice for a favorable trip and safe return, and as a result, I stopped worrying that day. The Milwaukee Road management agreed to wait until my ticket was obtained, though they advised against seeking a "clerical permit." Mildred and Jean Conley, along with the O'Donnells, were present; they had been attempting to obtain the clerical permit in my absence, but without success.
styled: had been with us almost ten years before that fearful carbuncle knocked him so completely out. Father Guardian and Brother Cook brought me to Fort Wayne to catch the Golden Arrow Train on the Pennsylvania, which if on schedule would reach Chicago in time to catch the widely advertised Hiawatha on the "Milwaukee". Ithad snown that morning however, and that meant a probable delay in the train service. Sure enough, the Conductor on taking our ticket as we left Fort Wayne lamented their being 25 minuete late, which meant that if they didn't lose any more time in 150 miles to Chicago, we'd make the said Hiawatha and thus reach St. Paul about 7 P.M. On leaving Huntington, however, we had said the Rosary for a favorable trip and safe return and, thanks be to God, I just forgot a- bout worrying that day. The Milwaukee management kindly consented to wait till they got my ticket, though they advised against bothering a- bout a "clergical permit". Mildred and Jean Conley were there and the O'Donnells: - had been trying in my absence to procure said clerical permit, but without success.

neutral: I hope you and your family are well during this challenging period. Thank you for your letters dated March 12th, one from a few weeks ago, and the one you sent before Christmas. I apologize for the delay in responding to these communications; I had intended to reply on several occasions. I have been meaning to write to you since the death of Father Maurice Joachim. As you are aware, he passed away on January 12th, 1949, which was the fifth anniversary of the death of my eldest brother, James. Coincidentally, his burial took place on the fifty-second anniversary of my own religious profession. At the time, I did not fully recognize the significance of these connections. One event occurred five years after the other, and the other occurred fifty-two years after my own profession. Upon further reflection, I find these connections more significant.
styled: God bless you these unsettled days; you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of March 12th as also that of a few weeks back, as well as the letter you sent me before Christmas. I am really ashamed of my- self not to have answered or acknowledged any of these before. I did start to do so a number of times. In fact its been on my mind to write you ever since the beautiful death of poor, dear Father Maurice Joachim; who as you know passed from time into eternity on the fifth anniversary of our dear eldest Brother James, January 12th, a year ago, ( 1949) and by happy coincidence we buried him on the fifty second anniversary of my own receiving of the holy Habit. Glory be to God! I hardly thought of it at the time or realized the beauty or the delicacy of the connection in each case, especially my own - the one five years apart, the other, ten times five plus. The more I think it over the better I appreciate it. Deo Gratias.

neutral: Hoping for a quick recovery. This message is from a permanent member, dated February 11th, 1947. Best wishes to Pat. Dedicate all efforts, acknowledging a significant sacrifice made for the benefit of all. May the intended course of events unfold. Requesting forgiveness for errors. Seek protection from severe consequences. Expressing compassion for those in a transitional state after death, particularly those most neglected. Do not be concerned, Pat. Instead, cultivate trust in a benevolent force by expressing gratitude for every positive outcome, even in advance. Please offer supportive thoughts for me.
styled: for speedy recovery, God willing - -perpetual member Feast of the Apparaition of our Bl. Imaculate Mary. - Febr. 11th - 1947 God bless you Br. Pat. Offer all to Jesus - Who has suffered so much for us all - for you and me. My Jesus - Thy will be done. Forgive us our sins. Deliver us from the flames of Hell. Have mercy on the souls in Purgatory - Especially the most abandoned. Don't worry Pat. Rather foster confidence in God's mercy by thanking Him for every thin - even ahead of time - Please pray for me -

neutral: I hope you are recovering, following the recent report from Mildred in Chicago. I have been sending you and your family my best wishes. I regret not writing more often. However, when I am confident that my loved ones are strong and persevering, and at the same time I know many others are struggling under their load of challenges, often with little guidance, I feel compelled to encourage and help them. Many people's sense of purpose and conviction seems to be dulled by materialism and a forgetfulness of their fundamental role as thinking beings: to live gratefully and acknowledge their ultimate source of well-being. Several months ago, I wrote to Chris Adam, a male friend from our early boyhood with whom we played and associated, along with his younger sisters, Lottie and Eattie. They were left as orphans at a vulnerable time in their lives, just as they were entering youth, and had received little guidance.
styled: I hope this finds you improving on the report received recently from Mildred in Chicago. I offered my holy Mass for you today and have been including you and yours in all my prayers and holy Masses. I am really ashamed of myself that I write so very seldom. Still, when I am confident that my dear ones are in the grace of God -- keeping up the "good fight" and at the same time when I know so many languishing under their icad of temptations -- so often with little or no faith I just feel I must do something to encourage and, like- rescue them. There are so many whose faith seems to be chilled and benumbed by materialism and forgetfullness of our primary purpose as rational creatures, viz; grate- fully to recognize our greatest Benefactor - our God and Saviour. -- I wrote a boyfriend of ours several months ago - Chris Adam - with whom we played and associated in our early boyhood, together with his little sisters, Lottie and Eattie; - poor youngsters! poorly instructed and left orphans at one of the most dangerous periods in life, just blooming into youth.

neutral:
Devotional badges were sent to an individual. The recipient, also in their eighties, responded with some appreciation but appeared focused primarily on material matters. The letter mentioned family details, such as one person named Lottie who never married, and another named Hattie who married and had three adult children; it also discussed the recipient's own family and grandchildren. This letter cannot be located at present.

Efforts are being made to encourage others to appreciate what the author considers the ultimate science: religion, defined as a joyful reliance on a higher power and on other people. The author expresses a belief that if everyone were to accept and live by this definition, the world would become an ideal preparatory stage for a spiritual afterlife.

Clergyman E'd visited for a full week in May. A letter was received from him, originating from White Plains, New York, indicating he appears to be in good health most of the time.
styled: I sent him badges of the Sacred Heart. He, too in his 8Os wrote back appreci- atively, in a way but seemed content with hardly any reference other than to material existence. "Lottie never married ... Hattie did ... and has three grown-up children ... " He wrote also of his own family and grand- children. Sorry I can't put my hand on his letter now. I am trying to get time to, kinda wake them up to renewed appreciation of the only science that in the end amounts to more that the snap of one's finger, Religion; The Science of our happy dependence on Almighty God and our neighbor. What a real vestibule to Heaven this world would be if everyone would just be convinced and try to live according to that simple definition! Fr. E'd was here with us a whole week in May. A letter from him in White Plains Y. He seems to keep well most of the time. Deo Gr.

neutral: A significant amount of time has passed since I last wrote, and the delay is difficult to explain. While I have been occupied, this should not have prevented me from acknowledging your Christmas cards, and particularly from expressing condolences to you and other family members regarding the tragic loss on January 25th. I intended to write a comprehensive letter, but being unsure of your address, I prioritized other obligations. Nevertheless, I have thought of you and wished you well, and intend to continue doing so. If your father could return now, he would convey what it meant for him in his final moments. He now understands, more profoundly than we can, the peace he achieved through his convictions.
styled: you. It must seem to you a long time now that I have failed to write I hardly know how to explain this neglect. True I have been busy; but that should not have held me from acknowledging your cards about Christmas and especially from expressing sympathy with you and our other dear ones so tragically bereaved - January 25th. I wanted to write you a real letter and not sure of your address, I left other duties demand first attention. I have prayed for you, however, and mean to continue to do so. You surely realize by this time something of the necessity we all stand in of praying and of having prayers .... O! could your dear Father but come back now and tell you what it meant for him in the end. Now he realizes better than we possibly can how fortunate he was to have hearkened to the plea Jesus made to His people in Palestine and now to us: "Come to me all ye that labor and are heavily burdened and I will refresh you" .....

neutral: The recipient likely has details about the death from Edward. New information about someone cared for is always appreciated. Since the author and the deceased were the only family members present, the author is providing these additional details. More details could be provided about this significant event. However, the author is a slow writer, only learning to type, and has many other obligations. To begin, a telegram was received from Edward Wednesday morning, less than an hour after M.J.'s death, stating: "Maurice Joachim died that morning at 6:20 AM." Expecting further details and presuming the funeral would be on Saturday, possibly in St. Paul or Prescott, Wisconsin, the author waited until the next morning. However, when the Provincial was contacted by phone at noon that same day in New York, the author was immediately instructed to attend the funeral. The recipient remembers M.J., of course.
styled: I know you have quite some details of that death - that happy transi- tion I hope - from Father Edward - Rt. Rev. Monsignor rather. But new details of anyone we've loved are always welcome and, since he and myself, of all the family and Clan were the only ones present, I feel I owe at least some such particulars. I probably ought to go into quite some more features of so interesting an event but I am a slow writer - only learn- ing to type - and there are so many other things I ought to be doing. Well to start with; we received a wire from Father Edward Wednesday morning, inside of an hour after M.J. 's passing: "Father Maurice Joachim died the morning at 6:20," Expecting further details and presuming that the funeral would be on Saturday and possibly in St. Paul or Prescott, Wis., I waited till next morning, although when I reached the very Rev. Father Provincial "long distance" at noon same day, in N.Y. he told me without hesitation to go to the Funeral. Of course, you remember Father M.J.

neutral: Youthful freshness fades, and ideals change over time. John Joseph M., at age 13, left school due to embarrassment about being in class with younger children. He joined the British navy and traveled to the Far East. Later, a business venture in London failed. He then joined the Hudson's Bay Company, became part of an Indigenous tribe, and was known as "Chief Black Eagle of the North." He was very charitable to the Indigenous people, whom he had grown to love. In a remote wilderness area, he discovered a small clearing where, nestled in the fork of a large tree, he found a weathered statue of the Virgin Mary. Soon after, he gathered his tribe members, resigned from his position, sold his extensive properties, and traveled to Rome, where he remained for five years.
styled: How like autumn flowers, bleaches the freshness of youth; and ideals change like raiments of the soul! May God bless you and give you holy resignation and, of course the crown ineffable that must follow, if perfect. Even in this side of the grave astonishments come as for such Christian virtue. A certain over-grown John Joseph M., a contemporary of your great-grand-father, a namesake and probably a relative, skipped school at 13 because ashamed to go to class with little boys; joined the British navy, went to the far East; later failed in an enterprise in London, joined the Hudson-Bay Co., joined an Indian tribe and became the famous "Chief Black Eagle of the North." Very charitable to the poor Indians whom, from the beginning he had learned to love, he was called to something greater. Deep in the wilderness he came across a sort of little clear- ing and there in the crutch of a big tree met a weather-beaten sta- tue of our Immaculate Mother. . .. . Calling his braves together shortly thereafter he resigned, disposed of his vast. estates, went to Rome and five Yrs.

neutral:
About forty years ago, while on vacation, he made an effort to attend a daily religious service when possible. He often worked until ten minutes before the service started, then ran across the field, covering the mile distance from their home to the place of worship, to arrive on time. They usually went together and sometimes raced.

At that time, daily reception of the sacrament was not recommended to them, unlike in more recent years. The speaker now considers this lack of recommendation regrettable. The speaker believes they missed significant benefits that would have strengthened them against the challenges and temptations of youth, which appeared to overwhelm many of their peers then, and perhaps even more so now.

The speaker expresses a wish for occasional insight into ultimate reality during life, suggesting that such a perspective, similar to what is believed to occur after death, would profoundly alter one's understanding.

The speaker states they have not been concerned about 'John and Tom,' believing, in agreement with a person named Maurice, that their well-being is assured.
styled: On vacation, nearly forty years ago he was careful to get to daily Mass if possible He would work often till ten minutes before Mass began and then run a- cross the field and try to make the mile we lived from Church in time not to be too late. We usually went together and sometimes raced. Daily Communion in those days was never recommended to us as it has been these recent years. How I often regret that it was not. I feel now that we missed so much that would have so strengthened us against the dangers and temptations of youth - the dangers and temptations that even these seemed to engulf so many contemporaries and now per- naps more than ever before. O! if we could but peep into eternity occasionally during our earthly existance, as the soul does when it separates from the body, how different would be our "Appreciation. . " ... I have not worried about our "John and Tom." I feel with Fr. Maurice that they were and are safe .....

neutral: The New Year has just begun. Good wishes are extended for many positive experiences before it, like all previous years, concludes. The sender hopes to write more frequently to loved ones if they can catch up on correspondence. It is pleasing that the recipient has found a partner, and that the relationship appears to be mutually compatible and promising. His age relative to the recipient's is considered a minor point. His limited knowledge of the specific faith could also be considered secondary, provided he or anyone else is willing to learn and resolve any doubts. It is believed that the Church can easily demonstrate the validity of all its teachings. Father John was deeply convinced of this. Although his death was tragic, it was nevertheless regarded as a holy death, a matter about which the sender had no concerns. P.S. Preparations are being made for... The recipient is encouraged to increase the frequency of their participation in communion.
styled: The New Year is still in its baby-hood: so I'll wish you all kinds of blessings before it passes as all others so far have gone. If ever I get up with my letters again I'll write to my dear ones more frequently. I hope. .I am glad you have found someone and that someone has found you wherecy mutual congeniality seems promising. .That he is older than you is a secondary matter. Even that he actually knows little about the True Religion might be secondary too, if only he or anyone else be desirous to learn - be willing to find out - and dispel doubts .. .It is so easy for the Church to vindicate her every Doctrine! !!.. . How your dear Father John was convinced of this! So much so that tho his death was tragic, it was never the less a holy death. I never worried about that. P.S. Preparing for ... Speed up your communions.

neutral: He later became a priest. After several years of service in London, he returned to Ireland and became widely known as John of Cork, a priest. It is a common belief that everyone experiences some form of hardship, and that greater challenges lead to greater rewards.
styled: later was ordained a priest; returned to Ireland and after several years mission in London became the famous Father John of Cork .... Who does not get a taste of the Cross one way or other and, if only with resignation: "The bigger the cross the greater the crown." . .

neutral: His regular spiritual practice was believed to have gradually and imperceptibly changed his perspective, especially regarding death. During a visit to Yonkers, N.Y., approximately a year before his second marriage, he appeared comfortable among the Capuchins. During a conversation, he stated, "I find no attraction in women any more; but I feel I ought to have someone to be with my little Helena." He eventually found a companion. This individual proved beneficial, initially for him, and subsequently even more so for his daughter Helena, along with two other individuals who joined the family for mutual love and companionship.
styled: i think it must have been his daily Communion that by degrees and imperceptibly made him "see things so differently, espec- ially death." When he visited me in Yonkers, N.Y. about a year before he married again and seemed so at home with the Capuchins, he re- marked one day as we talked things over " .... I find no attrac- tion in women any more; but I feel I ought to have someone to be with my little Helena." Well, Jesus sent him that someone, though at the time you probably failed to recognize her as such a "God-send" - for your dear Father at first and immediately, and now more than ever for his Helena, with two others for mutual love and companionship. How beautiful and wonderful are God's ways. And O, how far he surpasses us in generosity! Thanks be to God! ! ! Praised Be Jesus

neutral: A case documented on February 15, 1946, details Catherine Mahon of Woodside, L.I. She was admitted on August 25, 1945, after an operation for a brain tumor resulted in the loss of nearly half of her brain. Her doctors had considered her recovery impossible. Two days later, a specific action was taken on her behalf, and from that day, her condition began to improve. For several weeks, she experienced memory loss, including an inability to recognize faces or individuals. Her brain function now appears to have been restored. She plans to visit the institution as soon as weather conditions allow.
styled: = I hardly know what to do to keep the letters here from piling up. Otherwise I'd give you a number of the cases that we've had here at St. Michael's lately. I feel I must give you the second last note of the very few I have time and call to record. Feb. 15, 1946. " ... Catherine Mahon of Woodside, L. I. enrolled August 25th, 1945 having lost nearly half of her brain by operation on "brain-tumor" - doctors absolutely hopeless of her recovery. Two days later an enrollment was sent for the Poor Souls. From that day she be- gan to come back to herself. For several weeks was unable to remember - even faces - consequently could not recognize anyone. .. Now, thanks be to God, the brains seem to have grown back in place. She is figur- ing on coming to St. Michael's as soon as the weather permits. Again Deo Gratias. But why worry? "To worry about anything" St. Therese, the Little Flower claims, "is to indicate a want of confidence in God." She very likely speaks of excessive worrying; and yet, why should we worry a- bout anything - tumors? Cancers? Death?

neutral:
The passage describes the recurring arrival of a child, presented as a means to alleviate sorrow. The child's attributes, including love, grace, and gentleness, are depicted as an appeal to everyone to accept the child's presence, symbolized by a humble beginning. The child's birth, power, and remarkable deeds are stated as evidence that the child is the son of a virgin, as foretold in ancient prophecies. The author expresses a wish that the child's influence would separate individuals from wrongdoing and its associated negative feelings, and that the child's presence would be permanently established within people's inner selves. The author also conveys a personal belief that a higher power enabled them to understand the child, and that loving and serving the child represents a valuable and consistent life purpose. For those who are thankful, this experience is believed to initiate a state of profound well-being on Earth, which is considered to be of ultimate value.

Additionally, the author expresses a desire to hear from Casey M. and conveys a message that Casey M. is now mature enough to consider the personal responsibility and benefit of securing his own ultimate well-being.
styled: With love and with Christmas blessings to all Comes the INFANT once more to free us from sorrow. Whose love and Whose grace and Whose gentleness call To each heart and each soul for a manger tomorrow. Whose Birth and Whose power and Whose wonders proclaim Him, the Son of the VIRGIN as promised of yore. O ! May He estrange us from sin with its shame! -- And reign in our hearts as His crib evermore. God made me to know Him. O! What a blessd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's HEAVEN BEGUN for the GRATEFUL on earth To treasure aright ! ? ! HIGHEST HEAVEN its worth. P.S. Would be glad to hear from little Casey M. Tell him I said he is old enough now to think the responsibility and the privilege of working at his own Eternal salvation.

neutral: It is suggested to focus on a supreme being whose profound concern for individual well-being, encompassing both material and non-material aspects, is considered superior to all other forms of care. The recommendation is to cultivate trust in this entity's overarching plan by humbly communicating with it, acknowledging a relationship of dependence, and expressing gratitude. This gratitude should extend not only to past and present benefits but also proactively to any future hardships that this entity foresees as purposeful, both generally and in specific instances. This approach entails surrendering all aspects of life, including the timing and circumstances of one's death, to this entity's ultimate control. Adopting this practice is proposed to result in a significant increase in inner peace and contentment. It is further posited that this humble trust in the supreme being is exceptionally effective against adversarial influences.
styled: Why not rather turn to God, Whose solicitude for our individual welfare - temporarily as well as spiritually - puts all created solicitude out of the picture. Why not foster confidence in His divine Providence by humbly and in all child- like humility venture to remind Him - remind Him in the Person of our divine Brother Jesus - that we are His children - that we are, and at least want to be reckoned as amongst Eis "little ones"; and therefore, thank Him frequently for, not only the blessings of the past and pre- sent, but thank Him ahead of time for whatever He foresees is pleasing to Him that we suffer, and this not only in general but in each parti- cular case - leaving everything absolutely in His divine disposal, in- cluding with all its circumstances, when, where, and how He may be pleased to dispose the event of our death. Try something like this and see if it don't bring you a big in- crease of peace and contentmet. In my opimoon there is hardly any- thing else that the enemy of our souls dreads more than confidence - humble confidence in God.

neutral: A central point is that a higher power uses human abilities, provided human actions do not interfere with its intentions. This is because this power consistently plans positive outcomes for those who are patient and humble. This idea is supported by the principle that one must change their perspective and adopt qualities similar to those of young children. The sender had intended for this message to arrive before Sunday but anticipates it will now be too late.
styled: I wish to stress the verse I have underlined: "God condescends to use our powers, if we don't spoil His plans by ours." Because He is always planing wonders for the patient and the humble. Hence His own blessed words: " .. Unless ye be converted and become as little children ... " Now I'll have to say Good Night. I had hoped to reach you with this before Sunday but I rather fear I am too late for that now.

neutral:
From notes compiled over several years in Detroit, concerning cases associated with a specific organization, the following is one example out of more than a thousand. Many of these cases involved not only severe tumors but also aggressive and life-threatening cancer.

On May 25th, 1945, the notes record the case of Mrs. Catherine Nagle, a 45-year-old mother of eight children. Two weeks prior (May 9th), she underwent surgery at Providence Hospital. During the operation, doctors discovered her condition was so advanced with cancer that they closed the incision, concluding she would 'never to leave the hospital alive.'

She had been registered with the aforementioned organization multiple times. On this day, her husband made a special dedication for ten deceased individuals. The entire family was engaged in intense daily spiritual practices.

Mrs. Nagle returned home that day, unable to consume any nourishment. By May 29th, the notes reported a significant improvement in her condition: the severe abdominal pains and swelling had subsided, and she had a good appetite and was eating well. Her husband again made a dedication for deceased individuals as an expression of gratitude.

On September 14th, Mrs. Nagle was reported to be in Brooklyn, N.Y., in perfect health.
styled: Now I am going to give you briefly something from my "NOTES ON CASES THROUGH THE SERAPHIC MASS ASSOCIATION", that for several years I was making while in Detroit: Just one case in perhaps more than a thousand, -- a number of them not only fearful tumors but of most posi- tive and threatening cancer. May 25th, 1945. "Mrs. Catherine Nagle - 45 - mother of eight children, opened up for operation two weeks ago (May 9th) in Provi- dence Hospital. Found to be so hopelessly full of cancer that the Drs, simply closed her up again as ' ... never to leave the hospital alive.' "Has been enrolled in Ser. Mass Association several times. Today her husband enrolls the Poor Souls specially (10); - whole family storming Heaven by daily Communion .... " Mother comes home To-day; unable to take any nourishment ... May 29th. "Mrs Nagle as above May 25th. Thanks be to God: fear- ful pains and swelling gone from abdomen, has good appetite and eating fine. Husband enrolls Poor Souls again in thanksgiving." Sept. 14th, Brooklyn, N. Y. "Mrs. Nagle as noted above May 25 and 29th, here Today in perfect health.

neutral: Your letter of January 10th has been on my desk, and I have been hoping to find time to send a thorough response. I was hoping for a more positive outlook and better news than what your letter indicated. Yesterday, however, I received a letter from Martha reporting that everyone in Seattle and down the Coast is well, with the exception of one or two individuals, including Helena's husband, Ed Wilhite. Reports indicate that Ed Wilhite has been experiencing an ailment similar to what Maurice Joachim endured twenty years ago, when his condition appeared critical. Despite that, Maurice Joachim's stomach is now remarkably healthy. I received a positive letter from Ed Wilhite last week. Both Ed Wilhite and Edward are well.
styled: God bless you both and all you are interested in. I've had your letter of January 10th here before me on the desk ever since; hoping to get chance and time to send you a worth-while answer. Of course I've been hoping for brighter outlook and better word than what that letter would seem to intimate. Yesterday, however, I received an in- teresting letter from Martha to the effect that all are well in Seat- tle and down the Coast, with one or two exceptions and Helena's Hus- band, E'd Wilhite. From all reports he, your same Edward, has been suffering something similarly to what Father Maurice Joachim went through twenty years ago, when it seemed he was about done for. Yet think how remarkable is his stomach Today. Thanks be to God. I re- ceived a good letter from him last week. Both he and Father Edw'd are well. Thanks be to God and our Bl. Mother Mary.

neutral:
In situations where all conventional human and scientific assistance is exhausted, it is often considered practical to appeal to a higher source of well-being, which is perceived as responsive to earnest requests. With full confidence, one can propose an outcome believed to be aligned with this broader purpose, whether it involves protection from harm or the granting of a desired benefit.

Furthermore, the endeavor of raising children for the benefit of society and in accordance with universal good is seen as a profoundly positive undertaking. This holds true whether children are brought into a family through biological means or adoption, a distinction that appears to be equally valued. Consequently, the love experienced by dedicated and committed parents is imbued with a uniquely beautiful quality. This observation highlights the profound and unfathomable nature of universal wisdom and knowledge, and the often inscrutable processes by which events unfold.

A related document, a copy of a letter, is provided for further context.
styled: I find it always practical, especially in cases where all human scientifice help is despaired of, to just turn to the divine author of all good - always solicitous to be asked for favors - and with all the confidence we can muster, propose something that we are as- sured is pleasing to Him if we be only spared --? , or be granted the booned favor. But, to even try to raise children for God and society is so manifestly pleasing to God - and this, whether they be procured by natural generation or by adoption ( seemingly quite a matter of indifference to Him), that He has given a specially beautiful color- ing to the love of those whose privilege it is to have become earn- est faithful parents. So that quite appropriately the song of the Psalmist may be here also applied: " ... O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are His judgements and how unsearchable His ways!" (Rom. XI) I am herewith enclosing a letter of Fr. Edward's - rather a copy of Msgrs' that will speak for itself.

neutral:
Many exemplary figures demonstrate the virtue of confidence. A particularly clear illustration can be found in the account of Joseph and Mary, who were seeking a place for Mary to give birth to Jesus. This situation exemplified confidence, which, according to Mary of Agreda, Mary possessed from the beginning of her life. A significant outcome followed this event, marking a pivotal moment.

However, another point to consider is the adoption of children. It is a widely held belief that caring for the most vulnerable is highly significant. This suggestion is made with the condition that Eld recovers from illness.
styled: The lives of the saints abound with exam- ples of this virtue. Perhaps no where more beautifully than in the example of S: . Joseph with Mary, God's living Tabernacle seeking an abode wherin .. to give us Salvation. What an example of confidence it must have been to their thousand guardian angels - as Venerable Mary of Agreda was instructed to inform us, Mary had from the day of her Immaculate Conception. What an edification! And again what a surpassing reward that followed! What a HOLY NIGHT for them indeed! - a HOLY NIGHT, the positive dawn of humanity rescued. There has been something else in my mind, however, that I wanted to bring to your consideration. How about proposing to adopt one or more little ones - of whom Jesus assures us: "What you have done for the least of my breathren, you have done to me", if Eld give the doc- tors a surprise and get well?

neutral: The concept of a comforting reunion with deceased loved ones, marked by a joyful welcome, is described. A recent, moving family reunion in Seattle is recalled, which is then contrasted with the anticipated ultimate reunion of individuals in an afterlife. Therefore, it is suggested that one should be acknowledged for having another friend who offers support and is anticipated to be awaiting a future reunion, similar to the hope held for Ed.
styled: What a won- derful doctrine and consoling to think of our dear ones awaiting us with not only lited candles but greeting us at our arrival with music and hymns of heavenly sweetness. . .I've been thinking often of the really touch- family - reunion last summer in Seattle. But what about the great reunion awaiting the arrival of the just in Heaven! .. .I am inclined rather to congratulate you therefore, on another friend praying for you and awaiting your arrival as we hope Ed is ..

neutral: I hope you are in good health and spirits, and that your circumstances are improving. It is pleasing to know that John and Marian, along with their family, are doing better and experiencing fewer difficulties. I had intended to write to John and Marian last winter, but I was mostly bedridden for a couple of months. This significantly reduced my energy, and for several weeks I was able to do very little. I also attempted to write to Dorothy and Charles D'Amico, and to you, on several occasions, but time seemed to pass quickly. We are sending an enrollment card for the deceased Thomas Patrick La Plante to his parents, as directed. Regarding your primary concern, it is not surprising that as time passes and the pain of social losses diminishes, the principles governing both daily life and personal convictions tend to be re-evaluated.
styled: God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you continuing in good health and hopes and that things are brightening their smiles in your direction .. I am surely pleased to know of John and Marian doing better and sailing along more smoothly with their nice little family. Thanks be to God for the grace to do so. I started to write them away last winter - both of them - but was mostly in bed for a couple of months and that took quite a little pep out of me, so that for several long weeks I was able to do very little. I started to write Dorothy and Charles D'Amico too a number of times as well as yourself but I just do not know where the time flies to. We are sending an enrollment card for deceased Thomas Patrick La Plante to his poor, bereaved parents as directed. Now as to that primary problem of your own. I am not at all surprised that as time slips by and wounds of social bereavements heal, God's laws in common life as well as in the supernatural should seek to adjust their claims.

neutral: The speaker expresses a strong desire for all involved to increasingly recognize the significant benefits that diligent management of resources and affairs can offer. This management is considered beneficial for those who aim to deeply internalize the conviction that only those committed to justice can achieve a state of ultimate good, and that genuine moral uprightness requires a commitment to peace. Disregarding the demands of justice, under any pretext, consistently indicates superficial thinking; more precisely, it signifies a fundamental lack of genuine reasoning. Moreover, the speaker contends that the most defining characteristic of atheism is a disregard for justice and truth.
styled: I will pray that the good God guide things - that He dispose everyone concerned, more and more to consider the great profit conscientious administration of tem- poralities can be to souls that try to become imbued with the pos- itive conviction that only lovers of justice can posess the King- dom of Heaven and to be children of God we must be lovers of Peace. Disregard for the claims of justice - under whatever pretext - has always been a manifestation of - to say the very least, of shallow thinking. Rather I would say its a betrayal of a want of' real thinking. In fact it seems to me that the all-outstanding character istic) of atheism is nothing other than just disregard for justice and truth.

neutral:
Thank you for the message informing me of Edwin's death. The sender hopes that Edwin has transitioned from earthly struggles to a state of peace and fulfillment, free from anxiety and striving, where all ideals are realized. If not fully and immediately, the sender hopes he will soon achieve a state of ultimate peace and reward and receive a welcoming greeting, as believed to await those considered worthy.

You are now not only an orphan but also a widow. What does this signify? For those with strong belief and hope, it should mean a further detachment from worldly ties. It should also mean that you now have another beloved person, your husband, who the sender believes is interceding for you from beyond life, along with your departed Mother and Father and many others who loved you and have passed on.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your regards in send- ing me the telegram of your dear Edwin's passing - from time to eter- nity, from transitory struggling common to mortals, to the destiny, we trust where anxiety and struggling for existence gives place to confidence and union with every ideal ever dreamed of. If not this directly and fully, at least, please God, shortly to gain the crown and to hear the long hoped for greeting always awaiting the just and humble: "Come ye Blessed blessed of my Father possess to joys pre- pared for you ... " Now you are not only a orphan but a widow also. What does that mean? For you and for any one who have real faith and Christian hope it ought to mean "Another string broken that tends to bind our hearts to earth." It ought to mean that you you have now another faithful dear one as we confidently hope, a loving husband to pray for you beyond the grave together with your saintly Mother and Father and so many who have loved you and gone ahead.

neutral: A remedy has been provided to fully restore the motherly, fatherly, and spousal love that was temporarily absent from one's social and family life. Continued pursuit of guidance for oneself and associates is recommended, as this will lead to the best possible outcome. Between the two viewpoints in Seattle and Los Angeles, the former is favored. This is especially true if the judge's daughters are old enough to manage their own affairs and their father's household. Such cases frequently present a risk of jealousy, and the unpredictable nature of social interactions often leads to challenging situations. Regarding the financial or business matters mentioned, involvement is not desired.
styled: I have no doubt but that our dear Lord and His blessed Virgin Mother has provided a remedy where-by to fully supply what He permitted for a time to be with- drawn from your social and family existence, - a sweet mother- love, a dear father-love, a devoted husband-love. Only just keep on praying for God's merciful guidance - for self and associates - and in His divine wisdom God will not fail you in His guidance for the best. Between the two outlooks in Seattle and Los Angeles, I am in- clined to favor that in the former. This especially if the judge's daughters (are) old enough to take care of themselves and their father's house. In such cases there is nearly always the danger of jealousy. I hardly need tell you of examples in this phase of social wanderings: for as Moore rightly muses: "Poor wanderers of a stormy day, from wave to wave we're driven; And fancy's flash and reason's ray serve but to light the troubled ways; There's nothing calm but Heaven." As for the financial or business affairs referred to, I just do not like to dabble into them.

neutral:
Atheism is characterized as a profoundly wrong concept, viewed as the ultimate intellectual and moral decline. It is further described as a futile conclusion and a desperate refuge for individuals considered intellectually weak, morally corrupt, or foolish. Moreover, its primary leader is identified as Lucifer, portrayed as the foremost diabolical deceiver and, by divine permission, the ruler of Hell.

A communication was recently received, attributed to the stigmatic Capuchin, Pater Pio, from San Giovanni Rotondo, Italy. It is presented as a divine revelation given to him. The author considered this message especially relevant due to the perceived alarming increase in atheism and a corresponding decline in religious faith, which was understood to signify a loss of divine hope and supernatural charity. The revelation begins by stating that a powerful, thunderous arrival will occur on the world, which is described as sinful, during a cold winter night. This event will be preceded by scorching winds and violent earthquakes.
styled: Atheism, to every normally thinking mind a most blasphemous suggestion of the devil; the "omega" - climax - of intellectual and moral depravity at once; the hopeless con- clusion and the desperate refuge of shallow thinking, of degener- ate minds and of really damned fools, - their primary leader none other than Lucifer himself the outstanding prince of diabolical deceivers and - by God's permission - dictator in-chief in the kingdom of Hell. Only just recently I received a communication as coming from our stigmatic Capuchin the famous Pater Pio, at San Giovani Rotondo, Italy. It is given as like a revelation to him from our dear Lord; and to my mind, in these days of so appalling advances of atheism as just about what is coming to this generation, so fearfully apos- tatizing from faith in God; which of course means from hope in the ... divine and from supernatural charity. Here is how it starts out: "With frightful roar of thunder I will come upon this sin-laden globe in a cold winter night. Scorching winds will precede this disturbance, and violent quakes will shake the earth.

neutral: Lightning from storm clouds will destroy by fire all that is associated with wrongdoing or corruption and deemed necessary to eliminate. Humanity will then realize that a supreme, powerful force governs events, nullifying its self-serving plans. A powerful, destructive force, carried out by an agent of elimination, will permanently eradicate all entities permeated by deceptive and misleading arguments that are fundamentally contrary to established truths. When a destructive agent begins its deadly task, acting as an instrument of retribution, and when malevolent forces intensely target the righteous, especially those designated for suffering, with terrifying assaults, steadfastness and trust will be essential. Protection will be provided, and a sign will be given to mark the commencement of these decisive events. The principle that human plans are ultimately subject to a higher power's control is an ancient observation repeatedly proven true.
styled: Flashes of lightening from fiery masses of clouds will set on fire and turn to ashes all that is in league with sin or is in- fected and corrupted by it, so that it must be destroyed. Then the human race shall realize that there is an all-powerful will over it, which will bring to naught its empty plans of gain glory. The wrath of God at the hands of destroying angel will per- manently cut down all the forces impregnated with deceitful and blasphemous sophisms which cannot nor never could be the teachings of My Gospel. ..... When the angel of death shall begin to carry out his lethal mission with the avenging sword of justice, and when hell shall cast itself in uproar and rage upon the just, especially on my victim souls, to destroy them with its frightening terrors, then it is that your faith and confidence in me must be firm as a rock. I will protect you; I will give you a sign which will indicate the beginning of My judgements. = "Man proposes; but God disposes" is an old proverb that has borne out truth of Scripture millions of times.

neutral:
The development of atomic weapons in the current era is interpreted as a development permitted by a higher power, enabling individuals without faith to create destructive forces. These forces are believed to be aimed at a generation perceived as immoral, defiant, and lacking belief.

A referenced text describes a future event: a powerful, earth-shaking phenomenon occurring on a cold winter night. Instructions are given to seal off homes and avoid looking outside, as the event is considered profound and devastating. It is presented as a purification event, attributed to a higher power, for a select group of followers, who are advised to seek protection and remain calm.

The author emphasizes the perceived futility of valuing material possessions for their own sake in the current era. Their importance is deemed to lie solely in their utility for promoting a higher objective and charitable acts benefiting humanity, noting the inherently temporary nature of their perceived value.

A letter is being forwarded to E'd.
styled: And just these days of Atomic invention, it would seem that God might be permit- ting men without faith to be preparing the fearfully poisoned lightening fires with which He will arm His angels of wrath on an adulterous, defiant, atheistic generation. Another few lines from above referred-to: "In a cold winter night I will let thunder resound over the earth so that the very mountains will quiver. Quickly close your doors and windows; veil all vision to the outside world. Let not your eyes profane the most terrible of all' happenings with curious glances; for thrice holy is the wrath of God which will purify the earth for you, my remaining faithful flock. Commit yourselves to the protection of My holy Mother; and be not dis- mayed .... " P.S. What I'd like to stressits the very insanity of trying to reckon on anything material these days as amounting to any- thing of importance aside from its use in promoting the glory of God and charity toward lifting humanity - and the necessarily very short time such material things hold their evaluation, etc. P.S. II Dear Helena I am sending your letter on to Fr. E'd .....

neutral: Prescot was likely little more than a village at that time. Based on its condition 15 years later, Eagle Rock, located four miles downriver, would have appeared to be an ideal secluded wilderness spot at that time. This location, overlooking the Mississippi River, was where five individuals were born and began their lives. Bernard was an infant when his father became blind from ague for two weeks, requiring assistance. During this time, Bernard, the namesake, sustained a rupture from which he never fully recovered.
styled: At that time Prescot must have been little more than a village; and judging what the Eagle Rock - four, miles down the river - must have been at that time from what it was 15 years later, when I stayed two weeks at Aunt Mary Ann's, cone might get an idea of what a perfect hermitage in the wilderness might be. Here it was smiling down on the "Father of Waters", that five of us were privileged to breath our first morning air and "sing our first baby music", No doubt little Bernard must have been proficient in that music; because it was during his term of baby-hood that Papa went blind with the ague - when for two weeks he had to be led by the hand, and his little namesake got a rupture from which he never com- pletely recovered. Like in all other trials, however, the Good God had His designs herein also, and we can say with fullest conviction and in all gratitude To-day: "The Lord knows best." May He be in all His plans eternally praised! ... .

neutral: An 8-year-old child asked, "What is religion?" Several people repeated the question. A serious answer followed: "Religion is not merely a science; it is considered the fundamental science. It is the understanding of human reliance on a higher power and on other individuals, emphasizing the fundamental interconnectedness of all people."
styled: "What is religion anyway?" asked a little 8 year-old. "What is Religion re Echoed in the ears of several. "Ah!" came an Earnest answer, "Religion is not only a science; Its the science of all science. It is the science of our happy dependence (we being each our own first neighbor) on God and our neighbor."

neutral: The author noted being only partially convinced of certain beliefs, a process ongoing since October 1870. This observation was made near a chapel dedicated to Saint Felix. A fundamental question posed was about the purpose of human existence, with the answer given as understanding the ultimate reality. This was considered a profound purpose, with cherishing and acting in accordance with this ultimate reality being integral to it. This purpose was seen as originating from a higher plane and offering immense value to those who appreciate it, of the highest possible significance. From a logical perspective, aligning oneself with this ultimate principle was considered the most rational course of action. The author believed that suppressing logical thought and appreciation could lead to a rejection of the concept of a higher power. Atheism was described as the ultimate manifestation of extreme intellectual irrationality, profound moral decline, and utter defiance of the divine. On a specific Saturday, known as Holy Saturday, a personal well-wishing was extended to Margaret and her family, expressing hope for their continued well-being. It appeared to be a time when the rejection of a higher power, perceived as a force of opposition to the divine, was gaining significant attention and acceptance. The author questioned whether destructive choices were still being favored over virtuous ones, referencing a historical example of such a preference.
styled: Still only half converted - at it since Oct. 1870. In front of St. Felix Chapel. Rational mortal: - 2nd Q. Why did God make you? God made me to know Him. O What a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. Its Heaven-begun for the grateful, on earth. - To treasure a'right! ? Highest Heaven its worth. There is nothing more rational in reason than to love God. By stifling reason and gratitude sin begets atheism. Atheism? The unqualified climax at once of intellectual insanity, of moral degeneracy, of diabolical blasphemy . Holy Saturday. God bless you Margaret - you and yours. I hope you keep well these days .... .Ah! days, as it would seem when atheism - the voice of Anti Christ - is demanding and get- ting a hearing. Barabas still prefered? . .

neutral: As time and distance separate one from childhood and youth, memories of those periods become more pleasant and inviting. However, there is also a belief that the future holds greater promise. They were fortunate to have sturdy, honest, and virtuous parents. The efforts and journeys of these pioneers, often immigrants, are notable. For instance, their own parents relocated from urban centers like Boston and Philadelphia to "The River Bank."
styled: The fact of it is, I believe, that as time and distance separate me from the scenes and associations of my childhood and youth my recollections of both become sweeter and more reinviting - ...! ... But ...! The future holds a better part, .. .. " Surely we were fortunate children that the Good God gave us such sturdy, honest, virtuous parents. How can we ever be grateful enough? Thanks be to God! May their dear souls rest in the peace of the blessed! I often think of the wonderful designs of Divine Providence as revealed in the plans and strivings of these and simi- lar "children of St. Patrick" - so often pioneers indeed. In the case of our own dear Parents, e.g .; how they were directed from city-life in Boston and Philadelphia away to "The River Bank".

neutral:
Life there was prosperous and simple. However, dangers were present, causing the parents frequent anxiety. Wild animals and rattlesnakes were the most common sources of this anxiety. Additionally, two young cousins drowned together in the river just below their dwelling.

The Trimbelle area was similarly isolated, undeveloped, and scenic. It was rich in a variety and abundance of wild flowers, fruits, nuts, and berries. To the west were patches of groves. To the east lay vast forests, extending into the lowlands and across the Willow River in the county known as Trimbelle. To the south, valleys and rolling prairies stretched five miles down to Diamond Bluff on the Mississippi River, providing good grazing land for cattle, deer, and other wild animals.
styled: How we must have thrived there in real unworldliness and Innocence1 Dangers of course were not wanting, to keep dear Father and Mother "on edge" and often, no doubt in anxiety. Wild beasts and rattlesnakes seem to been the most common cause of such anxiety, though two of our little cousins were drowned together just be- low our little retreat, in the River - otherwise so generous, so noble, so majestic. Trimbelle too !!! How removed! How primitive! How picturisque! How rich in its varity and abundence of wild flowers and fruits and nuts and berries! !! - with beautiful patches of grove to our west, illimitable forests off to the East (down on the "bottoms" and across the Willow River of that county. They call it the Trimbelle. To the South, were vallies and rolling prairies down to Diamond Bluff five miles below on the Mississippi - a fair pasture field for cattle as well as deer and other wild animals.

neutral: The dwelling had a single partition downstairs, separating the parents from their three daughters, Ellie, Maryann, and Mattie. An upstairs loft served as a sleeping area for boys, who sometimes played there in the mornings until they quarreled. The stairs were low; an average-height person could walk down them normally, but a tall individual, such as J.B. Fahey (six feet two inches), had to stoop to avoid hitting their head on the cross-joists. The sole entrance door was on the sunny side, and a single window on each side provided light. Winters were often severe, with snowdrifts occasionally reaching the gable roof. However, the father ensured the dwelling was well-insulated before cold weather, maintaining comfort even during strong winds and very low temperatures.
styled: You may smiles at this title I honor it with, especially when you learn that it had a single partition only be- low, "the bed-room" - Father and Mother on the one side and the little girls, Ellie and Maryann and little Mattie on the other - and the loft above where little boys slept and in the morning sometimes played till they quarreled as little boys are wont to do. An ordinary man could walk straight down stairs, but there was one young J.B. Fahey - six foot two - who was careful not to bump his head on the cross-joices and, therefore, had to stoop a little. The only door led in from the sunny end while a single window on each side let in the light. Winters were often severe and snow-banks sometimes mounted as high as the top of the gabel roof: but poor, dear Father took care be- fore the cold weather set in, to bank well wherever he might, so that we were fairly comortable no matter how the wind howled or the mercury sank.

neutral: The area was susceptible to prairie fires, which nearly every year would darken the sky as they crackled and moved through abundant wild grass, prairie-tea, hazel, and other brush. On such occasions, "Lamb's Road," which ran east and west on a ridge approximately 30 rods to the south, nearly always provided significant protection. If the wind was not too strong, neighbors would have time to assist, often by lining up along the road and preventing the fire from crossing. This was a private road connecting the Miller farm (located to the southwest) to a twenty-acre field (located to the southeast). The public road ran past a log cabin, a one-story structure measuring approximately 12 by 30 feet.
styled: But it was also a fair race- track for our most dreaded enemy the prairie-fire, that nearly every year would darken the sky in its crackling rush toward us through a- bundance of wild grass, prairie-tea, hazel and other brush. On such occasions "Lamb's Road", running east & west on ridge about 30 rods to our south nearly always proved a great protection. If the gale were not too strong our dear neighbors would have time to come to our rescue, as they often did by lineing up along that road and preventing the the fire from crossing. It was just a private road to a twenty- acre field off to our S.E. from the Miller farm on our S.W. The public road, such as it was, ran just past our little log cabin - a one-story mansion about 12 x 30 feet.

neutral: The wind was strong, and Mother appeared anxious, giving instructions and preparing for what seemed likely: a complete burn-out. Ellie dug a small trench in front of the house and sprinkled water in it approximately halfway to the barn. By this time, the fire was spreading through the grass and brush between the property and Lam's Road, and dense, dark clouds of smoke drifted overhead. Then the barn ignited, approximately ten rods east of the house. Everyone moved, carrying some bedding, to the solitary tree that had long stood in the middle of the original four-acre field. This event likely took place during the second summer of their residence in Trimbelle. This estimation is based on the acquisition of a new field, approximately six acres, and the presence of large oak trees to the north.
styled: The wind was pretty strong too and poor dear Mother seemed quite anxious - giv- ing instructions what to do and getting ready for what must have look- ed probable, a burn out. Ellie scratched a little "hoe-mark" out in front of the house and sprinkled holy water in it about half way down to the barn. By this time the fire was crackling through the grass and brush this side of Lam's Road and the smoke rolled over our heads in thick, dark clouds. Then the barn took fire, some ten rods east of the house, and we all went down, carying some bed-clothes, to the lone tree that for a long time stood in the middle of the original four-acre field. This, I think, must have been about the second summer we lived in Trimbelle. Because we had a new field, if I remember right, of about six acres and the great oaks over to the N.

neutral:
Wishing you and your family well, I hope you are in good health. Wishes are sent from several individuals and families, including Francis Molloy and family, who visited yesterday, along with the Doonans, Sampsons, and others in Detroit. Additionally, greetings come from our niece Mary Casey, Jim's daughter, and Maurice, now known as Joachim, a member of the Capuchin Franciscan order from Huntington, Indiana. His address is St. Felix Monastery, Route 8. He appears to be well and anticipates taking his vows in September.

I understand it may sometimes appear that I have forgotten about those I once considered like younger siblings. I acknowledge that I rarely write and am slow to respond to their letters, and I feel some guilt about this. Despite this, I remember you all almost daily. I have before me letters addressed to these individuals, started on January 24th, February 24th, and March 25th. The letter from February is almost complete, which serves as an indication that I do remember you at times.
styled: God bless you and all yours! I do hope you are keeping well. Best wishes from all in Detroit - Francis Molloy & family, who were here yesterday; Doonans, Sampsons, etc,; also from our niece Mary Casey, Jim's daughter and of course from Father Maurice - now Fr. Joachim, O. F.M. Cap., of Huntington, Indiana. His address St.Felix Monastery Route 8. Thanks be to God he seems well and hopeful of making profession in September. No doubt it must seem to you at times that I forget all about my one-time little sisters and brothers. I know I seldom write and am tardy in answering them when they write to me; at least I feel somewhat guilty that way. Be that as it may, I hardly think there is a day passes but what I remember you all. I have here before me letters started to the above S.M.T. Jan. 24th, Feb. 24 and March 25. That of Feb. nearly finished; yet ...? This ought to be a sort of indication that I at least sometimes do remember you.

neutral: A feature was joined by one or two others along its path to the "Big Ravine". This valley curved north and then east among picturesque hills before merging into the lowlands of the Trimbelle. These hills and lowlands served as significant pasture areas. In these pastures, boys, including Maurice and the narrator (until Maurice departed for Stillwater to study), watched cattle and studied their catechism. Occasionally, they rolled rocks down hillsides, picked berries, fished, or swam. These activities continued until the cattle strayed and caused trouble, leading to concern about locating them. Sometimes, they faced consequences for their carelessness.
styled: This was joined by one or two others from the side in its course down to the "Big Ravine", a beautiful valley, that curved northword and then eastword among some of the most picturisque hills that I have ever seen -- off to loose itself in the bottoms of the Trimbelle. These hills and low- lands formed a great part of our pasture-lands where we boys, especial- ly Maurice and I till he leaft for Stillwater to study, used to watch the cattle and study our catechism. Sometimes we'd roll rocks down the hill-sids - great amusement for boys! - or pick perries or fish and swim till the cattle would stray away and get into mischief and then we would have our own anxieties finding them. Sometimes we got our medicine for carelessness; more frequently, perhaps, we es

neutral: It might seem unusual to refer to the dwelling as a mansion. However, every proper mansion includes a chapel of some size. Their home sometimes served entirely as a chapel, and at other times resembled a church. During their residence in the dwelling, which was clean and orderly despite its humble exterior, they customarily held morning and evening prayers together. On Sundays at 10 a.m., the father would lead Mass prayers. When weather conditions allowed and the roads were passable, he would walk approximately six miles to church, utilizing distant shortcuts. In his absence, Ellie, James, or another family member would lead the prayers. On one such Sunday, while the father and Jime were at church, black clouds of smoke were observed rising from the far side of hills to the South.
styled: You'll be wondering soon, more than before if I keep on in this strain, how it might be called a mansion. Well, every decent mansion has a chapel of some demensions .... Ours was at times all chapel, and at times something of a church. As long as we lived in that little abode - a "hovel" possibly outside but clean and neat as a palice within - we were wont to say our morning and night prayers to- gether; and on Sundays at 10 a.m., Father woud read Mass Prayers. Of course when the weather permitted and the roads were anyway decent he would trudge away to church about six miles taking short cuts dis- tant. Then Ellie or James or one of the others would lead the prayers. Sometimes they seemed pretty long. It was on such a Sunday that Papa and Jime had gone to church when we saw the black clous of smoke ris- ing from the far side of some of the hills off to the South.

neutral: Prairie chickens, which had previously been present in the eastern areas, were gone.
