I recorded the names you sent me recently via Rae Garland and am pleased to learn you are maintaining your efforts. Last week, I attended my annual retreat at the monastery. It is located across the Hudson River from Lady Cliff Convent and West Point Military College, with West Point situated approximately one and a half miles further along. It is an ideal location for quiet reflection and study. Approximately 75 priests, clerics, and lay brothers were present.
styled: You've been on my mind frequently these days. I wanted to write you but getting aquainted in a new place keeps one on edge pretty much. I inscribed the names you sent me recently thru Rae Garland and I am surely pleased to know your able to keep up the good work. Thanks be to God. The above Monastery is where I made my annual retreat last week. It is across the Hudson from Lady Cliff convent and West Point Military College - the latter about a mile and a half up. Thank God it is quite an ideal place for quiet reflection and study. About 75 priests, Clerics and lay brothers, ...

neutral: Congratulations, Grandma, on enduring another difficult period. We are thankful for your resilience. Please keep the rest of us in your thoughts, that we may find acceptance and strength in challenging situations. Best wishes to Mrs. Plunkett, Grandma Plunkett, and all her helpers and friends.
styled: for God's Holy Guidance - Thanks be to God Grandma! You've wethered another storm ... Congratulations! Pray for all the rest of us, that we learn to love God's holy will. God bless you Mrs. Plunkett God bless Grandma Plunkett and all her helpers and friends.

neutral: The current era is characterized by both restlessness and foreboding in the materialistic world, yet it also presents aspects that are vibrant and promising. Approximately ten years ago, Rabbi Rosenwasser expressed concern to a respected elder within his community about the increasing prevalence of atheism. The elder silently wrote (with Rabbi Rosenwasser's finger on the corner of the tissue paper): "If any good is to come from atheism — in itself the climax of insanity — it's going to force believers-in-God together." Striking the desk, the Rabbi exclaimed, "That's Inspiration!" He continued by noting that it is difficult to assess the extent of suffering endured by the Church in recent decades, and even harder to predict the negative consequences that seem imminent for those who oppose truth, as well as the positive outcomes for those who persevere through suffering for justice and truth.
styled: I hope you are keeping well these days - at once so restless, so foreboding in in the materialistic world; yet by the grace and mercy of God, so colorful and so promising! It is just about ten years now that a certain Rabbi Rosenwasser lamented to one of our fathers ... the prevalence of atheism. The latter without a whis- per, wrote (the R's finger on the corner of the tissue-paper) "If any good is to come from atheism -- in itself the climax of insanity -- "Its going to force believers-in-God together.' 11 Hit- ting the desk, Rabbi exclaimed: "Thats Inspiration! It is hard to reckon the extent of modern martyrdom the Church has suffered these several decades and probably less possible to surmise what seems still-shortly to follow, the judg- ment awaiting enemies of Truth as the glory reserved for those who will have persevered ... suffering for justice, for Truth. .

neutral: I thank you for your practical way of remembering me on my 76th birthday. I hope you remain with us until you turn 100. After all, that can't be much more than twelve years. So continue to live until you are ready for a peaceful end. Best wishes to you and to all our friends in Detroit.
styled: I surely thank you for your practical way of remember- ing me on my 76th birthday. I hope the dear Lord may be pleased to leave yourself with us till you round out the 100. After all that cant be much more than a dozen years. So take courage and stay till your ripe enough for Heaven to take a "no stop-passage." . God's blessing and graces to yourself and to all our dear friends in Detroit.

neutral:
We gather today with great joy, beloved father and mother, and with deep emotion, we honor you on your fiftieth anniversary.

For fifty years, you have traveled life's path together with devotion, experiencing both sorrow and joy, remaining steadfast in your principles.

When we were young, after our daily chores were done, we would gather around you at the end of the day. You taught us to express love and gratitude.

You faced life's challenges with strength and courage, progressing through life as faithful and true companions. We hope that wherever we go, beloved parents, we can be as loyal and steadfast as you have been.

And may the valuable lessons of confidence, hope, and love that we learned from you, beloved parents, serve as guiding principles for us as we navigate life's difficulties.
styled: Written - To the notes of "Believe Me if All" - (By Mamie G. Casey Mccluskey in 1913) With festival gladness we gather today, Dear old Daddy and Mother Machree, And with hearts overflowing sing homage to you On your Golden Jubilee. For fifty long years life's pathway adown, In devotion together you've trod With a tear and a smile in your eyes all the while, True as any to the "Dear Ould Sod!" In the May-time of Life, with our daily tasks o'er, We'd unite at the close of the day, Round you, then you taught us to kneel by your side, In love and thanksgiving to pray. In the world's field of battle, with hearts strong and brave, You marched, comrades faithful and true, Oh! may we, dear parents, wherever we rove- Be as loyal and steadfast as you. And may the sweet lessons of Faith, Hope and Love, That we learned, parents dear, at your knee, Be as beacons to guide us to Heaven above, While we sail over life's stormy sea.

neutral: Thank you for your kind assistance, received several weeks ago and duly noted. I apologize for the delay in acknowledging it. I wish you well.
styled: - Many thanks for your charitable favor of several week past duely received and noted. Please pardon my so long delayed acknowledgement. Keep well and pray for the conversion of the rest of us -- poor sinners as we all are.

neutral: Thank you again for your cooperation with the charitable missions. Although my shins are stiff and slightly swollen, they are improving, and I hope to resume my regular schedule soon. I hope Esther's condition is not serious and that she returns soon in good health. I just received a letter from Maurice in Graceville, Minnesota. You may recall he spent six years at Mount Hope Sanatorium in Baltimore. He appears to be recovering well. He was appointed as chaplain there last March. Edward is still working in St. Paul, lecturing, conducting missions, and leading retreats, until his bishop recalls him to the Islands.
styled: Many thanks again for your cooperation in the privileged work of the poor missions. Thanks be to God, though my shins are stiff and a little swollen, they are improving and I hope in a short time to get at my regular schedule. I hope nothing serious be found with Esther and that she be back soon in good shape. I just received a letter from Fr. Maurice in Gracevill Minn. You remember he was six years in Mt. Hope San. Baltimore. Thank God he seems to coming along o. He was installed out there as Chaplin last Mar. Msgr. Edw'd still working in St. Paul - till his Most Rev. Bishop call him back to the Islands - lecturing, giving missions, retreats, etc. . God bless you one and all again.

neutral: I hope you and your family are well. Thank you for your assistance on June 29th. I hope you have returned from your trip to the Southwest, that you found things positive, and that you will benefit from it in many ways. I will provide more details once I am settled in this new location. Thank you for your support. Please continue to offer it.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for kind favor of June 29th. I hope that you are back from your trip to the S.West. that you found things favorable and may you profit in many ways. More when I get settled in this new location. Many thanks for your prayers. Please keep them up.

neutral: I have received your gift and have arranged for spiritual support related to your specific concern. I hope things may brighten soon regarding that matter. However, you should definitely try to overcome that anxiety. Last year it was about something that now you smile about. Today it's about something that will not be serious if you approach it with a calm and trusting mindset every time it comes to mind, and maintain a sense of acceptance for future events.
styled: I just received your air favor and have inscribed you in the Seraphic Mass Association for your special Intent. Please God I hope things may brighten soon in regards to that same. However, and by all means shake off that anxiety of yours. Last year it was about something that now you smile about. To-day its about some thing that will not be serious if you raise your heart to God every time it comes to your mind and thank Him for whatever is to come.

neutral: I noted your request several weeks ago (August 29) and had hoped to find time to address a few details. However, I have repeatedly postponed it, and the situation remains unchanged. My correspondence is accumulating. In any case, I thank you (if I haven't already done so). I hope the problems in the Southwest have been resolved by this time. We will continue to hope for improvement.
styled: God bless you and yours. Having noted your kind reques several weeks ago (Aug. 29) I hoped to find leasure for a few details. I've put it off again and again and its the same thing. Ny letters acumulate more and more. At al events I thank you (if I havent done it before anyhow). I hope those annoying problems in the S.West have adjusted by this time. We'll continue our prayers that things improve. God bless you again.

neutral: Thank you for your letter of July 17th. I believe Mr. Lambert already acknowledged it. I am leaving for a trip to Baltimore to visit my ill brother. I brought your letter with me, hoping to answer it properly, but I am finding myself almost as busy on this trip as I am in my Detroit office. However, before I leave here, as planned, right after dinner, I want to express my appreciation and assure you that I will keep Joseph O'Donnell and yourself in my thoughts. It is time for me to conclude this letter. Goodbye.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of July 17th. I am sure Fr. Lambert acknowledged same befor. Leaving for a trip to see an invalid brother of mine in Baltimore. I took your letter along hoping to answer it as it deserves to be answered; but I find myself almost as busy on my "vacation as in the office in Detroit. However, before I leave here as expected right after dinner, I want to assure you of my appreciation and that I shall surely include Joseph O' Donnell in my poor prayers as well as yourself. Now it's time and for the present I'll say Goodbye and again

neutral:
We are very grateful for your generous donation of five dollars and your concern for the welfare of those in need. We apologize for the delay in sending this acknowledgement. We hope that by now your circumstances have improved.

This acknowledgement was written several weeks ago but was not mailed immediately, having been misplaced among other tasks. We hope your circumstances had already improved before you received this delayed letter.

Francis, Leo, and others send their best regards. As the holiday season approaches, we wish you a joyful Christmas and a Happy New Year.
styled: In acknowledgement of your charitable gifts of Five Dollars for which we are extremely grateful, and for your civic minded interest in the welfare of God's poor. Pl. pardon delay in acknowledgement. Hope by this time things have adjusted themselves brigher and better than before. P. S. God bless you Mrs. O"Donnell again. Having written the acknowledgement over several weeks ago without mailing it at once, I just found it snowed under other work. I hope things have adjusted themselves brighter before this. Brs. Francis and Leo and all send Best Regards. Now that the season for it is fast approaching we wish you all the blessings that go to make a really blessed Christmas and Happy New Year.

neutral: I hope you and your family are well. This is a quick note to thank you for the crate of excellent oranges, which arrived a few days ago in perfect condition. They are very good; I believe they are the best I've received so far.
styled: God bless you and keep you well. - you and yours. I'd like to write you a real letter but this is just to thank you for crate of fine oranges received here in excellent condition a few days back. They are very good. - in fact I think the best yet. How wonderful is the dear Lord in all His works!

neutral: Wishing you a joyful Christmas and success in your personal well-being and worldly affairs for the coming year and beyond. P.S. The fruit is excellent; two large bushels were well worth the effort. Protection is wished for all who carry the enclosed St. Christopher item.
styled: In short a joyful Blessed Christmas and success spiritually and temprarely the follow- ing year - years. P. S. The fruit is excellent ·-- Two big bushels really worth while God bless all. God bless and protect all who follow the inclosed St. Christopher --- just blessed.

neutral:
Thank you for the charitable contribution received yesterday. The timing of your gift, especially the smaller check, was excellent, enabling me to enroll several friends in the Ser Mass Association as a Christmas gift. This act serves as a double or triple charity.

Believing you were in Texas for the winter, I sent a letter to you last week, addressed to the Palner Hotel in McAllen, Texas. That address was taken from the labels on the two fine baskets of delicious fruit that arrived in your name, for which I want to thank you again. You will likely receive that letter after it has been forwarded. It contained relics of Venerable Mother Mary of Jesus of Agreda.
styled: My Dear Friends: God bless you and yours. Many thanks indeed for your charitable favor noted yesterday. I came just in nice time - especially the smaller cheque - to enroll quite a number of my friends in the Ser Mass Assoc'n for a Christmas gifte. - a double, tripple charity. Thinking you were down in Texas for the Winter I addressed a letter to you only last week - to Palner Hotel Mc Allen Texas - the address as - indicated on the baskets of fine fruit that came to us in your name - and for which I want to thank you again - for the twofine baskets of delicious fruit. You will very likely receive the letter forwarded withe relics of V.Nother fary of Jesus, of Agreda, which had inclosed.

neutral: Upon finding Tin's letter of January 13, I decided to write to you immediately. Rather than wait for more time to write a full letter, I decided to send these few lines. First, I have been wanting for what seems like two months to thank you for the second delivery from "The Grove," which was, if anything, an improvement on the first. The group certainly appreciated it. Many thanks also for your and Win's outreach efforts, which led to many new enrollments, including Father Solenus, who had previously been a source of significant concern. Thank you also for the other aspects of your monthly donations, which, as you must have noticed, often seem unappreciated. I hope you are both enjoying your vacation in your sunny Southwestern stay.
styled: Just uncovering Tin's letter of Jan. 13 I determined without further delay write you at least a few lines. - Better waiting for time to write a letter. First I've been wanting, it seem to ne two months, to thank for that second deliver; from the "Grove" - if anything an improvement on the 1st. The Brethren surely appreciated then. Then Many thanks for your mission-activity - and Win's too - in the many enrollments, including the old simmer who has given us here so much conscience trouble, Fr. Solenus - and the other features of your monthly donations - so often (as must seen to you) unappreciated. I do hope you are both enjoying your vacation in your sumy S.Western sojoum Praised be Jesus and Mary.

neutral: He is likely the most knowledgeable person in the Province of St. Joseph to advise on these matters. The education of students from low-income backgrounds has consistently been a significant challenge for the educational institutions. Many bright and promising students originate from low-income families, and no one has been rejected due to financial constraints. Nevertheless, this remains a significant challenge for the Province of St. Joseph. Any assistance you are able and willing to provide for the Province would be highly valued. The Provincial will be informed of your proposition, and a response is expected soon. He finds it reassuring when individuals are able and willing to help with such financial difficulties.
styled: He, perhaps better than anyone in the Provinc of Saint Joseph, would know best how to advise in such matters. I do imow that the education of poor students and candidates has always been quite a problem in our educational institutions. Often some of the brightest and most promising students come from poor familites and I am quite sure we have never as yet "turned down" on account of financial shortage. However, it is none the less quite a problem for the Province of St. Joseph - your own dear Patron. So I am sure that whatever you may fee able and disposed to do for the Province/ would be gratefully appreciated. P.S. Dear Joseph: I shall inform Father Provincial of your proposition and will probably hear from him before long. He naturally must feel a relief whenever he finds anyone able and willing to help in such a financial difficulty.

neutral: Thank you for your recent assistance, which was received and acknowledged. Clement, the Provincial, evidently appreciated your generous offer to help educate clerics for their religious training. He was unexpectedly called to Rome around that time. An appreciative letter was all he seemed able to send me regarding this. He also hoped to contact you later. I was surprised, not unpleasantly, by my transfer here to St. Felix. It is only about 90 miles from Chicago. Therefore, I anticipate seeing you soon.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your recent favor - duly received and noted. Rev. Fr. Provincial - Fr. Clement evidently appreciated your generous offer to help educate clerics, etc. for the Holy Priesthood. He was unexpectedly called to Rome about the time. An appreciative letter seemed to be about all he could send me in this regard. He hoped at his conclusion to get in touch with you later on. I was surprised - not unpleasantly - at my transfer hither to St. Felix. Only about 90 miles from Chicago. So I'll be expecting to see you some of these fine coming Nay days.

neutral:
We have received and noted your recent contributions.

Preparations are underway for the Corpus Christi observance, scheduled for this Thursday and next Sunday. A procession and Benediction service will take place at the Monastery's garden Shrine at 2:30 PM on the latter date. This event marks the only time annually that the garden is accessible to the Catholic public.

Additionally, a provincial Chapter meeting is scheduled for July 11-14. This meeting follows the appointment of our Provincial leader as General, which necessitated a move to Rome. We request assistance in seeking guidance for this meeting.
styled: Many thanks for your recent favors - duly received and noted. We are preparing for the glorious Feast of Corpus Christi this Thursday and next Sunday - with procession and Benediction at the Monastery - garden Shrine, at 2:30 the latter date. It would be an edifying treat - the only time in the year that the Garden is open to Cath. public. . . . Furthermore, since our Father Provincial was called to Rome to be Most Rev. General; we are to have a provincial Chapter, July 11 - 14th. Please help us storm Heaven for guidance. . . Praised be Jesus!

neutral: Joseph O'Donnell, I had intended to catch up on my correspondence before writing to you. However, the volume of incoming mail is increasing rapidly, requiring me to constantly attend to it. Consequently, less urgent matters are neglected the longer I wait. Nevertheless, I want to thank you for the large crate of excellent grapefruit. My sincere thanks. As you can observe, the typing on this Underwood typewriter is not expert.
styled: God bless you Josph O'Donnell - you and yours. I was in hopes to catch up with my correspondence and then write you, but it seems the letters come faster and faster so that I have to keep right on the job; and the longer I wait the more what's not too urgent gets snowed under. At all events I want to say at least thank you for the big crate of fine Grape-fruit. Nony thanks indeed. ^You can see for yourself. this is hardly an expert an underwood.

neutral: Its beneficial effects are widely acknowledged. The speaker would be pleased to meet again. However, the third Sunday of the month is visiting day for the novices, which is a busy day, particularly for the lay brothers and the novices themselves. Therefore, an alternative day would be preferable.
styled: Everyone a person meets seems to appreciate the great good it has done. Praised be His Holy Name ! Yes I would be glad to see you again some of these beautiful days. However, just incidently, the third Sunday of the month is visiting day for the novices and that is more or less a pritty busy day, especially for the laybrothe and the novices themselves. Another day, therefore, might be preferable.

neutral:
Thank you for your generous correspondence of March 19, which I have received and acknowledged. I am pleased to learn of your trip to the famous Shrine of Guadalupe, and especially of the hoped-for improvement in your health, which appears to be a partial result. I congratulate you and Mrs. O'Donnell on such a pleasant and positive experience.

Regarding the commendable proposal you are considering, specifically the education of a candidate for the priesthood: I view such a proposal as a deeply significant undertaking. There is a great need for such initiatives, and comparatively few outside the religious leaders and superiors of various orders fully recognize its critical necessity.

However, at this time, I would be reluctant to offer advice on such a proposal, as I know of others, due to their official roles or positions, who would be better equipped and more suitable to guide you. Therefore, I am referring your commendable proposal to our Father Provincial, Father Clement, OFM Cap., whose address is 1740 Mt. Elliott Ave., Detroit, Michigan.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your generous favor of March 19, duly received and noted. I am surely pleased to lmow of your privileged trip to the famous Shrine of Guadalupe, and especially of the hoped-for improvement in your health as surely a part consequence. I surely congratulate you and Mrs. O'Donnell on such a pleasant and praisworthy experience. Deo Gr. Now in regard to the laudable proposition you dream about, vis, the education of a candidate for the Holy Priesthood: I would consider such a proposition as always more or less of a supernatural inspiration. There is so much call for such activity - real Catholic Action - that, as I believe, there are comparatively few outside the Bishops and Superiors of the different Orders who realize its crying necessity. Personally and just at present, however, I would be relictent to advise in such a proposition, when I low of others, in consequence of their office or position who would be pleased and better able to guide you than I might. Hence I am referring your laudable proposition/our Father Provincial, the very Rev. Father Clement, OF. .. Cap. who's address is 1740 Mt.Elliott Ave.Detroit 7, Mich.

neutral:
I hope you and your family are well. I am pleased to hear you enjoyed your Southern and Southwestern trip and returned safely. Thank you also for the favor you mentioned.

Regarding the Groves and the young trees, we hope the enrollments will benefit them. We experienced a similar situation here this past Spring and Summer. On May third, a heavy frost occurred just as the apple trees and grapevines were in full bloom. Anticipating the frost, one of the clergy performed a ritual blessing over the entire plot, using a stole and holy water, hoping to mitigate its effects.

The next morning, the extent of the damage was clear. Despite the blessing, the frost had occurred and appeared to have frozen many of the apples and approximately 95% of the grapes. The situation appeared hopeless, particularly in the vineyard. The individual known as the Guardian, who was over 76 years old, had performed extensive pruning and other related work there.
styled: God bless you and keep you well - you and yours. I am glad to know you enjoyed your southern - S-Western trip and especially that you are returned safe and sould. Thanks be to God for all his wonderful, merciful designs. Many thanks to you also for your kind favor just noted. As to the Groves and the young trees; well we'll hope the enroll- ments and prayers otherwise may work something in their favor. We had quite an example here this past Spring and Summer. On the third of May (I believe that was the date), we had quite a heavy frost just when the apple-trees and grape-vines were nicely in bloom. We were rather anticipating what came; so that, in hopes the frost might be thwarted some way, one of the fathers went through the whole, plot or plotts, with stole and ritual and holy-water blessing everything. Alas! Next morning, you can imagine our dismay. Notwithstanding the blessing the frost had come and seemingly frozen many of the apples and about 95% of the grapes. It surely looked hopeless, especially in the vineyard. Father Guardian, now over 76 who had done so much pruning, etc.

neutral: On the occasion of her golden wedding anniversary, the speaker's mother recalled past events and places. Someone present commented, "It would be nice to return to those times." The mother replied, almost to herself, "I am glad it is over." The speaker later reflected that her mother's tone suggested she was reliving the difficulties of those pioneer days in West Wisconsin. Although those times were enjoyable for the children, the mother perceived them as periods of hardship and struggle that outweighed the pleasures, except for her conviction that she was fulfilling a profound purpose, contributing to the well-being of others, and holding out hope for brighter days as her promising family matured. She was guiding them through life towards their ultimate end.
styled: Still, as dear Mother remarked on the occasion of her golden wedding when talking about events and places familiar fort and more and less back some one remarked: "Wouldent it be nice if we could go back to those days?",Mother answered as half to herself: "Thanks be to God, I'm glad its over." I thought afterwards, infact it there was something in her voice that seemed to reinvision the trials of those pioneer days in West Sisconsin - happy as it was for the youngsters - as days of trials and struggles outweiging the pleasures, save that she was doing God's holy will, doing something for God and humanity and in hopes of brighter days as the years ripened for her promising family that she was then coaching on the one great pilgrimage to eternity.

neutral: Hello Joseph and Winnie. This brief message is sent before my departure southwest, in case you find it necessary. There is an enrollment for 'Emergent Managers and Employees of O'Donell's Texas Fruit Farm.' I hope the situation resolves without serious difficulty, and that the problem proves to be minor. Thank you for your letter dated September 6. I hosted Ed and M. E. Joachim last week. M. E. Joachim departed yesterday. Ed is expected back from Boston in approximately one week. Thank you again. Please keep the aforementioned issue in mind.
styled: God bless you Joseph and Winnie. Just a few words this time to catch you before going S.W. - in case you desid it necessary. An enrolling "Emergent-lenager and Employees of O'Donell's Texas Pruit Parm." I hope things smoothe off without any serious difficulty- and that the trouble prove "just a little ripple on the surface ..... Many thanks for your kind favor of Sept. 6. I had my two Rev. Brothers Misgr Ed and Fr. M. E. Joachim last week. The latter left yesterday. Expect former back from Boston in week or so ..... Again many thanks and God love and keep you both .... Just say the Our Father sloly and devoutly for above trouble.

neutral: A desire to follow the boats is sometimes felt, reminiscent of a childhood experience. As a child, small boats made of bark were regularly guided down streams of melting snow into larger ravines and deeper waters. During these times, practical concerns such as wet shoes and torn clothing were disregarded. Instead, there was often a contemplation of a profound, ultimate journey. These days are remembered as happy, a state attributed to an absence of guilt and anxiety. Furthermore, everything seemed connected to a realm beyond the ordinary.
styled: I sometimes imagine I'd like to follow them - as when a small child, when I was wont to coach little bark " boats" down the rills of melting snows to bigger ravines and deeper waters, - - forgeting all about soaked shoes and torn trouser and often thinking of my soul's journey to eternity. What happy days those! Why? I suppose because we knew nothing of sin and worry, and everything waiving to the wupernatural.

neutral:
Last fall and winter, conditions were particularly difficult, leading to a sense of deep disappointment. The individual recently stated that the situation had been very disheartening. However, within ten days, new shoots emerged and blossomed. Surprisingly, these newer shoots now appear larger and more promising than the initial ones.

The apple trees and other fruit trees, especially the pears and some of the peaches, look very promising this morning. A good rain is needed, as it has been quite dry for the last six or seven weeks. There is a strong hope for a good rain during a specific eight-day period.

It is pleasing to hear that the Garland Family is doing well and that Rae and Mrs. (Sr.) enjoyed their special visit to the famous sites associated with Joseph and Ann. It is hoped they will have a long life and many more positive experiences.

Postscript: The beneficial rain has arrived.
styled: last Fall and during the Winter, felt worse, seemingly than anyone else. Only yesterday, in a talk he gave us, he acknowledged that he could have cried. Nevertheless inside of ten days other shoots came out and blossomed and now the younger, to everyone's surprize, seem bigger and more promising than the first . Deo Gratias The apple-trees and others, especially the pears and some of the peaches look very promising this morning, if only now the dear Lord sends us a good rain; for we have had it quite dry for the last six or seven weeks. We are praying that during the octave of our Bl. Mother's Assumption at least we may have the favor from Heaven of a good rain. I am surely pleased to know that the Garland Family is doing so well and that Rae and Mrs. - Sr. - enjoyed their privileged pilgrimage to the famous shrines of St. Joseph and good St. Ann. May they live long and have many such happy experiences. P.S .- like. Thanks be to God and our Blessed Mother - The Mystical City of God - the good rain has come!

neutral: Thank you for your assistance, which I understand originated from Win-Chicago via Texas and was reinforced by Joe, as I just noted. I hope the situation improves before the end of the week, and that you return to the temperate zone feeling relieved and at least content, if not fully satisfied, with the outcome of your somewhat involuntary visit. It is unfortunate that the timing was not a couple of months later, so that you might have avoided some of the likely cold months we expect before the next orange harvest. Regardless, try to alleviate as much as possible of that persistent worry, a concern often observed among business people, including those of Chinese background, and also among individuals such as the O'Donnells, Kes, O'Caseys, and Mulligans. The weather here in the area of the Wabash and Maumee watershed is quite ideal. One part of the watershed flows southwest to the Gulf of Mexico, while the other flows northeast to the Great Lakes, and on to significant places like Montreal, Quebec, and across the Atlantic Ocean.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor - rather from Win- Chicago via Texas reenforce by Joe., just noted. I do hope that things brighten up before the week is over and that you return to the temperat zone relieved and at least content if not satisfied with the outcome of your, more or less force visitation. It almost seems too bad that it was not a couple months later, sothat you might escape some of the probably cold months we are likely to be in for before the ripening of the next oranges, etc. At all events try and shake of as much as you can of that over-due worry, so common to Chinese, etc business-men - like the O'Donnells and Kes, O'Caseys and Mulligans, etc. We are having quite ideal days here in the vicinity of the Wabash and Maumee "water-shed the one heading for the S-West to the great Gulf, the other North-east to the Great lakes and the shrines of Mont Reall, Qubec and across the briney Atlantic, etc.

neutral: Regarding the German candidate farm-manager whose religious affiliation is Lutheran: it would be preferable if he were a practicing Catholic. However, if he demonstrates honesty, religious devotion, and frugality, and has relevant experience, I would be more inclined to favor him over a recent university graduate with limited or no practical farm experience. The author notes that Lutherans generally possess a greater understanding of Christianity than most other non-Catholic Christian denominations. Furthermore, Protestantism as a whole currently appears to be in decline. The primary issue with sincere Protestants is their lack of understanding regarding the true relationship between their denomination and the Catholic Church. Assuming all other qualifications are equal, I would strongly prefer a conscientious Lutheran over a merely nominal Catholic. I have a long-standing appreciation for German Lutherans. If the climate change is not too drastic and his wife and daughter can assist, I would favor his candidacy.
styled: As to your German candidate farm-manager's system of religion - lutheran: well, it might be better and would certainly be more promising if he were Imown to be a practical Catholic; but if he give evidence of honesty and the fear of God and thrift as best he can - with experience bhind him, I would be water inclined to him rather than to a fresh graduate from most/ of our universities who have had little or no practical farm experien. After all the lutherans, as a rule, know more of Christianity than most any of the other non-catholic Christian denominations. Besides, these day protestantism as a whole seems to be rapidly crumbling. The whole trouble with honest protestants - and thank God there a lot of such - is that thy simply do not know the real relationship between their own denomination and the Mother-church. Otherwise equal, I would take a conscientious lutheran ten times in preference to just a nominal Catholic. I know from childhood how to appreciate German lutherans. If the change of clamate benot too radical and this man's wife and daughter can aide, etc, I would be inclined in his favor.

neutral: The peaceful expression on her face in the photo from her golden wedding indicates joy in her remembrance of past challenges, as well as confidence that her efforts to raise a family according to her deeply held principles were not in vain. Incidentally, I am unsure if I have shown you that photo before. If this has been overlooked previously, please remind me during your next visit. I would be pleased to show it, and anticipate you would also find it interesting. Apologies if this communication has become lengthy. I will attempt to contact you before your departure for the North. I request information regarding a significant personal transformation experienced by your manager there, or by someone who has undergone a more profound positive development.
styled: The peace that still still hovers on her brow - photo on that occasion of her golden wedding - bespeaks the something of joy in her soul at the rememberence of those day of trials for her as well as something of the confidence that filled her heart - confidence - that she had tried at least not in vain, to come up to ideal of raising a family for God and His Church. Incidently, I am not sure if I ever showed that photo. Ic case of neglect on my part heretofore, please remind me when you come the next time and I shall be pleased, as I am sure you will be. Please pardon if this is getting too drawn-out. I'll try and cach you before you leave for the North. God bless you again and I want you to bring me something about the conversion of that manager of yours down ther - or of one nearer the ideal.

neutral: Thank you for your generous gifts, including the excellent fruit and checks. This has been on my mind for weeks. Only late last night was I able to read your very interesting letter dated the 16th. I am grateful for the fortunate delay concerning the letter I had marked "Copy." I congratulate you on the opportune guidance you received during your recent trip. I will send the certificates and write to Mrs. Goodwillie soon.
styled: Many thanks for your generous favors - fruits excellent - and checks, prayers, etc. I have been with this on my mind for weeks 21st Only late last nigh did I get to read your very interesting letter of the 16th. Thanks be to God! How wonderful was His delicate "hold- up" of that letter I had marked "Copy." ....! I sure congratulate you on seemingly providential guidance on your late trip But after all, what might we not expect if we would trust in God and leave things more and more in His divine hands. Simplicity and confidence in God was the real secret of Young Tobias' success in the Old Testiment - and Jacob's too. I will try and send the certificates - and write to Mrs. Goodwillie soon ..

neutral: While searching for a copy of a letter I was writing to Police Chief McClellan of Detroit, which I had intended to emphasize further, I found two copies of the item in question, both marked "copy." This leads me to conclude that you never received either. This discovery provides an explanation for the current delay. There may be other, potentially more or less regrettable, aspects to this situation. It is fortunate that mistakes happen, and that the outcome is not ten times worse. The delay may possibly have been beneficial; it is hoped that this is indeed the case.
styled: I was just looking for something else - a copy of that letter I was writing to the big policeman, MeClellan of Detr't and that I wanted to "point up a little" - and I find two of the above and bothe marked "copy". So I must conclude that you never received either. I need no further excuse for tardiness this time - and perhaps more to be regretted of something less or more regrettable ?!?!? Thank the dear Lord for mistaks too. And thank Him that its not ten-times worse. Possibly the delay may to havebeen a salutary one. Please God it may not be other.

neutral: Your letter from yesterday has been received, and I hope to see you Monday night. There is no need to worry about arriving late. I rarely go to bed before 10 o'clock. Last evening, I wrote to my niece, Mrs. Dean Conley, at N. Riordan Road (I do not have the house number), informing her of your visit and asking her to let you know I was expecting you. I also invited them. I would like you to meet them. I believe you would enjoy each other's company. Regarding the farm: Such worldly matters are always a source of some concern, regardless of how they are approached. As you mentioned, the current situation is very unstable and unusual, making it difficult to operate most businesses successfully. It is challenging to know what ventures to pursue or where to invest. I had hoped from your letter a month or so ago—and I am sure you felt the same way—that your visit to the Southwest would prove beneficial. Nevertheless, I have confidence in Mr. Costello.
styled: I just received your letter of yesterday and am hoping to see you Monday night. Do not wory about coming late. It is very seldom I get on the matress till after 10 'clock. Only last evening I wrote my Niece, Mrs. Dean Conley, of (I just have not the number) N. Riordan Road, that you were coming and asking them to get word to you I expected you. I invited them too. I want you tomeet them. I think you would enuoy eachother's company. As for the Farm: Well, ofcourse such temporalities are always more or less a cause of worry what ever way one takes them. As you say: the times are so very upset and abnormal that it is no simple problem to carry on successfully at or with most any business. One hardly knows what to turn to or to invest in. I hoped from your letter a month or so ago - and I am sure you felt that way - that your visit to the S.West was providentially in your favor. I am inclined to confidence anyhow in Mr. Costello.

neutral: The speaker expressed a hope that the person would become more unselfish. During a threatening coal strike, the speaker conversed with Father Coughlin about the general outlook. Father Coughlin stated that "financial Jews" appeared to anticipate a serious depression, evidenced by their extensive selling of assets at that time. He and others concluded that these individuals were expecting an outcome more severe than what had resulted from the strike thus far. The speaker suggested continuing to do their best daily without excessive worry. The speaker recently discussed inviting the recipient and the Conleys with the local Superior, who also anticipates their arrival. The Superior stated that they could comfortably accommodate seven guests, and if needed, some of the men could be accommodated elsewhere. The Conleys have two young sons, the younger of whom is estimated to be slightly over two years old. The speaker suggested contacting the Conleys to make arrangements. Incidentally, the old violin arrived this afternoon.
styled: Perhaps we ought to pray more for him and wait gently, viz, that he become a little more unselfish, etc. However, I was talking with Father Coughlin during that threatening Coal-stike about the general outlook and he wastelling us that the finantial-Jews seemed to be expecting a seriou depression, from the fact that at that time they were selling everything they could. Therefore, he concluded as did others, that they were figuring on something worse than came at least from that strike so far. I suppose that we can hardly do better than just pray on, doing the best we know from day today and trust in divine Providence with out too much anxiety. May the Good God guide us all! I was just speaking to Father Guardian - our local Superior about inviting you and the Conleys and he too will be expecting you. He said: " .. We can acomodate seven guests nicely and fi necessary some of the men could be otherwise acomodated. The Conleys have two little boys, the younger must bealittle over two years old. If you dont mind you could call them up to that effect. INcidently, the old violin just arrived this p.m.

neutral: I am beginning my 77th year of life. I have just started to respond to your kind letter, received this morning, as work had kept me occupied at my desk until now. Thank you for your generosity and for your thoughtful remembrance on this occasion. Yesterday, friends traveled from Detroit to celebrate my 76th birthday. Last week, I was away for a period of personal reflection. On Sunday, I traveled to Detroit and then in the evening to Windsor, Ontario, Canada, to attend a farewell celebration for Julius. This event was hosted by his childhood friends from his former community. Julius was scheduled to depart for assignments in Guam in November. We returned on Monday evening, which necessitated catching up on work. I am grateful for everything.
styled: Yes, just starting my 77th anniversary as your wrie held me up at my above, first period after the date, - just starting to answer your charitable letter received this am. Many thanks for your generosity as well as for so kind a rememberence on this ocasion. I had some friends down from Detroit yesterday to remind me of and to congratulate on my 76thB-day. I was on retreat last week and on Sunday went to Detroit and in the evening to Windsor, Ontario, Can. to the "Send-off celebration" given to Fr. Julius O.F.M.Cap. by his old friends in the parish of his childhood - Our Lady of Prompt Succor. He was supposed to leave for Guam Missions in November. It was Monday evening when we returned and I felt I must get at my work and catch up, etc. Well, Deo gratia for every thing! Thanks be to Go.

neutral: Meanwhile, the author suggests seeking guidance and inviting deceased individuals (especially relatives) to participate in missionary efforts, promising them a share of the profits. This is considered a dual charitable act: benefiting those actively engaged in the cause (the missionaries and their work), and also benefiting deceased individuals. It has been reported that a significant factor in John D. Rockefeller's financial success was often attributed to his commitment to donate approximately 10% of his profits to charitable causes. The author finds such reports credible, as similar outcomes have been observed in other instances. The author apologizes for extending this concluding thought, as the intention was to conclude more briefly. This exemplifies the principle that rushing often impedes progress.
styled: In the mean time, however, let us pray for divine grudance - especially turning to St. Josep and the Poor Souls. How about inviting the latter to - especially our own relatives amongst them - to take an interest with us and become missionaries with a promise to enroll them, e.g., for a certain % of the proffits. That I always call a double charity; to our neighbor, viz, to our fellow members of the militent Church, the missionaries and their work and then to the Church-suffering, the poor, holy souls. Several years ago and frequently later on, I was assured that one of the great factors in the financial success of "old-man Rockefellow" was often attributed to his having kept a promise to spend something like 10% of his profits to one or other charitable work. I am quite inclined to take stock in such a report. I have seen the like work out in other cases. Plese pardon my prolongation of this conclusion. I meant to close in just a line or two here. Just another case of: "The more hury the less speed". God help us.

neutral: and is in good condition. This positive state is appreciated. Meanwhile, it is hoped that personal transformation will accelerate in the coming fifty years compared to the past. Naturally, the remaining period is likely to be shorter than the past twenty-five years.
styled: and is in good condition. Thanks be to God for all His unsearchable designs. In the mean time do not forget to say little prayer now and then that I make a little faster progress in conversion the coming fifty years than during the past. Ofcourse the next will probably shorter than the past twenty-five.

neutral: Greetings to J.J. and Win. I would write at length, but I primarily wanted to thank you for your communication of the 8th. I am very grateful for M.C.'s change. He could not have received my letter before Monday, as it was sent on Friday. This development significantly increases my optimism; it is excellent news. Pat has recovered from danger, which is a great relief.
styled: God bless you J.J. and Win. I'd write at length .. but I just want to thank you for favor of the 8th. Thank God for M.C's change! ! He could not have received my letter befor Monday. - sent Friday on 3¢. It only heightens my hopes in God's designs . . How wonderful! . Brother Pat. has snapped out of dange. . Deo Gr.

neutral: Due to his inability to leave Chicago during the last several weeks of your visit, his wife Winifred traveled to prepare for the meeting and to find a new caretaker. He later joined her for a weekend, and they appear satisfied that they found a desirable successor.
styled: I am glad too that while it was quite out of the question for him to leave Chicago the last several weeks you were with him, his Wife Winifred was able to go down and prepare things for the meeting and procuring of a new care-taker. He followed for a "week-end" absence and they seem quite satisfied that they struckin with a quite desirable successor. How wonderful the ways of the good God when we foster confidence in Him by just leaving at least somthing that seems important for Him to take care of! Blessed be His Holy Name.

neutral:
The O'Donnells informed me several weeks ago that you intended to write, having mentioned you briefly over the past few months. I recently located your letter from February 26th, which I had been seeking after it was somehow misplaced. Therefore, I am clarifying any potential questions you may have about my identity or interests.

You inquired about Appleton, Wisconsin. It was in St. Joseph's Church in Appleton where I officiated my first religious service on July 31st, 1904.

I cannot say I am precisely from St. Paul, Minnesota, although I spent many enjoyable days there visiting relatives and friends and staying as a guest at the Seminary. Two years ago in June, while traveling to Seattle, I visited an old friend, Mike Costello. He had been my oldest brother's childhood friend on our farms sixty-five years earlier, which were located about forty miles down the river on the Wisconsin side.
styled: My Dear Mr. Costello: God bless you and yours. The O'Donnells told me several weeks ago that you were writing me -- having told me quite allittle about you for several past months. Only just now did I come across your interesting letter of February 26th -- somehow mislaid -- that I've been looking for. So I am not keeping you in any possible suspence as to my identity, interest, etc. You ask about Appleton, Wisconsin. It was in St.Joseph's Church in that neat little city where I had my first Holy Mass, July 31st 1904. God be blessed.Deo Gr. No. I can not say that I am exactly from St. Paul, Minn; though many a pleasant day I spent in that thrifty city - with relatives and friends and in the Seminary, as guest. Coming two years in June, on my way to Seattle, I visited an old friend of mine Mike. Costello who had been moldest brother's bare-foot-boy friend on our farms sixty-five years before and about forty miles down the River on the Wisconsin side.

neutral: The community expresses its sincere gratitude for your generous donation of fruit, which was received in perfect condition. The shipment included two large eratis on March 17th and four baskets on March 22nd. Gratitude is also extended to everyone who has been involved or shown interest. Assisting others is regarded as a valuable act, and expressing appreciation for such assistance is similarly valued.
styled: You and yours. Many thanks from myself and our whole community for your generous donation of fruit received in perfect condition, - two fine big eratis shiped March 17th (Irish holy-day! ), and four fine baskets March 22nd. May our dear Lord bless yourself - as also everyone who in any way has been interested. · . What a privilege to do a favor for God in doing for our neighbor! The same too can be said of being appreciative and grateful for such favor - Communion of saints.

neutral:
February 5th, 10:30 PM. Before postponements.

A profound sense of wonder and gratitude is expressed for positive developments. The writer enjoyed the letter. While no specific individual was directly involved, it would be a rewarding subject to detail such a privilege and such a display of great kindness and generosity extended to everyone, including the writer. Gratitude is expressed for all beneficial outcomes, both those not immediately apparent and those that are clearly evident.

The Guardian came across the corridor to inform the writer that a Mass would be held on Friday for the recipient and their intentions. This would be the first of five such services for the recipient's intentions, in addition to enrollments.
styled: Feb. 5th - 10:30 pm - Before postponements How wonderful is the Lord in all His ways! How can we ever appreciate - be gratiful !!! I enjoyed your letter. . . . Not that this or that person was directly concerned, but it would be a happy theme if one had time a ability to go into details of such a privilege and such a manifestation of God's mercy and generous condescention to any - to us - poor sinners. Thanks be to God for all His hidden designs - as well as for those we praise as manifestations. Fr. Guardian just came across the corridor (almost expected a reminder to retire) to tell me we would have the High Mass on Friday for you and your intentions - the first of five for your Int. - besides Enrollments

neutral: When the narrator was approximately 17 years old, they served a sentence of less than two months at Stillwater Penitentiary. There, the narrator encountered Mike, who was already present, and they were assigned to share sleeping quarters. Mike was a boiler-maker, and his associate was a roustabout. These sleeping quarters, however, were located outside the main prison wall. Years later, one of these individuals became a lieutenant in the Saint Paul Police Department, while the other became a Capuchin priest. During a subsequent trip, the narrator and companions visited Mike, who was then in his eighties and nearly blind; he appeared rejuvenated by their visit. The narrator had spoken to Mike by phone several times but had not seen him in person for over thirty years. Therefore, when the O'Donnell friends expressed disappointment several weeks prior, the narrator suspected a mistake or misunderstanding. This suspicion proved correct, which the narrator considered a positive development. The narrator's experience with these friends over several years led to the belief that the relationship was one of collaboration rather than mere service.
styled: Later, when I was about 17, I did a term in the Stillwater Penetentiary (less thantwo months), and I found Mike there ahead of me and we became bed-fellows - he a boiler-maker and his partner just "a roustabout". However, we had our sleeping-quarters outside the wall. Some years after that the one became a lieutenant in the Saint Paul police- department; the other a poor Capuchin and a priest. Mike was in his 80s and wasalmost hlind when we went to see hm on said trip - seemingly rejuvanited at our visit. Ihhad spoken to him on the phone a number of times but for over thirty years had not seen him. So that, when our O'Donnell Friends seemed disapointed several weeks back I felt there must be a mistake or a misunderstanding "in the woodpile" somewhere. Thanks be to God for all interested it turned out to be so, - just another blessing in disguise I trust. For I feel that as you learn to know these friends, as I have known them for several years, you will come to feel that you are rather working with them than just for them.

neutral: After a period of suffering and preparation, she died peacefully on August 14th, appearing joyful. She is remembered always by her entire family, both living and deceased.
styled: Prepared by patient suffering and by the Sacraments and prayers of our holy Mother the Church, on August 14th With joyful countenance received the final call of the divine Lover, Bridegroom of our souls and gently passed to Eternity. Perpetually - with her whole family deceased and living

neutral: The author believes their purpose is to understand, love, and serve their creator, viewing this as a noble objective. This state is considered a form of ultimate happiness for those who are thankful, revealing immense worth and embodying a divine presence. The author extends good wishes to Joseph J. O'Donnell and their family, hoping they are well and refreshed after the beneficial rain. The author notes that the cards, started several days prior, are later than intended and not what was originally envisioned. However, the German saying "Nothing perfect in this world" offers comfort, which the author interprets to mean that no one in this life is fully perfected. The author expresses gratitude for the creator's infinite patience and reveres the creator's name.
styled: God made me to know Him. O what a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's Heaven begun for the grateful on earth. To treasure aright !-?-! Highest Heaven its worth. - God himself - even here. God bless you Joseph J. O'Donnell - you and yours. I hope this finds all 100% yourselves in the grace of God - smiling after the wonderful rain He sent us, like lillies and roses. I started these cards several days ago but some how or other they are later than intended and far from what I wanted. However, the little German saying "Nichts ..- " consoles me: "Nothing perfect in this world." In other words, no one is here on this side of Heaven fully converted. Thank the good God, He has infinite patience ! - Adored be his Holy Name!

neutral:
As an additional note:
The adage "haste makes waste" could apply to the other party involved in this correspondence, implying that it is disadvantageous for an inexperienced individual to rush.
Regardless, a very appreciative letter was received from M.C.C. It is believed that what annoyed M.C.C. in the previous letter was the mention of a suggestion that his heart attack might have left him not entirely himself. However, that particular point was found amusing. Otherwise, the letter was pleasant and clearly demonstrated a kind attitude towards the O'Donnells.

June 5th Postscript:
On June 5th, while preparing for a trip scheduled for the following afternoon, a carbon copy was discovered which had been presumed sent the previous week. Its delayed discovery caused some embarrassment. The writer's nephew, Bernard Maurice (Owen's son), has been present since Monday and will accompany the writer on his journey to Seattle.
styled: Just as a sord of P.S. Dear Friends "The O'Donnells". "The more hurry the less speed", the old say- ing could easily be applied to the other side of theis "document". I guess it hardly pays for an apprentice to speed up too much. Any how I thought you'd be pleased to know that I received quite an appreciative letter from M.C.C. I think what "raised his fethers" about my letter before, was my having quoted you as intimating that his heart-attack had possily left him ? not exactly himself. But really that feature just amused me. Otherwise it was a nice letter and quite indicative of a charitable feeling to the O'Donnells. June 5th P.S. Just straightening up for our trip tomorrow P.M. I came across this carbon I thought was off last week am almost ashamed to send it. My nephew Bernard Maurice (Owen's Son) is with me since Monday. He will acompany me on his way to Seattle.

neutral: On March 27, best wishes to Joseph J. O'Donnell, Winnie, and all your loved ones. As discussed during our phone call last Sunday, I had planned to attend your special service on Wednesday. However, that morning, Mr. Guargian informed me of a slight schedule change that would benefit you. He stated, "The dedicated service for the O'Donnells will be held next Sunday. Please inform them of this." I intended to do so that day, and every day since, but have only now found the opportunity. Therefore, I will include our simple seasonal greetings and best wishes, extended to everyone throughout the holiday period.
styled: (March 27) God bless you Joseph J. O'Donnell - with Winnie and all your dear ones. As surmised when phoning last Sunday, I was set for your high Mass on Wednesday but that morning Fr. Guargian whispered to me a little change in schedule in your favor. "We'll offer the solemn Mass for the O'Donnell intentions next Sunday. Write them to that effect ... " I wanted to do so that day - and every day since and now its almost time for the daily "pick up" So I'll add our simple Easter greeting and felicitations with a hearty God's blessing to all repeated for all the Easter Season.

neutral: The six crates of fruit arrived today in perfect condition. The kindness shown is appreciated. Further communication regarding this will follow. It is fortunate to be in the sunny South-west currently, as the local weather here consists of competing rain and snow, driven by a strong northeast gale. Good wishes are extended to your caretaker Johnson and family. There is a sense of familiarity with them. They are also held in positive regard. Regards.
styled: Many Thanks for your thoughtful kindness, with six crates of fruit that in perfect condition arrived Today. - about which, later. You are fortunate to be in the sunny South-west these days, - rain and snow in a sort of contention and gale from the N.E. urging them on. May the Lord bless your care-taker Johnson and family. I feel that I sort of know them too. Best regards. We pray for them too.

neutral: The sender expressed thanks for a kind and generous favor received and noted yesterday. They were pleased to hear of the recipient's well-being and that their daughter Adelaide's prospects were good. The sender hoped Adelaide would have great success on June 5th, noting its importance. Regardless of the outcome, they also hoped she would strive to maintain a close connection to her religious beliefs. The sender expressed disappointment, having anticipated it, that the recipient and Mr. O'Donnell failed to understand each other. However, based on the recipient's communication, the sender hoped their parting was for the best. One aspect that particularly pleased the sender was that both parties appeared clearly charitable toward each other. They hoped the recipient and Mr. O'Donnell would continue to maintain that truly constructive and friendly feeling, which was noted despite some anger from both sides.
styled: Many thanks for your kninly generous favor receive and noted yesterday. I am glad to know that you are well and that the outlook is bright for your Daughter Adelaide. I hope she may have best success June 5th is most important and - , seccess that day or no srecess - that she strive by every means that our holy Mother the Church offers us, to keep close and dear to the Holy Family, Jesus, Mary and Joseph. I was rather disapointed, as I quite surmised it reght along, that yourself and Mr. O'Donnell failed to understand eachother. However, as you write I hope it was best that you parted. One thing about it I am more than pleased with, viz, that you both seem decidedly charitable toward oneanother. I do hope to know that you keep up that really edifying and friendly feeling. All this even with a touch of "ire" on either side.

neutral:
February 22nd.
This message is intended to connect with you. It is hoped you will return in better weather and with brighter prospects than when you began your trip.

Additionally, observing concern about declining prices, some observations are offered to help alleviate anxiety. First, it is important to remember that success or lack thereof is not essential regarding material possessions. Sooner or later, these material possessions must be relinquished, if they are not lost to us first. Therefore, there is no reason to lose peace of mind over them.

Additionally, mistakes regarding worldly matters often occur, which can foster humility and lead to a more agreeable disposition.

Finally, this is a "Presidential Election year." This typically means a period of depressed farm prices, at least until after Election Day. Businesses tend to postpone investment until after the election.
styled: Febr.22nd. My Dear Friends: God bless you one and all. Just a word to meet you down there as friend from up north. I hope it may please the Lord to bring you back in better weather and brighter hopes than saw you start on the trip I'd like to have made with you. Permit me to follow in spirit! At the same time, seeing your rather undue concern at dropping prices, etc, I thought a word of observation might help a little to steady someone's nerves. First of all, however, we should re-remember at all events, that success or want of the same is not essential as pertains temporalities. Sooner or later we shall have to drop them - if they don't drop us first. Why, therefore, lose our peace on their account? Then again, God often permits us to make temporal blunders in order to foster humility in our souls so that in the sight of Heaven we may be more amible. Finally this is "Presidential Election year." That means more or less a depression in farm prices at least till after Election-day. Business men will not invest till Election.

neutral: A new observance focusing on Mary's maternity has been announced. I hope this message finds you all in good spirits. I am enclosing the overdue account that was discussed by phone last night. I hope you find it worthwhile.
styled: new Feast of "Maternity of Mary Bles'd Virgin." May this find you all in the best of outlooks - with lively, firm and ardent faith, hope and charity! - the triune virtue. I am just enclosing the belated account referred to over long-distance last night. I hope you may find it worth while.

neutral: The speaker understood the other person's perspective, as the person was about to reprimand the speaker, and the speaker felt this reprimand would have been justified based on a misunderstanding of the situation. A brief explanation, fewer than ten words, resolved the issue, even while the speaker remained on another long-distance call. Later, at the earliest opportunity, the person apologized for their earlier behavior.
styled: I surely sympathized with him as I saw him just ready to call me down and as I felt he would be fully justified if appearance had not deceived him. Less than ten words fully satisfied his demand without my even hanging up a long-distance call. The first chance he had afterward, he expressed regret at his manifestation of his weakness. May his dear soul rest with the saints!

neutral: April 10, 1948. Joseph O'Donnell and his family are greeted, with hopes for their well-being. The sender's strength is reportedly recovering satisfactorily, though slowly. It is hoped that O'Donnell is improving and has the necessary patience. Shortly after his consecration, Murphy of Saginaw experienced a serious accident that confined him to bed in the same position for approximately six months. A year later, his condition was perfect.
styled: April 10th 1948. God bless you Joseph O'Donnell. - you and yours. I hope you are all well. Thanks be to God my strength seems to be coming back in pretty good shape, though rather slowly. I hope that Fr. O'Donnell is improving by this time and that the good God may give him the needed patience. Shortly after his consecration Bishop Murphy of Saginaw met with a serious accident that put him on his back for about six months in same position. A year afterwards his condition was perfect. Thanks be to God! We'll include Fr. O'D. in our prayers.

neutral: Humanity's purpose is to comprehend the divine. This is a profound goal, and love and service are integral to it. This endeavor originates from a transcendent source for those who are appreciative during their lifetime. Valuing it correctly reveals its immense worth. The ultimate reward, even in this life, is the divine itself for each individual, contingent on one's ability to appreciate it and cultivate a deep sense of thankfulness.
styled: Hense the little verse: God made me to know Him ! O! What a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's Heaven-begun, for the grateful ON EARTH. To treasure aright ! ? ! Highest Heaven its worth. God Himself is the principal reward even here for each one of us inasmuch as we learn to appreciate; in asmuch as we put on Christian Gratitude. Glory be to God in the Highest! Bles't and prasd be the Hearts of Jesus and Mary!

neutral: As the eldest child, Paul began working as a cigar-maker in early boyhood to help support his large family. He later worked as a gardener, musician, and in various other professions. He was delighted to learn that, despite it being generally considered too late to study for the priesthood, there was still a possibility in America, specifically with the Capuchin Franciscans. His long-held hopes were immediately rekindled, and he promptly moved to America. He had no inkling of the setbacks and disappointments that still lay ahead before he could achieve his goal. Nevertheless, his calm expression was evident as he awaited the undertaker, positioned exactly as he had been for his final rest—with his left foot on the stool, his hand under his head inclined to the same side, and his rosary over his shoulder.
styled: Paul's " "For those who love God, all things turn for the best." He had become cigar-maker in early boyhood to help raise the big family, of which he was the eldest; and then a gardner and musician, etc. etc; when he learned to his great joy and hope, afteras was generally thought to be too late to study for the holy Priesthood, that in America there was still a possibility of becoming a priest and at that, a Capuchin Franciscan. His smoldering hopes at once revived and as soon as possible he came to America. He had never an incling of the knocks and dispointments still between him and the realization of his goal. Neverthe less, as his calmness of countenance attested while he waited for the undertaker, in exactly the position he had taken for his last long seep -- with his left foot on the stool, his hand under his head inclined to the same side and his rosary over his sholder.

neutral: The priest scheduled to perform the final service that morning moved quietly in and out, checking on a particular matter. He assumed the superior was simply catching up on sleep, as he often missed a lot of it at night. His often-expressed wish to die while still working was fulfilled. He had reiterated this desire just forty hours earlier, after his morning service and a sermon at Brother Cook's final vows ceremony. His extensive experience as a superior and the challenges he faced throughout his life had prepared him to be an ideal leader. Although I spent a lot of time with him, even assisting him at his first two services, I only saw him nearly upset on one occasion. This occurred in relation to something I was responsible for carrying out. I was personally indignant at how the situation appeared, as I immediately understood how it must have seemed to him.
styled: The Father who was to have the last holy Mass that morning tiptoed in and out, to see the special intention, never dreaming but that Father Guardian was just supplying, as usual, something of the sleep so much of which he was wont to miss during the nights. Surely his desire to "die in the harness", as he had so often expressed it -- and even about forty hours before, after his solm Mass in the morning and sermon at Brither Cook's final profession, -- was happily realized. Thanks be to the merciful God. How wonerful in His all ways! His long experience as superior and the difficulties metwith during his whole life, by the grace of God, had fitted him to be a really ideal Father Guardian. Much as I was with him - and I assisted him at his first and second holy Masses - I never but once saw him as really "next to upset"; and that was in connection with something that fell to my duty to execute. I was indignant myself at the very appearance of the situation, as I realized at once that it must appear to him.

neutral:
This message provides an update on Guardian's death. Before discussing Guardian, acknowledgement is made of your communication last week, which was received and noted as requested. This was inadvertently omitted during a phone call two nights ago.

Approximately a year ago, Guardian (Matthias) experienced a significant decline in health. For several months, until early March, he was unable to attend communal meals or services. During that period, he slept very little, and only in a chair. However, he had reportedly been reading about the life of a modern missionary, the late Bishop Hartman of India, and performed a nine-day devotion in his honor, requesting assistance to be able to fulfill the principal duties of his office.
styled: My Dear Friend Joseph: God bless you and yours, especially Mrs; ofcourse. Just a short word Tonight to tell you a little about Rev. Father Guardian's transition, as we all hopeto his better place in God's providence beyond the grave. First, however, I want to thank you for your kind favor of last week, duly received and noted as requested, which I forgot to acknowledge over the phone the night-before-last. About a year ago Father Guardian - Mtthias - took a very threatening turn and for several months, till early March, was not really able to come down to the refectory or to choir-services. During that period he was able to sleep very little and that only in the chair. However, it would seem he'd been reading the lifeof one of our great modern missionaries, the late most Rev. Bishop Hartman of India, and made a noveina to his honor and in petition that he do something for him, to be able at least to fulfil the principal duties of his office.

neutral: At the end of the novena, Father Guardian attended choir, refectory, and recreation until his final moments. Even on Sunday night, just hours before his death, he appeared more entertaining than usual, making it seem he would have been willing to converse throughout the night. He was an avid reader, and while he seemingly paid little attention to displaying his knowledge, the benefits of his extensive reading and study were frequently evident. Additionally, he was a person of deep conviction with extensive experience, having faced numerous trials and hardships from early childhood that consistently served to temper, mature, and soften his naturally fiery disposition. Perhaps the most significant disappointment of his life concerned his childhood aspiration to become a priest in the Capuchin-Franciscan Order. This disappointment, which he endured with acceptance, was eventually resolved.
styled: Athe the end of the novena, thanks be to God and the great missionary, Father Guardian came to Choir and refectory and also to recreation up to the very last. Even Sunday night, just a few hours befor his final sleep, he seemed even more than usually entertaining; so that one would almost think he would'nt mind conversing all niggt. He was always a great reader and though apparently cared little about showing his ability, the advantage of his reading and study was often manifest. What was better, he was a man of lively faith with an unusually wide experience and with trials and hardships from early childhood that were hardly ever wanting to tame and to mellow and soften his naturally firey nature. Peerhaps the bitterest disapoint of his whole life was that regarding his, from-early-childhood vocation to be a priest in the Capuchin- Franciscan Order; - a disapointment which having been suffered in resignation, was lifted in God's own merciful way and time; - surely an example in confirmation of St.

neutral: After finishing a card for Winifred last night, I want to send this along with it before I forget and something is overlooked. I had begun to offer advice in my short card, but after finishing it, I felt my effort was rather vague. Regardless, I am expressing these thoughts this morning and hope they contribute to her encouragement. Everyone living needs encouragement occasionally, at a minimum. This encouragement provides comfort and support during challenges and hardships, even when efforts are imperfect. When properly appreciated, it profoundly transforms difficult life circumstances, offering hope and joy that surpasses even ideal human experiences. If people could only appreciate and cultivate gratitude, they would experience profound contentment even in this life. Appreciation and gratitude are key.
styled: Having hinished a card to Mrs. - your winnifred- last night, I want to get this off together with it before I forget and something be "sowedunder. I started to kinda started to moralize in my short card but it seemed to me after I was through that my effort was rather vague. At all events I'm giving it to the air this Morning and hope it contribute something to her encouragement. For, this side of Heaven who is there living that neads no encouragement now and then, at least. How, beyond all conception of creatures, how marvelously has not our divine Master Jesus provided such encouragement - with consolations against trials and difficulties undertaken, even when only partly and imperfectly for His dear sake, that, if only appreciated properly on our part, lend to our "lot otherwise in this vale of tears", - Ah! colors and hopes that surpass in reality even the joys of humanity before the Fall in Paradise. O! If humanity could only appreciate, - if in studying appreciation and gratitude in the School of Jesus and Mary - what a taste of Heaven humanity would be given even in this earthly vestibule! Appreciation? Gratitude!

neutral: Greetings Mrs. O'Donnell. Thank you very much for your kind assistance from the frontier and the cotton fields. The cotton blossom was quite a surprise. I would like to provide more details, but this is only a card, and I have many other people to write to today, including your J.J. Therefore, I hope you will understand why I am only sending a card, and perhaps offer support and understanding rather than disapproval. I believe that both you and Joe have reason to feel good about yourselves, even amidst this experience of many sacrifices. It seems unfortunate that we do not all fully appreciate the idea that those who make sacrifices for a significant cause will receive great returns, even if these are not always realized in this lifetime. This concept should be a source of great inspiration to everyone, particularly during difficult times.
styled: God bless you Mrs. O'Donnell. - away on the range Many thanks for your kind favor from the "fronteer and the the fields of cotton. The dotton-blossom was quite a surprise I'd like to go into some details but this isonly a card. and I have about twenty other Joes I outht to write Today besides your J.J. So you'll be easy in me for taking only a card and perhaps let me have a prayer for inspiration and guidance rather than a frown. Really, I think both you and Joe have an occasion for merit even in this experience of manifold-sacrifice. It seems to me just too bad that every one of us hear those words of Jesus: " ... He that hath left ... for my sake, etc, will receive a hundred-fold even ... and not to every here in this life ... " - as to some one else trial and cross What an inspiration these and such promises ought to be toevery one of us! O!
