neutral: A recent communication from Joseph J. conveyed another disappointment. It is unclear what actions can or should be taken. A crucial strategy during any crisis is persistent effort and the avoidance of excessive worry. Though this may at times seem impossible, perseverance is valued. The future is particularly unpredictable at present. However, this uncertainty is not new; it is a recurring aspect of human existence. Therefore, the fundamental lesson appears to be the appreciation of a lasting existence, moving beyond a focus on temporary life. This requires courage and resolve.
styled: God bless you and guide you. - you and yours. I was just with Joseph J. He said had been in long distance touch with just before and - God help, us another disapointment! Well ?...? It is a problem what to do - or what it may be possible to do. One thing, which in the final will much mean much is to try again and again in time of any crisis, to keep our old heads from overmuch wrrying. At times of course this will seem impossible but God is always pleased to see us turn to him and His saints and try on. These days especially we just cannot surmise what may be ahead of us. However, that is nothing specially new, for its more or less the same story at ever tum in our earthly pilgrimage. In other words, it would seem that the great lesson Godhimself would want us to learn on that pilgrimage, is appreciation for the Life Eternal He has waiting for us, if by correspondence with His grace we begin to wean ourselves from this temporal - "momentary existance .... courage therefore ... Heroism!

neutral: To Mrs. O'Donnell, located in what was once considered the wild West, but is actually just across the Mississippi, approximately 25 miles north of my birthplace, which is 4 miles south of Prescott. In 1870, this area was a frontier region, yet it was also a very scenic part of the country. I recently spoke with Joe, and we are pleased to hear that your condition is showing positive signs of improvement and a promising outlook. I hope this marks the peak of the issue, perhaps a lingering effect from the previous year. I wish you a speedy recovery.
styled: God bless you Nrs. O'Donnell, away out there in the (once-upon-a- time) wooley West, in reality just across the Mississippi some 25 miles up from my birth - blace - 4 miles below Prescott. At that time in 1870 it was indeed a pioneer portion but a wonderfully picturesque section of the Country. Well I just had a talk with Joe and we are surely pleased that your trouble is so hopefully checked - and promising. I hope it may prove to have been the climax, left over from the old year, etc after all, however if, "Thoom the Lord loveth He chasteneth," we ought to thank God for the privileg of being mode to resemble His divine Najesty ... so now I'll say Good Night and again God bless you and yours - speedy recovery . . . Fr. Solanus, O.F.K.Cap.

neutral: Greetings to Joseph J. and Win. I have read your letter of July 5 and appreciate your dedication and generosity. Thank you very much. We hope that the new caretaker's positive report proves to be accurate. My new Associate, Simeon, drew my attention to a specific reference concerning the listing of my intentions. I asked him to record it using your own words: "I have many of them, and the O'Donnells are always included." Fortunately, I am feeling well again after only two weeks in the hospital. I am also grateful for the excellent weather we have experienced recently—not excessively hot during the day and cool at night. Thank you very much, and best wishes to everyone. - Solanus
styled: God bless you Joseph J. - with Win and all. I just read your interesting letter of July 5th and we surely appriciate your zeal and generosity. Many thanks and God's reward. We pray and trust that the new care-taker's hopeful report may turn out to have been not too optimistic. My new Rev. Associale, Fr. Simeon called my attention to special reference to enrollment of my Intent's. I just asked that he put it down in your own words. "I have plenty of them - and the O' Donnells always included. Thans be to God: I am feeling well again after just two weeks in the Hospital. Thanks be to God too for the ideal weather He has been sending us lately - not over hot during the day and cool rights. Many thanks and God's blessing to each and all. - Fr. Solanus, ofmc

neutral: Individuals should strive to monitor their excessive and irrational tendencies to indulge their own preferences and impulses, rather than prioritizing the will of a higher authority and even the most humble individuals—a commitment that extended to ultimate self-sacrifice. It is believed by some that the memory of difficulties experienced during one's life on Earth will be among the most profound satisfactions in a future, transcendent state. styled: I hope you are well and that you may enjoy your exile down there and find it more and more congenial - doing missionary work as long as you can. neutral: Wishing you and your family well during this time. Despite the tragic circumstances, there is hope and beauty. After all, if we reflect on past decades, we will likely find that our biggest worries have always been about things that never happened; for example, twenty years ago on your way to Quebec. Instead of worrying about anything—past or future—it is better to cultivate a confident and positive outlook by anticipating favorable outcomes.

O! Instead of worrying about anything - past or threatening to come - les us foster confidence in God by thanking Him ahead of time.

neutral:
No one can ever surpass the ultimate source of generosity or any other quality. This source generously bestows abundant blessings upon those who are confidently receptive.

Regarding post-mortem anatomical operations, there is no need for concern. Instead, even with minimal intervention in most cases, the purpose is often to assist those currently suffering or who may suffer in the future from similar conditions. Using one's remains for fertilization after death could be considered an act of charity.

Regarding worries about past mistakes and transgressions: One should be so focused on gratitude for being saved from severe consequences and uncontrolled desires that there would be no time to worry about anything else, except perhaps for slow progress toward personal improvement.
styled: No creatur, when there is question of generosity, can ever get within a weakest shadow of anythin like even dreaming to beat the Lord in generosity or anything else. But God loves to load confidently loving souls with supernatural, divine generosity. .. As for what they call an anatomical operation after death; it seems to me, such a thing should be the very last thing in the world to worry about. On the contrary, while in the vast majority of such cases there is very little operating done, the idea is possibly to help some similar case or cases still suffering or to suffer in future. For my part I shall consider it as doing an actof charity after my death if they can use my old bones for fertilizing. .... As for worrying because about past stupidities and sins: It just seems to me that we ought to be so occupied in gratefully thanks God for having rescued us from Hell and from the jaws of our unruly passions that we should find no time to worry about anything - save possibly, that about making so little progress toward progress in the way of perfection, etc. ....

neutral: One potential positive outcome of atheism is the fostering of unity among those who believe in God. If religion is defined as the understanding of the relationship between a divine being and rational creatures, including their dependence on their creator and their neighbors, then it implies that religion should inherently be singular. Any deviation from this unity is seen as opposing the peace that ought to permeate human society, both among individuals and between individuals and their Creator. This peace, described as transcending all comprehension, is believed by some to be ultimately established by the divine entity among individuals and nations, even if it requires significant hardship before it is fully realized.
styled: If there is a blessing of any kind to come from atheism - in itself the Climax of insanity - it will be this Unity among those professing to believe in God. After all, if Religion can be defined as: "The science of relationship between God and the rational creature, and dependence of the latter on his Creator - and his neighbor - then religion must be one, and whatever is contrary to that unity is opposed to that peace between men themselves and God their Creator that ought to permiate human society - the peace of which the Good God Himself, through the Apostle assures us "surpasseth all understanding" - the peace that the Divine Ruler of the universe will no doubt establish between men and nations even at the cost of hells on earth before that peace be perfected.

neutral:
An account from a nurse at the State Hospital in Cleveland, Ohio, describes a period of significant stress. She recalled a previous August when she was in Detroit, noting that conditions at the hospital were very challenging. She attempted to recall teachings about enduring hardship and concluded that she needed to adjust her own perspective.

She began a specific spiritual practice, reciting 7 Paters, 7 Aves, and 7 Glories in honor of St. Joseph's experiences. She undertook this practice to gain strength to endure what she perceived as numerous difficulties and unfair treatments. After starting this nine-day prayer cycle (novena), conditions initially seemed to deteriorate, but she persisted with the practice, feeling compelled to continue.

At a point when the situation was at its most challenging, and she felt she lacked the necessary support to cope, the afternoon newspaper reported the appointment of a new Superintendent for the hospital, described as "a very fair and peaceful man."
styled: It comes from a nurse-friend in the State Hospital, Cleveland, Ohio. Here follows some of the letter: " .... You will remember last August when I was in Detroit how very hectic things were at the hospital. I tried to remem- ber everything religious and beautiful I was ever taught: I tried to think how the Saints prayed for crosses and sufferings; and decided (rightly), it was myself that needed adjusting. "So I started praying to St. Joseph, saying 7 Paters, 7 Aves and 7 Glories in honor of the seven great Sorrows and Joys which he had experienced on earth. I offered this for the grace to bear the little crosses and in- justices that were heaped upon me - at least seemingly so to me. Having started the novena things seemed to get worse but I kept on praying. I was afraid in fact to stop my prayers. "One day when things were at their worst and I could not feel I were receiving any additional necessary grace to manage under such conditions, the afternoon newspaper announced that a new Superintendent was appointed to the Hospital, 'a very fair and peaceful man ..

neutral: He is a peaceful and fair man. His arrival brought an immediate sense of calm. I had nearly lost hope of such a change and was struggling to cope with various difficulties. The other women later asked me, "What is special about March 19th?" They did not recall the date's particular significance to me. I perceived this event as a thoughtful and personal occurrence, as if it had been carefully planned to surprise me and boost my morale. To Miss Whelan, I wish well for you, your friends, and all your experiences, both challenges and joys. Ultimately, happiness in life is found in the hopes we cultivate.
styled: 1 "He is indeed a peaceful man and very fair. Peace seemed to settle all over the place almost immediately upon his arrival. I had almost given up hope of any thing like that, and was just begging for grace to bear patiently with the many annoyances, etc. when on Thursday morning March 19th he came to our office and told us it was his birthday I fairly yelled with glee : "March 19th! What a wonderful birthday" The other girls asked me afterwards, "What in the world is there about March 19th?" ... never remembering that it is always the Feast of St. Joseph "Dont you think that was a generous answer from dear St. Joseph? And so attentive and personal. It just looked as if He had been figuring during the whole novena how to spring his delicate little surprise on me and this way increase my faith and confidence. 11 Now Miss Whelan; God bless you and all your troubles as well as all your friends and all your joys and hopes .... After all the soul of hap- piness here in this old world consists in the hopes we foster.

neutral: It is increasingly understood that life's difficulties and challenges primarily serve to encourage self-reflection and improvement, guiding individuals toward sound judgment and highlighting the transient nature of worldly experiences—both joys and sorrows—thereby fostering an appreciation for enduring values. The following account provides a practical example with a few details. A few years ago, one morning, a crowd was waiting in the Monastery office. An elderly couple slowly rose from their seats, approached the desk, and asked in German if they could speak with the individual present. As they moved to another room, a distinct odor suggesting illness was detected. The nature of the illness was not clear until the elderly woman explained that her husband had cancer and could no longer work. She acted as the spokesperson and was completely open about the situation. Subsequently, a question was posed regarding their regular participation in religious rituals. The woman responded, "My husband is not a Catholic."
styled: This is one thing that I have been advising Catholics to do for years and I assure you, in many cases, with quite astonishing results. Let her do something in her own honest way; whatever she may deem most pleasing to the dear Lord - only that she be earnest about it and as confident as possible. The following might be a practical example with just a few de- tails. It happened a few years ago when on a certain morning there was quite a crown waiting here in the Monastery office, and old-look- ing couple slowly rose from their seats and approaching the desk, asked in German, if they could speak to me personally. As we started into another room, I smelled a cancer, though I was not certain what it was till the old lady told me that her husband had cancer and could not work any more. She was the spokesman, and made no secret of it what- ever. After a little I asked if they went to the holy Scraments reg- ularly. "My husband is not a Catholic," she answered. "Then, Mr.

neutral: N. was advised to act honestly in a way that would be pleasing to God. N. asked what he could do, explaining that he was raised Lutheran but had not practiced any religion for twenty years. The speaker responded that this was an inadequate approach, particularly when considering the speaker's definition of religion as "the science of our relationship with God and our neighbor, or our dependence on God and our neighbor." The speaker further stated that not practicing religion made the primary purpose of human creation as rational beings—namely, to know God, love Him, serve Him, and be happy with Him—a secondary matter. The speaker then advised N. that to please God, he should earnestly begin the process of saving his soul. The speaker concluded by noting that if N. was a Lutheran, he believed in Jesus Christ, and the speaker, as a Catholic, also believed in Jesus Christ. Therefore, both were Christians and, in some sense, brothers.
styled: N.," I said, "You do something in your own honest way to please the God God." "What could I do to please Him? I was raised a Lutheran but for twenty years I have practiced no religion." "It's a poor way to be, man;" I answered, "and especially if you take it as I define Religion. THE SCIENCE OF OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR - I might say - OF OUR DEPENDENCE ON GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR. To practice no religion is making a secondary matter of the primary purpose of our creation as rational beings, viz., TO KNOW GOD; that we may love Him and serve Him and be happy with Him. Now I'll tell you what you can do to please God. Just start and be earnest about saving your soul." "After all" I added, if you are a Lutheran, you believe in Jesus Christ. I believe in Him as a Catholic; so we are both Christians, and one way or other we must be brothers.

Then, seeing his readiness and his growing interest, I added: "And, I can assure you beforehand that inasmuch as you are earnest and hon- est in this matter - and prayerful at the same time -- in just so much will it become as clear to you as twice two are four, that you have your Christianity not directly from Jesus. Indirectly, yes; but directly and historically you have it (inasmuch as it is Christ- ianity) as said before, from the "Mother Church" - call yourself what you may. Like a drowning man who grasped my hand when only a youth, so now this poor patient seemed to hang on every word of hope. "Hist- orisch" he repeated, "Historically? That is true!

neutral: Eight weeks later, on a Sunday morning, a significant personal ceremony was performed for the individual. The following week, shortly after two women (one of whom had breast cancer) had been informed about the individual, the individual entered, appearing very happy, to announce his return to work the following Wednesday. This is one instance among many similar ones, estimated to be one of thousands. Such details are rarely shared. Although this case has been used to encourage several cancer patients, it has not been documented in writing previously. It is hoped this account is not tedious. Instead, it is intended to serve as an inspiration and example for many, applicable not only to cases of eczema and cancer, but to any difficulties encountered.
styled: Eight weeks later, Sunday morning, I gave him his First Holy Communion myself, quite unexpect- edly, and a week from the next day just as I had finished telling two ladies about him - one of them a Baptist with a cancerous breast - he, like rushed in thru the door, beaming all over to announce; " I just dropped in to tell you I am going back to work next Wednesday." The above is a single case from many similar - I think I'd be safe to say one out of thousands. I very seldom go into such details and while I've tried to encourage quite a few cancer patients by tell- ing them about this one, I have never written about it before. I hope it may not be a bore to anyone. On the contrary; may it be an inspir- ation and an example for many, not only for cases of eczema and cancer, but for whatever trouble may be met with. Our sad weakness today is our lack of faith and consequently, want of confidence in God.

You mentioned observing others who appear very happy. Indeed, such individuals are seen, and it is beneficial that they exist. However, many who seem happy, or try to appear so, scarcely understand what true happiness is. Many do not realize or consider, using their reasoning ability, that the essence of happiness for mortals—those who will eventually die—is hope. Children are generally happy because a normal child thinks, "Someday I'll be grown up." In this regard, one should emulate children: there is always a persistent hope, such as "I'll be a woman" or "I'll be a man."
