Today, five of us are going to the Immaculate Conception Monastery, located across from West Point, for our annual period of spiritual reflection. In other words, we will attempt once again to renew our spiritual commitment for another year.

Postscript: I reopened the envelope to add the following: The two sacred objects should be beneficial for Juda. The white particle is from the linen shroud of Mary of Agreda from Spain, who was exhumed after 249 years and found to be perfectly preserved. She was believed to have acted as a scribe for the Virgin Mary in the writing of 'The City of God,' a work presented as the Virgin Mary's autobiography.
styled: God bless you all-you and yours. Many thanks for your favor of a few weeks back. I hope you enjoyed your vacation-you and your Father. I started to fix up a big card-certificate for the Poor Souls to sent your Mother but was not certain about her first name, so let it go. I am not sure if I sent your Brother-in-law certificates. Its taken me so far pretty much to get acquainted with the work, etc here. Today five of us go up to the Immaculate Conception Monastery across from West Point, to make our annual retreat. In other words we'll try a- gain to be converted for another year. P.S .- had to open envelope to say -- The double relic ought to, ought to work something for little Juda. The white partical is of the linen shroud of Venerable Mary of Agreda, Spain, who after 249 years was ex- umed and found perfectly preserved. She had been our Bl. Mother's secretary in the writing "The City of God" autobiography .

neutral: Thank you for your letter of the 5th. I hope you are feeling better. Your indifference to wearing glasses seems unwarranted. I have always believed that glasses often improve the wearer's appearance, and I think this would likely be true for M.K. as well. I was surprised today to find I could read your letter clearly without glasses. I began seeing a chiropractor in July, receiving two treatments a week, and I feel generally improved. My chiropractor in Detroit, Dr. R. N. Schon, located at 10050 Connor Ave. (across Gratiot from the Airport), helped me significantly within one month, after years of unsuccessful treatment by medical doctors. He has successfully helped several patients I referred to him, even those with severe vision impairment. If you decide to consult him. Best regards. Do not worry.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of the 5th. I hope you are feeling better by this time. It seems to me your apathy regarding glasses is uncalled for ..... As long as I can remember I was inclined to think that, in many cases, glasses quite improved the appearance of the wearer. I would not doubt this could easily apply to M.K. Thanks be to God I was surprized at looking at your letter today, I could read it nicely without glasses. I started to a Chiropractor in July - two treatments a week and I am feeling improved all round. My Dr. in Detroit who put me on my feet in one month - after trying M.Ds. for years - was Dr. R. N. Schon ( Chiropractor) of 10050 Connor Ave. - just across Gratiot from the Air Port. He positively helped quite a few patients I sent him - even when almost blind. If you go to him .... Best regards! .God bless you now and be grateful to God .... Don't worry . . ..

neutral: A prominent human weakness appears to be a lack of appreciation for the numerous advantages that are consistently present. This tendency likely applies to all individuals. However, it is remarkably fortunate that, despite these failings, beneficial circumstances persist and support for our well-being continues to manifest in countless ways. Therefore, we should abandon complaining and lamenting over minor difficulties. These difficulties, while unpleasant for individuals and those who don't reflect deeply, are often underestimated in comparison to the significant long-term benefits available to those who endure challenges, and they can easily be transformed into considerable advantages.
styled: Humanity's outstanding weakness seems to be a thoughtless want of appreciation for the uncountable blessings by which Almighty God is always surrounding it; and no doubt the Krausmans as well as the Kennedys and the KCs are no exception in part of that old humanity. But how incalculably fortunate we are after all that the merciful God has patience with us and notwithstanding such failings has patience with us and still manifests His solicitude for our welfare in such a next-to infinite number of ways? Let us, therefore, shake off the spirit of complaint and lamentation over triffling difficulties that, even though unpleasant for nature and for the thoughtless, who make little of an eternal happiness awaiting those who persevere in, at least resignation to poverty and, which dif- ficulties can so easily be turned to such vast advantage.

neutral: Well wishes are extended to the recipient and their loved ones. Gratitude is expressed for recent assistance. It is hoped that the recipient will begin to live with a daily spiritual focus, disregarding the unreliability of others, particularly those who seek lasting happiness solely through worldly achievements. The only path to building such a foundation for true happiness is through a spiritual institution that provides abundant spiritual support and strength. Without such spiritual strength, it is difficult to achieve significant spiritual fulfillment in this life. Therefore, it is advisable not to become overly distressed when difficulties and setbacks, regardless of their origin, occur unexpectedly. In essence, becoming discouraged, whether by one's own shortcomings or those of others, is unproductive. It is beneficial to promptly acknowledge one's own imperfections and the inherent value of the abundant positive aspects of life, such as the air we breathe, the light we experience day and night, and all the wonders of the natural world.
styled: I hope you are well -- you and all your dear ones. Many thanks for your recent favors. I hope that someday you'll just wake up and start to live for God one day at a time, forgeting the fickleness of creatures -- especially if they figure on getting "a nest in this world where they can find true happiness." The only tree in which to find place to build such a nest, is the Church that pro- vides the material to build in untold graces from God -- all sizes -- with crosses for cement. Without such cement no one on earth can get very far with anything like getting a little taste of Heaven in this world. So let us not take it over serious when trials and disapoint- ments-from whatever source-catch us sleeping. In other words it never pays to become discouraged-at the faults of others or at our own. The sooner we come to realize our own stupidity and unworthyness of the blessings surrounding our whole life and in which we are immurged -- the air we breathe, the light of the heavens we enjoy by night and by day and all movies of visible creation.

neutral: Muriel Krausman, I hope you are well. I have been meaning to acknowledge your letter of April 4 for the past ten days. You may recall my situation during my visit in January. My current difficulty is responding to correspondence, rather than meeting with visitors. Therefore, please excuse the delay. I thank you nonetheless and keep you in my thoughts, even if I am unable to write. Thank you again.
styled: God bless you Miss Muriel Krausman. I hope you keep well. You've been on my mind for ten days, - wanting acknowledge your favor of Apr. 4th. Well you remember how it was with me when I was up there in January. It is not audiences with callers now but answering letters that is my problem. So please have charity to overlook tardiness, etc. I thank you just the same and pray for you even though I fail to write. Many thanks again.

neutral: Thank you for your message, which I have received and noted. I attempted to contact you by phone last Monday, but due to a busy period, I was unable to reach you afterwards. I also would have liked to speak with your father. I understand your difficulties, particularly the challenge of being without housing. However, there is no need to overemphasize this particular hardship. Consider the millions who, in addition to their other hardships, also lack sufficient food. Instead, one could choose to find a positive aspect in this necessity or emergency, accepting it without complaint, much like someone who, despite lacking a place to rest, expressed no regret.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor just read and noted. I tried to get you on the phone last Monday and then with so many calling and so much hustling, etc, I failed to get you afterwards. I certainly would like also to have spoken to your dear Father. Of course, I sympathise with you all in your problems, especially that of being without a roof over your heads. But why make so much of that after all? How many millions have in addition to that lamentation . hardly a bite of food to put in their mouth? Why not make a virtue of a necessity or emergency by offering it all to the Heavenly Father in union with the situation in which Jesus found Himself when not in com- plaint or lamentation He whispered to the youth who proposed to be His disciple: 11. .The Son of Man hath not where to lay his Head." But alas!

neutral: Thank you for your communication dated June 6th. I am pleased you are feeling reasonably well; I am also coping day by day. A significant religious service was held today, marking the 35th anniversary of Brother Maurice Joachim's first religious ceremony. This event took place in Superior, Wisconsin, in 1911. He is currently in St. Paul, Minnesota, with Right Reverend Brother Edward, who has returned from the Philippines. Edward was rescued on March 23rd of last year and is expected to return there soon. It appeared that Japanese forces had been planning a general massacre of the entire camp on that day, targeting over two thousand individuals, including two Bishops, 150 priests, and 125 nuns. The prisoners had been engaging in daily religious observances, including rosary prayers and Benediction ceremonies, and weekly Pontifical services, hoping for a rescue that would avoid drastic measures. Most of the prisoners were severely malnourished, to the point where they could barely walk. Approximately 20 individuals died from malnutrition.
styled: God bless you Muriel Krausman and many thanks for favor of June 6th. I am glad you are feelin not too bad-like myself-battling along one day at a time .... Had a solemn high Mass today - 35th anniversary of my Brother Maurice Joachim's first Mass Celebration. That was in Superior, Wisconsin 1911. Thanks be to God. He is in St. Paul, Minn. now with our Rt. Rev. Br. Edw'd back from the Philippines. Latter was rescued last year, March 23rd. Will be going back before long. It would seem that the Japps had been figuering on a general massacre of the whole camp - that day - over two thousand, including two Bishops, 150 priests and 125 nuns. They ( the prisoners) had been saying the holy rosary and having Bene- diction every day and Pontifical Mass every Sunday that they might be res- cued without anything too drastic. Most of the prisoners were so starved that they could hardly walk. About 20 actually died of malnutrition - starved. . . .

neutral: Thank you for your support and recent kindness. Although I have been feeling unwell for several weeks, my condition is not serious. I hope to recover soon so I can address the many tasks that need to be completed. I am also pleased to hear that circumstances appear to be improving for you. It is often the case that challenges resolve favorably when one maintains confidence.
styled: Many thanks for your prayer and for your kind favor just noted. Thank God, while i have been "half down" for several weeks, still its nothing possitively serious. Of course we are hoping it will clear up so that I be able to do a little more toward so much waiting to be done. Thank the Lord too: I am glad things seems brightening up for you and yours. It always comes right if only we have a little trustful confidence in the good God and our Blessed Mother Mary Immaculate.

neutral: The author decided to write immediately. Their health has recovered, with few remaining effects from the ptomaine poisoning experienced two months ago. Greetings were extended to the recipient's father, Jack, and all mutual friends, and the author encouraged the recipient to continue seeking guidance.
styled: This time I just thought "I'll write at once." Yes, thank God, my health has adjusted itself again so that hardly feel any effects of my dose of ptomane of two months ago .... Best regards to your Father, to Jack, and all our friends, and keep pleading for God's holy guidance.

neutral: I hope you are well. Thank you for the kind remembrance on October 25th. I am grateful for my excellent health at 77 years old. My steps are naturally slowing down, as is to be expected. Next week, on the 10th, my Brother M. J. Ex- will celebrate his 80th birthday. I hope we are guided to live well and be a positive influence, especially in our final days.
styled: I hope you keep well. Many thanks for kind remembrance for Oct. 25th. Thanks be to God for the quite excellent He gives me at 77. Naturally of course my steps are slowing down as to quite to be expected. Next week (10th) my Rev. Brother M. J. Ex- to celebrate his 80th birth-day. Please pray that we be guided so as to please God to the end. Edify - at least in our last days ...

neutral: The welcome letter has been read, prompting an immediate reply to avoid delay. A two-week stay occurred at St. Joseph Hospital in Fort Wayne during June. The individual has since returned to St. Felix and reports feeling well. Worry is identified as a common challenge or vulnerability requiring vigilance. Instead of succumbing to this weakness, cultivating confidence is beneficial. This can be achieved through patience and by expressing gratitude in advance for what is deemed most suitable. Support will be offered for your intentions.
styled: I just finished reading your welcome letter and thought I'd answer it at once before overlooking. I was in St. Joseph Hospi- tal, Ft. Wayne for two weeks but that was in June and I am back to St. Felix and feeling fine. Deo Gratias. One trouble or weakness that we all have to guard against is worry . Instead of this weakness we do well to foster confidence in God. This we can do by not only patience, but by thanking God ahead of time for whatever He see best for us ... . We'll pray for your intentions too.

neutral: Thank you for your message received yesterday. It is good to hear that things are progressing well. I hope your niece recovers from her illness. Please take care of yourself and try to reduce your anxiety regarding your own health and the health of others. I am feeling well again, and I hope you will soon be able to say the same. Before putting your letter aside and potentially forgetting its contents, I had intended to send a brief note, but that attempt was unsuccessful.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of yesterday - Glad things are coming on favorably. Hope the your tiny niece shakes off that whooping, etc. Keep well yourself but shake off some of that anxiety about your and others' health. Thank God I am feeling fine again. Hope you can shortly say the same. Before laying your letter aside and then forgetting I tho't I'd just drop you a card - then spoild it. -

neutral: Your recent communication has been received and noted. I am sending you the certificate for Helen Mayland; based on your letter, I believe she particularly needs it. While I catch up on my correspondence, please extend my best regards to everyone, especially your father. I share your hope that his health and spirits will improve with the warmer spring weather, and that his general circumstances will become more favorable. I almost forgot to congratulate you on your success in February. Please excuse the hurried and brief nature of this message. I hope to communicate more thoroughly in the future.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor just Rec'd, noted. I am sending you the Cert. for Helen Mayland. I think she needs it especially from your letter. In the mean time and till I get up a little better with my correspondence, best regards and God holy blessing to all the others - your dear Father especially. I do hope with you, that with the warmer Spring his health and spirits bloom up again and that things in general pick up in his favor. I almost forgot to congratulate you on your February suc- cess, etc. Deo gratias. Please pardon haste and brevity. Hope for improvement in future.

neutral: The communication congratulates Miss M. Krausman on what appears to be an opportunity for advancement. It expresses hope that the principle "a change of work is as good as a rest" will apply to her situation. It is suggested that she should easily be able to convince her current supervisor of the appropriateness of accepting the offer. She is also advised to express gratitude for the supervisor's favorable attitude towards her as an employee, should the promotion be successful. The writer also notes an improved outlook for her father, particularly concerning her uncle's return to his faith community. The writer apologizes for frequently failing to respond to her communications, stating that answering all correspondence would be overwhelming.
styled: God bless you Miss M. Krausman; you and yours. I am inclined to congratulate you on what seems to be an opportunity of advance- ment. At all events, the old saying: "A change of work is as good as a rest," I hope will apply here in your case. It seems to me that you ought easily be able to convince your present Foreman of the propriety of your accepting the offer of advancement. At the same time show your gratitude his favorable attitude toward your- self as an amployee, i.e., in case you do succeed in the desired promotion. Thanks be to God too for the improved outlook for your dear Father, especially in regard to your Uncle coming back to the source of spiritual strength, our Holy Mother the Church. Deo Gr. I'm sure you will not take it amiss that I so often fail to answer your favors. If I had to answer them all - all my letters I'd be liable to at least lose my ballance.

neutral: M. does not exhibit what is considered a fundamental commitment. The situation calls for patience, acceptance, and waiting. In the interim, there is a hope for increased conviction and trust, until worldly matters are viewed as secondary. This might then enable authentic action and the honest expression of thoughts and feelings.
styled: Evidently M. does not love God as is the first duty of every one of us - to try to love Him .... What's to be done? We'll simply have to have patience, humble ourselves and wait .... Praying in meantime that the Good God increase our faith and confidence in Him till we can appreciate creatures as of secondary importance. Then possibly it will come natural for us to act naturally and tell what's honestly in our minds and hearts.

neutral:
Thank you for your message dated the 5th, which I have just read. I have noted the enrollments as requested. Additionally, a special service was held with the intention of seeking guidance for you and your friends.

Instead of worrying, it is better to reflect on the numerous remarkable events and processes that have led to our existence and sustained us thus far, despite our errors, poor judgment, and moral failings. The care shown for our well-being, both in the present and for the future, is consistently more apparent than that of even the most loving parents and friends.

We should always remember the profound teaching, which serves as both a philosophical warning and a benevolent invitation: "Prioritize what is fundamentally important." Consequently, patience is necessary. A guiding force works through our efforts, provided we do not disrupt its overarching designs with our own.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of the 5th, just noted. I noted the enrollments as requested - also the special holy Mass in honor of the Holy Ghost for your guidance and that of your friends. .Why should we worry? Why not rather ponder on the wonderful and innumerable manifestations whereby God in wis- dom and power and mercy has brought us into existence and thus far preserved us - notwithstanding our waywardness, our stupidity and our sinfulness. Is not His solicitude for our happiness - even temporal as well as eternal more manifest at every turn than that of all most loving parents and other friends? O if we would but keep in mind at all times the sweet words of our dear Lord - at once a philophic admonition and a paternally loving invitation - "Seek ye, therefore, first the Kingdom of God .... " Patience therefore, "God condescends to use our powers, if we don't spoil His plans by ours."

neutral: Thank you for your kind thoughts. Despite having several minor illnesses in recent months, my health has generally been good. However, today I feel a significant cold coming on. I am pleased to hear of your father's success in selling the property, which had been on the market for a long time. I hope his health, as well as M's, improves quickly. Regardless of future events, we should strive to accept the situation. Regarding my receipt of your letters, please do not worry. For several years, I have not been able to read most of my letters, let alone answer them. I am unsure what I would do without Jerome or someone to assist me. In fact, I have been considering for some time delegating all letter-answering to someone else, to be arranged by the Guardian. Please keep me in your thoughts regarding this decision. I deeply sympathize with the immense struggles faced by so many impoverished people in the world.
styled: Many thanks for your kind remembrances and prayers. Thanks be to God, though I've had several colds etc. these past months. My health has been good. Today however a real "cold" seems trying to get hold on me .... Deo Gr. Of course I was - am - pleased to know of your dear Father's success in selling that property, so long on the market, etc. We pray his health - as well as M's improve speedily. Whatever comes, however, let us try at least to be re- signed . As to my reception of your letters, please do not worry. For several years I have not been able to even read the majority of my letters to say nothing of answering them. I hardly know what I would have to do if I had no Fr. Jerome or some one to substitute him. In fact I have been thinking for some time of leaving the answering of all letters to some one else - provided by the Rev. Fr. Guardian. Please say a prayer for my guidance in this regard too. I surely do sympathize with so many poor people in the world, - struggle, struggle, Str.

neutral: Wishing you, Philip, and everyone else well. I am pleased to hear you are well. You consistently appear to be in good health there. I have been at this location since last April. It is an ideal place, with 18 novices whose ages range from approximately 17 to 23. I hope Philip remains well. Julius is currently in Tucson. He expects to travel to the Guam Missions in January. There has been discussion about our group acquiring a location in Tucson.
styled: God bless you His lamb with Philip and all the rest. I am glad you are well. You always seem well out there. I have been here since last April. Thanks be to God it is quite an ideal place - 18 novices. The youngest about 17 ... to 23. Hope philip keeps well. Our Fr. Julius is down there some where in Tucson. He expects to go in Jan- uary to the Guam Missions. There has been some talk of our getting a place in Tucson.

neutral: Best wishes to you, Miss Lamb, and your family. It was good to hear from you and about Philip. I hope the operation and its preparation are not too serious. Regardless, try to avoid anxiety and remain confident.
styled: God bless you Miss Lamb - you and yours. Glad to hear from you - and about Philip. I hope that operation - and preparation therefor, may be not too serious. At all events try and avoid anxiety - and trust in our Dear Lord for Every thing.

neutral: Thank you, Miss Krausman, for your message from a few weeks ago. I had intended to write for Christmas, but it became impossible. I am pleased to learn that despite the many difficulties your loved ones experience, the overall situation appears to be improving.
styled: God bless you Miss Krausman. Many thanks for your favor of some weeks past - I wanted to write you for Christmas but that be- came just impossible. I am glad to learn that notwithstanding the many difficulties your dear ones meet with, still in general things seem to improve anyhow.

neutral: Thank you for your communication of November 24th. It is hoped that Philip's arm will recover completely. The favorable conditions on your end are noted, with hope for their continuation. Best wishes for the upcoming season. The requested picture is being mailed. Best regards to all.
styled: And many thanks for favor of Nov. 24th Please God - . Philip's arm will be all okay. I am so pleased that you find things so favorable over there. Thank God. Hope it con- tinues so God's blessing for the holy season so near. I am mailing picture as requested. God bless you all.

neutral:
It is advisable to remain courageous and confident, recognizing that events are guided by an underlying order, even when its immediate effects are not apparent. Muriel has been re-enrolled, and additional individuals have also been enrolled. We hope for the best outcome. It is important to maintain confidence and accept whatever comes with a positive outlook.

Regarding Muriel: You have not called. Your letter from last Friday was only read this afternoon. The urgency concerning your sister and young niece was sufficient to warrant a call to Huntington 210. I would have called you, but I did not have permission. We will keep them in our thoughts; however, in urgent situations, it is considered practical to enroll even by telephone, with the hope that this expedited process will be acceptable. Please remain courageous.
styled: Take courage! Trust in God! His providence govems all things sweetly, even tho we cannot see it immediately. That is where we must have faith and confidence! Muriel has been enrolled once again and also the Poor Souls. God love you! We will pray for the best. Have confidence! Thank God ahead of time whatever He sends. P.S. Please Miss Muriel: God bless you and yours. You have never called up. (?) I only this P.M. got to read your letter of last Friday. And surely there was urgency enough about your sister and little niece to call Hunt- ington 210. I would have called you but I had no permis'n F.S. We'll pray for them of course; but in such urgent cases we find it practical even by telephone to enroll - hoping of course that the good God show His Mercy and give sanction to our presuming. God bless you now and keep courage.

neutral:
Miss Muriel Krausman,

Things have improved in several aspects, particularly concerning Mary Jane. However, I am concerned about the idea of a second operation. I am aware of multiple instances where a doctor's efforts at improvement have proven fatal. Approximately 20 years ago, Thomas Ryan of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, was deemed beyond hope of an operation. His in-laws contacted us from St. Rose Parish in Detroit, and he was included in a support effort. To their astonishment, he went back to work without any operation. After two weeks of work, doctors persuaded him to complete X-ray treatment. The same Thomas Ryan then suffered a relapse and died. I have known of several such cases. I hope doctors find further surgery unnecessary. A similar case is recounted in the "life" of Padre Pio, a stigmatic. A woman had a hopeless prognosis for cancer. She and her husband went to Padre Pio, and she was cured.
styled: God bless you Miss Muriel Krausman. Thanks be to God things have brightened in a number of ways, especially in relation with poor little Mary Jane. Indeed, thanks be to God. However, I rather - I do not like that idea of a second O. I know of more than one such "Miracles" where the doctor's efforts at improve- ment has turned fatal. About 20 yrs. back a certain Thomas Ryan of Pittsburgh, Penn. was passed all hope of operation. His in-laws phoned from St. Rose Parish Detroit and we enrolled him ... To their astonishment he went back to work without any operation. After two weeks work, the doctors induced him to go finish up on the X.R. Same T.R .-- Same T. Ryan got a relapse and died. I have known of several such cases. Be grateful to God, therefore, and attribute miracles to whom they due. I hope Drs. find further surgery uncalled for. There is a similar case related in the "life" of our stigmatic - P. Pio. A certain poor, good woman was quite hopeless with can- cer. She and her Husband went to Padre Pio and she was cured.

neutral:
I received your letter of August 29th. While I sympathize with your many difficulties, I nevertheless congratulate you on these experiences. These experiences are viewed as a form of discipline or a test for those who are favored, even though many might consider them misfortunes. If we demonstrate good intentions and accept the challenges that come our way with gratitude, we can be sure that eventually these will prove to have been beneficial outcomes.

I had hoped for some time that my young friend Philip might pursue a special calling or career path. However, that is a personal matter and often appears to be a very sensitive issue. I hope, of course, that he genuinely appreciates his spiritual beliefs. Theoretically, this begins with an understanding of fundamental spiritual principles, such as the concept of a divine presence within individuals. The other two principles are hope, which is considered essential for happiness in this world, and charity (love), which is seen as the ultimate fulfillment and reward.
styled: I just came across your favor of Aug. 29th on the con- viction that: "Whom the Lord loveth He Chastened", and even while I surely sympathize with you, in your so many difficulties, I do, nevertheless congratulate you on all these experiences that the crazy world considers such mis- forrtunes. If we only try to show the dear Lord a good will and ask Him for grateful resignation to the crosses He sends or permits to come our way, we may be sure that sooner or later they will turn out to have been just so many bless- ings,in disguise. I hoped for quite a time that my "little boy-friend Philip" might have a vocation to some thing special. That, however is a personal problem and in many cases seems to be a very delicate question. I hope of course, that he be earnestly appreciative of the holy Faith - theoretically first of the outstanding "Trace of the Trinity in our souls. The other two, hope and being essentially one with it - hope the soul of happiness in this world, charity, the life and crown of everlasting glory. . . . .

neutral: Hello Miss Beatrice Lamb. I am pleased to hear from you, and I hope you are well. I hope Sol. can catch up with our correspondence. I also hope Philip, our former young acquaintance, is keeping well. It is important to remember that on Earth, there is no actual Heaven, and that those who are loved often experience discipline.
styled: God bless you Miss Beatrice Lamb. Glad to hear from you. I hope you keep well. Please say a prayer that poor Fr. Sol. catch up with out cor- respondence. - With you and yours Hope our one-time little boy-friend Philip is keeping well .... .. .... God to remember that on this star (earth) that we are living on, there is no real Heaven - and that : "Whom the Lord loveth, He Chasteneth" . . ·

neutral: Thank you for your practical assistance to me, an individual who is rapidly aging. We value mutual assistance, and since we hold no personal property, our actions within the community are performed for the collective good. This often leads to reciprocal benefits, frequently in various forms. This principle of reciprocity was illustrated a few years ago by Rufin, who, while treating my other foot, expanded on my observation that helping others avoid effort benefits oneself, by stating that one gains at least double the benefit. Therefore, I hope you receive significant benefits for your contributions to Francis, myself, and the entire community. I also extend my gratitude for the medicine sent, the personal letters, and other items.
styled: God bless you and yours. While I feel it really a privilege to help one another and to save our neighbor a step whoever he be, I want to thank you for your practical assistance to this - I was going to say - poor old sinner. -- rapidly getting old at least. After all, since we have nothing of our own, what we do, in the order especially, we do for the community and in a way it is sure to come back so us again - in many cases it comes back in many ways. As V. Br. Rufin exclaimed when he was treating my other foot a few years ago, and I remarked: "Every time you save your neighbor a step you gain one for yourself" - "You gain at least two steps for yourself .. " So I hope you gain many favors for what you do for Br. Francis and myself and the whole community. Many thanks too for the medicine forwarded and the per- sonal letters, etc.

neutral: If any friends inquire, please inform them that I am improving and thankful for this restful contrast after nearly forty years, including over 18 years in Detroit. Hopefully, I will be well before long and possibly return to my previous activities. My best wishes to you, Francis, and all the brothers, novices, and the community.
styled: In case any of my friends ask - just cell them I am improving and thankful for such a restful contrast after nearly forty years - over 18 years in Detroit. God willing, I hope to be well be- fore long and possibly back "at the old stand. " .... God bless you again and Br. Francis too and all the brothers and novices and. .. community ... Praised se Jesus!

neutral: The passage observes that Mary encourages individuals to seek confidence and repentance, while also appealing to Jesus for mercy and clemency. The Provincial stated last Wednesday that they would return to Detroit together. He has been working on the Messenger, and it is expected they will be leaving shortly, possibly on Tuesday or Wednesday. The exact departure time is not yet known. Regards are extended to Francis and all other associates.
styled: secrets no doubt, as you surely have seen from "The Mystical City of God," is the fact that our Blessed Mother Mary is always coaching poor sinners on the one hand to confidence and penance, and on the other Jesus our Lord to have mercy and spare. P.S. Talking with Father Provincial last Wednesday he said we'd go back to Detroit together. He has been working on the Messenger and I think very probably we will be leaving here shortly - possibly Tuesday or Wednesday. I cannot say just when. God bless you again. Very best regards to V. Bro. Francis and to all our Dear ones.

neutral: It is difficult to determine which job or service is most advantageous, with the possible exception of the sacristan's role. Regardless, the role of a porter, despite its inherent risks, offers numerous benefits, provided one maintains a positive attitude and utilizes available support. Naturally, the work can sometimes become monotonous and extremely tedious, to the point of exhaustion. However, during such times, it is helpful to remember that even in moments of extreme personal hardship, one can still demonstrate patience and offer comfort to others, including those who may be adversarial, without discrimination. It is challenging to adequately express gratitude for such an opportunity and the privileged status it confers, even within contexts traditionally associated with humility or service. One feels profound gratitude for the immense patience shown towards individuals.
styled: To whatever office or service one may turn to it is not easy to say just which is the more privileged - possibly ex- cepting that of sacristan. At all events that of por- ter, even though fraught with dangers, has many ad- vantages, if only we be of good will and cooperate with the graces never failing on God's part and our B1. Mother. Sometimes of course it becomes monotonous and extremely boring, till one is neary colapsing; but in such cases it helps to remember that even when Jesus was about to fall the third time He patiently con- soled the women-folks and children of His persecutors, making no exceptions. How can we ever be grateful as we ought to be for such a vocation - to such privileg- ed positions - even in the Seraphic Order of the Poverello of Asissi? ... Thanks be to God that He .. One of the has such divine patience with us.

neutral: I received your card a few days ago and thank you for it, as well as for the accompanying personal letters. Further details regarding appreciation will be provided below, if I can locate them. Solanus caused the most difficulty during my time at St. Bonaventure's; it was fortunate that I only had to contend with one such individual. Yesterday, we held a celebration in honor of Gabriel. The Provincial gave him a farewell, commending his work as 'becoming quite proficient as a linotypist' and expressing gratitude for his contributions on behalf of the entire Province. I immediately thought of you and your message to him, which he appeared to appreciate. This also brought to mind the significant opportunity we have to contribute to the general welfare through small actions, especially within a communal organization, with each individual performing their role without regard for the specific nature of the task.
styled: God bless you and yours, - including that poor sinner Solanus, who more than anyone else gave me trouble as long as I was in St. Bonaventure's - Isent it a mercy that we really need examine only one "pair of conscience"! Well I received your card a few days ago and thank you for the same as well as for the personal letters therewith. Intimation of further appreciation below, if I can find it for you. We had quite a celebration yesterday of Br. Gabriel's nameday. Father Provincial gave him a nice little "sendoff", praising his work as, "becoming quite proficient as a linotypest" and thanking him for his work in the name of the entire Province, etc. I thought of you rightaway and of your message to him, which he seemed to quite appreciate. At the same time something came to my mind of our ineffable privilege in doing the little things we are able to do for the general welfare - most especially in a religious com- munity - each one in his place without thought or distinction as to what the work may be.

neutral: The bottle you inquired about contains water sourced from Lourdes. It is intended for use in situations of illness. It was sent directly from the Lourdes site. There is no need to be concerned about the absence of this item or any other item located in Cell #5. I have frequently considered disposing of the entire collection of items.
styled: The "bottle in the corner" you asked about is water from Lourdes. Use it in case of sickness, etc. It was sent me from the Shrine directly. . Do not worry about missing this or what piece of junk in Cell #5. I've often figured on how to rid myself of the whole collection.

neutral: I hope you are doing well. I have been in this new, important assignment for just a week. Tomorrow marks the forty-first anniversary of my first ordination service, and the day after that, the 21st anniversary of my arrival from Our Lady of Angels in Harlem back to St. Bonaventures in 1924. We should be grateful for so many benefits and opportunities. I hope you did not find the room that was my home for so long in too much disarray. I am concerned I left you a difficult task when I asked you to pack and send items here that would be useless to others but somewhat convenient for me. I am unsure if I brought a trunk from Harlem twenty years ago. If I did, it must have been worth very little, so any available box you find would work, perhaps even better than a trunk. The "Letters" box on top of the "wardrobe" containing Fr. Edward's letters is important.
styled: God bless you and yours. I hope you keep well. Thanks be to God, I am here in this new assignment of privileged duty just a week. Tomorrow will be the forty-first anniversary of my first Holy Mass, Deo Gratias -and the next day the 21st of my ar- rival from Harlem, Our Lady of Angels, back to St. Bonaventures - 1924. How grateful we ought to be for so many graces and privileges. Praised be God in all His works and ways! Now I hope you have not found that middle cell that succored me so long in too hopeless disorder. I rather fear having left you a difficult job when I asked you to pack up and forward things hither, that would be of no use to any one else and might be of quite a little convenience to me. I am not certain if I brought a trunk with me from Harlem twenty years ago. If I did, it must have been worth next to nothing, so any old box you might find would do, perhaps better than a trunk. The "Letters" box on top of the "wardrobe" containing Fr. Edward's letters are good.

neutral: Other items are not important. I would like to have the few unfinished pieces in the folder next to the desk, if they have not been discarded. Also, the brief statement on modesty that was being considered for the office. I had intended to bring it for the superior's approval, but he was not available. It was then neglected, and I subsequently traveled West. I hope to have more time for such matters here at St. Michael's, although so far, due to getting acquainted and other tasks, I have not had much spare time. However, I have gotten more sleep this past week than perhaps in the three weeks before my arrival. I am unsure what to do with any photos or pictures of Solanus or the others; you may burn them if you wish. However, I would like to have the framed photo of our golden jubilee, specifically the one with all the grandchildren. Some of them are grandparents now themselves. I will conclude now. I have nothing further to add. My best regards.
styled: The others are not important. Those few unfinished pieces in the cliper on the side next to the desk, I would like to have - if you've not thrown them away. Also that little prayer on modesty that we were figering on having in the office. I started over to bring it for Fr. Provincial's approval but he was not in and then it was neglected and I went off West. I hope to get a little more time for such things here at St. Michael's, although so far - getting aquainted, etc. - I've not had much surplus time. One thing, however, I've taken a little more sleep under the great archangel's wings this past week then perhaps in three weeks before my arrival. Any photos or pictures of Fr. Solanus or the others I hardly know what I should do with them: so you may burn them if you wish. However I , would like to have the one of our golden jubilee that is framed viz. the one with all the little grandchildren. Some of them are grandparents now themselves. Well I guess I'd better come to a conclusion. Otherwise -- ?? Best regards to Br.

neutral: I had intended to send you the enclosed card last Sunday before traveling to Yonkers for a special service and the Labor Day Parish reunion the following day. However, due to time constraints, I rushed to catch my train without mailing it. The day and celebration were very pleasant. Before going to the Hall, I made a brief visit and offered some prayers, as I was departing Monday night. A young Jack Kelly (now past middle age) took me to Brooklyn Bridge and into the subway. I do not have time to provide further details. Since I began writing this letter-card, your letter and package have arrived. Many thanks again. There are one or two items I have not yet found that would be quite beneficial here: some Solanus stamps and a dater. The former especially would help considerably. Many thanks again, and best wishes to all.
styled: God bless you again. I wanted to send you the inclosed card last Sunday before going to Yonkers for the High Mass next day -- and Labor-day Parish reunion. Time was urgent, however, and so without getting it off I made hast(e) to catch a train, etc. Thank God; we had quite an ideal day and celebration. I made a little visit before going down to the Hall, as I was leaving Monday night and offered a few prayers -- pater and Aves -- in honor of our holy Guardians and especially of St. Raphael --- A young Jack Kelly ( ... now past middle age) took me clear to Brooklyn Bridge and into the subway ... Thanks to God -- and His blessed messengers the angels. Time refuses me to give more details. Since starting this letter-card -- your letter and package came in. Many thanks again. Now one or two things I've not as yet found, that would be of quite an advantage here -- one or two of those Fr. Solanus stamps and a dater of some kind. The former especially would help considerably. Many thanks again and God's blessing and best wishes to all.

neutral: The original of this document is being sent to Miss Lyke. It is hoped this will help resolve the situation; however, the exact nature of her complaint is unclear. Perhaps she expected a personal acknowledgment rather than a standardized one. Numerous checks have been received from both St. Felix and St. Michael's, making it difficult to recall specific details related to minor discrepancies. It is recalled that during the nine or ten months at St. Michael's, there was rarely a time without letters requiring acknowledgment, even when this work extended past midnight. The workload was manageable, and health remained good. Occasionally, the effort felt overwhelming, leading to thoughts of discontinuing the work. It is possible she will write again. However, if her check was returned, it should be clear that the matter is resolved.
styled: I am sending the original of this carbon to Miss Lyke. I hope it may smoothe the thing off in a manner; though I am not just clear as to what she really com- plains about. Perhaps she expected a personal acknow- ledgement of somekind more than just a rubber-stamp. I've been getting so many cheques - bothe here at St. Felix and at St. Michael's that I would have to posess an extraordinary memory to recollect particulars like this little mixup might require. One thing I do remem- ber, that during the nine or ten months I was at St. Michael's it was very seldom, if ever, that I was with- out letters to acknowledge, even though I sometimes worked on them till after min-night. God be praised, however, I did not mind it and my health kept fine. Seomtimes my two faithful ole sentinels would threaten to go on strike and to quiet them down I felt I'd have to give it up. Well she will possibly writ again. Afer all if she got her check back, she ought to know that things were oky .. ?

neutral: We will hope for the best and seek guidance. In the meantime, we hope for each other's transformation until a time when we no longer commit wrongdoings and can transition to an eternal state, truly transformed. We will express joy while awaiting that desired day, recognizing the supreme universal force and honoring it forever.
styled: We'll hope for the best anyhow and pray for the dear Lord's gentle guidence. Praying in the mean time for one anothers' conversion - till some day we can sin no more and the good angels will be able to bear us off to the eternity; forever - really and truly CONVERTED, WE'LL sing on withe angels awaiting that blessed day: 110 all ye works of the Lord bless the Lord, Praise and exalt Him above all forever."

neutral: Thank you very much for your assistance with the office work over the past few years, and also for sending me numerous packages since I moved East. This year, we held a two-week program of reflection at a facility known as the Immaculate Conception Monastery. Fortunately, the weather was ideal, and the location was outstanding. Bonaventure and the others send their best wishes. My shins and other minor issues are recovering well; please inform Rufin not to trouble me significantly. I am relieved that I am trying to maintain a clear conscience, aiming for a state at least as good as the current condition of my shins.
styled: Many, many thanks for your helping in the good work in office these last few years, and again for your sending me those things - package after package - since I came East. We had our Retreat this year -- last two weeks -- in the Immaculate Conception Monastery. Thanks be to God it was ideal weather and the location could hardly be surpased. Bonaventure and all send best wishes. Brother . . my shins etc. are really doing fine; Tell Br. Rufin bother me very little. Thank God . . . Am trying to keep my conscience at least as good as the same old shins .

neutral:
Thank you for your assistance last week. I am sending you a few of the requested badges. We haven't received any recently. The person in Cleveland, who had been very active in that area for some years, wrote in October that she could not continue. Miss Modock also plans to withdraw from her current activities and will likely be unable to continue. However, we can share them as long as we have them. We appreciate the supply we have received and hope it can continue.

Leo, our equipment for the association's service activities is rather outdated. Could you see if Mr. Lambert could obtain an additional loose-leaf system, similar to the one you and Rufin (or someone else) introduced about a year ago? We would appreciate it for the new year. In the meantime, we will continue to manage and do what we can despite the limitations of our old equipment.

Best wishes.
styled: Many thanks for favors last week. . Am sending you a few of the badges asked for. We've not been receiving any of late. The sister in Cleve- land so active in that line for some years wrote in October that she ... could not continue. Miss Modock also hopes to go to the convent ... can probably not continue. O well as long as we have them we can share. After all it was the dear Lord sent them so far and if it please Him we hope the beautiful sup- ply may continue. Dear Brother Leo, our equipment here for Ser Mass Association is rather behind time. Will you see if Fr. Lambert could muster an extra loose- leaf outfit - as you and Bro. Rufin or someone else introduced a year or so ago. We would ap- preciate it for the new year. In the meantime we'll drill along and do what we can under handi- cap of old "machinery" etc. - always ocourse praying for one anothers final conversion. Praised be Jesus Christ. Best wishes and happy Feast of the Immaculate Conception.

neutral:
I received your letter and will be pleased to join you and your friends in Meldrom in offering support for Granma Kauffman. I regret not knowing about her condition before she was hospitalized.

A diluted solution of creolin, using 2 to 4 tablespoonfuls per pint of water, will provide significant relief by lightly sponging the affected areas once every two to three hours, or every four to five hours, or less frequently. Several years ago, before I became familiar with creolin, I applied the undiluted substance to various areas. Within a couple of minutes, I began to fear I had made a serious error, as it caused a burning sensation. It served as a valuable lesson, causing no injury. Few medical professionals seem aware of this simple remedy.

I have been concerned about a significant issue for over a year. I have discussed it with a Provincial and several religious acquaintances, seeking their support and advice. I began writing to F. several months ago.
styled: I just received your charitable letter and will be pleased to juin with yourself and your friends across Meldrom in praying for poor dear little "Granma Kauffman. Sorry I did not know of her trouble before she went to the hospital . . . Diluted creolin, say 2 to 4 tablespoonfuls to a pint of water will give wonerful relief by simply sponging the parts effected once over, every two or three hours. or every 4 or 5 or more hours. Several years ago, before I got acquainte with mistress creoin, I applied the pure stuff to quite some patches of No. i's area and very shortly - for a couple of minutes - I began to rather fear I'd possible made a fearful mistake - It made thins so hot for me. It was a good lesson without the least injury. Few doctors seem to know about this remedy; so simple != Now; Dear Br. Leo: I've had a big problem on my mind for over a year. - have spoken about it to Fr. Provincial and to sev- eral religious friends, asking their prayers, etc. I started months ago to write F.

neutral: Work on provincial details is ongoing. Producing significant written communications requires study and practice. Today, ten of the sixteen letters received were personal, consuming considerable time and making task management challenging. Approximately twelve letters are received daily on average. In Blase's absence, and at other times, Raphael handles many letters concerning the Seraphic Mass Association. Support for ongoing work is appreciated. Best regards are extended to all Novices, Candidates, everyone in the Monastery, and their parents and other family members. By contributing to the success of good works and undertakings, novices and candidates can demonstrate their commitment to the practical aspects of their order from the outset.
styled: Provincial particulars about and am still trying to get it off. Of course it is not easy to write important lines of any kind without study and practice, at least for me . To-day of sixteen letters received there were ten personals, which leaves me very little time, so that often it is not easy to what to do. On an average there about a dozen letter per day. In Father Blase's absence - otherwise too - Brother Raphael attends to many of the letters we get here concerning the Ser. Mass Assoc'n. So please pray . Best regard and God's blessing to all the Novices and Candidate & of course all in the Monastery and your dear Parents, etc. Just herein, viz, in praying for success of good works and undertakings the novices and candidates can fall in line as practical religions and Capuchins before-hand.

neutral: Your generous donation to the Capuchin Foreign Missions is appreciated. The missionaries will keep your well-being in their thoughts. Certificates of enrollment are being sent to you in a separate mailing.
styled: I WISH TO THANK YOU SINCERELY FOR YOUR KIND AND GENEROUS ALMS TO THE CAPUCHIN FOREIGN MISSIONS. I AM SURE THAT THE PRAYERS OF THE MISSIONARIES WILL, ASCEND TO THE THRONE OF GOD FOR YOUR WELFARE. UNDER SEPARATE COVER I AM MAILING YOU THE CER- TIFICATES OF ENROLLMENT, WHICH I TRUST YOU WILL LIKE.

neutral: Thank you and your young associates—novices and candidates—for your charitable contribution on the occasion of my name-day. We hope they all encourage the pursuit of callings to service, to increase globally within every order, society, and aspect of Catholic action. In doing so, they will be engaging in missionary work and securing their own calling to service, as well as their continued dedication to it. Anyone who appropriately values their calling, and is duly grateful, will support the increase of further callings to service. We have a very promising group of male candidates, including a very carefree, happy Black candidate.
styled: Just a line to thank you and your young associates -- novices and candidates -- for your charitable remen- brance for my privileged name-day. We hope and pray they all pray for vocations; to to multiply all over the world - in every order and every society and phase of Catholic action. Thus they will at once be doing real missionary work and insuring their own holy vocation - and perseverance therein. For no one who appreciates his vocation, as such a grace deserves, and is duly gratefull will fail to pray for a multiplication of further vocations. Thank God we have a very promising boquet of brother-candidates - including a very care-free, happy darky.

neutral: I am enclosing the ticket I mentioned yesterday when I asked for Judge Maher. I was pleased that you answered. I have been imposing on the goodwill of Judge Monahan and Judge Murphy, and they are likely to refuse further assistance to me and my friends soon. I hope you will be able to assist us again this time.
styled: God bless you and yours. Inclosed herewith I am sending you the ticket of which I spoke to you yesterday when I asked for Judge Maher. In a way I was pleased rather that you answered. I've been imposing on the good nature of both Judge Monahan and Judge Murphy that they are liable to throw me out some of these days with my unfortunate friends .. Trusting that they still have a heart, I hope you'll be able to take care of us this time too. .... God bless the court and all concerned.

neutral: The speaker intends to keep the recipients in mind during a significant observance tomorrow. The speaker asks the recipients to express the speaker's profound gratitude for the countless benefits and kindnesses received over 48 years. These benefits have been ever-present, like the air we breathe, often without full awareness. It is difficult for humans to fully appreciate or adequately express gratitude to the source of these benefits and to those who have helped them, while still alive. The speaker views certain foundational ceremonies as marking the beginning of a journey toward a transcendent state. Each participation in subsequent sacred rituals is seen as progress on this path, akin to earning a positive mark or seeking favor from spiritual guides. The speaker emphasizes the abundance of valuable opportunities available.
styled: I shall remember you all in my High-Mass tomorrow. Please have them all as much as conveinent - have them all - supply my want of appreciation and gratitude to God for the uncountable mercies and graces we have received these 48 years - graces and mercies that have, not only surrounded us but in which, without our half realizing it, we are continually immersed in God' merciful graces / like the air that permiates us. Glory be to God! How little is it possible for poor mortals that we are, to appreciate as we ought, or to be properly grateful to God and our benefactors this side of Heaven! But after all that is what we became candidates for - candidates for the Kingdom of Heaven - when we were baptized; and every time we receive the Holy Sacraments of Mother Church we take another step forward, virtually pleading with our angels for another white bean at every step. How wonderful and how legion are our privileged opportunités ! Glory be to God a billion.

neutral: You and your companions, especially the new members in training, appear to have relocated from your previous location at St. Bonaventure. Also, to Alouise, who has been my next-door neighbor at Saint Felix's for the past three or four years. I find myself missing him more than I typically would, having known him first as a new member in training and then again after nearly 25 years, possibly longer. However, such changes are common within this organization and in everyday life, though they tend to be more disappointing in the latter. Regardless, best wishes to Aloisius and all the new members in training. I wish everyone at St. Francis, your new training center, well. It is possible that I may have the opportunity to visit for a day or so before the summer ends; if circumstances permit, I would be pleased to do so. Until then, we should continue to mutually support each other's development and remember the earnest call to seek more individuals to contribute to the important work.
styled: you and yours, especially our young brothers the Novices, with whom you are now seemingly in a sort of exile from your former nest in St. Bonaventure. And of course to Fr. Alouise, for the past years (3 or 4) my next neighbor at Saint Felix's. I can hardly help missing him more than I usually do in most cases because I knew him ... as a novice and now again after close to 25 years - possibly more. However, that is the way it goes in the Order as well as in secular life; though in the latter it is very much more disapoint- ing. Anyhow, best wishes to Fr. Aloisius and to all the novices and God's blessing to all in St. Francis, your new Novitiate. It is possible that before the summer is over I may have the privilege there for a day or so, God willing so, I'll be pleased. Till then In the mean time we'll do well to continue praying mutually for further conversion and - hearkening to our dear Lord's Own most earnest plea . "Pray we the Lord of the Harvest that He send laborers into His harvest".

neutral: Upon receiving your recent note and practical request regarding the benefits of the Seraphic Mass Association, I was prompted to act on a project I had considered for many months. Your communication spurred me to make a decision about this long-held idea. The association's benefits appear numerous and varied; a comprehensive list would exceed the scope of a short letter, which is all the time I currently have available. However, I will provide a brief summary of these advantages. The institution recognizes this association as particularly important by granting a specific benefit, quantified as 300 days, to those who promote its work. This applies to any effort made, even a few words in its favor, to advance the association's interests.
styled: Since receiving your recent note favor- for which, MANY THANKS - and your practical request in regard to the benefits of the Sera- phic Mass Assotian, I am moved to earenst thought and action on a project that for many months has been floating in my mind. Thanks be to God for His patience with me in not lifting the thought away from me - the inspiration, perhaps I ought to say -- till your ap- preciated communication awakened me to decision. The benefits of this association, as seem to me, are so mani- fest in many cases and so mnifold that to enumerate them even briefly would require more than a short letter, time for writing which is about all I have at my disposal. I shall try, however, not to disapoint you entirely by giving you a short summary of such benefits or advantages. To start with our holy Mother the Church quite singles-out this association as outstanding in importance by granting to promoters of the work three hundred days indulgence for every enrollment - nay, for every effort made, even if it be but a few words in its favor, to further the interests of the Association.

neutral: According to an enclosed booklet (page 13), the many varied and significant reports of benefits received through this organization should demonstrate to anyone the substantial advantages its members gain. One example from records kept by this office, which may interest your organization's members, is provided. In August, Mrs. B., concerned about her son who was soon to deploy overseas, enrolled him in a special program offered by the organization. An entry dated October 5, 1945, states that Mrs. Fred Brewer reported enrolling her son Fred, his comrade, and the ship's crew. The ship crossed the Atlantic successfully. However, two hours before its scheduled landing, it struck a mine, causing the ship and its cargo to sink. Despite this, none of the 2,500 men on board were lost. The Captain stated that their survival was extraordinary. The text then addresses possibilities and obligations.
styled: (See inclosed booklet, page 13). The diversity and in some cases the magnitude of The manifold reports of favors received here as through/Associa- tion ought to convince any thinker', of the wonderful benefits acruing to its members thru this providential organization. Let me give here a single example at least, of the notes made in this office of such fav- ors as I am sure would interest the members of your esteemed organiza- tion. I think it was in August that a certain Mrs. B., anxious about her son shortly to leave for over-seas enrolled him in the "Seraphic Mass". The note follow "October 5, 1945, Mrs. Fred Brewer ... reports having enrolled her son Fred and his comrade and ship-crew, etc. The ship crossed the Atlantic Okay; but two hours before scheduled landing she struck a mine and ship and cargo went down. However, of the 2500 men on board no one was lost. The Captain himself said that the escape was miraculous." Now a word about possibilities and obligations.

neutral: On May 11, little progress was made two weeks prior on a card received from someone who suggested writing. Although a more detailed letter was planned, it has been difficult to make progress. Instead, a letter written to an individual who was then in Yonkers, N.Y., and tended to worry excessively, often about imagined issues or things that proved to be minor concerns, is being sent. It is natural for people to have such inclinations. Even prominent figures were not exceptions to this tendency. Historical accounts suggest these individuals were criticized for their excessive worry. It is natural and accepted that individuals are not blamed for seeking to maintain health. This aligns with fundamental human instincts.
styled: May 11# You see I made very little progress two weeks ago on the card Br. Leo gave me and suggested I write you. However, while I would like to write you more of a real letter, which in fact I proposed to do, I have found it not easy to get any where. However, I am sending you herewith a letter written to a priest who at the time was in Yonkers N.Y. and quite inclined to worry about one thing or another; - nearly always about imaginary things, i.e. about something that turns out to have been more or less just a temptation. Of course we are all naturally inclined that Tay . From our dear Lord's "Sermon on the Mount.", you can see how the Apostles themselves were no ex- ceptions. Just reat the 5th 60 and 75 chapters of St. Matthew ari see how our dear Lord almost scolded them for their want of faith. No one blames you, selfunderstood for trying to be healthy. That's only a part of the first law of nature.

neutral: Indeed, if we were only a tenth as appreciative as we ought to be, our gratitude for the benefits we have received, directly and indirectly, particularly through those in authority over us, would lead to perfect contentment with our current state and possessions, without wishing for what others have or regretting perceived missed opportunities. Furthermore, hoping for truly "true happiness" in this life has always been futile, merely a dream. The pursuit of ideals in the world often leads to disappointment, as reality tends to undermine them. The peace and similar promises offered by the world are often false and deceptive, ultimately leading to destruction. Of course, it is possible to experience a profound sense of peace or fulfillment in this world, as evidenced by the experiences of many individuals known for their virtuous lives.
styled: In very deed, if we were only one tenth as appreciative as we have every reason to be; our gratitude for what God has done for us - directly and through His creatures, most especially through our immediate superiors, - would be such that we would be perfectly content with what we are and what we have, without ever dreaming of what others may be in them- selves, or what in all the world we may have "missed". Furthermore, to ever hope for really "true happiness" this side of Heaven has been alway vain. only a dream Hence Father Ryan, the "Blind Poet of the South in his "Song of The Mystic": " ... I walked in the world with the worldly. I craved what the world never gave "And I said: 'In the world each ideal that shines like a star on life's wave; "Is wrecked on the shores of the real(ity), and sleeps like dream in a grave. The peace, etc promised by the world is the peace of the Serpent - ahellofapeace.Ofcourse, there is such a thing as getting "a teste of Heaven" in this world, as we see clearly inthe lives of many saints.

neutral:
Enrollment is open to anyone. This includes individuals seeking to adopt or change their spiritual or ethical practices, and those already engaged in such practices who wish to deepen their commitment and understanding. These activities occur within a framework defined as the study of one's relationship with a higher power and with other people.

Obligations are practical. Active members, recognizing the benefits of their participation, are encouraged to offer support for the organization's outreach activities, its outreach workers, and all fellow members. They are also encouraged to participate in a specific ritual, when possible, with these goals in mind.

Financial contributions are requested from those who are able to provide them, to support the organization's operations. The usual contribution is 50 cents annually, or a one-time payment of $5 for perpetual membership. Members may contribute more if they choose. A contribution of $2 or more is also requested for the inclusion of a deceased member in the organization's activities.

Direct and immediate benefits include the daily performance of approximately 525 specific rituals, totaling 188,500 such rituals annually. This does not include indirect participation in the broader beneficial activities of the entire affiliated organization, which also involves thousands of these rituals daily.
styled: Anyone may be enrolled: -- the sinner (atheist or believer) for conversion; the saint for further conversion and progress in sanctity - in RELIGION, THE SCIENCE OF OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR. (and, if yiu will, of our dependenc: on Both) Obligations are practical. If the parents you mentioned – one of whom was baptized Catholic, and the other, though well-intentioned, had little or no religious faith – were to embrace religious faith, a positive outcome is anticipated. Should they visit New York, a meeting would be welcome. Meanwhile, a positive outcome is hoped for. It was also noted that someone might wish to visit the Wheelers. According to records, when they visited last year, their address was 686 Manistique Ave., Detroit.
styled: He surely looked and seemed to feel happy. I have no doubt that if those parents of whom you wrote me - the one baptized a Catholic at least and the other, though good at heart, with little or no faith - would wake up and turn to the Good God they would get a happy surprise. In case they come to New York any time, I would be pleased to see them. In the meantime, we will hope and pray. P.S. I just remembered that possibly someone would like to go to see the above mentioned Wheelers. When they called on me last year, according to my notes, they lived at 686 Manistique Ave., Detroit.

neutral: I read your letter of the 11th and understand your situation. This difficult experience, which some might view as a failure, could perhaps be seen as an opportunity for learning. There is no need for discouragement as long as one maintains a degree of conviction. A more positive outlook can be achieved by cultivating conviction, optimism, and compassion. Life in this world is comparatively brief, suggesting that its successes or failures may ultimately be insignificant. It is difficult to reconcile the superficiality of those who prioritize worldly life above all else with the concept of rationality. Your current difficulty is seen as an indication of some underlying weakness. However, what is perceived as weak can often challenge or overcome what is considered strong.
styled: I hope this finds your out-look brightening. I just read your letter of the 11th -- pathetic indeed -- and surely do sympathize with you. Perhaps I ought rather to congratulate you on the unusual experience you are of course inclined to learn/ and which the unbelieving world must look upon as a sad indication of failure. But O: Why discouragement as long as we have a spark of faith left? What different view we get by exercising and by fostering the "triune virtue FAITH, HOPE, CHARITY! In the first place "life" here in this world is so short -- comparatively so momentary -- that in regard to its success or failure one is in- clined to think: " ... After all, what is the difference?" -- "life" so short, that worldlings are so inclined to worship as the only LIFE -- as everything worth. How is it possible that man can be so shallow-minded and still be considered "rational"? Your failure, yes, is an indication of weakness of some kind, somewhere. But if "The weak thing of this world hath God chosen to confound the strong ..... " as St.

neutral: Thank you for your contribution for the services. The requested services will be performed as soon as possible.
