Whether referred to as "Mystical Rose" or "Mystical City," she is considered the Mother of God and is also regarded as the mother of humanity, and therefore, our mother as well.
styled: Kindly accept our heartfelt thanks for your Mass offering. The Masses will be said as soon as possible. God bless you again Mrs. Weithoff. You may well con- gratulate yourself and be consoled that yourself and your lately deceased Mother have been clients of our dear Bles- sed Mother Mary - under whatever title -- for whether as "Mystica Rose" or Mystical City" she remains the Blessed Mother of God and by His divine wisdom and power and mer- ciful condiscention blessed Mother of redeemed humanity, . therefore, our blessed Mother too. . -

neutral: There is strong affirmation, supported by numerous historical examples and universal agreement, that discouragement is unnecessary, unless one's trust or conviction weakens. Instead, one should be grateful for opportunities to develop humility, and by expressing gratitude in advance for any future difficulties, cultivate confidence in an overarching wisdom. This kind of confidence is rarely attained without experiencing challenges and humbling situations. Even a seemingly minor or isolated failure can be a considerable difficulty for an individual to bear. A short saying that may be beneficial to remember and could help cultivate this confidence is: "A higher power utilizes human capabilities, provided human actions do not interfere with overarching plans." These overarching plans are always beneficial and excellent. However, for those who maintain patience, humility, and trust, these plans are profoundly wise and magnificent.
styled: Paul so wonderfully assures us -- and the history of religion abounds in examples and all creation says Amen -- then why ever be discouraged: unless it be that our faith, more or less weakens? Why dear sister, you ought to rather thank God for having given you such an opportunity to humble yourself and such a wonderful chance to foster humility -- and by thanking Him ahead of time for whatever crosses He may deign to caress you with, CONFIDENCE in His wisdom. Confidence in God -- the very soul of prayer -- hardly comes to any poor sinner like we all are, without trials and humiliations, and your failure, though simple and possibly single, has no doubt been quite a little cross, at least for a "little soul" to carry. There is a little verse I am sure will prof you to keep in mind and ought help you foster confi- dence in God. "God condescends to use our powers, If we don't spoil His plans by ours." God's plans are always for the best: always wonderful. But most especially for the patient and the humble who trust in Him are His plans unfathomably holy and sublime.

neutral: It is important not to lose resolve, and to maintain hope even when circumstances are challenging. Gratitude should be expressed constantly, regardless of the situation. This includes being thankful for existence and for all things, even for past designs or intentions that may have been altered due to human actions, lack of appreciation, or impatience. This gratitude should also extend to all future prospects, encompassing both challenges and positive experiences like joys and comforts, as well as illness and the eventual end of life. Drawing on ancient wisdom, one should encourage all beings to acknowledge and revere the fundamental origin and ultimate good – the beginning and the end.
styled: Let us, therefore, not weaken. Let us hope when darkness seem to surround us. Let us thank Him at all time and under whatever circumstances. Thank Him for our creation and our existence, Thank Him for every thing -- for His plans in the past that by our sins and our want of appreciation and patience have so often frustrated and that He so often found necessary to change. Let us thank Him for all His plans for the future -- for trials and humiliations for as well as got joys and consola- tions; for sickness and whatever death He may deign to plan; and with the inspired Psalmist let us call all the creatures of the universe to help us praise adore and Him Who is the Divine Beginning and the everlasting Good -- the Alpha and the Omega .

neutral: A guiding force often provides, or at least permits, experiences that serve to awaken individuals, preventing them from forgetting their ultimate purpose as thinking beings. This purpose is to understand their origin and, through devotion and service, to unite their being with that origin indefinitely. It is recognized that the recipient has engaged in significant charitable work in recent years, which is commendable. This suggests a greater depth of conviction and benevolence than many might acknowledge. However, effective benevolence starts with oneself. This implies cultivating and fostering within oneself fundamental positive attributes like conviction, optimism, and compassion, which are essentially intertwined. In other words, it involves a continuous effort to deepen one's understanding of the ultimate source of being, its restorative aspects, and its capacity for transformation. Understanding is a prerequisite for appreciation, just as knowing a person is necessary for affection.
styled: Hence the Good God, often in His mercy, sends something - at least permits it - to come to us for the purpose of waking us up, lest we forget the final purpose of our exist- ence as rational creatures, viz. to know our CREATOR and, in love and service to blend our existence with His for all eternity. Of course, I know that you have been doing a lot of charity-work these past years and I have thanked God to see it. It indicates to me at least, that you have more faith and more charity than many would like to concede. After all, however, rightly ordered charity begins at home. That means, in my figuering at least, the cultivation and fostering in our own individual hearts and souls the supernatural virtues of faith, hope and charity - essencially one virtue. In other words I might say it means for me personally, that I should strive continually to learn more and more about God my Creator, about God as my Redeemer, about God my Sanctifyer. Because in only as much as I know anything can I appreciate it. as I know a good person can I love him.

neutral:
The author expresses hope for the recipient's well-being and their ability to view their international adversaries, whom the author describes as often distorting justice and truth. The author further characterizes these adversaries as materialistic, atheistic, and foolish.

The author acknowledges receipt of the recipient's communication, delivered by Sister Mary Clarissa of the Guardian Angel Convent several weeks prior, and expresses gratitude for the recipient's generosity. The author explains a delay in responding, stating a desire to write a substantive letter and noting that, as of today, they are finally free from urgent correspondence after several months.

Sister Mary Clarissa reportedly informed the author of the recipient's adversaries, who were again attempting to cause problems, and requested prayers for the recipient's guidance. The author states pleasure in hearing from the recipient and receiving such requests, acknowledging the recipient's need for spiritual support, a need the author believes is universal. The author adds that this need is especially pertinent for someone whose abilities and work expose them to many enticements and significant opposition, as the recipient's do.
styled: God bless you and yours. I do hope you are well - and by this time able to smile at your poor inter- national enemies: in so many cases perverters of justice. and truth. Poor enemies! because in sad part materialistic - atheistic - little better than fools. I received your kind favor through Sister Mary Clarissa of the Guardian Angel Convent. I know you have need of prayers. Who in tis world don't need them ? And this, I might say especially for one whose abilities and whose work brings him in contact with so many teptations and such opposition as does yours.

neutral: I hope you are well and able to maintain composure despite your international adversaries, who are, in many cases, believed to distort truth and justice. I received your message through Mary Clarissa, from the Guardian Angels' Home, approximately two weeks ago. Thank you very much for it. I had hoped to write you a more substantial letter. However, the longer I wait, the less likely it seems I will get a break from my correspondence. So, I have decided to write to you briefly, at least for now. I am not surprised that they are attempting to cause you difficulties again; I am sure you have been more or less expecting this. I concluded this based on previous events. However, Doctor, perhaps there is a larger purpose or set of expectations that you are not currently considering. As time passes, I am convinced that people are quite similar in many respects. For example, we tend to minimize the importance of intangible and long-term aspects, while overvaluing tangible and immediate ones, often to the detriment of the former.
styled: God bless you and yours. I do hope your are well and able to smile at at your international enemies - in so many cases perverters of truth and justice. I received your kind favor through Sister Mary Clarissa of the Guardian Angels' Home. about two weeks ago; for which ... many thanks. I was hoping to get a chance to write you a really worth while letter. But the longer I wate, it would seem the farther I get from a "let up" in correspondence. So I've decided to write you briefly, at least for the present. Of course I am not surprised that they are trying again to make trouble for you. I am sure you have been more or less expecting it. This I concluded from what has gone before. But dear Doctor: perhaps the dear Lord is expecting something that you are not regarding. As time goes on I am convinced that we poor mortals are quite alike in many ways. For example, we are naturally inclined to minimize the importance of the spiritual and the eternal and to over-rate the physical and the temporal - the latter at the cost of the former.

neutral: The recipient performs many beneficial actions for the community, which are often unknown, unacknowledged, or disbelieved by others. However, it is suggested that the recipient might need to prioritize their personal spiritual well-being more earnestly. Philanthropy is consistently beneficial and merits encouragement. However, it is understood that self-care or personal foundational needs should be addressed first. This suggests that personal spiritual development, or the care of one's inner self, is a primary consideration. If the fundamental purpose of a rational being's existence is to understand its origin, to act in accordance with that understanding, and ultimately achieve profound fulfillment, then the primary obligation is to express gratitude for this origin through diligent understanding and appreciation.
styled: I know too that you do much for the community that men know little or nothing about - often are lothe to acknowledge, or to belive. However, dear Doctor Koch: I have been wondering if there is mt something else that our dear Lord may be expecting to see you do for Him; viz, more earnestness in providing for the "insurence of your own soul's salvation". Charity is always good; always to be commended and fostered. But after all, rightly ordered charity begins at home. To my mind that means it should begin right in one's own heart - to be practical, in my own soul. But if the primary object of my creation and my existence as a rational creature is to know my Creator, and this, in order that I may be able to love Him and serve Him, and finally by cooperating with His grace, blend my existenc with His in eternal, unspeakable glory; then my first obligation, my first charity is to fulfil my obligation of gratitude to my Creator by trying as best I may to recognize My Creator/that thus, I may intelligently appreciate and some way manifest appreciation.

This is because the primary and most certain sign of intelligence is appreciation for benefits received. neutral: The number of personal visitors at Bonaventure has decreased, but the volume of correspondence remains high, possibly due to personal handling. This support is crucial because the work, combined with other duties, often requires long hours, from 5 AM to 11 PM, even with help. Leo, Rufin, Gerard, and other individuals have provided this assistance. Ultimately, the identity of the person performing the work is not important, as long as the valuable tasks are completed and directed to the designated headquarters. The success and positive impact of the Association's work, in which the Promoters play a significant role, are evident from the numerous, often remarkable, and substantial positive outcomes that have been reported.
styled: Bonaventure's my personal callers have been by no means as heavy; though my letters - possibly because I have to take care of them myself - seem a heavy as ever; and you can imagine how I appreciate it to have someone like one of the Brothers or Fathers in Detroit continue their generous assistence in the work that, even with such help, often keeps me - with other duties - from 5 O'cl a.m. Il p.m. Brother Leo and Br. After all, as long as the wonderful work is done and it goes to the same headquarters, what's the difference who coes it. That Heaven is pleased with the work of the Associ- ation and you Promoters have mighty big share in the merrit - ought to be manifest from the number and often the astonishing nature and magnitude of the favors we have reported as thru the same great source of blessings. Thanks and glory to God!

neutral: Thank you for your message, which we have received and noted. We are always pleased to fulfill such requests. We hope our efforts are satisfactory. It is beneficial for promoting mutual support that we are interdependent. A significantly better society would result if everyone remembered the importance of how one treats the most vulnerable.
styled: Many thanks for your appreciated favor duly received and noted. May our dear Lord bless you and yours and give you His holy peace! We shall always deem it a privilege to comply with such requests. We hope that our efforts will be satisfactory. How wonderful, in the promotion of mutual and common charity, that -- next to our happy dependence on Almighty God Himself -- He has made us mutually dependent also on one another. And, inci- dentally, what a marvellously different society we'd have here, and what an ideal world to live in if we'd all keep in mind the assurance of Jesus, "What you have done to the least of my brethren you have done to me."

neutral: It is asserted that atheism is profoundly detrimental to both individuals and society, as it is considered fundamentally opposed to sound reasoning, hope, and the essence of human well-being. A significant definition will follow. The passage argues that if gratitude for received benefits is a primary and reliable indicator of intelligence, and if the most fundamental benefit for any creature is its creation and existence, then atheism lacks any justifiable basis. This point will be further clarified by the upcoming definition.
styled: For as a matter of fact Walter; in my opinion there can hardly be any thing worse for the individual or for society than atheism; - nothing more positively opposed to right reason and hope, the very soul of terrestial happiness. Hence, the fearful definition to follow shortly. But first, - Think of it! -- if "Gratitude for favors received is one of the very first and surest indications of intelligence" and if the very first benefit possible to any creature is its creation, its existence, then in the Name of God and of right reason and of decency itself, where is there a shadow of excuse/ the atheist and his atheism? We'll let the definition answer.

neutral: Thank you for your donation to the Capuchin Foreign Missions. The certificate of enrollment is enclosed. We also acknowledge your letter of June 12th. Your letter to Brooklyn was forwarded to us. The requested Masses have been noted.
styled: I wish to thank you sincerely for your kind alms for the Capuchin Foreign Missions. I am sure that the prayers of the missionaries will ascend to the Throne of God for your welfare. The certificate of enrollment are inclosed herewith. - Many thanks for your favor of June 12th God bless you Dear Mrs. Geraci. Yes, Mrs. Geraci, Your letter to Brooklyn was forwarde to me shortly. Noted the holy Masses as requeste and do trust that everything comes according to God's holy designs. How wonderful are His ways -- and His mercy is above all His works. Blessed be His divine Providence!

neutral: I wish you well in all your worthwhile endeavors. I understand you are experiencing difficulties again. Years ago, when we first met, you made a commitment, and I believed we had formed a strong friendship. I have often thought of you, Walter McClellan, since that night you made that commitment, which you successfully maintained. However, I have frequently wondered if Walter ever considered what he might be lacking by not embracing religious belief, the concept of God, and faith in Jesus Christ. I am convinced Walter would be a significantly different and happier person if he possessed such faith—a faith that has historically provided comfort and support to countless individuals over centuries. My respect for you serves as sufficient proof that I am confident you are not a genuine atheist, unless you are one of those who, despite their atheism, have been observed to express gratitude for it using religious terminology.
styled: God bless you and yours, - every thing that interest you worthwhile. I understand you are once more in trouble - as years ago when we two first met, you took the pledge and, as I thought, we became pretty good friends. (Not?) I have ofthen thought of you Walter Mcclellan, since that night when you took the pledge and, thank God you kept it. Many a time, however, I have wondered if "big W. Mack" ever tried to realize in any way what he has been missing in refusing to believe in RELIGION and in God, and in failing to foster faith in Jesus Christ. I am sure Walter would be quite a different, altogether happier man if he only had the Faith: - Ah! - that faith which down the centuries has been the consolation and the stay of uncounted millions. Of course, the very fact that I respect you as I do, ought to be proof sufficient that I am confident you can not be a real atheist, - except possibly such a one as have been heard to thank God for their atheism. !

neutral: It is good to hear you are feeling better. Continue to progress and avoid worry or discouragement, as such feelings are unproductive. A greater appreciation for the many positive aspects of life would leave no room for worry, with the only exception being a lack of sufficient appreciation itself. Congratulations to your husband.
styled: I am glad you are feeling improved. Keep up the improvement and don't give way to worry or discour- agement. That never pays. If we could only learn to appreciate the holy faith and the innumerable blessings flowing from it and the blessings other- wise surrounding us; We could never have time to worry about anything - except that we're so little appreciative. P.S. Congratulations to your Husband, H.

neutral: Thank you for your message of August 24th. I have taken action to include our intentions in a spiritual practice. I believe this will help us avoid many difficulties we might otherwise encounter. Thank you for your well wishes. Such support is greatly needed by all. I am grateful for everything.
styled: Many thanks for your appreciated favor of August 24th. I have enrolled the Poor Souls specially for your intentions and mine. I am confident they will help us out of many troubles that would otherwise come to us. Thank you for your kind prayers. That is something all need very much. Thanks be to God for all things.

neutral: Atheism is described as originating from extreme arrogance and malevolence, and as the ultimate form of intellectual and spiritual unsoundness. It is presented as both a hopeless conclusion and a desperate refuge, attributed to shallow thinking, perverse and degenerate minds, and utterly foolish individuals. Its immediate and destructive consequence is the loss of hope in a transcendent reality, which the author considers the fundamental source of happiness in this world. This loss specifically involves the inability to recognize a fundamental obligation of gratitude, a primary practical conclusion for those capable of understanding.
styled: "Born originally in the haughty pride of Lucifer himself, the prince of diabolical darkness, atheism as the climax of intellectual and spiritual insanity, is at once the hopeless con- clusion and the desperate refuge - suggested by the devil - 1st of shallow thinking, 2ndly of perverse, degenerate minds, and thirdly (fearful to say), of damned fools." Its first and immediate, ruinous effect which comes simultaneously with atheism, is the loss of supernatural hope, the very soul of hap- piness in this world; viz, for any one really able to draw the first practical conclusion, "obligation of gratitude".

neutral:
A letter was received concerning your daughter Lois' eye trouble. Sympathy was expressed for you and your husband regarding this matter, which was described as comparatively trivial, though there was hope it would prove to be no more than trivial.

Approximately twenty years ago, a young couple brought their first-born child to the Monastery of St. Bonaventure. The child's eye had a scratched pupil and had lost fluid. Their doctor accompanied them to a specialist in the D. Whitney Building, who recommended immediate eye removal. In their distress, they then came to St. Bonaventure and made a perpetual commitment to the institution, which included a pledge for more frequent religious participation. The eye healed quickly, and they did not return to medical doctors.
styled: I just read your pathetic letter in regard to your little Daughte Lois' eye-trouble. I certainly sympathize with you and your dear Hus- band in this, though coparatively trivial matter. We'll pray, however, and trust that it may turn out to be no more than trivial. It is about twenty years back that a young couple brought their first-born to us at the Monaster of St. Bonaventure, the pupil of whose little eye had been scratched and lost fluid. Their doctor went with them to a specialest in the D. Whitney Bld'g who wanted to remove the eye at once. · Then in consternation they came to St. B. and enrollied promising a perpetual enrollment and especially more frequent holy communion. Thank God the eye healed shortly and they never went back to the doctors. So dear Mrs. - and Mr.

neutral: Thank you very much, Alice O'Brien. I also appreciate your letter of October 6th, which I duly received and noted. I quite enjoyed the short overnight visit with the five guests. I knew your Mother Anna very well, almost like a sister. I stayed several weeks with Aunt Mary and Uncle Pat in 1887 while learning to operate the trolley cars. I believe Anna was a few years older than me, but we were close friends. Uncle Pat was also one of the guards when I started working at the State's Prison. Please convey a message to Joe when you write to him. I believe I owe him a letter or two, but my biggest challenge is keeping up with my correspondence. I hope to be able to speed up my writing. Regards, Solanus.
styled: God bless you Miss Alice O'Brien -- you and yours . Many thanks too for your kind favor of Oct. 6th -- duely received and noted. Yes I quited enjoyed the short visit with the five guests over night, etc. . . Indeed I did know your Mother Anna -- almost like a sister. I stopped several weeks while learning to run the trolly cars in 1887 with our Aunt Mary and Uncle Pat and of course. She was (I think) a few years older than I but we were quite friends: -- also when I started working in the State's Prison- - Uncle Pat one of the guards. . . . When you write to Joe, tell him. Best Regards and God's blessing from Fr. Sol. I think I owe him a letter or two: but my big problem is my correspondence. So please pray that be able to speed up. --- Fr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap.

neutral: The communication of February 6th has been received and noted with appreciation. It is noted that the situation appears to be improving. A few jubilee cards are enclosed. Privileges have been experienced for the past fifty years. The Clerical Novitiate (rear view) faces the city located 122 miles downstream on the Wabash River. There are 18 novices, with a capacity for 40.
styled: Many thanks for kind favor of Febr. 6th -- duly Rec'd and noted. Glad to know that things seem brightening up. Thanks be to God for all His mercies Am herewith inclosing a few "jubilee cards." Thanks be to God for such privileges as have been mine these fifty years. Clerical Novitiate (rear) -- looking toward City 122 miles down on the Wabash River. We have 18 novices -- room for 40. Pray

neutral: It is good to know you are still working towards a positive ultimate outcome. This is a significant and often difficult endeavor, particularly at times. I have arranged for support for a quick recovery, if conditions permit.
styled: God bless you Wm Hol's. Glad to know you are still on "the job - trying to make the grade to a happy eternity - some grade too .. not ? - now and then especially - I have enrolled for speedy recovery, God willing.

neutral: Thank you for the update regarding the 9%. While the outcome was not as favorable as desired, we continue to hope for a positive turn of events. It is best to accept the current circumstances and maintain a positive perspective on future outcomes. This approach helps to build resilience and optimism, which in turn strengthens our hopes for a positive resolution. Furthermore, by maintaining this positive outlook, we reduce the risk of sadness, a lack of acceptance, and impatience, which can hinder favorable outcomes. This highlights the importance of not hindering potential positive developments through our own actions. Additionally, I want to thank you for your practical interest in the distressing situation concerning Dr.
styled: I was pleased to receive your kind favor of the 9% even though it was not as bright, as of course, we all would like to see it. However, God knows best, and, while we'll still hope for a favorable surprise, we can hardly do better than, not only be resigned to whatever God permits, but even beforehand thank Him for His mercifully loving designs. In this way we can foster confidence in God, whis is the very soul of prayer, and con- sequently heighten our hopes for supernatural int- ervention. Not only this, but in thus fostering confidence, we greatly eliminate the danger of sadness, want of resignation and impatience which, though not necessarily sinful in themselves, never- theless sadly frustrate God's merciful designs. Hence the little verse : "God condescerds to use our powers If we don't spoil His plans by ours." Besides this, dear Mr. Morgan; I want to thank you for your practical interest in the apalling cas of Dr.

neutral: Thank you for your donation to the Capuchin Foreign Missions. The missionaries will wish you well. Certificates of enrollment are being mailed to you separately. Regarding your stiff knee, it is suggested that you consult a chiropractor or osteopath.
styled: I WISH TO THANK YOU SINCERELY FOR YOUR KIND AND GENEROUS ALMS TO THE CAPUCHIN FOREIGN MISSIONS. I AM : SURE THAT THE PRAYERS CE THE MISSIONA IES WILL ASCEND TO THE THRONE OF GOD FOR YOUR WELFARE. UNDER SEPARATE COVER I AM MAILING YOU THE CER- TIFICATES OF ENROLLMENT, WHICH I TRUST YOU WILL LIKE. P.S. With that stiff knee of yours, you ought to see a good chiropractor or ostiopath.

neutral: This issue has been a concern since July, and particularly since early September. While waiting in one of the rooms, the speaker observed a young man, estimated to be 15 to 17 years old, enter the office. Based on his voice and the subsequent interaction, the speaker inferred he was the doctor's son. The young man appeared intelligent and alert. However, the speaker was troubled by the lack of respect the young man displayed towards his father during their brief conversation. The disrespect was so pronounced that the speaker nearly interjected with a reminder to respect one's parents. The speaker later considered that the young man's father was absent, and his mother had changed her religious affiliation. This led the speaker to question who was responsible for the situation. Since that day, the speaker has been considering how to promote peace and unity within the family, which appears to be experiencing separation or discord. The speaker's aim is to reconcile the father with the rest of the family.
styled: Not since yesterday only Doctor, has this been on my mind; but since away back in July, and decidedly more so since early in September; when a youth came into your office while I was waiting in one of the apartments and whom, judging from his voice and the familiarity that followed between you, I took to be a son of yours of probably fifteen to seventeen years. He seemed promisingly bright and alert; but what pained me as the little dialogue proceeded was the sad want of filial reverence and even respect shown to his father. So much so, in fact that I almost called out to him: "Boy ... Honor thy father and thy mother". "Alas", I thought afterwards, "The poor lad has only an absentee father and his mother a convert . Where is the responsability? Who's to blame? Honestly dear Doctor, I've been thinking ever since that day, how to devise, or what, to induce something of Christian peace and harmony into that half-divorced family, - something to bring that father and whole, half-divorced family together.

neutral: Thank you again for your letter from November 1974. It was received and its contents noted. I have only now been able to reply. I am also enrolling you in the association. It is important to remember that our difficulties and opportunities for positive action are temporary. Therefore, let us dedicate all our actions to a higher purpose, so that they may contribute to the well-being of all individuals, including ourselves. It will also be very helpful to consider the concept of what truly endures. Augustine famously stated that things which are not enduring have little intrinsic value. This refers to temporary experiences, such as earthly joys and sorrows. Thank you for your support.
styled: Many thanks again for your kind favor of Nov 74 -- duely received and noted. Only today, however, did I get to answer it. I am enrolling you in the Seraphic Mass Association also. We do well to remember how very short after all it is till our suffering - and our time of merit too will be over. Let us offer everything, there- fore to the divine Soouse of our Souls that He may accept it as helping Him to save immortal souls -- Cur own included. It will help greatly too, if we keep in mind what is meant by Eternity. . St. Augustine was want to say : "What is not eternal is worth little. " That is, in itself - te restrial joys and sorrows alike. . Many thanks for your prayers.

neutral: It would be inappropriate not to express concern about potential difficulties. Just recently, a middle-aged couple, also your friends, expressed sadness to me that after several years of marriage, they had never had what I consider the greatest gift in life: a family. You, Doctor Young, also have no family. Is it perhaps because the family you were given lacks a leader? Regardless, this is a sad situation; and despite the common occurrence of similar cases, it is a deeply regrettable problem.
styled: Hence, Dear Doctor Young: I feel that I would not be your friend or even a decently grateful patient were I to be silent as to dangers ahead of you as I see them without any doubt. Only yesterday a middle-aged couple - friends of yours too - lamented to me that after several years in holy matrimony, they had never been blessed with - what I have long since considered the greatest blessing that, in the natural order, God gives on earth, A Family. And my Doctor Young has no family. ? Because the family that God blessed him with has no head. ? At all events, it is a sad situation; and notwithstanding the fearful prevalence of similar cases, it must be, in the sight of Heaven a most lamentable problem.

neutral: This morning, an unfamiliar person requested assistance for a specific objective. This individual appeared to be acquainted with you and your family, a fact that became clear after a brief conversation. Additionally, one of the main issues discussed, expressed with sincere concern, recalled a disappointing comment you made during my initial visit to your office. At that time, I had defined "THE GREATEST SCIENCE OF ALL AGES" as "the study of our positive relationship with a higher power and with other people," and stated that while numerous belief systems might exist, there could be only one overarching discipline concerning such beliefs.
styled: You can imagine my surprise this morning, therefore, when a hitherto stranger to me came begging for prayers to help "storm Heaven" for this very purpose. The party was evidently a friend of yours, as well as of your whole family. Of this I was convinced after a very few words. In- cidently, one of the primary causes lamented, with what seemed to me genuinely fraternal solicitude, brought back to me a rather disapointing remark you made on occasion of my first visit to your office. If you remember I had just given a definition of, "THE GREATEST SCIENCE OF ALL AGES" as, "RELIGION IS THE SCIENCE OF OUR HAPPY RELATION- SHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR", adding that, while there may be an in- definite number of "religious systems", there can be only one science of RELIGION".

neutral:
Wishing you and your family a happy holiday season and a prosperous New Year. I was sorry to hear you haven't been well, and I hope it is nothing too serious. Regardless of the severity, difficult situations, when approached with a certain perspective, often prove to be beneficial in the long run.

In any case, I am enrolling you in the Seraphic Mass Association and am engaging in prayer for your speedy physical recovery and subsequent improvement, and, what I consider to be of greater importance, your spiritual well-being. I believe that we all, due to our human failings, require a fundamental change in our outlook. Nevertheless, I hope your situation improves soon in both physical and spiritual aspects.

It is certain that if we act correctly, we will be supported. However, there is always a potential pitfall, as we are naturally prone to error. Consequently, we have a duty to caution one another when risks emerge.
styled: God bless you and yours for a blessed Christmastide and, please God too, a happy prosperous New Year. I was sorry to learn of your not being well. I hope its nothing too serious. But whether serious or not, we may be sure that inasmuch as we take such things as from the hand of God, they will never fail in the end to turnout as having been a blessing in disguise. At all events I am enrolling you in the Seraphic Mass Associa- tion and am praying for your speedy recovery and thereafter speedy improve- ment, - physically of course and, what is infinitely of more importance, spiritually. God knows that, in our stupidity we all need real conversion to Him. Anyhow, I hope things brighter for you soon in both regards. No question about it, if we do the right thing on our part God never fails us. Just here, however is always a danger. We are naturally so inclined to go wrong. Therefore too, our obligation to admonish one another when danger threatens.

neutral: Kraus's efforts and personal sacrifices in support of justice and truth, which the author framed as 'religion' (defined as a relationship with God and one's neighbor) in opposition to 'atheism' (described by the author as an extreme form of intellectual and spiritual dysfunction), have been outstanding and, at times, internationally recognized. It is hoped that action will be taken to rectify the significant injustices that Dr. Kraus has been opposing. There is confidence that Kraus's idealism, described by the author as profoundly Christian, will eventually prevail, despite the perception that he is fifty years ahead of his generation. The author believes that if Kraus perseveres, acts in accordance with divine favor, and consistently demonstrates good intentions, significant results will emerge from his ongoing, heroic struggle. It is also hoped that a benevolent higher power has a positive future in store for Rickey Grix. These views are held despite relevant scientific conclusions in one instance and despite the influence of political atheism in the other.
styled: Kraus; whose efforts and personal sacrafices in the cause of the very principles of justice and truth -- of religion as against atheism, the supreme science of our hanny relationship with God and our neighbor against the "diabolical climax of intel- lectual and spiritual insanity -- has been so out- standing and, at times, so internationally recognized. I do hope that something may be done to right some- thing of the flagrant injustices against which Dr. Kraus has been fighting. I am confident that sooner or later his idealism - so really Christian - will prevail; though it seems to me he is fifty years ahead of his generation. I feel that if he only persevere and cooperate with God's grace, never wanting to good wills, there will come great results from his so far, heroic warfare. So, too, do I hope that the good God whose ways are so unsearchable, have something ahead of poor, dear little Rickey Grix. All this, not withstanding scientific conclusions in the one case and, in the other, . . political atheism.

neutral: I have been concerned about you for nearly a year and feel compelled to inform you of a serious risk: that of completely losing what little commitment you seem to have left to your spiritual principles. You may wonder why I have reached such an alarming conclusion, but your current outlook is indeed serious. First, according to certain doctrines, the initial consequence of misconduct is the loss of spiritual purity, which leads to a weakening of one's inner resolve and a greater susceptibility to repeated or new misconduct.
styled: Tow dear Doctor Young; I want to tell you in all sincerity and truth, that for close to a year you have been a problem on my mind, and I feel that I would not be a friend of yours or a grateful patient were I to let the present holy Easter Season pass without at least fraternally calling your attention to the very grave danger ahead of you, of completely losing the very little faith in Jesus Christ and His Church which, (un) for- tunately at least, you seem to have left. But; "Why such an alarming conclusion?", you will ask. For indeed your outlook in my way of reckon- ing is grave. First. Because, according to the greatest theologians, the first punishment on sin is the withdrawal of sanctifying grace - of God himself, therefore, - and the consequent weakening of the soul to fall again with less resistence into the same and other sins.

neutral: I wish you and your family well. I am hoping for your overall well-being, particularly your inner well-being, but also your physical and social well-being, as I consider inner well-being to be of primary importance. I have wanted to write to you, Doctor, for several months. I even started a couple of letters before Christmas, especially after learning of your serious heart attack, and I included you in a religious support association. As a member of the community, I also want to thank you for your generous act toward the person known as Father Guardian several weeks ago. I was particularly pleased to hear about it, both for your benefit and for the benefit of those in need. It appears that such acts of charity have, in many instances, been crucial for the ultimate well-being of individuals who might otherwise have faced a negative outcome.
styled: God bless you and yours. I hope you are well. Perhaps I ought rather to say I am trying to hope for your welfare, - spiritual of course and especially, as well as physically and socially: because after all in the sight of Heaven, the first is what supremely counts. I have been wanting to write you Doctor these several months. In fact I started a couple of letters to you before Christmas, especially when I learned of your serious heart-attack and enrolled you in the Seraphic Mass Association. But first let me too, as a member of the community, thank you for your charitable favor to Rev. Father Guardian several weeks ago. I was doubly pleased to hear of it - for your own sake as well as for the needy poor. For it would seem in many cases that just such exercises of charity has meant the final salvation of many a soul otherwise most likely lost.

neutral: If you manage to regain a state of mental well-being, perhaps through sincere self-reflection, the intense fear and aversion you currently feel towards things you once valued will diminish, and you will likely gradually return to your former contented state. However, to continue on a path that leads to ruin, while in a state of serious moral transgression, and to delay actively seeking a positive change or lasting well-being, is an extremely dangerous approach. This behavior closely mirrors a regrettable example previously discussed and must be addressed with the utmost urgency. The intention is not to be overly critical or discouraging, but rather to prompt awareness of a serious situation before it becomes irreversible.
styled: If ever again you get back into the grace of God by a good, humble confession, that "preternatural fear and dislike you now experience for things you once revered and loved, will at once weaken, and, little by little you will in all probability come to your old happy self again. But to dance along the "wide road that leads to destruction" and in a state of most probable mortal sin, dily-dallying with a possibility of some day obtaining the grace of God and eternal salvation, is a fearfully perilous course to take. To my mind it is positively following the steps of our unfortunate judge above referred to, in an appallingly close imitation, and something to checkup on at every and all costs. Hoping dear Doctor, that I have not been over harsh in my conclusions and that this may not discourage you. Rather on the contrary that it may simply wake you up before it's too late, from your most threatening drowsyness, I beg to remain Please do not forget Doctor; I need prayers as well as any other poor sinner.

neutral: Reconciliation and harmony can be achieved with the universal governing force, which is simultaneously benevolent and just. This force demonstrates mercy and grace to those who appreciate its inherent goodness and cooperate with its principles, but also holds accountable those who are arrogant and resistant. This is a concept for general consideration. Pope Leo XIII's encyclical on the Holy Eucharist was a notable publication, widely regarded as a masterpiece. It was considered both profound and highly influential. A significant passage from this work states: "Historical evidence indicates that the moral and ethical qualities associated with the Christian faith thrived most effectively in contexts where its central communal ritual, the Eucharist, was frequently observed."
styled: we may recover our friendship and our peace with our God in Heaven -- at once -- the divinely gentle and loving Governor of the universe, and the no less divine Avenger of the proud and the stubborn who refuse to appreciate His merciful goodness and to cooperate with His gracious condescinsions. Something for me as well as you Friend, and us all to think about. Not? Then Doctor: you possibly remember reading the great encyclical of Pope Leo XIII on the Holy Eucharist, even when it first came out. Anyhow, I think it has been generally considered a decided master-piece, at once like-inspired and indeed very inspiring. Here is a notable passage from it that I have often considered and that have often wished were proclaimed again and again, in season and out of season: "History bears witness that the virtues of the Christian life have flourished best wherever and whenever the frequent reception of the Eucharist has most prevailed.

neutral: Conversely, it is equally clear that when people lose interest in the central practices of the Christian religion, such as receiving communion, the religion's influence and strength diminish over time. Since society comprises individuals, significant documents like encyclicals address the guidance and well-being of both individuals and society as a whole. Therefore, the text continues with a serious warning and encouragement: It was, in fact, a necessary preventative measure against a complete abandonment of faith that Pope Innocent III, during the Council of the Lateran, strictly mandated that all Christians must receive communion at least during the Easter season. This mandate was specifically intended as a safeguard against a complete loss of religious adherence. The author then questions the current state of various Protestant denominations and nations, asking where their "practical faith in God and in Jesus our divine Redeemer, or in God the Holy Spirit our divine Sanctifyer" now stands. The passage specifically asks about Russia, official England, official Germany, and France, concluding that these entities have prioritized individualism.
styled: And on the other hand it is no less certain that in days when men have ceased to care for this heavenly bread, and have lost their appetite for it, the practice of Christian religion has gradually lost its force and vigor." And because society is made up of individuals these great, great documents, - the encyclicals - pertain to the instruction and the welfare of the individual and society in general alike. Hence it goes on, like a divine admonition and exhortation:" "And indeed it was as a needful measure of precaution against a com- plete falling away that Innocent III., in the Council of the Lateran, most strictly enjoined that no Christian should abstain from receiving the Communion of the Lord's Body at least in the solemn paschal season." Ah! "as a needful measure against a complete falling away ... " Where are any of the protestant sects to-day or the protestant nations in their, "practical faith in God and in Jesus our divine Redeemer, or in God the Holy Spirit our divine Sanctifyer? Where is Russia? Where is official England or official Germany or France? etc? They have followed the individual.

neutral: A state of sin is incompatible with a positive spiritual connection. This principle must also apply to the blameworthy failure to cultivate and practice the faith we have freely received, which has been carefully and diligently nurtured within us from its very inception, with the diligent care of loving parents and tutors. Who can claim to be exempt from such guilt? If gratitude for favors is one of the first and surest indications of intelligence, then, logically and intelligently, we should have the maturity to acknowledge our weakness, our foolishness, our profound irrationality, and our guilt in an objective sense. Such humble acknowledgment is simple and straightforward, providing a clear path forward.
styled: For: "God will not remain in a soul subject (to) sin." But surely this must apply to the culpable neglect to foster and to practice that God-given faith that we have so gratuitously received and which has been so tenderly and conscientiously fostered in our souls, - God himself breathing it into our very immortal souls with loving parents and tutors so providentially solicitous. But, in God's blessed Name, who can claim exemption from such Guilt? I for one could never dare think of such a thing. Can you Doctor? Then, if "gratitude for favors is one of the first and surest indications of intelligence", then, in the name of everything that is logical, and intelligent and holy; let us be men enough to acknowledge our weakness, our stupidity, our real insanity and guilt in the sight of Heaven: thet by such humble acknowledgement - How mercifully simple and easy!

neutral: He eventually became largely opposed to religion, as indicated by his discouragement of a Freemason from investigating the Catholic faith. This information was provided by the Freemason's widow, who herself converted to Catholicism before her death, having requested a priest during her final illness. This event preceded the judge's death by several years; he reportedly died by suicide, hanging himself in secret, seemingly due to self-disgust and general disillusionment. Under the circumstances, and particularly in the individual's current mental and emotional state, a strong aversion to returning home to family is evident. This state has developed over a long period, likely originating from an initial deliberate failure to observe religious duties or some other significant transgression. However, the issue of returning to one's family is of secondary importance and can be resolved in various ways without significant difficulty.
styled: Finally he turned more or less against religion entirely, as it would seem, since he discouraged at least on 32nd degree mason from personally looking into Catholic claims and practices. Of this I was informed by same mason's own widow, who having called for a priest on his death-bed died a Catholic. This was several years before the unfortunate death of the judge, who seemingly having become disgusted with himself and with everything else, went secretly and hanged himself. I think dear Friend: this ought to suffice to convince you that my apprehension as above, is not at all far fetched. . I am not the least surprised Doctor; that under the circumstances and most especially in your present condition of mind and soul, you simply shudder at the thought of returning home to your family. That condition has been a long time growing in your mind and soul, - most probably starting with the first time you deliberately missed your Sunday Mass or some other mortal sin. Going back to your family, however, is a secondary matter and can in a number of ways be bridged over without great difficulties.

neutral: It was noted that you seemed to be striving for what is right and for happiness. For any rational being, this pursuit is fundamentally the same. The hope persists that you continue this effort. This effort, simply to try, is the maximum possible contribution and the fundamental requirement. Success, however, depends on external factors. There is an expectation, and an evaluation will be made regarding the utilization of available means to achieve the anticipated outcome, which will be determined by a principle of fairness. It is regrettable that relatively few individuals consider such an obligation. This leads to a lack of peace for individuals and widespread turmoil—domestically, nationally, and internationally. Everyone seeks peace with an inherent drive, yet for a rational being, peace is only attainable through voluntary alignment with its foundational purpose.
styled: I was happy to see you, as it seemed to me, that you were trying to do the right thing and to be happy. To the rational creature it must mean the same thing. I still hope you are trying. What more can any of us do? Its all the Good God requires or expects of us. - TO TRY. Success must depend on Him. He does expect, however, and He will be the Judge as to whether we will have used the means He offers to insure the success He expects and which His justice will demand. Alas for humanity! How sadly few comparatively, ever think of such an obligation? - Alas! Hence the want of peace for the individual. hence the turmoil! - domestic; - national, - international! Everyone seeking peace, - as positively as the stone in the air seeks rest - and there is no peace for the rational creature except in the willing service of its Creator.

neutral: Kay, I wish you and your family peace—a profound peace that is not widely understood. This peace has been notably promoted by certain historical figures and is, from a theological standpoint, considered the central purpose of a divine figure's earthly life, suffering, and death. Those who promote it are believed to be divinely favored. Doctor, I have wanted to write to you, but I was concerned about causing you embarrassment. I have also wanted to discuss matters with you, but I haven't had the opportunity. I was pleased when you brought the book you referred to as 'Companion of the Summa'. I would have liked to examine it further and discuss it with you, especially regarding the main reason for my visit. To be frank, while I appreciate your treatments, miss them, and thank you for them, they are of secondary importance compared to the state of your spiritual well-being and the risk I perceive you are facing of losing that well-being, along with your belief in a higher power and its associated institutions.
styled: Kay the Lord give you his peace!, you and yours - that peace of which the "world" knows little or nothing; the peace which St. Francis was so astonishingly successful in promoting, the peace to establish which, the Second Person of the Blessed Trinity came down from Heaven and lived, suffered and died as man and the promoters of which, "shall be called the children of God". I have been wanting to write you Doctor but I feared to embarrass you. I have wanted to talk things over but you've escaped me. I was pleased at your bringing that, "Companion of the Summa", as you. called it. I would wish to have seen more of it and to have talked it over with you - in connection with the primary purpose of my visit. For, to be frank, much as I appreciate your treatments and miss them and thank you for them, they must be altogether of secondary importance in face of the condition of your immortal soul and the danger of which I see you to be in of losing it together with your faith in God and His Church.

neutral: Some individuals have adopted atheism, which is characterized as an extreme intellectual flaw, a hopeless conclusion, and a desperate refuge for superficial reasoning. The author also criticizes Protestantism, asserting it lacks certain core religious practices and moral virtues. A funeral took place in Detroit approximately ten to twelve years prior, which was notable for those who attended. It concerned a once-prominent judge who, in his youth and early career, was widely regarded as an exemplary young Catholic. However, for unspecified reasons, he ceased the practice of regular participation in a central religious rite. Gradually, he stopped attending Sunday religious services, and soon after, he abandoned that practice entirely.
styled: To a sad extent they have fallen victims to atheism - the most diabolical cancer, because the climax of intellectual and spiritual insanity, -- at once, -- the hopeless conclusion and the "desperate refuge" of shallow thinking, of perverse and degenerate minds and, almost fearful to say, of damned fools. Hell is its officeal headquarters and none other their supreme knight than Lucifer himself, the prince of diabolical deceivers." Protestantism! Christianity without our eucharistic God! without Holy Communion! ? Christianity without the virtues of the Christian life! We had a memorable funeral in Detroit about ten or twelve years ago, - memorable no doubt for those called to attend it. . A one-time prominent judge who as a youth and as a young professional had been quite commonly looked upon and not infrequently referred to as "a model young Catholic", but who, for some cause or other abandoned the practice of frequent and regular Communion. Little by little he had left off attendence at Holy Mass on Sunday and shortly dropped that practice too, altogether.

neutral: Doctor, you have contributed positively to the community and are widely regarded as a valuable asset. You have utilized your abilities effectively and commendably. Have you not also experienced benefits, feeling a temporary sense of gratitude for the opportunity to serve others? However, will you continue, content only with the personal satisfaction and temporary advantages you gain, including the fleeting approval of an uncritical public? These questions are posed to someone capable of understanding the implications, and who cannot claim ignorance of the matter. Will you persist, until it is too late, in implicitly rejecting established religious institutions, convincing yourself that you can manage without their practices and, by extension, without a divine authority?
styled: But you dear Doctor; while in quite a number of ways you have been doing good - have been an asset and a credit to the Community at least as far as the general public sees. You have used the talents God has lent you to a great extent in a creditable manner. Has not God bles'd you too, and temporarily at least filled your heart with grateful appreciation for the ability to do for Him and for humanity? But are you going to drift on, and into eternity satisfied with the natural "rick you get out of it"? - and the temporal advantages, including in this latter the shadowy credit of an unthinking public? I am asking - addressing - these questions as to a brother who can draw conclusions; as to one who, in the sight of Heaven can not plead ignorance. Are you going to continue till too late, to tacitly defy the Church of the Living God - doping your conscience with the poison of modern atheism, the climax of intellectual and moral in- sanity, that you can get along without the Church and her sacraments and consequently without God? Get along without the Church?

neutral: Thank you for your message of August 2. Misunderstanding is common, but often challenges or errors help us learn and develop a clearer perspective on life and its purpose. I will also offer my good wishes, hoping you find contentment by aligning your intentions with what is beneficial.
styled: Thank you for your kind favor of August 2. The world is full of misunderstanding, but often God uses its mistakes to correct us, to give us the right out- look on life and its eternal destiny. Yes, I shall join my poor prayers to yours so that God may give you the happiness of always conforming your will to His.

neutral: You gave me a treatment on Tuesday. I am grateful for your help and hope to always appreciate it, as I believe that gratitude for assistance is a fundamental sign of intelligence. However, I felt that day that something was on your mind; that you seemed preoccupied and not your usual happy self. In fact, I've had that impression for some time. The next day I led a major religious ceremony, and as has been common for several months, J. P. was frequently on my mind. During a specific prayer, possibly due to intense emotion, when I reached the words concerning the principle of forgiving others as one wishes to be forgiven, I almost faltered. I experienced an internal response to the effect that I could not forgive until the other person forgave. That evening during an evening prayer service, you came to my mind again as I recited a psalm.
styled: it. Dear Doctor: You gave me a treatment on Tuesday. God bless you for I hope that I shall always appreciate such favors - every and all favors; for appreciation means gratitude and: "Gratitude for favors is unquestionably one of the very first and surest indications of intelligence." But I felt that day there was something on your mind; that you were not your own self - happy as you ought to be. In fact I've felt that way more or less right along. The next day I again had the great privilege of singing a High-Mass, and as usual for several months I had J. P. pretty much in my mind. During the "Pater Noster", possibly due to more than ordinary fervor, when I came to the words: " ... sicut nos dimittimus ... " - And forgive us .. as we forgive those who trespass against us", I almost faltered. There was something like an answer or a response in my very soul to the effect: "Unless and until he forgive ..
