styled: We have had cases that I am sure have been more threatening by far than hers, judging from just what you have told me, that have come out better than before afflicted. While waiting to hear from her I am sending you a letter for her, written by one of my reverend brothers to another - ordained just a year apart -- 1911-'12. For five yrs. the elder was hardly ever able to say Holy Mass. Now in his 80th year he says his office and Holy Mass every day. Thanks be to God. I am sure you will all like the letter.

neutral: I read your letter of March 1st late last night, which I had received and noted. Thank you for it. However, I regret that I could not find the name of the woman whose difficult situation you mentioned. I had intended to register her with an association that provides support, which is believed to be a significant factor in the positive outcomes reported to our institutions. Nevertheless, I will register her as best I can, hoping that this simple act will still be beneficial. In the meantime, please send me her name for registration. I would prefer her to write to me herself, as she suggested, and explain the situation as best she can. She should not hesitate. Of course, detailed information is not necessary, but a personal account would naturally be more helpful than a report from someone else. If she makes the effort, as you mentioned, I am confident we can assist her.
styled: God bless you and yours. Only late last night did I get to read your kind favor of March 1st, duely received and noted. Many thanks for same. I rather regret, however, that I failed to find the sister's name whose condition is lamented. I wanted to enroll her in the Seraphic lass Association - a great part of the secret (?) of the many favors reported back to our monasteries, as answers to prayer. I shall enroll her any- how, as best I know, in the hope that possibly the merciful God may deign to smile some way at our "daring simplicity". Adored be His blessed de- signs. In the mean time please send me her name for registration. Rather have her write me as she proposed to do and explain the trouble as best she can. Why should she hesitate? Details are not necessary of course. But something personal would naturally be better than a report from some one else. If, as you tell me, she tries I am sure we will be able to help her.

neutral: When individuals abandon their spiritual or ethical practices, they become vulnerable to Zell. Approximately ten years ago, a tragic death occurred in Detroit. A judge, who in his youth had been publicly praised as an exemplary young Catholic, had, even then, been prone to petty jealousy. Whatever the cause, he gradually ceased his religious practices and eventually abandoned religion entirely, ultimately dying by suicide.
styled: If he has given up the exercise of faith in God and the fostering of religion, rather I'll say that inasmuch as any of us fail in this vital matter, in just so much does the individual stand in danger falling a prey of Zell. Some ten years ago there was a fearfully tragic death in Detroit. A ce tain judge who as a young man had elicited high compliments publicly given as a "practical model of a young Catholic". Even in his youth, however, it would seem the same judge had been naturally inclined to petty jealousy. Whatever the cause, he had little by little given up the practice of his faith - the sad way we are all inclined - and finally abandoned religion entirely and in the end went and hanged himself. May the dear Lord preserve us such a fate!

neutral: I received your February 9th letter last night, which had been forwarded from St. Bonaventure's, Detroit. I was pleased with Jack's "Few Years" report, which exceeded my hopes, and to learn that you and Mrs. Turrell had completed a major religious observance on Christmas. This news was very moving. I congratulate you again on this milestone, as I did during our long-distance call that night. My congratulations also extend to Mrs. Turrell. After we ended the call, I realized I had not asked to speak with her personally to offer my congratulations. I was at St. Bonaventure's that night to receive this news and details directly. When I informed others the next day at dinner, they were very pleased.
styled: It was only last night that I came to your letter of the 9th (Febr.), forwarded hither from St. Bonaventure's, Detroit. How wonderful are not the ways of / Lord as well as His works! I surely was pleased with Jack's Few Years report - almost surpassing my most cherished hopes, that your- self and poor, dear little Irs. Turrell too had received your First Koly Communion on Christmas. It surely brought a tear to my eye, as even now it does writing about it. I once more am glad to congratulate you on your privilege as on that night I did on long-distance. Of course the same goes for Mrs. Turrell as I felt it did that night. I was surprised after we hung up that I did not ask to speak to her personally to con- gratulate her too, but then I thought; its better instead, that we just turn to God and thank Him, the divine source of such graces, such happi- ness, such consolations. Fortunately I was in St. Bonaventure's that night to receive such tidings and particulars, directly. When I told the others next day at dinner they were more than pleased.

neutral: Salesius and the others present who knew you in Bast were informed of my pleasant experiences meeting you two years ago in Los Angeles. I recounted how I contacted Mrs. Turrell, surprising her on the phone, and about our children's event the next day. I also mentioned Jack's details regarding the story of Anthony, which significantly influenced him, changing his hesitation into determination. A senior member of the group thoughtfully remarked, "That is quite a remarkable case." I've been considering lately, especially since Jack and all of you are rightly concerned about his success, even as a manager. Furthermore, given that the story of Anthony seemed to profoundly influence Jack's decision to continue his training and join the organization, we should proceed with confidence, trusting in Anthony's perceived support, and persist until Jack completes the task that Anthony may have intended when he inspired his protégé.
styled: Father Salesius especially and the others present who knew you while here in the Bast. When I told them of my pleasant experiences on meeting you two years ago in Los Angeles, how I had gotten in touch (with) Mrs. Turrell, surprising her on the phone and about our "children's Mass next day, Jack, with his details about St. Anthony, so tragicly changing his hesitation to determination, etc; Father Provincial thoughtfully remarked: "That is quite a remarkable case." I've been thinking of late, especially since Jack and you all are so rightly solicitous about his success, even as a manager, God will- ing, - why not? - and especially since Saint Anthony seemed so solicitous himself as to give "his life for Jack's decision" to continue instructions and actually join the true Church, we should go after him with confidence in his intercession and not let him rest till he finish the work he had possibly in his mind when (he) awakened his protege,

neutral: The passage defines "Religice" as the study of a beneficial relationship, characterized by dependence, with a divine entity and other individuals. Despite the existence of numerous systems or denominations within this field, the underlying science of religion is considered singular. It is the individual's responsibility, through the application of reason and in conjunction with divine assistance, to discern and select the most appropriate system among them. This selection significantly impacts an individual's personal tranquility and the harmony of their community, as well as their prospects for lasting contentment beyond life. It is highly probable that the difficulties being experienced stem from a deficit in this understanding or a lack of religious practice. This leads one to conclude that neither individual has made substantial progress in this severely overlooked field of study. Any past status or actions of your husband offer an insignificant basis for current reliance. He was certainly never an Apostle or an archangel. Judas was; Lucifer was.
styled: "RELIGICE, THE SCIENCE OF OUR HAPPY RELATIONSHIP ( dependence on), WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR". Furthermore, while there may be a thousand different systems of that science -- a thousand various denominations - the science of religion remains one. Its up to the individual with the use of reason, cooperating with God's grace to find which is the best system and to choose it rather than any other. On his choice depends to a vast extent, his own peace and that of the community - as well as their hope for eternal happiness hereafter. Kost probably the trouble of which you complain is an effect, a simple consequence of want of this science, lack of religion. One is almost forced to conclude that neither of you are much advanced in this appallingly neglected science. As to what your husband was once upon a time is a mighty small matter for him to "bank on". He certainly was never one of the Apostals or an archangel. Judas was. Lucifer was.

neutral: On March 26, 1943, Mrs. W.'s husband, a Methodist, had been deemed terminally ill with brain cancer after a third operation, with doctors expecting him to die within six months. (His first operation was on February 23rd). That afternoon, a weeping Mrs. W. was introduced by a neighbor who was Catholic. She stated she would do anything if her husband's life could be spared. Mrs. W. was advised to make a personal commitment: if her husband's condition surprisingly improved by the end of the week (it was Tuesday at the time), she should seriously investigate the relationship between her religious denomination and the Catholic Church. The following Friday, Mr. W. returned, bandaged but smiling. He had been discharged from the University Hospital in Ann Arbor the previous day, Wednesday. Doctors Wood and Pete had described his recovery as miraculous.
styled: Lest I be mistaken, However, here it is in brief. 'March 26, 1943. Mrs. W. ... W. was a methodist, had been given up after the third operation on a brain- cancer as destined for death inside six months. (The first opera- tion was on February 23rd). Mrs. Wh. weeping was introduced same after-noon by a Catholic neighbor. .. "Ill do anything to please the good God if he'll only spare my poor, dear husband"., she answered. "Then, Mrs. W.", answered, "This is about what I would advise you. "Make a promise or proposition to Almighty God in your ovm honest way as a methodist, that if your husband gives the doc- tors a surprise tomorrow or by the end of the week (it was Tuesday), you'll be earnest in looking into the difference or rather the re- lationship between your denomination and the "Mother Church". .... They returned the following Friday with Mr. W. all taped-up but smiling. He had come home from the Univ .- hospital in Ann Arbor next day Wed. Doctors Wood and Pete had pronounced his recovery miraculous.

neutral: The author has read the letter and expresses sympathy for both the recipient and their husband. The author states a particular concern for the husband, believing he faces a greater risk to his final outcome, which the author suggests could be averted if the recipient were to change their fundamental beliefs. The recipient states that Grace Panyard guided them to this point and also that they do not share the author's faith. Regardless of the recipient's beliefs, the author believes their very being needs to be secured for its final well-being, and the author is willing to help achieve that. The author presumes the recipient identifies as a Christian of some denomination. If this is correct, the author argues that stating a lack of shared faith is mistaken, as the author believes there is only one form of Christianity. The author encourages the recipient to consider this perspective. The author elaborates further, stating that if religion can be defined as a science, then it is not merely a science but the most significant science across all eras and generations. The author asserts it is the only science that ultimately matters, rendering all other sciences meaningless without it.
styled: I have just read your pathetic letter and do surely sympathize with both you and your husband, - with him possibly the more, because of his greater danger of losing his soul, unless you be induced to turn back to God. You tell me as much as that our friend Grace Panyard guided you hither and again that you are not "of my faith". Whatever you be, you have an immortal soul - your ownself - to save for God; and I am glad to help you do that. I presume that you are a Christian of some denomination. If I am right, then in saying you do not belong to my faith, you err in a way; because there is only one Christianity. Think a little and see if I'm right. I go further. If religion can be defined as a science, and I claim it is not only a science but the very greatest science of all times and of every generation; in fact the only science that in the end counts for aught, and without which all other sciences are vain allusions. Ah!

neutral: On October 18th, a year and a half later, the two individuals returned for what would be their final visit. The man appeared to be in perfect health, showing no signs of prior illness. This visit occurred two nights after the woman had contacted the narrator by phone, expressing concern about the man's health. The narrator had urged her to fulfill a commitment she had made months earlier, contingent on her husband's recovery. Additionally, the narrator had provided her with a copy of a book titled "Mystical City of God," described as a biography of a significant religious figure. The narrator considered it to be an autobiography, with its author, Mary of Jesus of Ágreda, acting as a transcriber. The man, in particular, seemed enthusiastic about the book that night, having evidently spent the preceding days actively reading it.
styled: October 18th a year and a half later they came back - the last time I saw them and he looked and acted as he'd never been sick. This, however, was two nights after she had phoned me, lament- ing that he was not well, etc, and I had admonished her to do some- thing toward the fulfilling of the promese she had made so many months before, if her husband were spared her. Besides, I had given her a copy of the "Mystical City of God", - the winderful Life of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which I honestly consider her own autobiography; the actual writer being as her secretary Venerable Mother Mary of Jesus, of Agrada Spain. He especially seemed enthused over the book that night - had evid- been on the "job" of reading the book, those couple of days.

neutral: Wishing you and your friends well. It is hoped that you are well and that your friend, the patient, is not declining. Your message was received several nights ago, and M. O'Laugh'n was enrolled in a designated spiritual support program as an emergency case. Today, your special contribution was received, and a perpetual member is being enrolled, as the enclosed document will show. Several notable cases of recovery have been reported through this method, both locally and in places like Detroit and elsewhere. Instead of detailing instructions for anyone to follow, a brief summary will be provided of a letter written several months ago to a Presbyterian whose father, grandfather, and great-grandfather were all Presbyterian ministers. This individual is believed to be undergoing instruction or may have already converted to Catholicism. In fact, two non-Catholic cases are involved here. The letter continues: "I am sure Mr. R.J., I told you of the W. case, which was noted here approximately two months before yours."
styled: God bless you and your friends, and us all. I hope you are well and that your friend-patient is not losing. We received your wire some nights ago and enrolled M. O'Laugh'n in the Seraphic Mass Association as an emergency case. Today we received your special and are enrolling as the enclosed will indicate, a perpetual member. Thanks be to the merciful God, we have had several notable cases of cures reported as through this means here as, especially in Detroit, and esewhere. Rather than detail instructions what for anyone to follow, I am going to give you here a brief resume of a letter I wrote several months back to a presbiterian whose father, grand-father and great- grandfather were all presbiterian ministers and who I believe is now taking instructions or is possibly already a practical Catholic. In fact there are two cases here involved, - bothe noncatholic, therefore, Seery or an O' would say: "on the other side of the fence". It follows about thus: " ... I am sure dear Mr. R.J., I tolde you of the W. case, noted here just about two months ahead of yous.

neutral: It is difficult for anyone except a parent to fully comprehend the impact of such a death on the author's in-law. The man appeared to be in a state of bewilderment, and this experience prompted him to reflect more deeply on fundamental aspects of life. However, this was not the most severe hardship. Just six years later, after a brief illness, his wife, Kathleen, also died, leaving him to raise three children on his own as best he could. He communicated that initially, he questioned if hope could ever return. However, this event appeared to be a turning point. The most profound lesson he had ever experienced—her consistent display of strong moral principles—had fostered an admiration for such values within him.
styled: But you were considerate in the details of your letters to me and I hope these may be to good in one way or more, so just briefly, I am inclined to believe it difficult for anyone except a parent to realize what such a death must have meant to my in-law. The poor man just seemed to wonder. It certainly made him think more deeply about essentials. However, that was not the worst. Just six years later after a brief illness, his said Kathleen also was taken; leaving him three children to mother for himself as best he might. He wrote me at the time that at first he had just wondered like if the sun might shine again. This, however, seemed to be the turning-point. The greatest sermon he had ever witnessed -- her example of never failing Christian virtues -- had planted seeds of admiration for Christian faith in his

neutral: I hope you are well, as your interesting letter suggests you are doing reasonably well despite the difficult loss of your patient wife, Mercile. I would have liked to have seen her and offered comfort before it was too late. Specifically, I would have encouraged her in her demonstration of virtues such as patience and acceptance, and her spiritual convictions. It is considered a valuable act to assist someone in their final struggle, offering spiritual comfort and encouragement when circumstances appear dark and hopeless. From what you have written about her struggles and challenges, it appears she learned much of the important skill of facing death with grace. Separately, an atheist relative by marriage lost his eldest child ten years ago while traveling with his family to the diamond jubilee of his wife's parish, St. Joseph's in Prescott, Wisconsin.
styled: God bless you and yours. I hope you are well, as evidently you are not too bad to write such an interesting letter as that which I have just read from your pen. And all notwithstanding your trying berievement of losing your dear, patient Wife Mercile. I surely would like to have seen her and consoled her before it were too late. Rather I should say, to encourage her in her acts and disposi- tions of faith, hope, charity, patience, resignation, confidence in God etc. What a privilege; what a happiness to have been of assistence to anyone in their final struggle and to have whispered an encouraging prayer into the ear of the patient when naturally everything must seem dark and hopeless! From what you have written of her, however, with all her struggles and humiliations, etc, I think she must have learned quite a little of the one most important art of "dying well". Incidently, I had an "atheist" in-law lose his eldest born, ten years ago on his way with his family to the diamond jubilee of his wife's parish - St. Joseph's in Prescott, Wis.

neutral: If you frequently engage in sincere and humble reflection, seeking guidance not only for yourself but especially for each of the friends you mentioned, you should not feel particularly anxious about the important matter of your vocation. In the meantime, we will offer our support and good wishes for your intentions.
styled: If you go to the divine Headquarters by receiving holy Communion frequent- ly, and earnestly and humbly plead with the divine Spouse of our souls for guidance not only for yourself but particularly for each of those friends of whom you write - I am sure you will have nothing to be par- ticularly anxious concerning the important matter of your vocation. In the meantime of course we will be glad to include your inten- tions in our poor prayers.

neutral: Tommy has grown and is doing well. A photograph was taken beside the Chapel of St. Felix Monastery on November 4, 1947. Wishing Mrs. O'Flaherty and her family continued well-being. Apologies for the delayed acknowledgment. Thank you. An intention to write a letter was not fulfilled. Human capabilities can serve a greater purpose, provided human plans do not obstruct that purpose.
styled: So glad "little Tommy" is bigger now and doing so well Thanks be to God. Snapped to the side of the Chapel St. Felix Monastery, Nov. 4th 1947. God bless you, Mrs. O'Flaherty. I hope you are all continuing well. Please pardon delayed acknowledgment. Many thanks. I wanted to write you a letter : but ---! "God condescends to use our powers If we don't spoil His plans by ours."

neutral: In that location, I and several of my siblings, including one brother who was a Reverend, had undergone a baptism ceremony. He was considered an atheist because he had received little or no religious instruction during childhood regarding God or religious principles, and as a result, had not affiliated with any religious denomination. He was, however, a person of good character and moral conduct. Influenced by the exemplary conduct of his wife, Kathleen C'Brien (her maiden name), and the serene atmosphere of their home, which was characterized by regular prayer, he had come to admire the strong faith she practiced and fostered, which was a source of hope and genuine compassion. Their son drowned in Chicago while they were traveling to the Jubilee. This occurred on his seventh birthday. They transported the child's body, and it was buried in her family plot, a short distance from the graves of my two younger sisters who had died within a single week in 1878, when I was eight years old.
styled: That was where myself and a number of my brothers and sisters had been baptized, including one of my Rev. brothers. I said "atheist" because he had never been taught much, if anything in childhood, about God and the science of religion and consequently had never joined any denomination. He was a good, clean-living man, however, and from the outstanding example of his wife - Kathleen C'Brien her maiden name - and the sweet prayers and peace pervading his home as a result; he had learned to admire the wonderful faith, so inspiring of hope and real supernatural charity, she practiced and fostered. The son drowned in Chicago on their way to the Jubilee. It happened on his seventh birthday. They took the little corpse along and we buried it in her family plot a few paces from the graves of my two little sisters who died in one week when I was eight, 1878. Pardon such details.

neutral: The communication dated the 8th has been reviewed. While its content was somewhat concerning, it does not suggest a need for excessive worry. Good housekeepers and good businesspeople ensure that everything has a designated place and is kept there. This reflects an underlying principle of order and purpose, suggesting that every individual also has a specific role within a larger system. A supreme power could create individuals directly, without parents. This power could also impart knowledge without formal education or institutions, and facilitate significant spiritual experiences without the need for religious officiants. However, this overarching system or power has chosen to involve its intelligent beings, assigning them roles in its operations according to their individual abilities. More accurately, this involves their participation and cooperation in the unfolding of this universal activity. Therefore, there is no need for excessive worry about matters that are inherently of greater concern to this supreme power than to any individual.
styled: God bless you and yours. I have just read your favor of the 8th - pathetic enough in its way, though indicating nothing to be over anxious about. Good housekeepers and good busines-men are careful to have "a place for everything and everything in its place." In this they show a trace of the divine character of the universal Guide and Master, Who of course, has a place for each one of us. He, the Creator and Divine Governer of the universe in all its details, could create children as in the case of Adam and Eve without parents. He could teach little children without nuns or schools and give the holy sacraments as has been the case on several occasions, - without priests, therefore. In His divine economy, however, God has been pleased to honor His creatures- most especially His rationals - by giving them, each accord- ing to his ability, a part of His own work to do. Rather I ought to say, by participation and cooperation in His won divine activity, etc. Why be over anxious, therefore, about something that God himself is infinitely more solicitous than any of His creatures can be?

neutral: November 4th. Thank you again for your generous support of October 16th. Thank you specifically for enrolling me. Your enrollment brings the total to about a dozen perpetual enrollments I have received this year, and I do not know how many annual enrollments I have had. The ongoing benefits we have reported through this association have given me an appreciation for such enrollments that I would not have gained otherwise. Regarding the adoption of children, I view it in accordance with the principle that helping the most vulnerable is an act of great importance. Given the late hour, this communication will conclude for now. This year, we have 24 promising novices. We could assign a hundred more priests to domestic and international missions if they were available. P.S. Congratulations on joining the Franciscans.
styled: November 4th. Again many thanks for your generous favor of October 16th. May the dear Lord bless you for same. Thank you specially for enrolling me. Yours must make about a dozen perpetual enrollments I've had this Jubilee year, and I have no idea how often I've been enrolled annually. The continued favors we have reported as through this association gives me an appreciation for such enrollments that I could hardly have otherwise. Thanks be to God. .. As to taking children for adoption, I look at that according to our dear Lord's own appreciation: "What you have done for the least of my brethren You have done to me. " -- It is getting late now: So. I'll say Good Night for the present and clerical novitiate. This year Thanks be we have 24 promising novices. to God. We could place a hundred more priests if we had them -- in home and foreign missions. P.S. Congratulations on your joining the privileged Family of the Franciscans.

neutral: Thank you for your letter, received a month ago. It has been noted. I have been intending to write a comprehensive reply, but haven't found the opportunity. I hope Mr. Flaherty is well by now, and that Tommy continues to enjoy his time at the Seminary. It is fortunate to appreciate and embrace the path one has chosen. This principle applies to all chosen paths, as it is a privilege to contribute in any capacity. Even natural elements like flowers, birds, and bees contribute.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of just a month ago -- duly received and noted. I've had it right here waiting to get a chance to write worth while and it just seems such a time never comes; I do hope that by this time Mr. Flaherty is quite o.k. and that Tommy continues to like it in the Seminary more and more. Indeed that is a grace initself for which we should never cease praying viz. to be grateful for and love the vocation to which, in His great mercy God has called us. This of course really applies to every vocation, for after all, What a privilege to serve God in even the least capacity! -- Nay even as an irrational as the flowers and the birds! and the bees that praise the Lord providing for man. !

neutral: It is challenging for anyone to fully appreciate such a significant role. Our best efforts are all that can be expected. Please remember to submit the name of your friend who is facing difficult circumstances. Also, encourage as many people as possible to offer support and positive thoughts, not only for her but also for many others in challenging situations, including those in hospitals. These individuals often do not believe in extraordinary or unexplained phenomena and are skeptical of remarkable interventions. The hope is that a significant event might lead them to consider seeking a new perspective, which is readily accessible.
styled: How little it is possible for any mere creature to be adequately grateful for such a privileged calling! We can only try and that suffices. Do not forget to send in the name of your little "hopeless case" friend, and to have as many as possible to offer prayers and holy Communions, not only for her but for so many more sadly unfortunate "big shots" in hospitals and elsewhere who, having little or no faith, in the super- natural, refuse to believe in even the possibility of miracles, and who by a manifest miracle might be induced to at least pray for the gift of faith -- which Almighty God is only waiting to be asked for. Sincerely

neutral:
A letter was received several weeks ago. Attempts to enroll the individual referred to as a "hopeless case" in an organization were delayed because no name was provided for enrollment. To clarify a suggested course of action, details are provided about a significant past case, likely unknown to the recipient.

On Saturday, January 10, 1925, the recipient's parents were brought to a specific institution in Detroit by a neighbor from Port Huron. The father was largely unable to speak but attempted to describe his condition, stating that doctors had diagnosed "ulcers of the stomach." It was later understood that he had been sent home with a diagnosis of incurable cancer. He was informed about the organization and encouraged to contribute to its charitable activities. The individual's name, Mr. Eagen, was then recorded, and he was offered the option of permanent enrollment if desired.
styled: I recieved your very interesting letter several weeks ago and started a number of times to enroll your little "hopless case" in the Seraphic Mass Association; and each time I found no name to record. Consequently post- poned further action. Now I am going to give you a few particulars about that notable case that you probably never heard. Then you will easily conclude something as to what I would suggest and advise. It was Saturday Morning January 10th 1925 that a neighbor-friend of theirs from Port Huron, brought your dear Parents to the St. Bonaventure Monastery in Detroit. Your poor Father was hardly able to talk. He tried, however, to tell briefly how he felt and that the doctors said he had "ulsers of the stomach". Later on I learned that they had sent him home as a hopeless case of cancer. I told him quite a little about the Ser -- Mass Association and suggested that he do something for the missions. "Now I have you name Mr. Eagen." I said. "And you can enroll perpetually if you wish.

neutral: Wishing you and your family a happy Thanksgiving once again. And especially if I don't communicate with you again before then, I wish you a happy Christmas celebration, along with success for the upcoming New Year and beyond.
styled: Wishing you and yours God's blessing again for a happy day of national Thanksgiving; and especially in case you do not in the mean time hear from me again, the grace of a blessed and happy Christmas celebration with all success for the coming New Year and thereafter. Sincerely Yours in Christ.

neutral: If funds were insufficient, it was advised that he enroll for only one year initially, with a commitment to perpetual enrollment once circumstances allowed, provided things progressed favorably. He responded with a weak, trembling voice, affirming his intention. He appeared to be 75 years old or older; his wife also appeared elderly. Eight days later, on a Sunday morning, he drove his own car to fulfill his commitment. Based solely on their appearance, they were barely recognizable. However, the moment he spoke, he was recognized as the individual from Port Huron. He appeared thirty years younger. He was, in fact, only thirty-nine years old at that time. He then asked for an opinion regarding the doctors in Port Huron's recommendation for an X-ray. He was then asked about the cost, which was stated as $25. His wife, who was smiling, was then asked for her opinion. Both individuals were smiling broadly. She exclaimed that he did not need it, pointing to his appearance. The narrator then said, "Listen."
styled: If you are anyway short, however, I would advise that you enroll for just a year now and promise a perpetual enrollment as soon as convenient, if things go favorably." With a feeble quivering voice he answered: "I sure will." I took him to be 75 years old or upwards; Your poor Mother looked old too. Sunday morning eight days later your Father dove his own car down to keep his promise. From their appearance alone I would hardly have known them; but themoment he spoke I thought: "This is the fellow from Port Huron!" He looked thirty years younger. He was only thirty-nine at the time. . "But Father"; he said, "The I doctors in Pt. Huron want to take an exray ... What do you think?" asked him : "How much is it going to cost you?" " ... $25." "What do you think?" I asked your smiling Mother, They were bothe smiling all over. "Father, he don't need it. Look at him!" she exclaimed. "Listen." I said.

neutral: Thank you for your assistance from several weeks ago. I intended to acknowledge it sooner and hope my delay does not cause any offense. However, I want to thank you not only for this assistance, but also to express our deep appreciation for your generous involvement over the past several years in the important and challenging work of international humanitarian efforts. I am confident that you have been rewarded in many ways for your practical interest in this significant charitable work. Additionally, I want to commend you for the way you wrote about a business associate, the young man you offered condolences to regarding the death of his kind mother. It is always a relief to know of such a person. The fact that he was a diligent student of religious texts should be seen as a positive attribute. This is notable, even though, without appropriate direction, many who study religious texts have adopted problematic views.
styled: God bless you this blessed day of the Lord, - you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of several weeks back. I started a number of times to acknowledge same. I hope my tardiness may not scandalize. Not only this favor, however, do I want to thank you, but more I want to assure you of our appreciation of your generous activity these several years in the really privileged, though not less arduous work of the holy foreign missions. I am sure that the Good God will bless - has blessed - you in many ways for your practical interest in this outstanding phase of really Catholic action. Besides this, I want to congratulate you on your having been so guided as to be able to write of a business associate as you do of the young man with whom you condole on the death of his amiable mother. It is always a relief to know of such a person. The very fact of his having been a "bible student" ought to spell something in his favor. This, even though, for want of proper guidance, many a "bible student" has anchored in dangerous waters.

neutral: The passage suggests that despite the current prevalence of atheism, it is considered a positive development when individuals show significant interest in the messages conveyed through the Bible. This is presented as a clear indication of the decline of the public education system, which is believed to be reversible only through the intervention of genuine religious principles. styled: But these days when atheism, the very climax of intellectual stupidity, of moral insanity, of diabolically devilish perversity; it is a hopeful indication to see anyone of good will taking more than ordinary interest in the divine messages from Heaven as are those conveyed to humanity through the inspired writings, the divinely guided compilation and the appreciative, prayerful study of the Holy Bible. This all the more now, that in the family of governments one of even the "big powers" is not only permitted to show its shamelessly criminal face, but brazenly to insist on dictating hell's own principles of peace. Indeed an unmistakable indication whither our godless system of public-education is, not only tending but tumbling; unless by an effective S.O.S. call of true religion. Pardon my digression. I would have enrolled your friend-associate as also his deceased mother, but I did find their names. I have no doubt but that they would both profit thereby. So if you just send me their names I shall be glad to do that for you and for them.

neutral: A promise was made to include a specific group in a future activity, contingent on forgetting a scheduled appointment. The individual then decided to allocate half of the activity's benefit to this group. For several months, he made weekly visits. On February 29th, with his family present and having included others as was his custom, he requested that the specific group be included as promised, allocating $14 from a total of $25. Years later, the narrator visited an elderly woman in Smith's Creek who subsequently died of stomach cancer. The father of the letter's recipient, learning of this visit, took the narrator to a particular farm, where the narrator saw a child named Dorothy. The narrator expressed a long-held hope for Dorothy to pursue a particular life path, which the narrator regarded as an exceptionally rare and significant honor, comparable to being specially chosen for a supreme role.
styled: "You make a promise to the poor souls in Purgatory, that if you are able to forget that apointment tomorrow, you'll enroll them for a part of it." "Gee!" he said, "I'll give them half of it. I'll go them fifty-fifty." After that he drove down every week for several months. Febr. 29th - I believe he had the whole Family down - having enrolled some other, as he nearly always did, he concluded about as follows: "Now Father; I want to enroll the Poor Souls as I promised them I would. Put them down for a good half of that $25. - fourteen dollars." Some years afterwards I was up to see an old lady in Smith's Creek who died shortly after with cancer of the stomach and your Father having heard of my visit came and took me over to see the little farm you refer to and I remember seeing little Dorothy. Congratulations on my "dream" even then of her vocation. Try at least to become appreciative for such a really surpassing privilege. - Think of it Sister M.C. of. .. A chosen spouse from among millions, - a spouse of the eternal King/kings!

neutral: Thank you for your letter dated May 6th. I do not clearly recall the issue you mentioned from December, as I often confuse different cases. styled: Many thanks for your favor of May 6th. It is rather hazey in my memory what your trouble was in December, since I get different cases often mixed. However, I feel you are taking a practil way for any and every "hopeless" -- so called. neutral: Wishing a speedy recovery. Warm regards to Mrs. Turner, a special member. Please do not worry. Best wishes to Mrs. Turner. If courage is a major factor in overcoming challenges, then unwavering confidence ensures certain success, irrespective of the objective outlook.
styled: for a speedy recovery, God willing. Special member God bless you Mrs. Turner, Do not worry. God bless you Mrs. Turner. If "courage is half the battle" then with confidence in God it must mean sure triumph -- whatever the natural outlook.

styled: Many thanks for your charitable favor of Dec. 22nd duely received and noted. Only To-day, however, did read it. I've been "half down" for several weeks and have not been in condition. Thanks be to God for it all and that things are clearing up again You were right · about the Poor Souls, I did refer to those in Purgatory primarily. You idea further is right too. So many poor Souls. I am glad to know that you know from actual experience so much about the benefits of the Ser. Mass Ass'n. I hope it brings the hoped-for results.

neutral: Thank you for your communication dated July 19. I hope your intention is fulfilled, provided it is beneficial to you. I do not believe I know Mrs. Jennie Ferreri personally, and cannot recall her at present.
styled: Thank you for your kind favor of July 19. I shall pray that the good Lord will grant your intention, if it is for the good of your soul. I do not think that I know Mrs. Jennie Ferreri personally, at least I can't recall her just now.

styled: As to the stole proposition; well I do not remember or know of any one specially in need of such a prized garment jus off-hand now. Probably the simplest solution would be to give the equivalent to some one in immediate touch with the mission-work going on in so many places. I am sure Brother Rufin or any one at the desk in St. Bonaventure's in Detroit would be able and pleased to receive the favor. neutral: Encourage a contented acceptance within yourselves, as exemplified by Mrs. Turner's statement: "I have reduced my prayers for a complete cure, feeling that perhaps my constant inconvenience may assist those in need and contribute to the moral improvement of others." She also stated, "God knows my needs," and similar sentiments. This suggests cultivating trust in a higher power, which is considered highly beneficial and personally advantageous. Such acceptance and trust is a significant benefit in itself, which should always be encouraged. Promoting veneration of the Virgin Mary through the practices of the rosary and the scapular is believed to bring immense benefits to you and your family. Continue these efforts, as there is profound appreciation for such a uniquely chosen and highly regarded figure, considered the mother of a divine entity and queen of all creation. This figure, through immense benevolence, wisdom, and compassion, is believed to have been bestowed upon humanity, provided she is valued.
styled: God bless you, and keep you fostering the happy resignation in your souls which looms out in that little word of Mrs. Turner: "I have eased up on offering prayers for a complete cure; feeling that perhaps my constant inconvenience may help the poor Souls and also in the conversion of poor sinners." And then again: "God knows my needs, etc., etc. That really sounds lile fostering confidence in God, than which hardly anything can be more pleasing to God and at the same time more profitable to our own poor souls. Such resign- ation and Confidence is a great grace in itself, which we should at all time and in all circumstances foster. Your promotion of devotion to our dear Bl. Virgin Mother Mary by means of the rosary and the scapular will surely bring untold blessings on you and yours. By all means keep it up. for we can never be to grateful enough to such a singlarly chosen and privileged blessed Queen of the entire creation, God's own blessed Mother, whom, in His infinite condescention, wisdom and mercy has deigned to give to each and all of us if we only appreciate.

neutral: Bernard, discussing the concept of scandal, concluded: "Given the profound offense caused by the execution of Jesus, it is never rational to allow oneself to be similarly offended by other events." This event was considered the most extreme offense of all. Yet, a divine entity transformed this event into a means of deliverance for those destined to be saved. The ways of this divine entity are indeed mysterious; its judgments are beyond understanding, and its methods are unfathomable. Regarding you, Agnes Carmel; after reading the initial pages of your extensive letter, I am convinced that your mental state is entirely sound. It appears to me that you have been experiencing hardship on behalf of others—most likely your parents and family—and simultaneously undergoing humbling experiences that lead to your refinement. You should express gratitude for being given such a task. Perhaps it would be more accurate to say for having it imposed upon you, as you would otherwise likely not have had the courage to agree to it. I refer to the personal cost it has entailed for you. And the triumph (over adversity and offense) has not yet been achieved.
styled: Bernard had this in mind when speaking of scandal he concludes: "Since the scandal of the Crucifiction of Jesus Christ it is never reasonable to take scandal." For that was surely the most terrible scandal of all. And still Almighty God has turned it into the salvation of those who will be saved. O the mysterious ways of the Lord! "How incomprehensible are His Judgement! And how un- seachable His ways!" As for yourself dear Sister Agnes Carmel; since I read the first half dozen pages of your big letter, I have been convinced that there is nothing wrong with your mind atall. It has seemed to me that you have been suffering for someone else - most likely for just your same dear Parents and folks, and of course at the sametime for your humiliation and con-sequently your purification. You really ought to thank God for offering you such a mission. I might rather say for imposing it on you; for other- wise you woul hardly have had the courage to consent to it. I mean to the sacrifice it has cost you. And the victory (over the devil and scandal), is not as yet gained.

Dear Sister Agnes Carmel: After the above conclusion I read your interesting letter of April 27th last, which I should have taken time to do before writing; and again as before I would stress the necessity of humble patience -- of patient humility. neutral: When I received your last letter, in which you requested the return of that long letter, I didn't know where I had put it and was therefore unable to return it. A few days ago I found it and decided again to write to your father to see if I can do something to promote his well-being and that of his family. I am sure that after these long years of separation from religious community and practices, he must be longing for a change of some kind. I am confident that he will find the support he needs, as I believe he genuinely wants to do what is right. This is especially important since I haven't heard from you—or about him—in a long time, and the overall situation may have changed.
styled: At the time of your last letter, when you requested the return of said long letter, I did not really know where I had put it and consequently had to let go. Just a few days ago I came across it and I decided again to write to your Father and see if possibly I can do somthing to promote peace in his poor soul and in his family; for I am sure that after these long years of estrangement from the Church, from the Holy Sacraments and from religion which alone promotes peace that the world can not give, He must be longing for a change of some kind. I have no doubt God will have mercy on him and help us. For I believe he has a heart that wants to do right. I thought, therefore, dear Sister Agnes Carmel that before I would write him, I would ask you about any change that possibly has come to your Father since you wrote me about him. This es- pecially sinc it is so long that I have not heard from you - and about him, And otherwise too the outlook may have changed.

styled: God bless you Mrs. Alvera McCarroll. I am glad to hear from you though sorry to learn of your poor dear Husband's affliction. However, it must be for some good purpose and will turn out to have been such if you keep courage while battling along and making the best of the situation. Try and have your Husband and friends go to Holy Communion more frequently with you. Nothing like frequent communion to bring peace into a family or into a soul. At the same time it fosters faith in God and heavenly relationships - with all God's dear ones gone ahead of us. Many thanks for your prayers for poor Fr. Solanus. styled: -- are natur- ally providential guards against one of the very greatest dangers to genious, "the big-head". styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of a week ago. I certainly do remember you and your folks. How fortunate you have been in the faith God has given us strengthening it so often by super- natural responses to prayer -- as in the case of your dear Father Earl -- with his "hopeless" cancer! Glad to know he is well as also your little Sister Dorothy -- now V. Sister Mary Celia -- also wrote me. I have told hundreds of your Father's case when they brought him first time to St. Bonaventure's January 10, 1925, and how he surprised us when eight days later he brought your good Mother with him driving his own car -- looking 25 years younger !.

neutral:

The letter was written by a friend of mine whose outstanding courage and perseverence in the face of unbelievable odds and handicaps I have since more than fifteen years admired. It is by one whose earnestness and honesty and really deep thinking has been proven beyond the shadow of an honest or reasonable doubt. And that "poor-guy-friend" of mine and, if you will, possibly one of God's very least brethren," is Dr. A. J. Kraus. in many ways an

neutral: If gratitude for receiving benefits is considered a primary indicator of intelligence, and if existence itself is regarded as one's initial benefit, then an atheist's ingratitude inherently suggests a severe lack of intelligence. Consequently, regardless of any other talents or brilliance, such an individual would be deemed fundamentally unintelligent. A notable illustration of such extreme lack of appreciation and ingratitude is found in the narrative of Lucifer and his followers, which, in that context, led to a significant reduction in the population of a celestial realm and necessitated the creation of a punitive domain, described as the most severe confinement facility imaginable.
styled: In fact, if "Gratitude for favors is one or the very first and surest indications of intelligence", and again if according to all logical reasoning, one's first possible benefit is his crea- tion; then the ingratitude of the atheist, must of its very nat- ure - without further proof or parley - condemn him with his atheism as most woefully wanting in intelligence; and consequently, whatever his tallents or brilliance my be otherwise, must rate him as an unqualified fool. The most fearful example of such insane want of appredation and of such damnable ingratitude, is that of Lucifer and his reprobate legions, where-Heaven itself was depop- ulated and Hell's creation was made necessary - the most terrible prison-asylum ever designed or conceived.

neutral: If a rational being's primary purpose is to understand its origin and relate to it positively, and if, according to certain texts, only an irrational person would deny the existence of a supreme being, then it would logically follow that the existence of this supreme being must be evident, in some form, to all rational individuals. Consequently, every normal, thinking person is capable of and obligated to acknowledge this origin and show reverence. Failure to do so would result in ultimate loss and severe suffering. However, given the profound importance of this matter, merely meeting the minimum requirement would be insufficient. The preceding points do not fully address what is truly needed or desired.
styled: If the primary purpose of my creation as a rational crea- ture is to know my Creator so that I can love Him and serve Him and be happy with Him; amd if according to Holy Writ, no one but a fool can say in his heart, "There is no God"; then the necessary conclu- sion would seem to be that God's existence, at least, must be mani- fest, one way or other, to every one who is not a fool; consequent- ly, that every normal person able to think, can and ought to recog- nize his Creator - can and must worship God. And this under pain of losing everything good in the end and of damning his own soul - "cast out out into exterior darkness, where there shall be weep- ing and gnashing of teeth". However, in a matter of such tremendous importance it would be nothing less than positively criminal to be satisfied with the minimum. The foregoing is simply no answer atall to what we ought to have, -- and Please God to what we shall have.

neutral: A wise person should not boast about their wisdom, a strong person about their strength, or a rich person about their wealth. Instead, if one is to boast, they should boast about understanding and knowing the entity that demonstrates mercy, judgment, and justice in the world, as these qualities are what the entity values.
styled: LET NOT THE WISE MAN GLORY IN HIS WISDOM, AND LET NOT THE STRONG MAN GLORY IN HIS STRENGTH, AND LET NOT THE RICH MAN GLORY IN HIS RICHES: BUT LET HIM THAT GLORIETH GLORY IN THIS, THAT HE UNDERSTANDETH AND KNOWETH ME, FOR I AM THE LORD THAT EXERCISE MERCY AND JUDGEMENT AND JUSTICE IN THE EARTH: FOR THESE THINGS PLEASE ME, SAITH THE LORD". (Example: The graduate from Calcutta) "Dr" Schroeder (unfinished draft)

neutral:
To understand is to appreciate, to value what is good, to reject what is harmful, and to acknowledge an ultimate reality. This offers significant comfort and a hopeful perspective. It provides a profound outlook for individuals, even those who have made mistakes, especially if one considers that hope is essential for happiness in this life, and if the fundamental purpose of human existence—to understand the ultimate creator—is kept in mind.

This perspective is summarized by the idea that the ultimate creator designed us to understand this entity. This represents a profound objective. To love and serve this entity is inherently part of the same purpose. This brings a profound sense of fulfillment to those who appreciate it; its value is immeasurable.

However, how can one understand what the senses cannot perceive? How can one comprehend the ultimate creator, whose attributes—wisdom, power, goodness, and compassion—are limitless? A simple question may, in the first instance, require a simple answer.
styled: To know is to appreciate - is to love what is good - is to reject what is of evil - is to adore the Divine. What consolation this offers us! What a hopeful outlook it ought to afford! What a sublime horizon for poor sinners, -- if "hope is the very soul of happiness here" and if the revealed purpose of our creation, TO KNOW GOD is kept in mind -- what a horizon for us, even though we be sinners -- if we but keep in mind the primary purpose of our creation, TO KNOW GOD. Hence the lines: God made me to know Him. O what a bless'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. Its "Heaven Begun" for the grateful on earth; -- To treasure aright? ! Highest Heaven its worth. But how can I know what the senses fail to perceive? How know the Incomprehensible God whose attributes - wisdom and power and goodnes and mercy-are infinite? A simple question may, in the first place, demand a simple answer.

neutral:
It is prudent to recall a common observation: simple questions or objections can pose a challenge for even experts to answer. An uninformed person can also raise such questions. Perhaps the uninformed person is implicitly included in this observation, as to the extent someone is uninformed, they ultimately demonstrate a degree of foolishness. While it would be unfair to assert that every fool is uninformed, it is consistent to state that every uninformed person is a fool.

However, a straightforward response to the objection concerning the difficulty or impossibility of a limited being comprehending an unlimited one might involve posing other simple questions: Do our senses directly perceive electricity within a live wire? Or do people gaze directly into the sun to understand its benefits? Such objections are unproductive and futile, and if intended to justify the rejection of an ultimate source, they are considered a grave error. There is no justification for any rational being to refuse to acknowledge its ultimate source.
styled: But right here, we shall do well to rem- ember a trite proverb: "A fool can ask questions - can make ob- jections - that will puzzle a philosopher to answer." A nave of course, can ask such questions too. But perhaps the nave is sup- posed to be included in the proverb; because after all, in asmuch as anyone is a nave in at least somuch does he prove himself in the end to have been a fool too. While it would be uncharitable, therefore, to say that every fool is a nave' it is always logical; to say that every nave is a fool. However, a simple answer to the above objection intimating the difficulty or impossibility of a finit creature knowing the infinite God, might be to ask another very simple question; viz. Do the senses perceive the electricity - "the juice" in a live wire? Or again: Do men gaze into the sun to consider its bene- fits? Objections like the above are futal and vain and if meant to excuse athesim, are criminal. For there is absolutely no ex- cuse for any rational creature refusing to recognize its Creator.

neutral: There is an inherent aspect of human nature and of all rational beings that instinctively senses a reliance on something transcendent. Both history and philosophy unequivocally support this idea, as does common sense. Theological perspectives also assert this, viewing serious questioning of this dependence as implying atheism or a denial of a divine being's existence. Such questioning is, from this perspective, considered an insult to reason and to the understanding of all preceding generations. It is also described as a blatant disregard for sacred texts, divine revelation, and the supreme authority of a divine being, who is depicted as admonishing, pleading, and commanding complete devotion and love.
styled: In the first place, there is something intrinsically in the very nature of man - and in the very nature of every rational creature -- that instinctively feels its dependence on something greater than itself - on something supernatural. History and philosophy alike prove this beyond the shadow of an honest doubt, -- to say nothing of common sense; or of theology, the queen of all sciences, so much so, in fact, that to question it seriously, would be to intimate atheism again or a denial of God's existence which accord- ing to all sciences is nothing less than an insult, not only to honest reason to every normal generation back to our, Adam and Eve, but a most flagrant ignoring of Holy Scripture, and of divine re- velation and of Gods own supreme Majesty, Who admonishes, Who pleads, Who commands: ". . . I AM THE LORD THY GOD . . . THOU SHALT LOVE THE LORD THY GOD WITH THY WHOLE HEART AND WITH THY WHOLE SOUL AND WITH ALL THY MIND AND WITH ALL THY STRENGTH . .

neutral: Your association is being enrolled. This message is for Mrs. George Schulte. Your son, Thomas, is being enrolled in the Seraphic Mass Association. styled: We are enrolling your Association. If he be God bless you Mrs. George Schulte. We are enrolling your little Thomas in the Seraphic Mass Association. If he be not improving by the time this reaches you, let us trust in God's goodness that the doctors get a good surpris of some kind. neutral: Being well often implies being hopeful. This hope is frequently overlooked, negatively impacting both mental and physical well-being. A notable historical example is the offense some early followers took at Jesus' chosen method for establishing his teachings, specifically the cross and Calvary. This offense led Peter to say, "Master! Far be it from you," to which Jesus responded, "Get behind me, adversary, you are not thinking from a divine perspective." This type of offense was not confined to the early Christian era. Bernard, a prominent medieval scholar, noted that after the controversy of the cross, it is never rational to be offended. Another occasion when early followers were offended was Jesus' detailed insistence on his role as essential for their inner sustenance, stating, "I am the bread of life. Your ancestors ate manna in the desert and died."
styled: I hope this finds you well, which means of course hopeful too. This latter is something that is sadly overlooked, to the great de- Triment of spiritual progress as well as physical. The probably all-outstanding example or proof of this is the historical scandal that some of the disciples took at Jesus' choice of the CROSS AND CALVARY whereby to establish His Reign of love, rather than any other; - the scandal that drew from St. Peter Lim- self: "Master! Far be it from thee .... " and the alarming response: "Get thee behind me satan. . . , Thou saverest not of God". It is well to remember that such scandal was never intended to be confined to the Apostalic-age. Hence, Saint Bernard - the out- standing Doctor of the Middle-ages - wisely reminds: "Since the scandal of the Cross it is never reasonable to take scandal". A- mother occasion of the first disciples taking scandal is the detailed insistence of His giving us Himself for our own life of soul: "I am the bread of life. Your fathers did eat manna in the desert and are dead.

neutral: This report details a recent trip undertaken to attend the funeral of Maurice Joachim. The report was begun the day after the funeral services, which were considered solemn. A telegram received around 7:30 AM on Wednesday, January 12, from Ortonville, Minnesota, announced: "Father Maurice Joachim died at 6:20 this Morning". It was mistakenly assumed that the funeral would occur on Saturday. Further details were awaited until almost midnight, when a call was received from an individual lamenting their divorce. During a long-distance call, authorization was given to travel to the location. It was concluded that the funeral might take place on Friday, and a decision was made to proceed without delay to ensure timely arrival. Therefore, plans were made to take the Hiawatha train, which was considered the most reliable for making the necessary connections. It snowed that Thursday morning, and to ensure catching the "Golden Arrow" train on the Pennsylvania Railroad, an early departure was made for Fort.
styled: No doubt you will have been expecting a report of some kind con- cerning the privileged trip conceded me recently to the Funeral of poor, dear brother, Father Maurice Joachim. I started to do this the day after the solemnities; for all considered it was a real solemn funeral and seemingly a happy one. Blessed be God in His angels and in His saints. A wire at about 7:30 Wednesday, January 12 from Ortonville, Minn. announced to us: "Father Maurice Joachim died at 6:20 this Morning". I erroneously took it for almost self understood that the Funeral would take place on Saturday, waiting for more particulars till near midnight, when a call came; but it was from a poor party - convert - lamenting their unfortunate divorce. Your Very Rev. Paternity, on my long distance call had benignly bidden me go thither. Deo gratias. We concluded that possibly the funeral might be Friday and decided accordingly to take no chances. Hence, our plans to catch the Hiawatha as probably - surest train to make the desired connections. It snowed that Thursday morning and to be sure of catching the "Golden Arrow" train on the Pennsylvania, we left early, for Ft.

neutral: The train arrived at the station at 3:30. Moonlight had been visible throughout the night, though faint. The presence of snow on the ground contributed to a general sentiment that it was a beautiful night. Approximately thirty miles from the final destination, the individual was able to move to an empty car, which provided more comfort than a cramped seat. This provided significant relief. While partially asleep, the individual was awakened by a train attendant and exited the train to meet the local clergyman, who was waiting patiently. The train was thirty minutes behind schedule. George Campbell, the clergyman, honked his horn upon seeing the individual disembark and offered a warm greeting. The clergyman was associated with a modest building named St. Mary's, which featured a single central platform and could accommodate approximately two to three hundred people. Following the morning religious service and breakfast, they traveled twenty miles through a dense, freezing fog, arriving about twenty minutes before the scheduled event. Ed'd, another clergyman, had not anticipated the individual's arrival and was disappointed, as he had planned for Reaordan of Minneapolis, a high-ranking clergyman and former leader at M.E.J., to deliver the main address.
styled: It was 3:30 when we pulled into that station. It had been moon-light all night, though rather pale, but with the snow on the ground I heard the train-men's view come out in harmony with my own: "Its a beautiful night". We were about thirty miles from our train-destiny when I was able to stretch my bones in the empty smoking-car which was better than in a corner of a seat. Thank God that was a relief. I was at least half-asleep, when the gentle brake-man called me and I went out to find the Pastor patiently waiting. We were a half hour late. He, Father George Campbell, tooted when he saw me leave the train and greeted me like an old friend. He has a nice little (Church) - one altar - to accomodate about two or three hundred, St. Mary's. After holy Mass and breakfast, we made the twenty miles in a dense, freez- ing fog about twenty minutes before services. Father Ed'd had hardly expected me and was disappointed in his figuering on Monsignore Reaordan of Mineapolis - a one-time pastor of M.E.J., to give the ser- mon.

neutral: The group, consisting of Cook, Ignatius (who was driving), and Guardian, departed from Fort Wayne. Upon departure, the conductor announced a 25-minute delay, which suggested a tight connection for the Hiawatha train in Chicago if no further time was lost en route. After leaving Huntington, the speaker's worry subsided. They successfully made the connection, even though the train had a brief wait until a ticket was obtained for the speaker. The speaker had planned for the funeral to be on Saturday and to stay overnight in St. Paul. However, upon being the first passenger to exit the train car, friends intercepted the speaker. The speaker had to reboard the train, and the friends accompanied them to Minneapolis. From there, after an hour and a half, the speaker was to take another train for a 200-mile journey to Ortonville, Minnesota, near the South Dakota border. The following morning, after a morning service, there would be a 20-mile drive to Graceville for the funeral at 10:00 AM.
styled: Wayne; - Brother Cook, Ignatius at the wheel and Rev. Father Guard- ian accompaning. Leaving Fort Wayne, the Conductor had to lament that he was 25 minutes late, which to me meant that we'd be nip and tuck in catching the Hiawatha in Chicago, if we didn't lose any more on the schedule thither. On leaving Huntington, however, we had said our Rosary for Divine guidance and protection and safe return and thanks be to God, I forgot all about worrying. We made it, even if the train had to wait a little, till they kindly got me a ticket. I was still figuering on the Funeral being on Saturday and on my staying over night in St. Paul till, the first passenger off the Coach, my friends held me up. I had to go back on the train and they accompanied me on to Minieapolis, whence, after an hour and a half, I was to take another train and go on two hundred miles further to Ortonville, Minn. , right near the S. Dakota border; thence, after holy Mass next morning drive twenty miles to Graceville for the fun- eral at ten ocl.

styled: No one else seemed ready for that privilege; so that I was a- shamed to decline when asked if I would say a few words. A nice crowd of in- telligent looking school children together with the silent sermon of a happy death of one who had weathered the storms of 81 winters con- secrated to Almighty God, naturaly inclined my thoughts to vocations. (for 20 minutes) .

The speaker, having just arrived in the parlor from the chapel, urgently requested a vessel, stating a need to vomit and that they would wait on the floor. Although there was strenuous retching, little came until the vessel arrived, and then only a small amount. styled: I had hardly come to the parlor after blessing them with several relics and a little visit in the Chapel when I urged, "Sister, please get me a vessel quickly. I'll have to vomit. I'll wait right here on the floor". Luckily noth- ing came but strenous reaching till the vessel arrived, and then very little, with quite a relief of very short duration ~ again and again- till the ambulance came and took the patient to St. Michael's Hospital for about 40 hours. . . There is another very interested party, a certain Mrs. Gordon Thorne, quite a benefactor who without effort could donate the whole Prize ($1,000,000.) and possibly will do as much, if successful in her present efforts to break away from a trast-company that has been charging her $40,000. annually for their service. She is preparing for a battle in court on this score next Monday, 25th. She expects them to appeal the case if she win. .. She asks for prayers. A daily communicant and quite a "live wire" , with far-reaching views, she seems solicitous to make up for lost time while her non-catholic, though seemingly very charitable, Husband, Montgomery Ward Thorne, lived.

At the cross, Jesus told his grieving mother, "Look, your son," indicating the young Apostle John. Theologians and early church leaders have consistently interpreted this as also referring to all followers of his teachings through John. Immediately afterward, Jesus told John, "Look, your mother."

If religion is considered the most important field of study across time, defined as "the study of our beneficial reliance on a higher power and our fellow humans"—a definition that appears to be widely accepted—then only one religion can exist. Similarly, if it is true that "We are followers of Christ only to the extent that we believe in Jesus Christ and adhere to his teachings," then only one form of Christianity can exist.

Consequently, each individual must reflect on their own conscience to determine if they are genuinely followers of Christ or merely so in name. Furthermore, it should be considered a beneficial opportunity to continually improve oneself in that belief system and to identify its unerring guide on Earth.
styled: "Behold thy son." Jesus said to His sorrowing Mother and the foot of the Cross, referring to the youthful Apostle John - and in him as theologians and the fathers of the holy Church have always taught, - in St. John - refering to all followers of His doctrine. Then as in the same breath to St. John: "Behold thy Mother." If religion is the greatest science of all ages - "The science of our happy dependence on God and our neighboy.", which definition no one seems to question, then there can be but one religion. In like manner if: "We are Christians only in asmuch as we believe in Jesus Christ and keep His words - His doctrine - so there can be but one Christianity. Therefore, its up to each one of us individually to examine into our own conscience whether we be Christians in reality or only in name. Too, it ought to be our happy privilege to prefect ourselves in that faith more and more, and to findout its infallible Guide on earth.

This passage provides context for a rhyme-letter titled "a remedy for the blues." The letter was sent by a missionary in the Philippines to a senior member of his religious order, located in Yonkers, NY, who was 12 years his senior.

The senior brother had experienced health issues during his early studies, which led to his departure from the seminary. This was a source of personal and family disappointment. For twenty years, he worked to promote religious callings, aiming to compensate for his perceived failure. However, while assisting at the first religious service of one of his junior brothers, he decided to re-enter the seminary. He joined the junior brother (who is now the missionary) in the seminary and became a priest one year before him.

neutral:
The author notes a perceived widespread increase in atheism, which they describe as the ultimate intellectual and moral failing and a threat to civilization. This situation, the author suggests, should lead to collective agreement and cooperation.

Regardless, the author expresses a willingness to join in prayer for Donald Jay, specifically to seek divine intervention for him to gain sight. The stated purpose of this prayer is for Donald Jay to fulfill a religiously defined purpose and promote peace among people and nations.

The author posits that religion is a science, and indeed the greatest science, asserting that there can only be one true religion. This singular religion is defined by the author as 'the science of our happy relationship with - dependence on - God and our neighbor.'

Given the perceived widespread and aggressive nature of atheism, the author questions whether it is time for collective action to prompt humanity to consider its direction without religious belief and without cultivating what the author considers the greatest of all sciences. The author notes that most people, in their perceived 'blindness,' refuse to acknowledge religion as a science. The author apologizes for the digression.
styled: The fact too, that there seems to be such an avalencehe of atheism - the very climax 02 intellectual insanity and of moral depravity - threatening to inundate civilization: That ought to bring us all into mutual agreement and harmony of some kind. At all events, we shall be pleased to join our prayers with yours in favor of poor dear little Donald Jay; viz. in "storming Heaven", that God be pleased to give him sight wherewith to glorify God Himself and promote - be instrumental in promoting - peace among men and nations. . . Afterall, as a science (and religion is, notonly a science, but the greatest science of all ages) there can be but one religion, viz: "The science of our happy relationship with - dependence on - God and our neighbor." In the face of so much - such brazen and threatening atheism, is it not time we come together and get humanity to consider something about whither it is tending without faith in God and without fostering this greates of all sciences, which outside of the comparatively few, refuse in their blind- ness even to recognize it as a science atall? .. Pardon the digression.

neutral: Regarding your situation, I received your recent letter and understand your distress. Such a diagnosis of "Blindness, Deafness" is deeply disappointing for any loving parent. It is hoped that D.J. will surpass the doctors' expectations, as sometimes happens. Regardless, you have been fortunate to have another bright boy, and even in Donald's situation, he possesses other positive attributes. However, physical or temporary advantages are less significant than deeply held convictions. This applies to all of us, even if we differ on some fundamental points. Furthermore, we share many commonalities, and we should be patient with common human weaknesses, particularly regarding the practical application of beliefs or principles.
styled: My Dear Friends: God bless you and yours. God bless all our afflicted brethren of good (will). I received your pathetic letter yesterday and I surely do sympathize with you. What a disapointment to any loving parent to hear such a diagnosis. "Blindness, Deafness". I surely hope D. J. will give the doctors a surprise as nearly always happens when we trust in Almighty God. At all events how merciful has not God shown Him- self to you in blessing you with another bright boy, and even in Donald's case, otherwise endowing him with such happy faculties! And yet dear friends; what are all purely physical or temporal blessings in comaprason with the faith that God has given us? - You and me, even though (we) differ, as may be, in some essentials. Besides, we have somuch in common - and this we can say of all who honestly believe in God and hope in Him, that we ought surely to be patient with weaknesses so common, if not in systems of religion at least, in application and practice.

neutral: I had intended to send this acknowledgement a day or two after receiving your communication, but I was reluctant to send it in such a disorganized state and regret not having rewritten it. However, you and young Donald Jay have been on my mind continually since receiving your letter. I am confident you will understand some of what I intended to write. If I had more time or were a skilled typist, I would rewrite it completely. However, I hope I am not too presumptuous if I congratulate you on the positive outcome we both hoped for. I hope you receive a favorable report tomorrow. I am mailing this tonight, hoping for good results.

Surely you ought to keep in close touch with her and inform her about everything that transpires as affecting this, your so really threatening and fearful experience; - an experience that I for one, have not the least doubt is - for your final "doing or undoing", for time as well as for eternity.

neutral: It is time to retire, but I must at least begin writing to you before the day ends, even if this is only a brief communication.
