styled: God bless you this happy feast of our dear blessed Mother Mary; Queen of Lourdes, Queen of Mercy, Queen of the Universe and of the Most Holy Trinity. It is really time to retire, but I must at least start with a few words to you before this date is gone, - even though it be as yet only a "duplex." I received your letter of Wednesday last evening and, as much as time would permit, have studied it since. I want to go into some details in response to it but can not do so just now. In general, however, I must say that I am greatly encouraged at its upright tone and the good will it indicates all around, - an example of patient forbearance and of gentle readiness to relent in charity. 15th 9:30 P.M. - A late start again. God Help us! It just seems that I get nowhere; and yet so many things I ought to be doing. Glory be to God! I did remember you in my holy Mass this morning and blessed you at the end.

neutral: I am sending this urgently. You will hear from me shortly. This message supplements previous communications. The contents of your letter from a month ago have been a constant preoccupation. I have been increasingly concerned about your profession, observing your complex problems, growing difficulties, and the significant threats to your material and overall well-being. Most concerning was your apparent unawareness of these issues, until your final, reassuring paragraph.
styled: I want to catch mailman. neutral: It is a remarkable act of mercy to be received back for the second time in as many months, as one who had left, simply by complying with the requirement of again wearing the uniform of your Order. Such an example is rare in history. This demonstrates, more than any actions, the Mother General's confidence in her wavering subordinate. It appears that a guiding force was influencing the Reverend Mother on that occasion, seemingly orchestrating events to smooth the path and facilitate the return of Constance, despite her many lapses in commitment. However, those who sow doubt will question, asking 'If...' and 'Why...', and will suggest that there is something amiss—something other than compassion, wisdom, power, and benevolence—in the divine handling of individual circumstances. These questions of 'If' and 'Why' resemble manipulative arguments. It is frustrating for human inclination to be denied an opportunity for self-justification.
styled: But what a morcy of God to be, the second time inside as many months, received back a "prodigal" on the simple obedience - the coveted boon itself - of again putting on the holy Habit of your Order: Where in all history is there another such example? It surely speaks more than any works, for poor, dear Mother General's confidence in her wavering daughter. Ah! To me it looks as though Jesus Himself were someway behind Rev. Mother on that occassion, - as indeed He does seem to be someway coaching every- thing that tends to smoothe off and, notwithstanding her many infidelities, to facilitate the return of His, sadly inconstant, Constance. Still, the enemy of souls will ask - and the destroyer of the souls' peace - "If ... "and "Why" .. and will dare to intimate that there is something wrong - something other than mercy and wisdom and power and love in God .. . concerning His adjustments of our individual cases. Ah! These "Ifs and Whys" ! Do they not sound like the wily philosophy of Grand-Mother Eve's garden adviser? ... Yes, it is disappointing to nature, to be deprived of a chance for self-justification.

neutral: For several months, I have been attempting to encourage you. My hope has been that this encouragement, combined with the many wishes for your guidance and a change in your perspective that I know are being made for you, might fully convince you that your ultimate well-being, both now and in the future, depends on a complete and dedicated commitment of everything you have to a higher principle. Your difficult experiences over these past months, which nearly resulted in tragedy, were in themselves remarkable instances of favorable circumstances for you. These events should help persuade you that this is the only logical conclusion for you to reach.
styled: Dear Sister Mary Constance: God bless you and may He be your Stay , your Refuge and your divine Guide these days. I have hoped that by enc- couraging you as I have been trying to do these several months, that with the many prayers that I know are being offered for your guidance,- your conversion indeed - you might, by cooperating with God's holy grace, be fully convinced that your only salvation, for time as well as for eternity, is a generous and whole-hearted sacrifice of your --- your everything to God. Your desperate experiences these same months (hair-breadthly border- ering on fearful tragedy), -- experiences -- inthemselves and in reality extraordinary manifestations of God's mercy to you Sister Mary Constance, -- which ought surely to help convince you that such is about the only con- clusion for you to come to.

neutral: There is strong hope that during these challenging experiences, you have not significantly deviated from your commitments. However, it is also believed that, had you remained truly committed to your commitments and completely rejected worldly temptations and negative influences two years ago, you would have by now achieved a far deeper and more joyful fulfillment, something vastly surpassing your highest aspirations. You have experienced a significant setback, but this mistake is not irreparable. With benevolent assistance and your humble and grateful cooperation, you can not only regain your previous state of favor, but just as some individuals have transformed from adversaries to prominent advocates, you too can—and out of humble gratitude should—become outstanding in upholding truth and justice in the ongoing struggle against destructive ideologies and opposition to belief.
styled: While I have still more than hope that during these fearful experiences, you have not strayed mortal-sinfully from your Rule; nevertheless I believe on the other hand that, had you been really faith- ful to your vows and absolutely turned down the promises and the allure- ments of the world, the flesh and the devil as you should have done (two years ago), God would have promoted you before this to an incalculably more intimate and happy confidence and espousals with the divien Lover of Souls - to something vastly surpassing your highest ideal. You have lost out fearfully Sister: but your mistake is not irrepar- able. By the mercy of God and your humble and grateful cooperation therewith, you can, not-only regain your former standing in the Hearts of Jesus and Mary; but like St. Paul who from even a zealot persecutor of the Church became an all-surpassing Apotstle, Vessel of election, you too can -- and out of humble gratitude ought to -- become outstanding on the side of Truth and justice in the already-raging warfare against Antichrist and atheism.

neutral: Your choice to seek comfort and peace from sources other than a specific central belief, and the many subsequent related errors, have evidently caused confusion and distress, and obscured your professional outlook. Otherwise, you would not speculate with so many 'ifs' and 'whys' or present what might be considered 'half-truths.' Love itself is always beautiful, but when it becomes excessive or uncontrolled, it loses its inherent beauty and becomes unacceptable. Love considered illegitimate is always excessive; the reverse is not always true. Here is an example of the latter: Approximately twenty years ago, a practical schoolteacher married and had a family of six boys. Everything was initially positive and promising until some time after the first child was born. Her husband's attitude became indifferent and even cold. For several months, she did not suspect the reason for this unusual change in attitude. She did not suspect until she herself had lost much of her affection and respect for her husband.
styled: Your mistake of seeking solace and peace from other sources than in the Cross and the Crucified, and innumerable lesser mistakes that in consequence have followed since have evidently disturbed and muddled your spiritual waters, to say the least and beclouded your vocational horizon. Otherwise you would hardly moralize with so many "ifs" and "whys" and we might say "half truths." .. Yes, love in itself is always beauti- ful, but when and inasmuch as even love becomes inordinate it loses that native beauty and like an immortal soul in sin, becomes hedious in the sight of God and Heven. Illegitimate love is always inordinate; not always visa versa. Here is an actual example of the latter: Just about twenty years agoa certain practical school-mam married and was blest with a family of six boys. Every thing was bright in the beginning and indeed promising till a while after the first baby came. The attitude of her Husband became indifferent and even cold. For several months she never suspected the source of this unnatural attitude. Never suspected, till she herself had lost much of her affection and respect for her Husband. Ah!

neutral: The tendency to defend oneself to others is ultimately unproductive, a fact often not fully grasped. This stands in stark contrast to instances of silent composure when faced with accusation, unlike the common practice of loudly defending oneself. The writer acknowledges having frequently demonstrated such manipulative cleverness. This type of cleverness is also noted as a persistent weakness for Solanus. Consequently, this is presented as an act of compassion, preventing someone who is struggling or inconsistent from further embarrassing themselves, by discreetly resolving potential difficulties. The recipient of the letter had reason to be surprised that Mother only recognized them in their religious attire. However, the writer suggests this should have been interpreted as an act of Mother's profound gentleness and foresight, effectively resolving potential difficulties and embarrassments.
styled: .. No doubt that is because of our corrupt nature's want of realization that in the science of the saints, and in the sight of all Heaven, self justification before creatures, is never a victory for the Christian soul. Ah! When we behold the astonishment of the Roman Governor and his whole court - Pilate before Jesus divinely silent. - What a contrast to our noisy self justification! Sad to say, I feel myself to have been many times a "past- master" at that kind of worldly cleverness. Just that kind of cleverness is still one of Fr. Solanus' unhappy weaknesses. Hence, another instance of mercifully sparing from embarrassment. in the sight of Heaven a wavering daughter, -- an inconstant spouse - so solicitously smoothing embarrassments away, before the Guardian Angels and all the triumphant Church and Heavenly Court, - really preventing some one from still further making a F. of herself. Ah! Dear Sister: you had cause for wonering at Rev. Mother's not seeing you other than in your holy habit; but was it not - should it not have been wonder at Mother's overwhelming gentlenes and forethought? Rather, was it not Jesus again smoothing off difficulties and embarrisments?

styled: V. Dear Sister Mary Constance: God bless you and yours this holy season -a Blessed Eastertide if not too late. I hope this finds you well and tasting at least something of that peace which the great triumph of the RisenSaviour ought to inspire and insure. Appreciation for one's work is the natural foundation of gratitude. Gratitude is considered the primary and most reliable sign of intelligence. This idea aligns with the poetic observation that the lives of accomplished individuals demonstrate that we can elevate our own lives and leave a lasting, positive impact. Pope Pius XII, a proponent of doctrine, morality, and international peace, emphasized this quality as a fundamental and serious obligation.

In 1909, the author had completely lost hearing in their left ear, and the condition was quickly affecting the other ear. One Thursday evening, after visiting a specialist, the author returned with a throbbing earache, having undergone a very painful treatment and facing very delicate and dangerous medical recommendations. Five years prior, the author had read the biography of Sister Therese Martin, who was then relatively unknown, and found it very beneficial, feeling a strong connection to her story. From the initial reading, the author had a strong premonition that she would be canonized.
styled: And at the same time appreciation for one's vocation; - appreciation - the natural foundation of gratitude which, in its turn, - "Gratitude, the very first and surest indication of intelli- gence." Hence the poet's happy dictum: "The lives of all great men remind us that we can make our lives sublime. "And, parting leave behind us worthy footsteps in the sans of time" . footprints Pope Pius XII; peerless and outstanding champion To-day of dogma, of morality, of peace among men and nations; stresses this virtue as man's first and gravest duty. Lives of saints? ... In 1909 I had completely lost the hearing in my left ear and the same condition was rapidly threatening the other side. I had returned a certain Thursday-evening from the specialist with a throbb- ing ear-ache after a very painful treatment and very delicate and dangerous propositions. Five years before that, I had read the life of Sister Therese Martin, till then seemingly quite unknown, and had greatly profited thereby; happy in the communion of saints as I felt, on having met another heavenly little friend. I had felt from thefirst reading that she would be canonized.

neutral:
The speaker's wife returned home without a headache. They had desired to have children for thirteen years and were understandably becoming discouraged. Although they held Christian beliefs, they had never been baptized. They encountered significant difficulties, which they overcame, before being accepted into the Church and for several months thereafter. The challenges they faced seemed designed to deter them from their goal.

It is emphasized that one should perform an act of gratitude or commitment in recognition of a positive outcome, based on an initial understanding of this principle. For Catholics, for example, this might involve more frequent participation in Holy Communion if a desired outcome is achieved, with a strong preference to begin immediately. For non-Catholics, the recommendation is to seriously investigate the claims of the Church, or the relationship and dependence of other denominations on the Mother Church, and to act based on that understanding.
styled: "That's my Wife". She had come home without any headache. Glory be to God! They had been praying for a family for thirteen years and were naturally discouraged or becoming so. They believed in Christianity but had never been baptized. ... It is next to "Unbelievable", what diffi- culties they met with and, by God's grace overcame, before being re- ceived into the Church, and even for months afterwards. All Hell just seemed determined to shake them from their purpose. We make it a point to stress the importance of making sacrifice in recognition of a favor received - having started out with an under- standing, at least to that effect. For Catholics, e.g., more fre- quent holy Communion if favor is granted and preferable, by all means to start at once - to "get ahead of the Good God in generosity" if possible. For non-catholics, that they be earnest in looking into something of the claims of the Church; or something of the relation- ship - dependence of the denominations on the Mother-Church, etc and working accordingly. ....

neutral:
During these days of unrest and suspense, I wish you and your family well. I have read your letter describing your difficulties and deeply sympathize with you and your loved ones. I hope that this unique hardship may ultimately prove to be a positive development, as it is often observed that significant challenges can lead to beneficial outcomes. We have encountered several similar cases, some of which were initially perceived as even more tragic and hopeless, that ultimately resulted in genuinely positive and unexpected outcomes.

A single example occurred over ten years ago when a reserved lady, after waiting nearly an hour until others had left, introduced herself. She explained that although she was not Catholic, she wished to receive a similar positive interaction, mentioning that she had always suffered from headaches. Her accent, more than her physical appearance, suggested her specific background. Approximately three hours later, a visitor with a dark complexion and distinct features, sharing the same surname and identical accent, requested a rosary. I informed him about the person with the same name who had visited around 11 a.m.
styled: God bless you these days of unrest and suspense - you and yours. I have read your pathetic letter and do surely sympathize with you and your dear ones. I hope that the good God may manifest something of His merciful designs in favoring you with such a peculiar cross; for indeed, from sacred history the truth of the old saying - of St. Paul (? ): "Whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth", is most manifest. We've had several cases similar to yours and some of them alto- gether more tragic and hopeless - turn out to have been indeed real blessings in disguise. A single example: It must be ten or more years ago that a certain modest lady, having waited close to an hour, till all else had gone, introduced herself: " ... I's not Catholic, but I would like to get a bessin too. I's always had head-aches". Her accent rather than her color indicated something of her particu- lar origin. About three hours later a well featured but very dark visitor of the same name and identical accent asked for a rosary. I told him of his namesake who had been in about Il a.m.

Regardless of one's circumstances or position, individuals can contribute to positive development by supporting and encouraging others to find their purpose. Regarding your significant concerns and other interests mentioned, a practical solution can be found in the preceding advice, which is primarily intended for your personal guidance. styled: Praying for vocation, if not a poitive vo- cation in itself, is surely an essential and outstanding feature in the character of every ideal Christian as well as in every practical missionary. Think it over, Encourage, foster vocations. Wherever we may be or whatever our state in life, we may in many ways become in- struments of the Holy Spirit by praying for and promoting vocations. Now, as to your "big problem"; as well as the minor interests to which you refer. I think you ought to be able to find a practical solu- tion in the above, as primarily intended for your own personal guidance. It was a privilege of mine to be assistant in that dear parish twenty-five years ago and chaplain at the - then - comparatively new but leading cemetery.

neutral: That night, experiencing anxiety, the individual made a silent commitment: if a specific person would help restore their hearing, the individual would reread that person's biography. The individual was confident that this person could help and, believing the person was in Heaven, would do so. The individual slept well that night without further issues. The next morning, when water was applied to the face, a sensation like a bubble breaking occurred in the impaired ear, leading the individual to conclude that the eardrum was not broken. Within 24 hours, hearing was fully restored. Since then, the individual has experienced virtually no hearing problems. The individual attributed this recovery to God and Saint Therese, also known as 'The Little Flower.' Subsequently, the individual read Therese's book fifteen times and believes to have received at least that many benefits.
styled: Well, in my anxiety that night I made a "mental proposition" to her that if she would help to save my hearing I'd read her life again. I was even then confident that she could help me and that being already in Heaven, she would. John Martin - Frater Don Bosco, o. f.m. cap. (at least in spirit and hope, I trust) With no further trouble that night I slept well, and next morning at the first douche of water on my face, there was like a bubble broke in my bad ear and I thought: "Thank God! My drum is not broken". Be- fore 24 hours my hearing was perfect; and, what is further notable, I've had practically no trouble with my hearing ever since. Thanks be to God and His little spouse, now Saint Therese "The Little Flower. I have read her book fifteen times since thet and have had at least that many favors. The above will give you an idea of how I would advise you if you still hope for a vocation.

neutral: Sympathy is extended regarding your many difficulties. It is a common belief, often cited as encouragement, that challenges can be a sign of a deeper purpose or care. The validity of this idea is strongly affirmed. styled: God bless you I surely do sympathize with you in your manifold troubles. However Saint Paul assures us, for our encouragement no doubt and for our consolation; "Whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth." have been long since convinced of the inspiration of this saying. · I The fact that Almighty God has permitted so many and such trials and crosses to come your way, till in a way you are forced to seek help where otherwise you would hardly ever dream of turning, indicates to me that the Good God must love you specially. I would wish I might express something of the peace that I hope will come to you as a direct result of your bravely humbling yourself just to appeal as you have done. God bless you for such effort. neutral: which is beyond all understanding. Regarding your non-Catholic status: You may be more aligned with Catholic principles than you imagine, if you understood the full meaning of 'Catholicity'. It is asserted that individuals are considered Christians only if they believe in Jesus Christ and follow his teachings and commandments, regardless of how they identify themselves. There can be only one form of Christianity, given that there is only one Jesus Christ. Furthermore, if religion is defined as a science—and it is argued to be the greatest of all sciences when properly studied—then there can be only one religion, and consequently only one such science. Throughout history, those considered truly scientific and educated have understood "the Science of the Saints" to refer to religion, specifically the relationship between God and humanity.
styled: which surpasseth all understanding" . As to your not being Catholic: You are probably more so than you imaginge, - if you only just knew what Catholicity is. I am confident that you will agree with me when I claim that, whatever we may call our- selves, - you or I, or anyone else, - we are Christians only in asmuch as we believe in Jesus Christ and keep His word, His Commandments. Truly scientific and educated peoples have in all ages understood "the Science of the Saints" to refer to religion, i e, to the relationship between Almighty God and His rational creatures.

neutral: To you and your family during this festive season. I hope you are well. It is pleasing to hear that your parents and others are doing as well as they were years ago when I assisted at Saint Paul's. I wish you success with your plans to take over the Episcopalian church of St. Peter, which has long been diminished in size and recently lost its leadership. If the members are capable of independent thought, as their responsibilities imply they are, at least in this situation, then they should realize that, given that the religious faith of perhaps most people has weakened recently, hope and benevolence, which are often associated with it, have also diminished.

neutral: While concern for others is commendable, it is crucial to recognize that the primary purpose of a rational being's existence is to understand, appreciate, and deeply value the source of its being with thoughtful, personal gratitude. Enthusiasm and care for others are certainly praiseworthy and are regarded positively by many, inspiring to communities, and valued by thoughtful individuals. While this is a particular calling for religious leaders, the principle that gratitude for benefits received is a primary indicator of intelligence means it applies to all individuals, especially all rational beings. This includes, particularly, guiding others towards their higher purpose or well-being, which also contributes to their own hope, happiness, and fulfillment.
styled: But laudable and all as is such sol- icitude (and even in laudable: "No quid nemis") it is never rightly -ordered charity for me to forget that the primary purpose of my creation and of my existence as a rational creature, Is to recog- nize and to know, to appreciate and to love -- with an intelligent, personal grateful love -- God my Creator, my Redeemer, my Sanctifier. Zeal and solicitude for others is certainly praisworthy and pleasing to Almighty God and edifying to the Church and to all observant men. Such is the vocation of, not only the Priest and the Pastor to whom it specially refers; but if, "Gratitude for favors received is the very first and surest indication of intelligence", then it applies also to every Christian and indeed to every rational creature; viz, in the spiritual world especially, to gain souls for God; which means too for their own hope, happiness, glory.

neutral:
The writer notes it is somewhat late for Easter greetings but extends good wishes for the post-Easter period. The hope is that something worthwhile will occur before a specific Sunday in late spring, to improve the recipient's situation and offer the recipient and the Maltese community they serve at least some relief, especially for their ailing, elderly parents.

The writer, as a former assistant to Mr. Cefai, feels compelled to caution the leader. This caution is to ensure the leader remembers -- as people often forget -- the fundamental principle of personal development in all aspects, from practical matters to the most rigorous self-discipline. This principle is that one's primary responsibilities are to those closest to them. It is probable that Mr. M. Z. believes he is acting in accordance with this principle, given his concern for his community and the area he serves, and to some extent, this is true.
styled: It is getting a little late for Easter greetings but neverthe- less I do wish you a blessed Eastertide; hoping that something worth while may come your way before Holy Trinity Sunday to brighten your path and ligten your horizon, that may offer you and your dear Mal- tese People at least a sigh of relief. This most especially for your poorly, dear old Parents. But dear Father Cefai: as your one-time privileged assistant I am going to kinda beg leave to scold the Pastor, lest he lose sight of or forget -- as we are naturally so inclined to forget -- the primary rule and purpose of spiritual progress, in every thing from common sense to the very climax of highest asceticism; viz, "Charity begins at home." It is quite probable that Fr. M. Z. feelshe's doing just that, in his solicitude for his people and his parish. In a way he is.

neutral: For ethical development, consider addressing challenges directly. This can help maintain integrity, especially during periods of inexperience or youth. Such an approach fosters confidence and a strong sense of purpose.
styled: - forpatient progress in virtue - Why not offer our temptations themselves to God - for perseverance in purity, etc of inexperience, youth, etc .... fostering confidence in God, the very soul of prayer. Bles'd be God in all His designs.

neutral: A perspective holds that difficulties, when met with effort, ultimately prove beneficial. This viewpoint extends to current, significant challenges, suggesting they too can be seen as advantageous. Given that past difficulties are often remembered positively, and if it is understood that challenges are necessary for achieving desired outcomes, there is no need to worry about past or future struggles. Instead, one can focus on acknowledging progress made in navigating challenges successfully so far, despite numerous shortcomings. Furthermore, it is suggested to anticipate and accept all future difficulties that may arise, as these are frequently transformed into positive experiences.
styled: How wonderful with the inestimable gift of faith, whereby, with our cooperation, all and each such trial turn to have been blessings in disguise. Thank God too even for the present -- seemingly the supreme -- crisis. If "The memory of past difficulties is pleasant." as an old Latin proverb has it and if according to Saint Paul and every teacher of true asceticism: behoves us, by many tribulations to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.", why worry about struggles, etc, -- past or to come? Why not rather focus all attention on thanking God for having seen us safely thus far notwithstanding our many, many, innum- erable weaknesses and sins !!! ? Let us go a step further and thank God ahead of time for every trial and cross He may see fit to permit our meeting in this "vale of tears" -- that, in His mercy and wisdom He so often sweetens into tears of joy?

neutral: It is hoped that the recipient is well and that Mary's condition has improved. The letter was set aside after its contents were noted and thanks were expressed. It was subsequently misplaced, which prevented a personal response. Sympathy is extended to the recipient and their family. Numerous cases similar to Mary's have been observed, with the majority recovering remarkably well. The outcomes are sometimes astonishing.
styled: I hope you are well and that by this time things have brightened in regard to your little Mary. I put your letter aside - having noted your favor, for which many thanks, a special Mass at the time - and then lost track of it, I wanted to answer it personally. I surely sympathize with you and your family. We have had quite a few cases similar to little Mary's, the majority of which, thanks be to God, have come through astonishingly well. They sometimes seem miraculous. Glory be to God.

neutral: One can emulate a revered figure who, despite being highly honored, became more humble. This figure, following a primary, supreme model, was characterized by meekness and humility. Instead of blaming others for suspicion or persecution, as one might initially be inclined to do, one should exercise patience and offer support for them. This approach aligns with wise guidance and will ultimately lead to their positive change and one's own success.
styled: In other words, in as much as any of us can immitate our Blessed Mother Mary, Mother of God, who the more she was hon- ored, somuch more did she humble herself. Ah! Because next Jesus Himself the supreme, the divine Model, she too was indeed: "Meek and humble of heart." Let us not blame anyone for suspecting or persecuting us, as at first we are naturally inclined to do. On the contrary if we have a little patience and pray for them instead, thus we will surely be following the diving counsel and in the end have the consolation of converting them and of gain- ing our own Triumph.

neutral: It is beneficial to include in this concept of self-discipline and trust the challenges and potential difficulties that may precede our eventual death, regardless of any difficulties that may arise. It is hoped that you continue to remember Miss Daly, as she has been a source of support for you over the years. Naturally, she would be disappointed if you failed to show appreciation for her friendship, as gratitude is highly valued and ingratitude is considered unacceptable. If you approach this with genuine humility – and this applies to everyone – a positive outcome will be assured.
styled: We do well it seems to me, to in- clude in this ascetic idea -- this exercise of confidence, the trials and probable struggles of the happy death awaiting us, notwithstanding whatever adversities in His infinite wisdom and loving mercy He may see fit to permit. I hope you still pray to Miss Daly, even while praying for her she has been praying for you all these years. - I believe that - Naturally, therfore, she would be disapointed as at a want of appreciation of her Girl- Friend down here on earth if you should fail in this; because too, as a certain sister for whom St. Theresa of Avilla had prayed long and earnestly, - on its way to Heaven- assured her " . . . Pray for you Mother Terese! Ah! Mother: . for there is no place for ingratitude in Heaven." If you honestly humble yourself, dear Miss Gibson, -- and this applies to each and every one of us - your victory will be certain.

neutral: A spirit of goodwill and understanding is hoped to inspire all individuals, past, present, and future, who are unselfishly dedicated to Mercy-Hall's activities. The history of Mercy-Hall is an extraordinary record of its endeavors, marked by struggles that were at times desperate, and escapes from situations extremely close to disaster. These challenges included financial difficulties, bankruptcy, envy, suspicion, misunderstanding, and defamation. Some of these difficulties arose even before the full concept of Mercy-Hall was developed or its foundational plans were clear. The foundational plans for Mercy-Hall were revealed through a profound and enduring inspiration, originating from an event or memory associated with Miss Daly's grave, which was considered a remarkable development. A clear and urgent recommendation was given: "Get started; if necessary, with a single patient in some old attic." The underlying belief was that starting small would lead to eventual growth and development. Despite the challenges—from initial plans to struggles, narrow escapes, and repeated crises—these experiences were ultimately viewed as valuable.
styled: God bless you this glorious Feast and Easter Season, you and yours. May the divine Prince of Peace Himself breathe His Spirit of good will and harmoneous enlightenment on all and each of those unselfishly interested in Mercy-Hall activty, -- present, past, future. Glory be to God; what a record is not the story of that fair flower of Christian activity; and of practical Catholic action! -- a record of struggles sometimes bordering on the desperate, and of escapes, hair-splittingly close to disaster; struggles with and escapes from financial difficulties and bankruptcy, from envy and suspicion, from misunderstanding, calumny, etc. And some of all this in a way, before the idea of Mercy-Hall was fully conceived or its Heaven-sent "blue-prints" unfolded. -- as it was unfolded in that "miraculously" developed and unfading blooming slip of im- mortal from your Girl-Friend, Miss Daly's grave -- ) and it was de- finitely and urgently counseled: "Get started; if necessary, with a single patient in some old atic. God who loves tiny beginnings, will know as He always does know, how and when to provide develop- ment." Ah! Blue prints? Struggles? Escapes? Crisis after crises? Thank God for them all.

neutral:
The Mercy-Hall activity is portrayed as a hopeful new beginning. The passage expresses a wish that this activity may always serve as a source of support and stability throughout human life, which is perceived as both fleeting and, at times, protracted. It conveys a desire for goodwill and harmonious understanding to inspire all individuals, past, present, and future, who are unselfishly dedicated to the Mercy-Hall activity.

The history of the Mercy-Hall activity is presented as a remarkable account of genuine, benevolent, and practical community work. This record details periods of both success and difficulty, characterized by struggles that were nearly desperate and by extremely narrow escapes from disaster. These challenges included financial difficulties, bankruptcy, suspicion, criticism (some of which was sincere and well-intentioned), and malicious ambition that resulted in misrepresentation and slander.
styled: Ah! the aurora of Salvation's Day. Next to Jesus Himself and always with Him may she be ever our refuge and our stay during this pilgrimage on earth, in reality so very short at the longest and still, at times so seemingly long. Indeed I say again God bless you, and May Jesus the true Light breath His own Spirit of good will and of harmoneous anlightenment on each and all of those unselfishly interested in Mercy-Hall activity, - present, past, future. This has been my prayer for you and for them. Glory be to God! What a record is not the story of that fair flower? -- a record indeed of genuine, Christian activity and of really practical Catholic Action; a record of ups and downs; a record of struggles, bordering on the desperate and of escapes hair-splittingly close to disaster: struggles with and escapes from financial difficulties and bankruptcy, from suspicion and criticism (sometimes honest and well meant), and from envy and ambitions intriguing and consequent misrepresent- ation and calumny, etc.

neutral:
I hope you are all well and feeling optimistic. The present moment is fleeting and brief. Thank you for remembering January 15th, especially given the completely unwelcome circumstances, and also for the remembrance from two days ago. Your actions merit a great reward.

In response to your recent acts of remembrance, I am arranging for an enrollment in a prayer association for the deceased. This enrollment is specifically for those who have passed away from St. Paul's small Maltese Parish on 4th Street, as well as for both deceased and living benefactors from whom we are currently seeking prayers and financial assistance.

Among these individuals, as I mentioned several weeks ago, I have been thinking of the exemplary Monsignor Connolly and his distinguished brother, the Judge. Their early deaths were greatly mourned in Detroit. I had the opportunity to meet Monsignor Connolly for several years and assisted at the church associated with his proposal. Few people are aware of his prediction regarding a new form of Catholicism.
styled: I do hope you all keep well and that this finds you in hope- ful outlook. After all the present is so passing and so quickly gone that in the sight of Heaven it must appear nothing more than momentary. Many thanks for your kind remembrance of January 15th under such "prorsus" unwanted circumstances. Also that of the day-before yesterday. May the dear Lord Himself be your Reward. I am applying this latter as an enrollment in the Seraphic Mass Association, of the Holy Souls inPurgatory; -- especially the deceased of St. Paul's little Maltese Parish on 4th Street as also the deceased and living- benefactors / to whom we are appealing these days for prayers and for material assistance. Among these latter, as I suggested several weeks back I have had in mind the model and saintly Monsignor Connolly and his eminent Brother the Judge, both of whose early deaths Detroit so much lamented. I had the privilege of meeting the former for sev- eral years and of helping-out in the church that / his proposition and what few know about, his prophecy of a new Cath.

neutral: Before the full concept of Mercy Hall was developed or its detailed plans were understood, it was emphasized that work should begin immediately, even if it meant starting small, perhaps with just one patient in an unsuitable location. The implication was that the necessary resources and guidance for future development would become available at the appropriate time, even when starting small. These plans were indeed considered to be of extraordinary origin. The remarkably developed, continuously blooming small plant slip from the girlfriend's grave was regarded as precisely such an extraordinary blueprint. In fact, it had an even greater impact; observing that exceptionally blooming slip inevitably strengthened one's belief and confidence in extraordinary forces and guidance. This small plant slip remained available as a source of inspiration for as long as it was needed. Once it had served its purpose and Mercy Hall was well established, the plant slip was no longer present; the manner of its disappearance was considered unimportant.
styled: -- and in a way some of all this, before the idea of Mercy Hall was fully conceived or its "Heaven-sent blueprints" unfolded and it was at once stressed: "Get started. . if necessary with a single patient in some old attic." intimating at least in effect: "God who loves tiny begin- nings will know -- as He always does know best - how and when to provide developments". "Heaven-sent blue-prints"? Indeed! For that "miracilously- developed", unfadingly blooming, little slip from the girl-friend's grave was nothing less than just that, Heaven, sent blueprint. In a way it was more; for who with a spark of supernatural faith in God, could even behold that phonimally-blooming little slip without a decided heightening of his faith and confidence in the super- natural and in the divine providence of Heaven? In His merciful, unfathomable wisdom and goodness, Almighty God left that little relic with you as long as you needed it for just that kind of inspiration. And when it had served its purpose and Mercy Hall was well started, He lifted it away from you, (how, is quite secondary.

neutral: To prevent curiosity and a resulting lack of appreciation or respect from diminishing the subtle and profound nature of its underlying plan. This plan not only incorporates but actively emphasizes the hardships and setbacks encountered, and the repeated crises that are sometimes allowed. Despite these challenges, individuals are strengthened to benefit from them more than from almost any other experience.
styled: ) lest curiosity and consequent want of appre- ciation and of reverence mar the delicacy and the supernatural fragrance of that -- ? -- His own little blue-print? . · · · Aye! Glory be to God and blessed be His holy Name in all His designs! and in these designs; not merely including, but positively stressing just the knocks and the humiliations we meet with and the crisis after crisis He sometimes permits even while by His grace He fortifies us to profit by them all more than by anything else, save by the actual reception of the very Sacraments themselves.

neutral:
To Miss Loretta Mry Gibson:

During these unsettled days, the writer perceives opportunities for individuals who value their positions of responsibility. I am sending you a copy of the "Prayer for Peace," which you are likely already familiar with. I first encountered it after arriving at St. Bonaventures last January. It immediately seemed to me to originate from a sorrowful perspective. I experienced a strong emotional response upon my first formal reading of it.
styled: God bless you Miss Loretta Mry Gibson God bless you and yours these unsettled days - glorious days, however as always, ... for men who for men of good will. can humbly appreciate what enables them - us poor sinners - to glory in actually holding a place of trust Even near - at least in sight of - the General - our crucified Jesus. I am sending you a copy of the, "Prayer for Peace," of which you have likely known away ahead of me. I heard it first, only after coming to St. Bonaventures last January. . . It strck me at once as from a saddened heart. My own heart filled up, at my first official praying thereof.

neutral: The words of Isias are considered applicable to many modern scientists, educators, statesmen, and governments. The quote states: "The entire world is made desolate because no one considers things deeply." This criticism specifically targets scientists who refuse to recognize as a science the relationship and dependence of rational beings on a creator and preserver of the universe.
styled: If ever the words of Isias, have been applicable to a people or a generation of nations, they are surely appropriate today in reference to the majority of our modern "scientests", "educators", "statesmen", "Governments": "With desolation is all the world made desolate, because there is none that thinketh in their hearts." "Scientests" that refuse to recognize as a science, the most privi- leged and most fortunate relationship and dependence of the rational creacheron the divine Creator and Preserver of the Universe!

neutral: An object associated with Stephen Eckert is enclosed, along with a mention of Maurice. This is intended to focus well-wishes for Stephen Eckert, hoping for his recovery and for him to pursue a chosen life path. Especially for Stephen Eckert, there is a strong desire for extraordinary events to occur, which would advance the process of his beatification and subsequent canonization.
styled: Brother Maurice - and especially our Father Stephen Eckert - whose relic I am herewith inclosing to pray for him and if it please God that he be spared - and have a vocation. For Father Stephen especially we a hoping for miracles so as to promote his Cause of beatification first and then his canonization.

neutral: Some professionals, including scientists and educators, fail to acknowledge fundamental principles that are clearly evident through rational thought. One such foundational principle, which underpins moral codes and legitimate governance, states that a supreme being holds ultimate and absolute authority over all people, in both their personal and public lives. Furthermore, everything individuals are and possess, both individually and collectively, originates from this supreme being's generosity. Therefore, people are obligated to show the utmost respect and profound gratitude to this supreme being as their ultimate benefactor.
styled: "Scientests" and "educators", etc, that fail to see or refuse to recognize "general principals the truth of which can be plainly perceived by the light of reason"; as Pope Leo XIII, in his Encyclical on the Holy Eucharist de- clares, - giving - "for instance", the most important, all-outstanding principal whereon rests to humanity the sanctity and the soul of the Ten Commandments of God and the authority of all legitimate, divine authority; - "for instance, that the dominion of God our Creator and Preserver over all men, whether in their private or in their public life, is supreme and absolute; that our whole being and all that we possess, whether individually or as members of society, comes from the divine bounty; that we on our part are bound to show to God, as our Lord, the highest reverence, and, as He is our greatest benefactor, the deepest gratitude."

neutral: The hope and confidence expressed for little Maurice are noted. The author had a brother named Maurice Joachim Casey, who was talented and, from an early age, aspired to become a priest. At 16, during his third year in the seminary, his health declined, and he returned home, which was a disappointment for the family. Despite this, he actively promoted religious vocations and was pleased when others pursued them, particularly one of his ten brothers (the second youngest), E'd F. Casey, who had recently returned from missionary work in the Philippines, with his mission headquarters in St. Paul, Minnesota. Twenty years later, when the author was ordained and Maurice assisted at the author's first religious service, Maurice decided to resume his studies. After seven more years of study, he was ordained at the age of 43, rather than 23. This was considered a very positive development. Therefore, there is hope for a similarly improbable positive outcome for little Maurice. The author plans to remember their deceased Reverend in hopes of a positive outcome for Maurice.
styled: I am certainly pleased to see your hope and confidence in the mercy and gracious wisdom of Almighty God in regard to your little Maurice. I had a very dear and amiale brother of that name Maurice Joachim Casey. He was very talented and from earliest childhood seemed to dream of being a priest. When 16 in his 3rd year in the seminary his health failed and he came home - a family disapoint- ment. However, he worked generously in promoting vocations and was extremely pleased to others take his place - especially our 2nd youngest of ten brothers - just now back from the missions in the Philippines with his mission Headquarters in St. Paul, Minn. - Rt. Rev. E'd F. Casey. - Well after 20 years roving when I was ordained and he served at my first Holy Mass, he decided to " ... try it again and after seven years further study was ordained - at 43 instead of 23. Thanks be to God a billion. So we will hope an for something of a miracle for little Mau- rice. I am going to pray my deceased Rev.

neutral:
Dear Mother Mary Hilda,

I wish you and your supporters well, especially those at Beech Grove Hospital. I hope they increasingly appreciate the value of supporting someone who endures significant challenges and difficulties in their chosen path.

July 21st. Dear Mother Hilda, I haven't made much progress since my last attempt a week ago. I hope you maintain your courage and persevere through these challenging times. These can be meaningful times if we uphold our convictions and, when possible, are able to fully defend our principles.

Indeed, society appears to be rapidly losing its former rational balance. However, there are still individuals within society who, like historical figures known for their wisdom and foresight, maintain their principles and sense of purpose. But, unfortunately, modern society, civilization, and humanity face significant challenges.
styled: God bless you Rev. Dear Mother Mary Hilda. May He be favorable to you and to all your benefactors - most especially those in Beech Grove Hospital and bring them more and more to realize and to appreciate the privilege of harboring a religious "so tempted and tried in the humilia- tions of extraneous "warfare in the world. July 21st. Dear Mother Hilda. God help us! You see I did not get far a week ago. I do hope you keep up courage and persevere these trying times, - glorious times if by God's grace we persvere in "keeping the faith: and, God willing, having the privilege of finally giving our life its defense. For surely "civilization" has been rapidly losing its one- time rational balance. Thank God however, there are still members of society - of the human-race - who like the seers of old and the prophets and apostles keep faith with God our divine Creator and Preserver; but, Alas! for modern society! civilization! humanity!

neutral: To Mother Mary Hilda, on the day commemorating St. Ann. I have attempted to write to you multiple times over the past six months. Despite the delay, I regret not having expressed my appreciation for your kind thoughts and to thank you sooner. I wish to do so now, with profound gratitude. I hope you maintain your health and courage, remaining steadfast in your principles and contributing to the moral and spiritual betterment of others, including yourself, as personal development often begins with one's own efforts. It is often underestimated how valuable the opportunities are to face various difficulties and to dedicate these experiences to a meaningful cause. I have been reading a book titled 'The Way of Divine Love; or The Message of the Sacred Heart to the World,' which was recorded by a contemporary, Josefa Menendez, a lay sister born in 1890 who died on December 29, 1923.
styled: God Bless you Mother Mary Hilda this happy feast day of most priviliged Grand-Mother dear St. Ann. I have started to write you several times these last more than six months, and whatever the trouble, I can hardly excuse myself for such negligence in failing to express my appreciation for your kind remembrances and to say thank you, as I want to do now at least, with a thousand times God bless you. I do hope that you keep up in health and courage, persevering in keeping the Faith and helping Jesus our Savior in the saving of poor sinner's souls - including our own of course, charity beginning at home. God help us! How little we appreciate our privilige of being given opportunity after opportunity of suffering in diverse ways and of offer- ing all in union with and for the intentions of the Sacred Heart of Jesus! I have been reading: "The Way of Divine Love; or The Message of the Sacred Heart to the World", as jotted down and noted by a most privi- leged contemporary of our own, the little, kitchen-lay-sister Josefa Menendeth, born in 1890 and called to Heaven December 29, 1923.

neutral: The clear message to emphasize is the old motto: "Per aspera ad astra" (Through trials to triumph). This principle is also articulated as the necessity of experiencing many difficulties to achieve a desired ultimate state. It appears that these difficulties—trials, humiliations, and disappointments—are not merely present but are emphasized, playing a role second only to certain highly significant experiences. This process seems purposefully designed to purify individuals, especially those striving for continuous improvement ("ALWAYS EXCELSIOR"), from self-conceit—a common human tendency—and to gradually lead them into a state of clarity and profound understanding.
styled: obvious lesson it ought to stress, as seems to me, is the old addage or An motto: "Per aspera ad astera", - "Through trials to triumph": or straight prose as St. Paul gives it: "It behooves by many tribulations, to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven." Bles'd be God again in all His designs - not only including them simply - but stressing the trials, the humiliations, crosses, disappoint- ments, etc. whereby, next to the reception of the holy Sacraments in impor- tance, it would seem divinely providential that those whose motto ought to be: "ALWAYS EXCELSIOR", be purified from self conceit, so natural to origin- ally tainted human reason, and introduced gradually into the light and in- timacy of confidence with the Divine.

neutral: She acted with strict but gentle adherence to her deeply held convictions and the directives of her superiors. She endured significant physical and emotional suffering, which she actively embraced, believing it contributed to the well-being of others. While still a child at home, Josepha struggled to support her impoverished parents, whose limited financial resources had been depleted by their failing health and unforeseen family expenses, including her father's early death. From these experiences, Josepha learned many practical lessons in patience, acceptance, and trust in a higher purpose. Humility permeated all her actions, supporting her through demanding sacrifices, and she maintained hope for a positive ultimate outcome.
styled: - all in strict though gentlest obedience to Jesus and her superiors. What sufferings of soul and body she went through - what agonies she learned to welcome! - for the sake of helping Jesus to rescue straying souls! Glory be to God! Would that we might be convinced - that we might real- ize - in the time of temptation, of trial and struggle, and when the clouds seem most threatening that just then it is that Our Dear Lord in nearest and that just then too we ought to offer all to Jesus - turning to Him with the holy fear at once and the confidence of the Apostles :" Lord we perish! - Save us! " As still a child at home struggling to support herpoor parents, whose modest means had become exhausted through failing health and un- forseen family expenses, including the early death of her father, Josepha had learned many a practical lesson in patience, resignation, confidence in God; - humility permeatingall, supporting every step toward the heights of Calvary and confidence in Heaven.

neutral: September 17, 1951. I hope this message finds you well and continuing to navigate life's challenges, which I believe offer valuable opportunities for personal growth. Miss B. from Decatur visited this afternoon with her two sisters, niece-in-law, and young daughter. They were pleased to hear about your visit. I later found this letter, which I had started about a month ago but set aside to address a more urgent matter. I am sending it now, hoping it is not too late or inconvenient. As a context for Miss Gibson's letter that I gave you on Sunday, I will try to obtain a copy of the letter she wrote to me approximately a week before the trial, when the situation appeared very serious. I believe you will find it interesting, as it will enhance your understanding and appreciation of the subsequent letter.
styled: Sept. 17, 1951 - God bless you Rev. Mother Mary Hilda. I hope this finds you - still on the way of the cross, the best school wherein to learn appreciation for and love of Jesus Cricified divine lover of souls. Our friend Miss B. from Decatur was here this P. M. with her two sisters, niece-in-law and little girl, - pleasantly surprised on hearing of your visit, etc. Afterwards I just came across the above started letter which I had pulled out of the machine about a month ago to get something off that seemed more immediately urgent. So, hoping that it is not too late or too inopportune I'm sendingit just as it is. However, as a sort of key to the letter from Miss Gibson which I gave you Sunday, I am going to try to get a copy for you of the letter she wrote me a week or so before the trial when things seemed so very threatening. I am sure you will enjoy it - as heightening the interest and beauty of the one that followed.

neutral: We hope you are doing well. Given what you have been experiencing over the past several months, we understand that 'well' implies maintaining your spirits and sustaining a hopeful perspective. It would be even better if your physical condition does not worsen, leading to a clear improvement and eventual full recovery. The main purpose of this card, as I was unable to complete the letter I intended to send, is to reassure you that we are thinking of you and will continue to remember you.
styled: We all hope this finds you well - which, for one ex- periencing what you have been going through these several months, must mean that you are keeping up courage and by the grace of God continuing to foster confidence in His merciful wisdom and goodness - all the better of course if the physical condition, at least does non get worse, till we see a decided im- provement and final recovery, God willing. The purpose of this card, since I cannot finish the letter I wanted to send you, is primarily, to just reassure you that we are keeping you in mind and please God will not forget you in our prayers.

neutral:
The communication dated June 20th was received. It was initially set aside and almost disregarded until its conclusion was reached.

Although the situation remains fundamentally unchanged, encouragement is offered regarding the stated problems concerning the concept of a deity and the relationship between scientific and religious perspectives.

For individuals adhering to the Church's practices, these problems are largely resolved through a specific ritual of initiation. Through the efficacy of that ritual, the individual is understood to acquire core principles of belief, expectation, and benevolence. As a result, from the outset, the individual becomes readily disposed to accept beliefs, and to perceive the Church and trust it with increasing certainty, viewing it as having a supernatural origin and being unerringly directed. This is in its role as a guiding and nurturing entity for individuals believed to possess immortal spirits, who are considered candidates for a state of ultimate, everlasting fulfillment. This state is described as being beyond human perception or imagination, reserved for those who demonstrate devotion.
styled: Many thanks for your pathetic communication of June 20th, which I had to put aside at the time and which frankly, till I neared its conclusion, I was inclined to ignore. However, though the situation is not essen- tially changed, I feel bound to offer you something of encouragement for the "problems" of which you complain, viz, about God and about "science and religion". For "practical children of the Church" such problems are to a great extent solved at baptism; so that by the grace of that Sacrament the principles of the "triune virtue of Faith - Hope - Charity" are divinely infused into the soul whereby, from the very start it be- comes docilly inclined to believe; and to behold the Church and to confide in her with growing conviction as divinely founded and as infallibly guided in her capacity of mother and mistress of immortal souls - of human candidates for the life of eternal glory; of which St. Paul writes: "Bye hath not seen, ear hath not heard, nor hath it entered into the heart of man to conceive what things God has prepared for them that love Fim".

neutral: First, it is important to acknowledge a significant failure, which is not limited to an individual but extends to all of humanity. This may be humanity's most profound failure, occurring despite our capacity for thought and reason, our scientific progress, and the extensive historical evidence suggesting that disregarding fundamental dependencies leads to unfavorable outcomes. Humanity has largely failed to acknowledge as a science what could be considered the most crucial understanding for all rational beings: the fundamental reliance on ultimate principles or a higher power, and the interconnectedness with fellow beings.
styled: But let us first lament your failure - which is not yours only but humanity's to which we both belong. Perhaps our sadest failure, notwith- standing our faculties for thinking and reasoning, notwithstanding our advanced steps in every phase of science and, (what ought to count most of all in the natural order of conclusion) notwithstanding uncounted ages of bitterest experience of men and angels, that ingratitude to God never pays. We have in great part failed to recognize as a science, the one, in the sight of heaven, greatest science of all times and of all places wherever pertains to rational creatures. We have failed to recognize as a science OUR MOST FORTUNATE RELATIONSHIP - absolute depen- dence on the Almighty, all merciful God, and together with that, our dependence on our neighbor.

neutral: I hope you are doing well and that things are going favorably for you. I recognize that my delay in acknowledging your kind communication of December 6th was likely disappointing. I will be dedicating my next complimentary religious service to your intentions, guidance, and welfare. Incidentally, we are able to dedicate two such complimentary religious services each month.
styled: I hope you are well and that things are coming favorably for you. I am sure my failure to acknowledge your appreciated favor of December 6th last, must have been deeply disapointing. Please pardon! I can hardly explain further than that, wish- ing to thank you personaly for such a favor, I put your brief letter aside and, some how or other it was simply "snowd under." Besides this, I am going to offer my first - next - "Free Mass" for your intentions, your guidance, and welfare. Incidently we have the privilege of two such "free-Masse " each month.

neutral: Miss Gibson's friend experienced another difficulty, which left her distressed. Miss Gibson often described this friend as highly virtuous and continued to trust in her support. After spending time at the grave, Miss Gibson took a small cutting from a plant growing there, known as an "immortal." She placed it into a small, round container, approximately two inches wide and half an inch deep. She quietly remarked to herself, "This will be my keepsake." Soon after, while packing her luggage for a journey west, she casually placed the container into her trunk, giving it no further thought. Weeks later, while searching for another item, she unexpectedly rediscovered the small container. She thought, "Here is my keepsake!" Her emotional reaction to finding the plant not only fresh and green but also perfectly in bloom was profoundly intense, far exceeding simple surprise.
styled: Just another knock for the girl-friend left to weep and to pray - - - of whom she was wont to speak as being a saint and on the help of whose prayers she still seems to have confidence. Having lingered at the Grave . . . Miss Gibson plucked a slip of an "immortal" (a little plant grow- ing on the grave), and simply put it in a little, round "vanity-box" perhaps two inches wide and a 1/2 of an inch deep, half saying to herself: "This will be my relique." Shortly afterwards she was packing her trunk to come West and without further ado, like tossed it into the trunk to take care of itself. Weeks afterwards she was looking for something else when the little "vanity-box" unexpectedly appeared. "O!", she thought, "Here is my relic!". Her emotion on finding it not only fresh and green but perfectly in bloom was un- speakably more than surprise.

This unique information, along with the enclosed sample letter, is expected to alter perceptions of the institution and potentially reverse previously held attitudes toward the foundress. This is intended to provide relief and acknowledge the foundress's endurance. The delay in sharing this information is regrettable.

Approximately twenty-five years ago, two young nurses visited Saint Bonaventure Monastery in Detroit to seek guidance on establishing a cancer hospital. They were enrolled in the Seraphic Mass Association and were assured of spiritual support for their project. These visits occurred repeatedly over a period of two or more years, leading to an initial impression that they might be unrealistic in their aspirations. Eventually, while Miss Gibson was ill in a Detroit hospital, her friend, the other nurse, Miss Daily, died in New York.

Rev. Paternity. Ah! for your own joyous relief as well as her estremely tried fortitude. I beg pardon for such culpable hesita- tion. Glory be to God. Following are a few details. About twenty-five years back two young nurses came to Saint Bonaventure Monastery in Detroit seeking guidance in regard to starting a cancer-hospital. I enrolled them in the Seraphic Mass Association and promised to pray for them and their project. This repeated itself a number of times for two or more years; so that I was inclined to take them for a "sort of dreamers" (?) . . . Finally while Miss Gibson was sice in a Detroit hospital her girl-friend the other nurse - her "saintly friend" as she consi- dered, (a certain Miss Daily), died in New York.

styled: The sacred Historian, (Genesis III), assures us that the very first thing our poor, dear First Parents, Adam & Eve did, after their sin of disobedience, was to make aprons for themselves, - evidently to avoid giving scandal. neutral: Bernard, a prominent religious scholar of the eleventh century, often advised people of his time, particularly against being offended or causing offense. He would state that since the crucifixion of Jesus Christ, it is never reasonable to be offended or cause offense. The passage asserts the belief that from that ultimate offense, God saved humanity and brought about its restoration. Writers on self-discipline emphasize the importance of openness and trust with those in authority, and with those perceived as representing a higher authority. Regarding members of a religious community who refuse to communicate with other members over minor offenses or personal dislikes, the author considers such behavior to be indicative of a regrettable narrow-mindedness. Patience is advised in such situations, along with a call for self-reflection and a desire for positive change in others, emphasizing that positive change begins with oneself. The author suggests this approach contributes to what is presented as Jesus's purpose of transforming and saving humanity. However, the author also expresses concern about the infiltration of communist ideology into religious communities.
styled: Bernard the outstanding Doctor of the Church of the eleventh century was wont to exhort the people of his day, especially against taking scandal: "Since the Crucifixion of Jusus Christ, "he would admonish, "it is never reasonable to take scandal." . Ah! Because from that climax of scandal God saved Humanity - decre- ed Heaven's rehabilitation. Glory be to God! ... Ascetic writers always stress openness and confidence with our superiors as with those represent- ing or taking God's place in our regards. As for "religious" in a community who persist in refusing to speak to member of the community because of some petty offense or dislike ? ! The very fact of such example would in my opinion indicate as a rule, PITIFUL narowness. Patience in such cases and prayer for conversion of sinners - always including one'self - charity beginning at home. In this way we can help Jesus in His great purpose of converting and redeeming Humanity. However, there is such a thing as "red communism" stealing into convents and monasterys.

Best wishes and affection to Brother Guss and Frank, and to all, including Aunt Jennie.
styled: Tell little Francis that he must foster and cultivate continually a great love for Jesus in Communion so that he may become some day an imitator of his great patron - the Seraphic Father St. Francis of Asissi. And Oh how Therese ought to imitate the little Servant of God Therese of Lisieux - "Little Flower of Jesus". Dear Margaret, if ever there was good for a family like yours, her autobiography is one. She died only about fifteen years ago. Her cause for beatification is now in Rome and I am asking her for entire reconciliation between J.T. and T.J. - as also other favors. She is our manager just thinking of it, of our contest. You ought not fail in procuring this book. She makes sanctity so really atractive and so beautifuly simple. I think the book costs $2.00 at P.J. Kennedy and Son's Barclay N.Y. Do not fail to bless your family with its presence. But Dear Margaret I'll now have to conclude. Hoping you are all continuing in good health of body, mind and soul, I remain P.S. Best wishes and love to Brother Guss and to Frank - and to all "Aunt Jennie not forgotten.

neutral: The natural scene currently visible is as picturesque as any historical scene. The Hudson River's mouth appears like a silver lake on the horizon, with hills, valleys, and human structures in between. The author considers nature to be merely a foundational layer when viewed in comparison to a higher, non-natural reality. The author questions the value of natural blessings without the prospect of immortality. They believe they would become distressed, longing for something more profound, if their only sources of enjoyment or hope were natural elements, even if they possessed every natural advantage and benefit ever experienced by humanity. The author expresses gratitude for their belief system, for their parents (described as simple, honest, and faithful), and for their life's calling and the ability to pursue it, even if imperfectly. They also express gratitude for a profound hope: that during their earthly existence, they will eventually achieve eternal unity with a select group in a state of peace and belonging, within a context of ultimate love and fulfillment.
styled: Surely the natural scene now before me when I turn my head to look at it is as picturesque as any scene of long ago - the mouth of the Hudson shining like a silver lake away in the horizon in the clouds I was going to say with hills and vallies and human achievement between. But what is nature in the light of the supernatural? Ah, a substratum! And what are natural blessing with hope of immortality? I believe that I'd go crazy, yearning for something higher if I had noth- ing to enjoy or to hope for but the natural - even had I all the natural gifts and blessings ever enjoyed by man. But thanks be to God for the True Faith! Thanks be to God for the simple honest, faithful parents that God gave us! Thanks be to God for vocation and for strength to fol- low the call, at least imperfectly! Thanks be to God for the blessed hope that He gives us here in our exile of once being eternally united with His chosen ones in the peace of our true home, in the love of His Sacred Heart!

neutral:
I began writing a card for you on July 20. I remembered you that day. You are probably wondering why I am in the hospital. I did not come here for pleasure. Nevertheless, I am grateful for the entire experience since my arrival. I believe a few details will be interesting and beneficial. I will share some of them now and explain their purpose afterward.

On Saturday night, Dr. Edgerton examined me and diagnosed gangrene, declaring the case urgent. He instructed that Dr. Kirchen be present at 10 o'clock the next day. Dr. Edgerton then told the nurse that they would administer anesthesia and make an incision. I had spent the entire night counting the hours, at times wondering if I would be able to perform my scheduled duties at 6 o'clock, and how I would manage to endure until 10 o'clock.
styled: I started a card to you on your nameday - Feast of St Margaret V. and Martyr - July 20 the eve of my own dear Patron's feast day. I did not forget you in my holy office and Mass that day. You will probably wonder what the cause is for my being in the hospital, etc. Well I did not come up here for pleasure, of course. Yet I thank God for the whole experience here since my arrival. No doubt a few details will be interesting, and I hope profitable. I will give you some of them now and tell you their purpose afterward. Examined by Dr. Edgerton (excellent physician) Saturday night my case was pronounced gangreenous and - a Sunday case i.e. urgent. "Tell Dr. Kirchen to be here at 10 oclock tomorrow", and he said to the nurse(our cousin Joseph Parker) an excellent Tertiary, "We'll give him a whiff of gass and slitt that open.". I had counted the hours all night wondering at times if I'd be pos- sibly able to say holy Mass at 6 oclock as prearranged, and how I might hold out till 10 oclock.

neutral: The individual was removed from danger. Due to a mistaken permission (which was discovered the following evening), the individual began officiating a religious service on Tuesday and has continued to do so since. On Monday, the individual's participation was limited to receiving a religious sacrament.
styled: me out of danger .* By God's dear providence on a mistaken permission (as I learned the fol- lowing evening), I said holy Mass Tuesday and have been celebrating since. *I had to be content with receiving Holy Communion (Monday).

neutral: In his final letter, my father stated that he had enjoyed the good things of this world and hoped for genuine gratitude. From the few details I have received about his passing, his final struggle was the most difficult, and his ultimate triumph was the most significant. I had intended to send this yesterday, but I fell asleep and was unable to. I am feeling better today, though my chest cold is still severe. I want to acknowledge your Christmas letter, as well as the one you wrote from Klamath Falls. I would certainly have answered both, but in addition to not being a skilled letter writer, my time is limited, and I am therefore unable to write as often as I would like. I must thank you once more for your thoughtful well wishes. I hope to always be grateful for them.
styled: In his last letter to me Papa, Lord have mercy on him. wrote, "I have enjoyed the good things of this world - pray that we may be truly thankful." .... but from the few details of his beautiful death that I have received, his last struggle was the hardest, his last victory the most glorious. Thanks be to God and all His Saints! Well dear Margaret, I wanted to send this off yesterday but I guess sleep kind of over came me or something of the kind and I had to let it go. I am feeling better today, thank God, though my chest cold is still heavy. I want to acknowledge your welcome letter for Christmas as also the one you wrote from Klamath Falls. I certainly would have answered both of these, but you know dear Sister that besides naturally a poor letter writer, my time is not my own and I am not at liberty therefore to write letters as often as I might like. I must thank you once more for your beautiful boquet of prayers etc. I hope that I may never be ungrateful for the same.

neutral: This description aims to be as literal and plain as possible. Following a pleasant and confidential exchange with the doctors, their demeanor became less serious, though they maintained their white caps and gauze-covered mouths. Dr. Egerton then instructed them to roll the patient in, head first. On the sixth breath of gas, and with effort, the patient called out "all right." During the initial breaths, the patient had doubted the effectiveness of the gas. Consciousness was rapidly fading when bells began to ring from St. Joseph's Hospital for consumptives across the street. A voice gently announced, "There's the Angelus." The sound of the bells and the announcement provided comfort. The patient realized that consciousness was at its end.
styled: Of course it might be given other and otherwise, but that's how the music measure runs and we wanted it as litteral and as plain as possible After some joking with the doctors - better say, confidential and pleasant, humors thought-exchange - They put off their "long faces", though keeping their white caps and gause-covered mouths. Dr. Egerton concluded: "Well roll him in here now ... only head first." .... With my 6th breath of gass, and an effort, I called out: "all right!" ( the first couple of breaths, I almost doubted if "the stuff was any good.") Life and light was going fast when beautiful bells began to ring: (St. Joseph's Hospital for comsumptives is just across the street) and a voice gently and piously reminded: "There's the Angelus." O, how sweet that music to my soul and the announcement, - how confidence - inspiring! I realized that consciousness had come to the very end.

neutral: This communication acknowledges a letter received several weeks ago. The correspondent is preparing to depart Yonkers for a new assignment in the city center. This involves leaving the Sacred Heart Monastery and Parish, where the correspondent has worked for nearly fourteen years. A provincial Chapter meeting was held in Detroit last week (July 11-14), and the changes were announced today. Maurice recently mentioned your new responsibility. Children from five years ago are now becoming young adults. The correspondent's new address will be: [New Address]. A copy of Edward's 'Jubilee Poem' is requested, as the correspondent's copy was lost.
styled: Just a few words in acknowledgement of your kind letter of some weeks ago. I am just about ready to leave Yonkers for a new field down in the very heart of the metropolis. In a way I almost feel sad to leave the Sacred Heart Monastery and Parish where I've been labor- ing (if laboring is the right word) for close onto fourteen years. We had a provincial Chapter in Detroit last week (July 11 - 14) and we just learned Today of the changes made. Fr. Maurice was telling me recently of your new little charge that God has entrusted to you. Thank God for all things! I suppose little boys and girls of five years ago are quite becoming "youths and maidens" Well God bless them all and call them to His special service and direct them all and us all according to His "holy will".
