styled: Many thanks for your kind favor just noted. I have given my enrollment over to the Poor Souls in Purgatory - especially for those of Kenneth's rela- tives - that they help to obtain the necessary peace for him to be consciencously earnest. In the mean time, have as many as possible "storm Heaven by daily - or more frequent - Communion". Hop- ing to get better word the next time and praying for God's guidance, I beg to remain

neutral: A significant problem is our failure to adequately appreciate the commitments made to us, contingent on our loyalty. Without divine assistance, and given the many benefits present in the natural world (even in this life, which is seen as a prelude to what comes next), we risk completely overlooking those commitments that pertain to an existence beyond the natural and temporal. Regarding these profound commitments, which deepen with contemplation, particularly when viewed through the exemplary lives of devoted individuals, a historical figure, Paul, points out: "No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human mind has conceived what is prepared for those who are dedicated." Discouragement is a common experience, often serving as a cunning and effective method to mislead individuals who lack experience in navigating moral or psychological challenges. Yielding to it is never beneficial. Such visionary experiences or insights are often believed to originate from a higher power.
styled: The great trouble is that we take so little pains to appreciate the promises that God makes us, if only we keep faith with Him, that without the grace of God and in view of the manifold blessings He gives in all nature, even in this, like - a - vestibule to eternity, we are liable to lose sight entirely of those promises of a supernatural and eternal nature. Refering to these latter that grow in greatness in proportion to the reflection given them in the light of God's grace as seen in the lives of the saints, St. Paul reminds us: " .... Eye hath not seen, ear hath not heard, nor hath it entered into the heart of man to con- ceive what God hath prepared for them that love Him. . Discouragement? ! Who is there that is without temptations in that, one of Satan's most weily and successful means of entraping souls, spirit- ually inexperienced. It NEVER pays. As to such dream-likes you mention; they are often from God.

neutral: Thank you for your kindness, which I have received and noted. I intended to write a more detailed letter, but I haven't had the time. However, I am pleased to hear that you and Thed enjoyed your visit here. I hope it benefited both of you and, more importantly, contributed positively to the significant path that lies ahead for each of you. This earthly life, though brief when considered against a longer timescale, is a profound mystery composed of many smaller mysteries. It can be compared to a medical procedure one must undergo to achieve good health, particularly for those who are unwell. The implication is that everyone experiences some form of suffering or imperfection.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favors duly Rec'd and noted. I wanted to write a real letter, but it just seem to be out of the question to get the time. However, I am pleased to know that you and our friend Thed enjoyed your little visit here. I hope it did both of you good and more, that it will have been to the advantage of what after all is what counts for aught, the great Providence of God ahead of each one of us. This whole earthly existence, momentary as it all is - in view of eternity - is such a big mystery made up of mysteries, that its like an operation one has to submit to before enjoying good health, viz, for those who are ailing, and since the Fall of Adam and Eve - God help us, who isn't ailing.

neutral: Gabriel visited us today after driving from Notre Dame. He mentioned that you have been unwell recently. I sympathize with you and hope for your speedy recovery. A trip to Quebec, Mont Royal, and other locations would be beneficial for you and your companions. I would enjoy accompanying you. Please communicate with us. Stay well.
styled: Our Friend Fr. Gabriel drove down from Notre Dame Today and had quite a nice little visit with us. He was telling of you not being too well recently. I surely sympathise with you and hope your re- covery may come speedily, God willing - God Willing. .... It would a great thing for you if you and your Brothers could, a little trip to the scenes of Quebec, Mont Royal, etc. .. I surely would enjoy going. Please let us hear from you. . Keep well . .

styled: Joseph), she exclaimed: "That's the man who rescued me from the bear!" .. She at once started to find out about St. Joseph and would have no rest till she became a Catholic and a fervent member of that community of St. Joseph in Mt'Real. Pray too, of course that your poor, dear Parents may wake up and have more faith. Ah!

She lost consciousness. When she regained consciousness, she immediately realized she was being held gently by a man with a very kind and inspiring face. He then set her down at the edge of her father's clearing. She turned to thank the man, whose brief glance as he set her down had immediately filled her with confidence and warmth, but he had already vanished.

Her parents were wealthy by conventional standards and traveled frequently, not only within their own country but also in Europe and other places. The girl traveled with them, and whether at home or abroad, she always hoped to encounter her unforgettable benefactor, whose face remained vividly in her memory. Eventually, they visited a St. Joseph's Convent in Montreal. Upon entering, she saw a picture of St. Joseph above the main altar.
styled: like way and with as much confidence as she could as she swooned away totally unconscious. When she came to herself, she at once realized that she was gently enfolded in the arms a most inspiring-countenanced man, who let her down at the edge of her father's clearing. She turned to thank such a benefactor, the momentary meeting of whose glance as he let her down had inspired her at once with confidence and love but he had al- ready vanished. .. Her parents well to do, according to the standards of the world, whose estimation and appreciation hardly reach to touch the supernatural, were wont to travel quite a lot.
