neutral: It is desirable that everyone recognize and adopt the three interconnected virtues of belief, hope, and compassion. These virtues are essentially unified and represent a fundamental and significant aspect of human nature. However, belief is considered to hold theoretical precedence.
styled: that we all wake up and with holy faith put on, as vestment to our souls, the brightened and happy triune virtue of faith, hope, charity; essentially one and the all-outstanding trace of the Holy Trinity in our immortal souls; faith, however, being theoretically first - as is the Eternal Father in the Holy Trinity.

neutral: Gratitude for favors received is identified as the primary and most reliable practical indicator of intelligence. According to Pope Pius XII, humanity's foremost and most serious duty is gratitude for favors received.
styled: God bless you Wallace - Wallace Bedolfe and all your dear ones. O Lord Jesus! Blessed God! Teach us appreciation that we may learn something of the first and surest practical indication of intelligence - Gratitude for favors received. According to Pope Pius XII Man's first and gravest duty is just that. Gratitude for favors received.

neutral: Maintain courage, as it is a significant part of overcoming challenges. Fostering confidence is believed to lead to certain success. Individuals, like autumn flowers, have a brief existence. The speaker finds a profound lesson in the lives of others. The speaker acknowledges mortality, but believes in a continued existence beyond physical death, culminating in a complete, restored form. The speaker expresses hope for rapid health improvement, contingent on favorable conditions, and for guidance.
styled: God bless you Barbara. Keep Courage "-half the battle": Foster Confidence in God - Victory assured. Dear Brothers Like flowers of Autumn we bloom and shortly fade. and sisters your lesson to me is your very life. Like you I must die but my soul continues and finally will claim my whole risen self. Blessed be God in all His designs! -for speedy health-improvement, God willing and for His guidance

neutral: The long-awaited copies have arrived. The first copy is being sent to W. V. Bedolfe, along with an expression of gratitude for the valuable books. The author considers it highly beneficial to perform a specific contemplative practice before reading them.
styled: Well the waited-for coppies have come finally and I am sending the first one to you W. V. Bedolfe and at last thanking for those precious books. I find it a great advantage, to pray to the Holy Ghost - Third Person of the Blessed Trinity before reading them.

neutral: Your letter from several months ago has been received and its contents noted. The delay in responding is regretted, as the letter was not read until today. Concern is expressed regarding your child's eczema. For eczema, applying diluted creolin by sponging is suggested, using approximately a teaspoonful or more per pint of water. Enrollment in an association has also reportedly produced very positive results.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of several months ago - duly rec'd and notes. Please pardon delayed acknowlegement .. I surely sympathize with your little one who has eczema. I do not know how it came that only To-day I got to read your letter. To sponge with diluted creclin is good for eczema. - say . a teaspoonful or more in a pint of water. Enrollment in the Seraphic Mass Assoc'n too has brought wonder results. ..

neutral: Thank you for your communication dated June 29. I apologize for the delay in responding, as I only received it a few days ago. However, we have had several cases that clearly indicate the Association's benefits begin as soon as an offering is made or a name is recorded. Therefore, I hope that things went favorably for your sister or that they will soon improve. After all, life on Earth is so short and uncertain that it sometimes seems it should be called something else.
styled: Many thanks for your favor of June. 29. Sorry I only got to it a few day ago. However, we have had several cases that would plainly in- dicate that the benefits of the Association start as soon as an offer- ing is made or the name is recorded. Hence my hope that things went favorably for your dear sister or that they shortly come the right way. Let us pray at all events, that we be guided according to God's holy will -- at all times and in every thing meritoriously resigned to the same. After all "life" here in this "Exile is so short and so uncertain that it some times seems it ought to have another name.

neutral: I am awaiting copies of an informal letter from Monsignor Edward regarding the death of Grace Agatha Brady. She died on the Friday of Easter Week after a long illness of twenty months. Her husband had also died suddenly, though his death was anticipated and peaceful. Grace remained conscious until the end. Wallace likely remembers her visit to Toronto six years ago in January, when she traveled from San Francisco for the speaker's fiftieth anniversary. It had been several decades since she had seen Wallace's mother, Blanche, who is also the speaker's cousin. She reportedly enjoyed her two-week stay.
styled: Dear Wallace: I am waiting now for a number of coppies, one of which I want to send you, of the informal letter Father Edward - Monsignore - sent me on occa- sion of what we think was our Sister Grace Agatha Brady's peaceful and beautiful death. Yes, Friday of Easter Week, after a cheerfully suffered, long twenty months - including her husband's peculiarly foreseen and peace- ful, even - if sudden death, having received everything and been conscious till the last - poor, dear, little GrandMa Grace, like a tired child con- fident in the arms enfolding it, sighed-out her soul to Heaven -- like the last tickings of a clock - "Holy Mary ... take, me, home." I am sure you will remember her from her visit in Toronto six years last January, when she flew-in from San Francisco on occasion of my fifty years in the Order. I think it had been several decads since she had seen your dear Mother - our Cousin Blanche - and seemed at the time to have quite enjoyed her couple of weeks stay.

neutral: Hello Mrs. Sullivan McCarthy. I hope you and your family are doing well during these challenging times. I started to write to you several times since receiving your letter about a month ago. I did not realize how simple and modest your request was until this morning when I reread it. Please pardon my oversight and the resulting delay. I hope the following information will be useful. I certainly remember you and your entire Sullivan family, and I have pleasant and grateful memories of you all. I did not know your husband, Mr. McCarthy, very well. I believe he was known as quite a genius with pencil and brush. I was unaware of your marriage (which, according to your recent letter, took place on January 26th, 1949) until you visited Saint Felix shortly after, presumably with Mr. McCarthy and your sister Myrtle, and introduced him as your husband.
styled: God bless you Mrs. Sullivan Mccarthy. God bless you and yours these days, at once of threatening forebodings and of God's outstanding mercies. I hope this finds you all well. I started to write you several times since receiving your letter of about a month ago. Somehow I did not realize how simple and modest was your request till this Morning when I read it over again. Please pardon my oversight, etc and my consequent delay. I hope the following may not be without purpose. Yes: of course I remember you and your whole Sullivan Famile, and that, not without pleasant and grateful memories. I did not know your Hus- band McCarthy so well. I believe he was known as quite a genius with pen- cil and brush. I had not known of your marriage, (which had taken place according to your recent letter, on January 26th 1949), till you came down to Saint Felix shortly after as I would naturally suppose, with Mr. McCarthy and your Sister Myrtle and introduced the former as you Husband.

neutral: Wallace Bedolfe, residing in Toronto, I acknowledge the safe receipt of the three sets of "Mystical City of God" by Venerable Mother Mary of Jesus of Agreda, which you generously sent. Although I knew you had already been informed of their arrival, I regret my delay in formally acknowledging this much-appreciated gift. I hope you will overlook this oversight and pardon me, as I find it impossible to respond as I would like, or even acknowledge half of the many interesting and often urgent letters I receive for my attention. I regret my inability to adequately address these many cases.
styled: God bless you Wallace Bedolfe this beautiful morning and solemn season - 2nd Sunday after Easter. Yes. May He bless you all up there in Toronto. Though I knew of your being informed as to my safe reception of the highly appreciated books you so generously sent me - three sets of the "Mystical City of God", by Venerable Mother Mary of Jesus of Agreda, - though I knew of your having been informed thereof - I am nevertheless ashamed of my tardiness, etc, in acknowledging such an appreciated favor. I feel, however, that you will overlook my negligence - rather the culpability thereof and pardon me - if I assure you that I find it simply impossible to answer as I would like to do or even acknowledge one half of the interesting and often urgent letters coming hither for my inspection. I hope that my poor prayers may in some way make up for the deficiency in so many cases that otherwise I can only regret.

neutral: Regarding your communication of May 28th: Mr. Panyard's name has been inscribed as requested, and his certificate is being sent separately. It is believed that his current difficulties are intended to have a positive outcome. The situation is expected to improve if his friends commit to specific positive actions, and particularly if he himself commits to a regular weekly practice for six months, or at least monthly for a year.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of May 28th. I in- scribed Mr. Panyard's name as requested and am sending his certificate under separate cover. .I have not the least doubt that the trouble he finds himself in is meant to be a blessing in dis- guise .... If his friends promise something specially pleasing to God, and surely if he himself promised weekly Communion for 6 months - or at least month- ly - for a year, everything will be OK ....

neutral: Thank you very much for the perfect job on ".... Cure for the Blues" and for the copies. It was good to hear that Grandma had a very happy birthday celebration, and we hope for many more.
styled: God bless you and yours --- with a thousand thanks for the perfect job on the " .... Cure for the Blues" - and the few copies. Glad too that Grandma had such a happy birth-day cele- bration - Many happy returns please God.

neutral: An initial positive reaction to the announcement was followed by a momentary feeling of embarrassment due to an unexpected apathy towards the wedding. Subsequently, the later expression of distress regarding the husband's sexual impotence provided an explanation for the earlier, unenthusiastic congratulation. Sympathy was felt for both individuals. Sympathy is extended to anyone whose life circumstances, obligations, and anticipated joys and pleasures depend on such essential physical capabilities. Conversely, these capabilities can be secondary or nonessential, and their absence may, in many situations, provide relief from significant responsibilities. Such physical limitations, which can affect anyone, have often been observed to facilitate a complete detachment from worldly concerns and a dedicated pursuit of an ascetic life.
styled: I was glad at the announcement, etc, But whether I must have sensed something lame about the wedding affair, (which I hardly think I did), I do remember a sort of embarrassment which I experienced momentarily just then, on account of my own unwanted apathy. At all events, your lament shortly afterwards, concern- ing your Husband's trouble, (impotentia sexualis), seemed more or less like a mysterious key for that unwonted, halfhearted congratulation. I surely felt sorry for both of you. I cannot but sympathize with any one so hampered, whose state in life and consequent obligations, as well as, to a great extent, whose privileged duties and laudable joys and pleasures presuppose just such-we may say-vital faculties. Otherwise of course, they may B altogether secondary, nonessential and their absence, in many cases at least nothing less than a relief from weighty obligations. In fact, Church history and the Lives of the Saints abound in examples just such and similar weaknesses - which incidently, is liable to come to anyone - has been the last tie in the world from a complete break with worldness and a positive, determined "take-off for Heavenly existence.

neutral: Thank you for your communication dated August 25, which I have just received. I hope the situation between the two families resolves amicably. If you have the opportunity, emphasize the importance of peacemaking, noting that overlooking a neighbor's shortcomings is a practical way to achieve it. It is anticipated that the enrollments will be beneficial, as they rarely fail. I had a significant long-distance conversation with Rae Garland and several others from Detroit this afternoon. Everyone seems well and optimistic. Last week, we attended a successful retreat near Garrison on the Hudson at the Monastery of the Immaculate Conception. P.S. I hope to find a system to catch up with my correspondence.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your favor of Aug. 25 just noted. I hope things smooth off amicably between the two families. If you have opportunity, try and stress " ... Blessed are the Peace-makers for they shall be called the child- ren of God" .. Who is a more practical peace-maker than he who overlooks short-comings of a neighbor. - Please God the Enroll- ments will the Poor Souls will help. Thank God they hardly ever fail. I had quite a talk with Rae Garland and a number of others from Detroit this p.m. - long distance. All seem well and hope- ful. Thanks be to God. We had a fine retreat up near Garrison on the Hudson last week in the Monastery of the Immaculate Conception. P.S. pray that I get some system whereby to catchup with my correspondence.

neutral: Best wishes to you and your family. Thank you for your message, received and noted yesterday. I am pleased to hear that things are progressing smoothly. I hope Grace remains courageous and overcomes her worries. I'm glad to hear that my namesake is already active, even if still crawling. I am grateful for all positive developments. I hope the Kuhns encounter no significant problems in finding a suitable location. Please inform Mother not to be anxious or overly disappointed about our planned visit. In just three more years, a new phase will begin, and it's uncertain how our situation will be adjusted. I find the best approach is simply to trust that everything we have and everything about ourselves will be managed. Thank you for offering copies of the "Rhyme Letter." I would certainly appreciate a few dozen. I am sending you a copy of another one by Ed. Perhaps you created it yourself. In any case, I hope you will like it.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your favor Rec'd and noted yesterday. I am glad to know thing are smoothing along favor- ably. Hope Grace keep up courage and shake off the enemy of soul and body - Worry. Glad to hear my namesake is already able to display his ener- gies, even if as yet only on all fours. Thanks be to God for all His blessings. I hope the Kuhns meet no serious difficulty in finding a suitable location. Tell Mother not to be anxious or too disapointed about our proposed visit. Only three years more and we'll have another chapter and who knows what they'll do with adjusting of the, us. Best way I find is simply to leave Every thing we have - and every thing we ourselves - in God's holy keeping. Many thanks for your prof- fered favor of copies of the "Rhyme Letter" I surely would appreciate a few dozen. I am sending a copy of another one of Fr. Ed's just for your- self. Possibly you made it yourself. At all events, I hope you'll like P.S.

neutral: I hope you are all well and have recovered from the snow-wind storm that affected your area a week ago and impacted us last Thursday and Friday. I am writing to ask a favor, which I believe you will also consider a compliment. Regardless, I want you to see the photo of someone who is widely considered a saint and is hoped to be canonized someday: Father Pius, the stigmatic from Foligno. I would greatly appreciate it if you could have a simple frame put on it for us. It is the only one of its kind I possess. The smaller photo, which is also unique among my possessions, is for Doris, and I believe you will find it suitable for her prayer book.
styled: God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you all well - and surviving your snow-wind storm of a week ago that reached us last Thursday and Friday. Thanks be to God for all. I am taking the liberty of asking a favor of you that I think you'll take as a compliment too. At all events I want to have you see the photo of one who in many quarters is considered a saint - some day please God to be cannonized, Fr. Pius the stignatic from Foligno. I would appreciate it very much if you would have a simple little frame put on it for us. Its the only one of the kind I have. The smaller one which is also the only one I have but which I think you will like for your prayer book is for Doris.

neutral: Greetings to all our friends at St. Paul's. I regret that I have not been able to join you as before. However, I will be thinking of you. I believe that promoting understanding of Mary is especially relevant during these turbulent and uncertain times. It almost seems as if malevolent forces are at work. I believe that prayer is necessary, and that a deeper understanding and appreciation of Mary could lead to a better understanding of the ultimate source of all things. I had hoped to send a more substantial letter, but the day has been extremely busy. However, my health is improving, and I hope to be able to join you again soon. I received an interesting letter from Mother Mary Generose at Holy Family Convent in Manitowoc, Wisconsin. They have requested that we keep them in our thoughts. They enjoyed their visit with us on November 1st.
styled: God bless you and yours-all our friends at St. Pauls To-morrow. Regret I have not been able to be with you as formerly. However, I shall remember you all in my prayers and holy Mass and be with you in spirit. If ever it were in place to make our Blessed Mother Mary known, then it seems to me to be most opportune these days - so full of tur- moil and uncertainty. It would almost seem that anti Christ were already pushing his feindish plans. We must pray, therefore, and by learning to know our Bl. Mother and to love her more merit a better knowledge of the Creator of all. I hoped to reach you with a letter worth while but its been rush Rush all day long. Thanks be to God, however, my health is improving and I hope that before long I shall be able to be with you again. I received a very interesting letter from Rev. Mother Mary Gene- rose in Holy Family Convent, Manitowoc, Wisconsin ..... They ask our prayers. They quite enjoyed their visit with us last Nov. 1st.

neutral: Appreciation is expressed for your charitable contribution dated December 12th. The names were recorded only today. It is currently 5:30 PM. This communication has been started multiple times since 9:30 AM, and the sender has lost count of the attempts. An intention existed to send the cards, but it was determined that they would likely not be used. Consequently, blank cards are being sent in case they are desired.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your charitable favor of Dec. 12th. Only To-day did I get to note down the names. It's now five:30 and I baraly know how often I've started with this little note since 9:30 a.m. I wanted also to send the cards: but then I thought probably you would not use them anyhow. So I am sending you blanks in case you wish them.

neutral: Enrollments for Grace and Thom have been completed. Grace's request, received yesterday, has been noted. The large family photo was sent to my brother M.E.J., who is expected to appreciate it.
styled: As requested I have made the enrollmens - of Grace and Thom also. And have just noted Grace's request, received yesterday. Many thanks for your kindness in sending the large family - photo to my Rev. Brother M.E.J. I am sure he will appreciate it.

neutral: The Mother is well and anticipates traveling to the Monastery, located near Huntington. An experienced driver should be able to complete the trip easily in five or six hours. The distance from Chicago is approximately 125 miles, and it should be possible to reduce this by fifty miles using a straighter route, for example, via South Bend, Elkhart, or Coldwater. Coldwater might be out of the way, but if a direct highway exists from the North, guidance could be provided from that point. Religious personnel from Detroit and Huntington typically use the Coldwater route, which is 100 miles from Detroit. However, this route would be too far eastward for the current traveler. Coldwater is 70 miles from Fort Wayne. Highway 17 is accessible from Coldwater. From Fort Wayne, Highway 24 is 30 miles southwest.
styled: I am glad to know that your Mother feels well enough and is looking forward to making the little trip down to our Monastery here just up over the hill from Huntington. I think an experienced driver ought to be able to make the trip easily enough in five or six hours. It is only about 125 miles from Chicago, and it ought not be difficult to cut off fifty of that by a straighter route, e.g. via South Bend, Elkart or Coldwater. This last might be out of your way but in case there is a direct highway from the North I could guide you pretty well from that point. The Fathers of Detroit and Huntington usually go that way when driving. Its just 100 miles out of Detroit. That would be to far Eastward for you. Well we'll just pray the dear Lord to be your Guide - Maybe as He was to the young Tobias, through St. Raphael. P.S. Coldwater is 70 miles from Fort Wayne - I think its 17 (Hi-way) out of Coldwater - there from FrWay 30 miles S.West #24.

neutral:
I intended to call you Monday evening. However, it became too late to call, and the following evening you were at George's. I was pleased that your mother evidently enjoyed the trip and visit. That night, I went outside a couple of times after dark and found it was not dark at all, but beautifully moonlit. I was confident that you were having a pleasant, moonlit return to Muskegon.

I was not surprised that you all liked the photo. It always reminds me of a truly beautiful and touching celebration. The first eight of the sixteen individuals who have passed away have done so peacefully.

Doris, I would appreciate it if you would send that photo to Father M. Joachim Casey (my brother, to whom it belongs, as I believe I mentioned). I will inform you about the Chapter as soon as we learn the results.
styled: I wanted to call you Monday evening. But the first thing I knew it was so late that I was ashamed to call and the follow- ing ev. you were up to George's. I sure was pleased the your Mother so evidently enjoyed the trip and the little visit. I went out a couple of times after dark that night to find it not dark at all but beautiful moon-light. I was confident that you were having a pleasant moon-light return to Muskegon. Thanks be to God. ... . I was not surprized that you all liked the photo It always brings back to my mind a really beautiful and touch- celebration; and thanks be to God again the first half of the 16 to cross the border into eternity, have gone beautifully, in peace. Now Miss Doris: I would sure appreciate it if you would send that photo to Father M. Joachim Casey (my Brother to whom it belongs as I think I told you. Please God I'll let you know about the Chapter as soon as we learn the results, etc.

neutral: Thank you for the ample supply of Ben Gay (Baume Bengue), a general remedy. This supply should last a considerable time, as my eczema has largely cleared. I hope you are all well.
styled: Many thanks for your generous supply of my favorite general remedy, Ben Gay -- Baume Bengue. The same ought to hold me a long time, now that my Eczema is pretty well cleared up. I hope this finds you all well and well dis- posed for special graces these blessed days. -- and a Joy- ful Easter tide.

neutral: Appreciation is expressed for the assistance provided on April 27th. Gratitude is also extended for the prompt response concerning the violin supplies and related items. Further thanks are given for the beautiful roses, which arrived in time to enhance the decoration of the altars for the First Friday event. As of this evening, the duration of the stay will be one week. The location is considered ideal for work, prayer, and study. It is suggested that once the weather improves, a trip to this location would be pleasant, although it is likely further than Detroit.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your favor of last week - April 27th - Also for your prompt response with the violin supplies, etc - and again for the beautiful roses, just in time to enhance First Friday decoration of the altars. This evening I will have been here just a week. Thanks be to God, it is quite an ideal place - to work and pray and study - and thank God, and hope - for Heaven. I think when the weather settles a little more it would be a nice trip down here - though it must be further than Detroit ....

neutral: I hope you are all well. I was somewhat disappointed recently, as my intention was to contact you all. However, upon hearing Grandma's voice, I considered that sufficient contact and informed the operator accordingly. I also wish to thank Grace, George, and all others for their favors, which have not always been acknowledged. I hope you all have a happy Christmas. I also request that you occasionally remember me in your thoughts.
styled: Hope this finds you all well. Was a little disapointed the other night. I hoped to get in touch with you all. Well, when I heard Grandma's voice I thought that would suffice and I told the operator "OK." I want to thank Grace too and George - and all the others for their favors not always acknowledged. I hope you all have a Joyful Christmas in the peace of the Lord. Also I ask you all to continue a little prayer for this poor sinner once in a while.

neutral: The item's placement in a specific desk is unknown, but it is plausible given the number of people present during an important event involving John. This explains the lack of communication from Seattle three years prior. This releases you from all obligations related to the check, with the exception of a smile and a silent good wish. Gratitude is expressed for the many acts of kindness and generosity, along with good wishes for the Panyard Family and their many friends.
styled: How it came to be put away in Dad's desk, I do not know but it could easily have happened, so many were in and out at the time of John's First Solemn Mass." So that ex- plains my silence from Seattle coming three years ago. And this releases you of all obligations pertaining to the checque, -- save a smile and just a little, silent prayer. Thanking you again for your many proofs of kindness and gen- erosity, and wishing God's blessing to all and each of the Panyard Family and their many friends, I beg to remain,

neutral: I hope things are improving for you, and that Grace is feeling better and less busy with her activities. I am returning the enclosed check, which may come as a surprise. I hope this is a pleasant surprise, and I believe the following explanation will clarify everything. You have likely long forgotten about waiting for its return and have compensated for it through other acts of generosity. Nevertheless, I want to express my thanks, as I would have done had I received the check in Seattle along with your timely greetings and wishes. We had a memorable celebration and a pleasant family reunion. My sister's message regarding the check states: "We are moving next week to another house, and while cleaning out his desk, Pat found the enclosed envelope. Thinking it might be an advertisement, Pat opened it, and so we are sending it to you."
styled: God bless you and yours. I hope things are brightening and that Grace is slowing down a little with her hustling, etc, and feeling better. No doubt I am giving you a little surprise by returning the enclosed check. I hope it will only mean just a little smile, and when you read the following explanation, I think that is about all it will cost you. You've no doubt long since forgotten about your having waited for its return and made up for it before this by other proofs of generosity. However, I want to thank you just the same as I would have wished to do had I received it in Seattle, with your very timely greetings and wishes. We surely did have touching celebration and a pleasant family re-union. Thanks be to God. Here is what my "baby sister" says relative to the cheque. "Dear Father Solanus -- We are moving next week to another house, and while cleaning out his desk, Pat ran across the inclosed enve- lope. Thinking it might be an ad, Pat opened it, and so we are sending it on to you.

neutral: We extend our sincere thanks for your generous favor of May 4th, which has been received and noted. We hope for further positive developments, specifically that a more significant outcome will follow the $1000.00 turkey dinner. We are pleased to learn of Grace's favorable surprise. We express gratitude for all positive circumstances.
styled: God bless you Miss Doris Panyard. Many thank for your king favor of May 4th, duly Rec'd and noted. We'll pray for that. Rev. Father and will hope something bigger and better may follow the $1000.00 turkey dinner. Glad to hear of Grace's favorable surprise. Thanks be to God for every blessing.

neutral: Doris Panyard, I hope you are well and that your situation is improving by now. I wrote to you about a week ago, intending for it to reach you the day after George called, but I made an error with that correspondence, so this message is delayed. This morning, I received a telegram from my brother Edward, informing me that our other brother, Maurice Joachim, passed away this morning at 6:00 AM. He was ready for his passing, having lived a challenging life of over 81 years, marked by many struggles.
styled: God bless you Doris Panyard. I hope this finds you well and that things are brightening up by this time. I wrote you about a week ago, hoping to reach you next day after George phoned, but spoiled the card and this is the late result. I received a wire this Morning from my Rev. Brother Edward that our other Rev. brother, Father Maurice Joachim, died this Morning at 6 o'clock. R.I.P. Please pray for the repose of his dear Soul. Thanks be to God he was well pre- pared - over 81 years of a warfare - and probably one thousand of pitched battles. last.

neutral: In response to a previous inquiry, the publisher of the wartime correspondence between President Roosevelt and Pope Pius XII is The MacMillan Company, New York.
styled: God bless you and yours. Y' asked some time ago for the publishers of that War time correspondence between Pres. Roose- velt and Pope Pius XII. It is the MacMillan Company, New York. It is fine work. Its "tripple introduction" ought to insure it a wide circulation .... again, Many thanks.

neutral:
Tomorrow is the eve of the Assumption of Mary.

You had previously inquired about what Rae should do with funds provided to him for promoting the "Mystical City." Until approximately a year ago, the expectation was that he would eventually serve as the publisher. However, when Jerry contacted me from Notre Dame, my perspective shifted. Immediately afterward, a realization occurred: that significant accomplishments are often achieved by those perceived as weak. It was noted that V.M.M. of Agreda encountered numerous challenges before successfully completing her notable work a second time.

It became apparent that K.S. intended to assist L.W. Bern'kn. It was determined that, for the present, effective assistance required collaboration with L.W.B. and harmony with L.B.
styled: Tomorrow is the Vigil of the glorious Assumption of Mary our B1. Mother. Thank God! How privileged we are in being able to say so much! How little we can possibly appreciate her in this poor exile from Heaven !. You asked me sometime back about what Rae should do with certain money given him for promoting the "Mystical City." ..... Until about a year ago I had hoped that he would eventually be the publisher. However; when Jerry called me from Notre Dame and I was tempted to ask to speak to his Father - who I knew was there waiting to speak to me - I changed my view. It came to me immediately after that something like as follows: "God chooses the weak things of the world .... to do His greatest works. ." What Humiliations did not V.M.M. of Agreda meet before succeeding in writing the out standing master- piece the 2nd time!" It became clear that little K.S. wished to help L.W. Bern'kn. Only in conjunction with L.W.B. it seems to me for the present may one hope to help . Only in harmony and in conjunction with L.B.

neutral: The generous assistance was received yesterday, following a phone conversation. This communication is being dispatched today; due to the imminent arrival of the collector, it is brief. We hope for the success of all projects and activities undertaken by the Panyard Setup.
styled: Many thanks for your generous favor received yesterday just after our "long distance". I am trying to get this off To-day and its time the collecter were here so pardon haste. God's blessing to all the works and undertakings of the Panyard Setup.

neutral: Gratitude is expressed for recent kindness, including writing materials and other items, and specifically for the item titled 'Storm of St. Therese's Glory'. The item is considered interesting. This item was received on Monday. Additional gratitude is expressed for a bouquet received this afternoon.
styled: I hope this finds you all well with hopeful outlook. I want to thank you for your kindness recently received - the writing materials, etc and especially the very nice little "Storm of St. Therese's Glory". I surely find it very interest- ing. This favor came Monday - day before-yesterday. Many thanks too for the beautiful boquet just came in this afternoon. God bless you. May He speed up your plans and perfect undertakings!

neutral: Wishing you and your family well. This message is being sent today due to time constraints. Thank you for the item received yesterday. The sender intends to remember the recipient each time the item is used.
styled: God bless you and all yours: Miss Panyard, almost time ... I am trying to get this off today. Many thanks for your kind favor Rec'd yesterday. Please God I'll remember you at least as often as I use same.

neutral: The sender hopes the recipients are well and that circumstances are satisfactory. Gratitude is expressed for the "Wartime Correspondence between President Roosevelt and Pope Pius XII." The sender considers it an excellent compilation of significant ideas from influential thinkers, focusing on fundamental principles and the parallel operations of Church and State during a crisis, demonstrating their effective collaboration. It is suggested that the work would be suitable reading for all students from 8th grade through college. The sender believes its triple introduction should ensure widespread distribution. The work would naturally avoid any suggestion of communist involvement in Roosevelt's premature removal from power. However, the sender speculates that if Roosevelt's ideals, as presented in the letters, were widely known, communists would likely not hesitate to eliminate him, a fate some suspect Roosevelt himself may have experienced. Regardless, gratitude is reiterated. The sender plans to attempt a call on Saturday or Sunday after 7 P.M. The sender is identified as Det. T.
styled: I hope this finds you all well and that things have been going at least not too bad. I want to thank you for Wartime Correspondence between Pres. Roos'vlt and Pope Pius XII ... It is quite a masterpiece of compilation of masterpieces of master-minds on basic principles and parallel lines in Church and State in time of crisis pulling in perfect harmony together. It could be well placed in the hands of every 8th grader as well as every high- school and college student. Its tripple introduction ought to insure it an immense circulation. Of course expression of any suspicion of communistic influence in hurrying Roosevelt out of the picture would be out of question in such a work. But if his ideals as expressed in these letters were known, it is certain that the communists would not hesitate at such a liquidation as many seem to suspect Roosevelt's to have been ..... At all events, I thank you again and may the Lord guide you and all of us. Will try to call (Saturday or) Sunday after 7 P.M .- Det. T.

neutral:
Miss Grace Panyard,
I recalled my promise regarding the leaflets and other items. Here they are, and I trust they will be suitable.
Please inform Doris that the Fatima statue is expected to arrive at the Monastery a little after 3:15 P.M., in case she is in the neighborhood.
styled: God bless you Miss Grace Panyard, I was just in at my Hour and thought of my promise of the leaflets etc. Here they are and I am sure you will like them. Please tell Doris that it is three 3: 15 P.M. a little after that we expect that Fatima - Statue of Our B1. Mother Mary to arrive here at the Monastery, in case she's in the neighborhood.

neutral: I wrote to your brother Fred yesterday, and I am now responding to your letter of February 12th. Thank you for your letter. I have just noted your request concerning the deceased, and I hope the situation improves soon. Please tell George I am sending him a playful ear tug. Also, tell him that life is too short to be discouraged about anything in it.
styled: God bless you and yours. I write your Brother Fred yester- day and now I come to your favor of Febr. 12. Many Thanks I've just noted your request for the Poor Holy Souls .... and hope that things brighten up soon. Tell George I send him one of my good ear pulls. Tell him "life" that the world is so inclined to worship is too short to act discouraged about anything in it. Ha Hal

neutral: Thank you very much for your letter. I have temporarily misplaced it, but to avoid further delay or forgetting, I am sending this card that Rufin began. Please convey my regards to George, Mother, and especially Doris. I hope Mother and Doris enjoy their trip to Wisconsin and return safely and in good health. Please also thank Doris for her assistance last week.
styled: God bless you Grace and many thanks for your favor. I've mis- laid your letter just for the moment; but before neglecting it further and then forgetting I am just sending this card that Br. Rufin started. Please give "Best Regards" to George and and to Mother especially and to Doris. I hope these latter will enjoy their trip to Wisconsin and get back in good shape. Thank Doris also for her favor of last week.

neutral: The parents are healthy and treat the children well. Please remember Bernard Brady. This was a notable letter for a seven-year-old. Since that letter was written, there were frequent indications that the writer might pursue a monastic life, though this now seems improbable. However, the workings of destiny are beyond human comprehension, making it impossible to fully understand them. Therefore, one should acknowledge and respect the profound wisdom, power, mercy, goodness, and foresight that guide these workings. This was intended to be sent yesterday, but it is now Friday. Best wishes to you, your colleagues, your parents, all your loved ones, and even any adversaries you may have, with the hope that everyone finds a path of moral improvement. P.S. Written after returning from Texas and Washington.
styled: Papa and Mama are well and are good to us children. Please pray for your little nefue Bernard Brady". Quite a letter for a little seven-year-old. Not? · There were indications quit often since that little letter was penciled, that the writer would land somewhere nearer a monastery than would at present seem ever likely. God's ways, however, are so sublimely above our limited reckoning that we are simply lost when we venture to fathom even their shad- ows. So let us praise and adore Him in His decrees and in the very shadows of His adorable omnipotent wisdom - Power - Mercy - GOODNESS -- PROVIDENCE. I tried to get this off yesterday but it is now Friday. . . God bless you and your associates as well as your dear Parents and all your dear ones -- your enemies too if you have any, that they - that we all - be converted to God. P.S. - after return from Texas and Washington.

neutral:
Greetings to Grace Panyard. I hope this message finds you feeling more optimistic and with greater inner strength. Thank you for your many kindnesses.

I recently mentioned to Doris a highly esteemed individual, Countess Mary Therese Sedochoska, whose biography I had just read. Doris said she would get a copy to learn about her and seek inspiration from her life. I am confident you will join us in learning about her and finding guidance from her example during difficult situations.

Please tell Georg not to lose heart, regardless of the difficulties he encounters. Instead of worrying—which is never productive—encourage him to spend some time gratefully reflecting on the countless positive aspects and good fortunes that have been, and continue to be, part of our lives.
styled: God bless you Miss Grace Panyard. I hope this find you with brighter out-look and more confidence in our Blessed Lord God. Many thanks for your many kind favors. I told Doris recently of a venerable candidate for Beatification, --- Countess Mary Therese Sedochoska, whose life I recently read. Doris said she wold a copy and get acquainted with her - and ask her to help. I am sure you will join with the rest of of us in learning to know her and in turning to her in all kind of emergency. Tell Georg not to get discouraged whatever turns he meet with. Instead of worrying - never any good - tell him, let us spend some of the time in gratefully thinking over some of the innumerable blessings Almighty God has surrounded us with and still surrounds with.

neutral:
The concept that divine compassion surpasses all creations should inspire hope, presenting a positive prospect for individuals. This outlook is significant, especially if one considers hope to be fundamental to happiness and the primary purpose of intelligent beings to understand the divine. This understanding is attributed to a higher power, and the author believes their existence was intended for this comprehension. This is considered a valuable purpose, with actions of devotion and service seen as integral to it, offering a profound reward to those who appreciate it during their lifetime.

The author found it remarkable that a letter from the recipient's mother, along with the first and last letters from the author's namesake, B., were unexpectedly received on the eve of Owen Joseph's twenty-fourth birthday. This information is from a letter dated May 2, 1919, which marked the first anniversary of the recipient's grandmother Casey's death.
styled: What hope this should inspire when we remember that the mercy of God is above all His works! What an outlook for poor sinners! What a sublime horizon if, "Hope is the very soul of happiness here" and the purpose of the rational creature TO KNOW GOD, which covers everything, be kept in mind! Hence, thanks be to Divine Providence. God made me to know Him. O what a bless'd aim! To love Him and serve Him, sure rests in the same. Its "Heaven Begun" for the grateful, on earth; To treasure aright ! ! ! Highest Heaven its Worth. You are possibly surprized at the above introductry details; and it did strike me as remarkable that a letter from your dear Mother, together with the first and last that my little namesake B. ever sent me, should unexpectedly fall into my hands on the eve of the "New Baby" Owen Joseph's twenty-forth birthday. From letter dated "May 2, 1919." - first anniversary of your dear GrandMa Casey's + .. Dear Br.

neutral:
Bernard expressed that his previous sorrow had turned into joy, as they were happy about the birth of their fourth child, Owen Joseph. She added a postscript to Bernard's letter, including a sample of young Bernard's letter-writing and expressing a hope that he might follow Bernard's example. The postscript continued, stating that if he maintains his convictions and earnestly pursues what is considered the most important life's pursuit, he would be emulating respected figures. The author expressed hope that all recipients were doing the same.

A letter from young Bernard, addressed to Bernard (a priest), stated: "I was 7 years old on March 7 and am in the second grade at school. I participated in a significant religious ceremony a year ago. I have a small devotional display and enjoy performing my evening devotions in front of it. Thomas is 5 years old. Rosemary is 3 years old, and we have a new baby, Owen Joseph, who will be 4 weeks old next Sunday. I like my teacher at school very much; she is a nun named Bernard."
styled: Bernard; Well, thank God all my sorrow has most certainly turned into joy; for we are again happy over the birth of our forth child little darling Owen Joseph .. " and she adds a P.S. to B's letter: "Dear Bernard - Here is a sample of young Bernard's letter-writing. Pray that if its God's will he may follow in your footsteps." If he keep the faith and try earnestly to save his immortal soul which means success in the one thing necessary, then he is following the footsteps of all the saints. I certainly trust you are all so doing. From the "first and last letter ... " so far: Dear Father Bernard I was 7 years old March 7 and am in the second grade at school. I made my first Holy Comunion just a year ago. I have a May alter and love to say my prayers at night in front of it. Thomas is 5 years old. Rosemary is 3 years old and we have a new baby Owen Joseph he will be 4 weeks old next Sunday .. ... "I like my Sister at school very much her name is Sister Bernard.

neutral: Best wishes to you and your family, especially your Parents, Grandma, and her Husband. I regret not having seen her before she experienced cognitive decline. Now all we can do for them is to remember them. I am glad to hear from you that you are still living. I recall that when you were three, doctors had low expectations for your survival. Best regards and wishes to your Parents. I used to enjoy my visits to the West Side twenty years ago. My health has been good since I took a vacation to the West Coast to attend an event for my nephew in Seattle, Washington. It is much easier here, though keeping letters from accumulating is not a small task. I am adding your name to my emergency list for your speedy improvement and recovery.
styled: God bless you and yours - your dear Parents especially and His mercy and your dear old Grandma and her good Husband. Sorry I could not have seen her before she became childish. Now all we can do for them is to remember them in our prayer and Masses. I am glad to hear from yourself - that you are still with us. I think it was when you were three the doctors would not have bet much on your living. Well, thank God for Everything .. . Very best regards and wishes to your dear Parents. I used to quite enjoy my visits over there to the West Side twenty years back. Thanks be to God, my health has been good ever since I went West for a vacation to the First Mass of my nephew in Seattle, Wash'n. It is much easier here though it is not a small job to keep the letters from accumu- lating. I am inscribing your name in my emergency list for your speedy im- provement and recovery - please God.

neutral: A sense of peace will come to you, eventually. There is likely a reason for your struggles, just as there is for everyone else's, even when these difficulties seem beyond our control. An ultimate authority will assess the extent of our failings and difficulties, and will, at the appropriate time, elevate us beyond our current state. We need to be patient, trusting that circumstances will improve and that the underlying intention is always for our benefit. Our efforts can be utilized effectively, as long as our own intentions do not interfere with a larger, beneficial design. This holds true even though we are all flawed individuals, regardless of how others may perceive us as exemplary. There is no need to be anxious about the future. Both the future and the past are beyond our immediate control. Worrying about past events or future possibilities serves no practical purpose. It is, however, appropriate to acknowledge and express remorse for our mistakes, of which we have all made many. But to worry and fret is unproductive.
styled: God in His infinite wisdom and merciful power give you His peace! He will give it to you - sooner or later. He must have a purpose, how- ever, in permitting you to fall - even like the rest of us. - even like against our wills. ..... He is the Master and the Judge, to recon the depth of our guilt and of our humiliation as well as how high above our- selves in His own good time He will raise ua. Only we must have patience till He change His attitude: because God is always figuring on our best. "God condescends to use our powers - if we don't spoil His plans by ours." And all this even though we be stupid sinners. For that we all are, though the whole world proclaim us heros and saints. But why dear Sister be so anxious about tomorrow? The morrow like yesterday is in God's keeping. To worry about the past or the future is really to no purpose. Quite a different thing is to regret our blunders - and God knows we have all made plenty of them - and humbly deplore them. But worry and fret? No.

neutral:
The author describes a personal experience of walking alone through a silent, dim valley, perceiving no other presence besides their own. They recount engaging with the secular world but finding it unfulfilling, concluding that high ideals in that world are often shattered by reality and ultimately lost. The author then describes this "Valley" as metaphorically situated between two significant experiences: one of profound sadness and another of hopeful contemplation.

The author apologizes for any inaccuracies in quoting "Song of the Mystic" by Father Ryan, a poem they had attempted to memorize some years ago and recently again. The author finds the poem to be a source of comfort and resilience, especially when confronted with the frequent accounts of misfortune, sorrow, and disappointment received at their office. Since the preceding text, including the manuscript, was sent by air on April 9th, the author has received official information regarding Father [incomplete name].
styled: "I walked down the Valley of Silence; down the dim voiceless val'y alone And I heard not the fall of a footstep around me, save God's & my own, "I walked in the world with the worldly. I craved what the W. never gave And I said "In the world each ideal that shines like as star on life' wave Is wrecked on the shores of the real and sleeps like a dream in a grave Do you ask me the place of the Valley, ye hearts that are burdened with care It lieth afar between mountains, and God and His angels are there; And one is the dark Mount of Sorrow; and one the bright Mountain of Prayer.' Pardon for spoiling the Blind Poet, Father Ryan's beautiful "Song of the Mistic". I undertook to memorize it some years ago and just lately again. I find it a sort of nerve tonic from the tales of misfortune and of sorrow and disapointment so almost continually brought to the Monastery Office. ... Since the above - upto and including manuscript - took its air trip on April 9th I have received official information of Fr.

neutral: You are being enrolled as an emergency member in the Seraphic Mass Association. It is hoped this will help you, and that you will regain the ability to sign your name. A desire for mutual positive change, physical and otherwise, is expressed. It is suggested that for the recipient, this transformation ideally begins with the simultaneous improvement of physical function and emotional well-being.
styled: I am enrolling you as an emergency member in the Seraphic Mass Association. I do hope it help you - and, God willing, that you be able again to sign your name. We'll pray for one another's con- version - physical and otherwise. In your case that it start - as would be perhaps best - with your hand and heart together ....?

neutral:
I also want to congratulate you on your 24th anniversary. I will attempt to contact you by the end of the week, provided I am not too frequently interrupted, to remind you about your birthday, which coincides with a day known as Passion Sunday.

I hope you are well and maintaining your beliefs, because in these times of unrest and international turmoil, when atheism is widespread, it is important to remember the fundamental purpose of our existence and to live consistently with it.

I often recall the second question from the small religious instruction book we studied in our youth, in the pioneer environment of western Wisconsin, while playing among grazing cattle on slopes and wooded lowlands. The question was: "Why were you created?" The answer given was: "To understand one's creator."

If, according to philosophy, "To know is to appreciate," then it could be argued that to know is to love what is good, to reject what is bad or wicked, and to revere the ultimate good. No higher purpose seems conceivable.
styled: God bless you and yours. And before I forget, let me congratulate you on your 24th anniversary. I'll try to reach you by the end of the week if not interrupted too frequently; so that you may have a reminder on the solemnity corresponding to that on which you were born, - Passion Sunday. I hope you are well and keeping the faith; for in these days of un- rest and of international turmoil when atheism - the positive climax of insanity - is so rampant, it is no trifle to keep in mind the great pur- pose of our creation and to live consistently, as for God. Ah, how often has not that second question of the little catechism we used to study while romping with grazing cattle on the slopes and wooded lowlands of pioneer west Wisconsin, come back to me! "Why did God make you?" And the beautiful answer: "To know God ... "! !! If according to philosophy: "To know is to appreciate." may we not say that, to know is to love the good; is to reject the bad, the wicked; is to adore the Divine? Could we think of a higher purpose? ....

neutral:
Instead of yielding to negative impulses, it is better to find positive aspects, appreciating the patience and understanding extended, even when one might feel undeserving.

Dear Mary Dorothy,
I have not forgotten you; your letter of June 29 has been on my desk since it arrived. I have wanted to write something worthwhile, but I am constantly falling behind with my work. Today, upon seeing your letter from the 14th, I started this message simply to assure you that I will write soon. You have no idea how much I need support—personal improvement for myself and for you.
styled: Because that hell wants us to do. Rather draw good out of them by praising God for His mercy to us and His infinite patience in not kicking to blases as good for nothings .... Dear Sister Mary Dorothy: I have not been forgetting you I've had your letter of June 29 here on the desk before me ever since. I've wanted to write something worth while but am always falling be- hind with my work. To-day on coming to yours of the 14th I started this just to assure you I'd write soon. You have no idea how much I need prayers - conversion as well as u.

neutral: Grace traveled to Toronto and is expected to meet Uncle Ed Traynor and his family. Owen accompanied the speaker on Saturday, February 1st, but returned the following day. Yesterday, Owen sent a telegram from Seattle reporting that Patrick is unwell. At 11 a.m. today, a telegram from Minneapolis stated a hope to see Patrick by Friday morning in Seattle. The speaker sent Patrick an expedited air delivery yesterday, following Owen's telegram.
styled: Grace went to Toronto and will probably meet the Uncle Ed Traynor and Family. Owen came down with me Saturday Feb. 1st but went back next day. Yesterday he wired from Seattle that our Brother Patrick is not well and just now ( 11 a.m. ) a wire from Minneapolis from Msgr. says he hopes to see Pat by Friday a.m. in Seattle. I sent Br. Patrick an air special yesterday after Owen's wire.

neutral: Thank you for your letter dated the 27th. I hope you are feeling better and continuing to improve. I recommend you consult a chiropractor. I had been receiving treatment for my feet and legs for at least three years, using a cane for several months and experiencing significant lameness. In less than three weeks, Dr. Ralph Schorn restored my ability to walk, making my cane unnecessary. His office is located across Gratiot Avenue from the Airport, at 10050 Connors Avenue.
styled: Many thanks for your kind favor of the 27th. God bless you too Maurice O'Connell. I hope this finds you improved and improving. However, I think you would do well to see a good Chiropractor. I was doctoring for at least three years for my feet and legs - using a cain for several months and quite lame. ..... .. In less than three week Dr. Ralph Schorn had me on my feet - with my cain a forgotten thing. His of- fice is just across Gratiot Ave. from the Airport - 10050 Connors Ave. Hoping this finds you 100% in God's grace and service.

neutral: Providing detailed information is not feasible here and will be left to others. A continuous series of beneficial events occurred over 50 years, culminating in a significant ceremony. This event was regarded as a crucial milestone in an individual's life journey. The profound significance of one's core beliefs was emphasized. Conversely, the state of those embracing atheism was lamented. Atheism was characterized as the peak of intellectual and spiritual irrationality, a futile outcome and a desperate recourse for superficial thought and morally compromised individuals, with its ultimate source attributed to a figure representing profound evil. An individual referred to as E. returned to St. Paul on Tuesday afternoon.
styled: To go into details is so out of the question here that I'll simply have to leave that to others. If I were only one tenth as grateful and appreciative as I ought to be I would hardly be able to do more than wonder and weep for joy at so many and so great favors following one another for 50 years, etc, all leading up to such a solemnity - as to just another decided "landmark" on the way of an individual's pilgrimage to real LIFE with the God of everlasting glory and the unfading love of the chosen servants in Heaven. How can we ever thank God as we ought for the inestimable gift of the true faith? A on the other hand, how lament the unfortunate lot of the vic- tims of atheism? - "The climax of intellectual and of spiritual insanity, the hopeless conclusion and the desperate refuge of shallow thinking, of edgener- ate minds and ( fearful to say), damned fools, none other their primary leader than Lucifer himself the prince of diabolical darkness. . Rt. Rev. Msgr. E'd had to get back to St. Paul. So left Tuesday P.M.

neutral:
Thank you for your contribution of January 26th, which was received and noted. I offer my condolences on the death of your mother. I had intended to write sooner, but I have difficulty managing the volume of calls and letters that require my attention. It is reassuring, however, that she seemed prepared for and accepting of her death, and I hope she finds peace.

On the same day you wrote, we held a significant celebration in Detroit – a formal service of thanksgiving commemorating my fiftieth year in the Franciscan Order. By now, you have likely heard some of the interesting details. Monsignor Edward and Brother Owen telegraphed the previous day, stating they would arrive in Detroit at 7:10 p.m. Meanwhile, Mrs. B. Brady flew in from San Francisco and met them at the station. All three arrived at the Monastery together around 7:45 p.m.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your charitable favor of Jan, 26th duely receiven and noted. I surely sympathize with you on the passing away of your dear Mother. I wanted to wrote before but it is difficult for me to get through with calls and letters that demand attention. Thank God, however, that she seems to have been well prepared and willing to respond to God's final call. May she rest with the saints in the peace of which the unbelieving wordl never dreams - awaiting all and each who try .. The same day you wrote, we had a very notable celebration in Detroit, - a solemn Mass of thanks giving as commemorating, my fiftieth year in the Habit of St. Francis. By this time you will no doubt have heard a number of the interesting features. Rt. Msgr. Edw'd and Br. Owen wired of their coming the day before to arrive in Det. at 7:10 p.m. Grace - Mrs B. Brady in the meantime, flew in from San Francisco and met them at the depot - all three arriving at the Monastery together about 7:45.

neutral: Thank you for your recent communication. We are enrolling Maureen in a prayer association, hoping this will lead to a surprisingly positive outcome for her, exceeding the expectations of her doctors and all others involved in her case. We also recommend that you encourage as many friends as possible to offer intense and regular prayers for Maureen. Additionally, we suggest you promise your deceased relatives – especially those believed to be undergoing purification and who are thought to be concerned for their living family members – that you will perform a special act for them. This is on the condition that they join your friends in advocating for Maureen as effectively as possible. We have observed wonderful results and received astonishing reports from including deceased relatives in these efforts; for example, some have reported a reduction in medical expenses due to unexpected recovery.
styled: God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of just noted. We are enrolling your little Maureen in the Seraphic Mass Associa- tion that if it be God's holy will she may give the doctors and all who may be interested in her case, a good surprise. At the same time I would suggest that you get as many of your friends as possible to help you storm Heaven by frequent and daily Communion. And I might add, that you promise the Poor Souls - especially your own family- relatives, there doing penance and always interested in the welfare of their dear ones there left behind, that you will do somthing special for them if join the rest of friends as well as they may, by their pleading the cause of little Maureen as best they can. I've seen wonderful results and have had astonishing reports as throuth enrolling the Poor Souls, e.g., for a given percentage of the a- verted "doctor-bills". Thanks be to the merciful condesntion of Almighty God - and the all surpassing intercession of our B1. Mother Mary

neutral: Receipt of your letter dated April 29 is acknowledged. Apologies for the delay in responding. The reported improvement in your condition is noted. It is hoped that your progress continues. The Masses have been completed. Enclosed is an item intended to be satisfactory in place of what you requested. The envelope was opened to insert a card.
styled: Many thanks for your favor of April 29. Please pardon delayed ac- knowledgement. Thank the good God for your improvement reported. May He continue to brighten things for you. The holy Masses have been solved. I am sending you herewith something will, I hope be satisfac- tory in place of what you ask. P.S. Am opening envelope to incert card. - "more haste less speed !. "

neutral: It is hoped that your circumstances are improving. While profound positive change can be challenging, it is believed that seeking assistance can be beneficial. Even if specific requests are not met as desired, alternative positive outcomes or personal growth may emerge. Regardless, try to gather support from your friends to help seek a cure or improvement of some kind, enabling you to continue and accept the situation until the end. You are being registered again, and support will be offered with hopes for positive results soon.
styled: I hope this finds things brightening some way with you. You know that only God can work miracles. And when we turn to Him with con- fidence He never turns us down - if He forces it is for the good of our souls and to His glory. If not He always gives something better for us than what we ask for. At all events, try and get as many of your friends to help you "storm Heaven" for help - a cure or improvement of some kind so as to carry on and be at least resigned to His holy will till the end. We are enrolling you again and will pray for you and hope for results soon.

neutral: Congratulations, James, on your new and long-awaited status. I've started writing to you a few times since receiving your letter, and I now feel this message might be overdue. I am thinking of you and everyone in Colorado and hope to see you on Sunday.
styled: God Bless you Dear James - but now I must God bless Father James, So at long last and hearty Congratulations. I started to write a couple times since receiving your personal letter and now I feel almost too late. Anyway I am remembering you and all the folks over on Colorado and hope to see you Sunday.

neutral: Seek guidance for yourself and for all involved parties. If your relatives wish to contribute to fairness and harmony, they should support your search for direction while you consult a trusted advisor. However, you should disregard any other demands or instructions. You cared for your parents, and as a result of your kindness towards them, you were given the homestead. Therefore, it is fair that you should keep what was arranged for you to have.
styled: Pray to the good Lord for guidance, and to guide all concerned. If your Sisters and inlaws want to do something to promote justice and peace, they should join you in prayer for guideance while you consult a confessor, a priest. But you must turn a deaf ear to any other dictations. You took care of your mother and dad through the grace of God, and God in His goodness arranged for you to have the homestead because of your kind- ness to your mother and Dad. So in all justice you should keep what the Good Lord arranged for you to have.

neutral: I am grateful to you and our friends who have generously supported me through their prayers and other contributions, including their religious observances. I have been praying for them and including them in my religious services, and will dedicate my next service for your and their individual intentions and guidance. I would like to write to each person individually, but that would prevent me from performing more urgent duties. Therefore, I must be brief. I hope that you all receive blessings, grace, and good health for the upcoming special season and holidays, including the Immaculate Conception, Christmas, New Year's, and the subsequent annual cycle.
styled: Many thanks to you and our dear friends who has so generously remembered me in their prayers and other alms - especially in their Holy Communions, Masses and rosaries. I have been including them in my prayers and holy Masses and will offer my next "Free Mass" for your and their individual intentions and holy guidance. ..... . I would like to write each one but that would not permit me to perform more urgent duties. So I'll have to be brief. Praying that you each and all be blessed with God holy grace and health for the coming privileged holy season and feasts - Immaculate Con- ception - Christmas - New Years and following again around.

neutral: The letter dated November 12, 1947, concerning your son, Dan, has been received. An enrollment card for the Seraphic Mass Association is being sent, as it is unclear if one was previously provided. An update on Dan's current status is requested, specifically whether he is still alive or has passed away. The writer's perspective is that if Dan has passed away, it would be a fortunate outcome for him and his parents. Hope was also expressed that the new baby is bringing joy to the home.
styled: I just came across your pathetic letter of Nov. 12th '47 and was wonder- ing what might have come to your little Dan. Not sure if I ever sent you an enrollment card for the Seraphic Mass Association, I am sending you one now. At all events I would be pleased to know if little Danny is still living or is he already gone to Heaven - for to die in a state of such innocence as he was in, and his physical condition, would mean that he would go to Heaven at once. In such a case, how supremely for- tunate for the little saint! Also how fortunate the parents. . I hope too, your new Baby is already able to fill your home with sunshine.

neutral: I received your letter of February 24th today and have just finished reading it, despite several interruptions. I'm not sure what advice to give, beyond suggesting you practice patience with yourself and others, whether in a classroom, a religious community, or anywhere else. It is certain that we make no progress in moral development or personal growth without patiently humbling ourselves in the face of difficulties that serve to curb our self-importance and pride. If you feel called to a higher level of moral commitment, and if you have recognized the significance of such a calling, perhaps repeatedly, eventually agreeing, even if reluctantly, to pursue this demanding path, then it is natural and logical to anticipate various difficulties. These challenges will help you develop the virtues that overcome adversity and lead to beneficial results.
styled: Only Today did I come to your favor of February 24th and though several times interrupted have just finished it. I hardly know what to advise you, other than that you simply practice patienc with yourself as well as with your neighbor - whether in the class -room or in the Convent or elswhere. For we may be sure that we come nowhere in the practice of virtue or in spiritual progress with patiently humbling ourselves in the face of the difficulties where-with the divinely jealous Lover of our poor souls is pleased to cheque our selfconceit and pride. If the Dear Lord has deigned to invite you to more than ordin- ary virtue and if on your part you have, perhaps again and again, seen something of the privilege of such an invitation, - finally concencenting even half generously to follow the CRUCIFIED SPOUSE, then you may quite naturally - locically rather - expect difficul- ties of some kind or of any kind to exercise you in the virtues that put the enemies the Cross to shame and make Heaven rejoice.

neutral:
Your letter of March 5 has been received. Certificates of enrollment in the Seraphic Mass Association have been mailed. The positive news about your brother-in-law has been received. A wish is expressed for his continued spiritual perseverance and eventual salvation.

Regarding joining a "Third Order" or an order of "Oblates," the specific choice is not critical, as either option can lead to salvation. The important factors are the motivation for joining and adherence to the spirit and rules of the chosen order. From a practical perspective, it is suggested to join the one that is most appealing, as human nature tends to conform more easily to the spirit and rules of an order that resonates personally. It is recommended to gather information on all three options, consider them thoroughly, and after a period of careful reflection, join the one perceived to be most beneficial for one's salvation.
styled: Your letter and kind favor of Mar. 5 is gratefully acknowledged. Certificates of enrollment in the Seraphic Mass Assn. have been mailed. Glad to hear the good news about your brother in law. May he persevere in God's Holy Grace, and thus eventually gain his eternal reward. With regard to joining a "Third Order" or an order of "Oblates", to the Good Lord, it really doesn't matter which one you join, since you can insure your eternal salvation in any or either one. The important thing is the motive for joining, and the observance of the spirit and rule of the one which you belong. From a human standpoint however, we would be inclined to join the one that has the most appeal to you, since then our human nature would readily conform to the spirit and rule of that order. I would suggest that you obtain information on all three, taking all things into consideration, and after spending sufficient time in prayer and medi- tation, join that one which you feel will do you the most good, in regards to your eternal salvation.

neutral: Periods of intense, unspeakable grief and distress, once time has brought healing and calm, can become the source from which numerous positive qualities and strengths emerge. The experience of grief can deepen compassion and leave a lasting impression of love on those who share it. Acts of sympathy and kindness often arise from past pain and sorrow that has been overcome.
styled: "The hours that fill the soul with silent grief, - that flood it with unutterabl woe - Become, whin time hath given calm relief, the fountain whence a hundred virtues flow. "The mourner's tear hath furrowed kindly faces and left the light of love abiding there. SWeet sympathy and tender deeds are traces of pain and sorrow, soothed in silent Prayer. "Christ wraught Redemption from despair and sin. By His dear Cross the clouds of grief "Tis Bethlem and Calvary that win, from pain and sorrow, the seets of Heaven were riven. E. F. Casey. as a student. Hope you'll lake the lines herewith inclosed. Pray for the conversion of sinners - always including 1st yourself and then the writer.

neutral: Humility is considered the fundamental virtue from which all other meaningful virtues originate and are sustained. Enclosed is a letter written several years ago by Edward F. Casey, who was rescued from a Japanese prison on February 23rd, 1945. It is believed that careful reading and study of this letter will be beneficial. Under all circumstances, frequently seek guidance and strength, particularly for patience and humility, to effectively respond to life's challenges and opportunities. I received your message yesterday. I am available to meet on any Saturday or Sunday that is convenient for you.

If you are driving, a suggested route is via Route 112 (and Willowrun) to Coldwater. From Coldwater, take Coldwater 2, then Route 24 to Jefferson Avenue in Huntington. Turn right for three units (e.g., blocks or turns) until St. Felix is visible half a mile to the left. To reach Fort Wayne, take Route 27. If the road is muddy and soft, it is advisable to return two or three blocks to the first paved street. St. Felix is approximately 1.5 miles from the city center.

Meanwhile, I am sending you a copy of a letter that, if read correctly, should significantly help you alleviate the excessive worry you appear to be experiencing. This worry should be resisted. Worry is unproductive, and in most cases, it is about something that is unfounded and therefore does not materialize.

The Wabash train that departs Detroit at approximately 7:30 AM stops in Huntington.

One often does not appreciate good health until it deteriorates. It is important to acknowledge both life's challenges and its comforts.
styled: Its nearly a year now since your little visit the St. Felix Friary .. Many thanks for your kind favor of June 11th duly received and noted. How little we can appreciate our health until it fails us. So we really ought to thank God for trials and crosses as well as for joys and consolations.

neutral: Thank you for your thoughtful gift, which was very useful for several guests who arrived last night and this morning. Twenty-six novices took simple vows during the formal services. However, I must now shift my tone and express my concern about your unusual preoccupation with your health, doctors, or other matters. You undoubtedly wish for a favorable ultimate destiny. But how can one achieve such a goal without enduring hardship? Yet, by vigorously protesting against various difficulties, you are, in effect, communicating to a higher power (or fate) that if you cannot have at least some choice, you will give up, unable to succeed. Consider what would have happened if, at a crucial juncture, a significant individual had prioritized personal desire, saying, 'This is too much!', instead of accepting a difficult, predetermined course of action with the sentiment, 'Not my preference, but what is necessary.' Where is our conviction? Where is our demonstration of devotion, if enduring hardship for the sake of a cherished cause or individual is considered a testament to love?

neutral:
It is important to remember, despite human limitations, especially during difficult times, the concept of an endless future and how it contrasts with the briefness of individual human lives, as well as the fleeting nature of temporary experiences, whether pleasant or painful. One should be grateful for all experiences.

Even Jesus, in his human aspect, required significant internal resolve and external support to accept a challenging destiny. This underscores the importance of continuously seeking such strength and assistance. Consequently, there is an encouragement to emulate this pursuit, even if imperfectly.

Consider the ultimate reward. It is invaluable, far exceeding any possible cost or effort. This value is underscored by the belief that Jesus, a revered figure, sacrificed his life for humanity. Therefore, the specific manner or timing of one's death—whether from illness, sacrifice, or any other cause, today or in the distant future—becomes inconsequential.
styled: We ought to keep in mind as much as our poor frailities permit, especially in times of pains and sorrow; the thought of ETERNITY and the contrast of it with momentary passing for each one of us and the vanity of temperal phenomina - be they pleasant or painful to nature. We ought to thank God for both - for each and all these experiences. Even Jesus could not have accepted that decision of His heavenly Father, according to His human nature and with the divine nature, viz, without the grace of the Father. Hence, His continual communion with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Hence too our obligation to imitate Him, at least try at a distance. To get to Heaven! Think of it. 01 Is it not infinitely more than we can pay for it whatever way we consider it? When it was so great in the estimation of the Son of God Jesus and His for each one of us that He died for each of us! Then, what matter if I die with cancer or TB or a martyr some other way - To- day, tomorow or fifty years ahead?

styled: Surely it is a promisin turn in the outlook for a five- year paralytic. Their fraternal-Christian interest as shown in response to the Chaplain's appeal for a so helpless sister-Mrs. Mary O.D., is surely to the high credit of the Boys in Cap (at the Gross Ille Base") . If every one of Mary's friends do what they can to please God and to sanctify their own souls, God in His merciful wisdom and power will give them the surprise of their life.

Mother yesterday and gave her every every assurance of my approval of your joining them - in fact congratulating them on your aquisition and enrolling their community in the Seraphic Mass Association in the hopes that you may in one or more ways presage a speeding up of vocations -- Ahl God willing, a speeding up in numbers and holyness before God. An uncle named Jerry McCarthy died in Neutown, Massachusetts, at the age of 104.

The recipient is currently experiencing a difficult period. The sender hopes the recipient can benefit from this situation and advises accepting the difficulties. styled: Dear Jerry: I hope this may not have bored any one too much. When we get a little older and we may have a little more leisure I'll have to tell you about my Uncle, another grand (old) Jerry Mccarthy, who died in Neutown, Massachuttes at the age of 104. God bless you agani Jerry: and that you may profit by this little holdup you are experiencing these days, just try and take the whole thing and all its difficulties as from the hand of the Allwise and Merciful and Gracious God. Thank Him at all times and possibly when you get a little stronger you might think of some little way wherin personally to improve in His privileged service, possibly more frequently to receive if He speed the return of your health and surprise the doctors and your many friends. . . Deo Gr.

neutral: Best wishes to you, Jerry McCarthy, and your family. We have been hoping for your health to improve. Although reports were not very positive yesterday and today, we still hope you are feeling better and continuing to recover. Regardless of the circumstances, we encourage you to make the best of the situation. Furthermore, we are grateful in advance for any positive developments that may arise in response to our hopes. Yesterday, I suggested to Miss Franklyn that we all make a concerted effort for your swift recovery, and that each of us make a small personal sacrifice. She immediately agreed with the idea. I believe you will find the suggestion amusing when she eventually shares it with you. I was very pleased by her willingness. I regret not being able to speak with all of your staff. I was certainly pleased to meet them on December 10th.
styled: God bless you Jerry Mccarthy; - you and yours. We have been praying for your health-improvement; and although reports were not too good yesterday and today; still we hope this find you improved and improving. At all events dear Jerry, make the best of the situ- ation by offering everything to God in union with the sufferings and joys of Jesus' sacred Passion and victorious Resurrection. Not only that dear Jerry; but let us Thank God ahead of time for how and by what blessings He may see whereby best to answer our pleadings. I proposed yesterday to Miss Franklyn that we all join in "sort of storming Heaven" for Jerry's speedy recovery, God willing, and that we each make some little sacrifice of somekind. She surely seemed to fall in line with the idea at once. I am sure you will smile some day when she tells you the suggestion proposed. I was surely pleased at her willingness manifested. Sorry I could not talk with your whole Personnel - of whatever denominsyion. I cer- tainly was pleased to meet them as we did have the privilege to do so December 10th last. Glory be to God.
